His saying, Exalted is He: {فدلاهما بغرور}: The bāʾ is for the ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: [the two of them] accompanied by delusion, or [he] accompanied by delusion; so it is a ḥāl either from the agent or from the object. The bāʾ may also be causal, i.e.: he brought them down because he deluded them. الغُرور is a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose agent and object are omitted, the implied form being: by his deluding them. His saying «فدلاَّهما» may be from التَدْلية, from the meaning of "he let his bucket down into the well", the meaning being: he made them covet. Abū Jundab al-Hudhalī said:
2170 - أَحُصُّ فلا أُجير ومَنْ أُجِرْه ... فليس كمَنْ تَدَلَّى بالغرورِ
(I am shorn [of allies], so I give no protection; but whomever I do protect is not like one let down by delusion.)
And it may be from الدالّ and الدالّة, which is boldness, i.e.: he emboldened them. The poet said:
2171 - أظن الحِلْمَ دَلَّ عليَّ قومي ... وقد يُسْتَجْهَلُ الرجلُ الحليم
(I think my forbearance has emboldened my people against me; and the forbearing man may be provoked to folly.)
On the second, the origin is دَلَّلهما; the succession of three like letters was found heavy, so the third was changed into a soft letter, as in their saying تظنَّيْتُ for تظنَّنْت, and قَصَّيْت أظفاري for قَصَصْت; and the poet said:
2172 - تَقَضِّيَ البازيْ إذا البازي كسرْ ...
(…the swooping of the falcon when the falcon folds its wings.)
الذَّوْق is perceiving taste with the mouth, and eating is expressed by it. It was said: الذوق is touching a thing with the tongue or the mouth. One says of it: ذاق يذوق ذَوْقاً, like صام يصوم صوماً and نام ينام نوماً.
His saying: {وَطَفِقَا}: طَفِقَ is among the verbs of commencement (afʿāl al-shurūʿ), like أخذ, جعل, أنشأ, عَلِق, هَبَّ and انبرى. These indicate engagement in the beginning of the action. Their ruling is the ruling of the verbs of approximation (afʿāl al-muqāraba) in that their khabar (predicate) can only be an imperfect verb, and it may not at all be joined with أَنْ, because it is incompatible with them, since they are for commencement, which is present, while «أَنْ» is for the future. The khabar may occur as a nominal clause, as in the poet's saying:
2173 - وقد جَعَلَتْ قَلوصُ بني سهيلٍ ... من الأَكْوارِ مَرْتَعُها قريبُ
(The young she-camel of the Banū Suhayl began to have her pasture near the saddles.)
[Translator's note: The verse number appears in the source as 3173, evidently a misprint for 2173.]
and as a conditional, like إذا, as in the saying of ʿUmar: «فجعل الرجل إذا لم يستطع أن يَخْرج أَرْسَلَ رسولاً» ("and a man, if he could not go out, would begin to send a messenger"). One says طَفِقَ with fatḥa and kasra on the fāʾ, and also طَبِق with the single-dotted bāʾ. The alif is its ism and «يخصفان» its khabar.
الخَصْف is stitching in sandals, which is placing one layer upon another and stitching them together. المِخْصَف is what one stitches with, namely the awl. The poet said:
2174 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
أَنْفِها كالمِخْصَف
(…its nose like the awl.)
الخَصَفة is also a basket for dates; الخَصَف is coarse garments; خَصَفْتُ الخَصْفة means I wove it; and الأَخْصَف and الخصيف are a food of mixed colours, its origin being that milk or the like is placed in the خَصْفة and takes on its colour. Al-ʿAbbās said, praising the Prophet ﷺ:
2175 -. . . . . . طِبْتَ في الظلال وفي ... مستودَعٍ حيث يُخْصَفُ الورقُ
(…you were good in the shades, and in a place of deposit where leaves are stitched together.)
He alludes to the Garden, i.e. where [the leaves] are stitched and laid one over another.
His saying: {أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا}: this affirmative-interrogative (taqrīrī) clause may be explicative of the calling, having no grammatical position; and it may be that there is an omitted "saying" which governs it, i.e.: and He said: "Did I not forbid you two?", that saying also being explicative of the calling. The Shaykh said: "It is preferable that the pronoun in «عليهما» refers to their two private parts, as though it were said: they were stitching over their private parts; it refers with the dual pronoun because the plural is meant as two. The pronoun may not refer to Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ, because it is established in the science of Arabic that the verb of an overt noun or of an attached pronoun does not pass to an attached pronoun that is accusative in form or position, outside the chapter of ẓanna and فقد, عدم and وجد. You may not say: زيد ضربه ('Zayd struck him[self]'), nor ضربه زيد, nor زيد مرَّ به, nor مرَّ به زيد. Had we made the pronoun in «عليهما» refer to Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ, it would entail that «يَخْصِفُ» passes to a pronoun accusative in position while it has made nominative an attached pronoun, namely the alif in «يَخْصِفان». If that is taken on the omission of an intended muḍāf, it is allowed, its implied form being: يَخْصِفان على بَدَنَيْهما ('they stitch over their two bodies')." I say: like that in what he mentioned are {وهزى إِلَيْكِ} [Maryam: 25] and {واضمم إِلَيْكَ جَنَاحَكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 32], and the poet's saying:
2176 - هَوِّنْ عليك فإن الأمور ... بِكَفِّ الإِله مقاديرُها
(Take it easy on yourself, for the measures of all affairs are in the hand of God.)
and also his saying:
2177 - دَعْ عنك نَهْباً صِيْح في حَجَراته ... ولكنْ حديثاً ما حديثُ الرواحلِ
(Leave aside a plunder over whose sides the cry went up; but tell a tale — what is the tale of the riding camels?)
[Translator's note: The discussion of «عليهما» (from «يَخْصِفَانِ عَلَيْهِمَا») appears in the source under «أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا»; the passage seems displaced, and the heading «أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا» is treated again below.]
As for {مِن وَرَقِ}, «مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the extent or for partition. Abū al-Sammāl read «وطَفِقا» with fatḥa on the fāʾ, which is a dialect, as stated.
Al-Zuhrī read «يُخْصِفان», from أخصف; it admits two views. The first: that afʿala has the meaning of faʿala. The second: that the hamza is for transitivity, the object on this view being omitted, i.e.: they make themselves stitch, i.e. make themselves stitchers. Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Mujāhid and Ibn Waththāb read «يَخِصِّفان» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, kasra on the khāʾ and the ṣād doubled; the origin is يختصفان: the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād, then the khāʾ was made to follow the ṣād in its vowel. This reading will have a parallel in Yūnus and Yā Sīn, such as {يهدي} [Yūnus: 6] [Translator's note: the source has «يهدي»; the reading meant is evidently «يَهِدِّي» in Yūnus 35] and {يَخِصِّمُون} [Yā Sīn: 49], if Allah the Exalted wills. Maḥbūb transmitted the same from al-Ḥasan, except that he gave fatḥa to the khāʾ and did not make it follow the ṣād; this is also the reading of Yaʿqūb and Ibn Burayda. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «يُخُصِّفان» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and the khāʾ and a doubled kasra on the ṣād; it is from خصَّف with doubling, except that he made the khāʾ follow the yāʾ before it in its vowel. It is a reading difficult to pronounce. What shows that its origin is from خَصَّف with doubling is the reading of some «يُخَصِّفَان», likewise, except with fatḥa on the khāʾ according to its origin.
His saying: {أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُمَا}: this clause is in the position of an accusative by an implied "saying", that saying being a ḥāl, its implied form being: and He called to them, saying that. The name of the caller was not stated explicitly here because it is known. «لكما» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «عدو» because of the verbal meaning in it. It may also be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl from «عدوّ», because had it come after it, it could have been an adjective of it.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying, Exalted is He: {وَإِن لَّمْ تَغْفِرْ}: this is a condition whose apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer of the implied oath indicates it; for before the conditional particle there is an implied lām of preparation (tawṭiʾa) for the oath, as in His saying: {وَإِن لَّمْ يَنتَهُواْ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَيَمَسَّنَّ} [al-Māʾida: 73]. What indicates that is the frequent occurrence of the lām of preparation before the conditional particle in their speech. The i'rab of what follows has been given in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ}: The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ibn Dhakwān read «تَخْرُجون» here; and in al-Jāthiya: {فاليوم لاَ يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْهَا وَلاَ} [al-Jāthiya: 35]; and in al-Zukhruf: {كَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ} [al-Zukhruf: 11]; and at the beginning of al-Rūm: {وَكَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ} [al-Rūm: 19] — they read all of them in the active voice, and the rest read them in the passive. At the beginning of al-Rūm there is a disagreement [in the transmission] from Ibn Dhakwān. By "the beginning of al-Rūm" I exclude His saying {إِذَآ أَنتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ} [al-Rūm: 25], which was read in the active voice without disagreement. Some did not mention Ibn Dhakwān's agreement with the two brothers in al-Jāthiya. Both readings are clear.
And [regarding] His saying: {قَالاَ رَبَّنَا} [al-Rūm: 23] [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse is al-Aʿrāf: 23]: the benefit of omitting the vocative particle here is the glorification of the one addressed and declaring Him transcendent. Makkī said: "In calling upon the Lord, the omission of «يا» is frequent in the Quran. The reason for that is that in omitting «يا» from calling upon the Lord there is the meaning of glorification and transcendence. That is because the vocative contains a share of the meaning of command; for when you say 'O Zayd', its meaning is: come, O Zayd; I summon you, O Zayd. So «يا» was omitted from calling upon the Lord so that the meaning of command would disappear and diminish, because «يا» emphasises it and makes its meaning manifest; so in omitting «يا» there is reverence, glorification and declaring transcendence."
[Translator's note: The source places this verse 23 discussion under the heading of verse 25.]

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {يُوَارِي}: in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective of «لباساً». His saying «وريشاً» may be of the type of conjoining adjectives, the meaning being that He described the garment with two things: covering the private parts and adornment; He expressed the latter with «الريش» (feathers), because feathers are an adornment for the bird just as clothing is an adornment for human beings. That is why al-Zamakhsharī said: "الريش is the garment of adornment, borrowed from the feathers of birds because they are its clothing and adornment." It may also be of the type of conjoining a thing to something other than it, i.e.: We sent down upon you two garments, a garment described by covering and a garment described by adornment. This is al-Zamakhsharī's preference, for he said, after what I have just related from him: "i.e. We sent down upon you two garments: a garment that covers your private parts and a garment that adorns you, because adornment is a valid aim, as the Exalted said: {لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةً} [al-Naḥl: 8], {وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ} [al-Naḥl: 6]." On this view the speech amounts to omitting a described noun and putting its adjective in its place, the implied form being: and a feathered garment, i.e. having feathers.
Concerning الرِّيْش there are two views. The first: that it is a noun for this well-known thing. The second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun): one says راشَه يَريشه رِيْشاً when he puts feathers on it. So الريش should be shared between the maṣdar and the concrete noun; this is the verified view. ʿUthmān, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Sulamī, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and his son Zayd, Abū Rajāʾ, Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, and ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission from each, read «ورِياشاً». There are two interpretations of it. The first — and al-Zamakhsharī held it — that it is the plural of رِيْش, like شِعْب and شِعاب. The second: that it is also a maṣdar, so ريش and رياش are two maṣdars of راشه الله رَيشاً ورياشاً, i.e. Allah bestowed favour on him. Al-Zajjāj said: "[It is] the garment"; on this view both are nouns for the thing worn — they said لِبْس and لِباس. I say: al-Farrāʾ allowed it to be a maṣdar; so al-Zamakhsharī took one of the two views and others took the other. And they recited:
2178 - ورِيْشي منكمُ وهَوايَ مَعْكمْ ... وإن كانت زيارتُكم لِماما
(My goods come from you and my love is with you, even if your visits are but rare.)
His saying: {وَلِبَاسُ التقوى}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Kisāʾī read «لباسَ» in the accusative, and the rest «لباسُ» in the nominative. The accusative is by conjunction with «لباساً», i.e.: We sent down a covering garment and adornment, and We also sent down the garment of piety. This strengthens the view that «ريشاً» is a second adjective of the first «لباساً», since had He meant it as an adjective of a second garment, He would have made its described noun explicit, just as He made explicit this garment annexed to piety.
As for the nominative, it has five explanations. The first: that «لباس» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «ذلك» a second mubtadaʾ and «خير» the khabar (predicate) of the second, the second with its khabar being the khabar of the first. The link here is the demonstrative, which is one of the five agreed-upon links; we have a sixth that is disputed, to which attention has been drawn before. This is the soundest of the analyses of this noble verse. The second: that «لباس» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: and it is the garment of piety. This is the view of Abū Isḥāq al-Zajjāj, and it is as though the meaning of this clause is an explanation of the preceding garment; on this view His saying «ذلك» is another clause made of a mubtadaʾ and khabar.
Makkī construed it better than al-Zajjāj's construction, saying: "And covering the private parts is the garment of piety." The third: that «ذلك» is a separating pronoun (faṣl) between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar. This is the view of al-Ḥūfī, and I know of no grammarian who allowed that, except that al-Wāḥidī said: "Whoever said that «ذلك» is superfluous (laghw) found no evidence for his view, because it may be on one of the [explanations] we mentioned." I say: his saying "superfluous" is close to the view of separation, because the faṣl has no grammatical position according to the majority of grammarians, Basran and Kufan. The fourth: that «لباس» is a mubtadaʾ, «ذلك» a badal (substitute) from it, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it, or an adjective, and «خير» its khabar. This is the sense of the statement of al-Zajjāj, Abū ʿAlī and Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī. However, al-Ḥūfī said: "My view is that «ذلك» is not an adjective of «لباس التقوى», because the vague nouns [demonstratives] are more definite than what has the alif and lām and what is annexed to the alif and lām, and the norm for an adjective is to be equal to the described noun or less definite than it. If anyone has held this view before, it is an oversight."
I say: as for holding it, it has been held, as I mentioned from al-Zajjāj, al-Fārisī and Ibn al-Anbārī; Abū ʿAlī also stated it explicitly in «al-Ḥujja», and al-Wāḥidī mentioned it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is the noblest of the views." Makkī mentioned the three possibilities, I mean its being a badal, an explicative apposition or an adjective. But what al-Ḥūfī argued is correct from the standpoint of grammatical craft, and in that the correct view in the ranking of definites is what he mentioned, that demonstratives are more definite than the noun with the article. Yet it may be said: the one who holds it to be an adjective does not make it more definite than the noun with alif and lām. The fifth: Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «لباسُ» to be a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, i.e.: and the garment of piety is a covering of your private parts. This is a construction there is no need for.
Attributing the sending-down to the garment is either because أنزل has the meaning of "created", as in His saying {وَأَنزْلْنَا الحديد} [al-Ḥadīd: 25] and {وَأَنزَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ الأنعام ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ} [al-Zumar: 6]; or according to what the scholars call gradation (tadrīj): that is, He sends down its causes, namely the water that is a cause of the growth of cotton and flax and of the pasture eaten by the animals with wool, hair and fur from which clothes are made. It is like the poet's saying, describing rain:
2179 - أقبل في المُسْتَنِّ من سَحابَهْ ... أسنِمة الآبال في ربابَهْ
(It came on in the rush of its cloud, [bearing] the humps of camels in its white cloud.)
He made it come bearing the humps of camels figuratively, since it was a cause of rearing them. Close to it is another's saying:
2180 - إذا نَزَلَ السَّماءُ بأرض قومٍ ... رَعَيْناه وإن كانوا غضابا
(When the sky [i.e. rain] comes down on a people's land, we graze it, even if they are angry.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made what is on the earth sent down from heaven because He decreed it there and wrote it; and from it is «وأنزل لكم من الأنعامِ ثمانيةَ»."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Also, Allah's creation and His acts are from loftiness in rank and station."
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ubayy: «ولباس التقوى خير», dropping «ذلك»; it strengthens the view of separation (faṣl), badal and explicative apposition. Al-Naḥwī read: «ولبُوسُ» with wāw and the sīn in the nominative. As for the nominative, it is according to what was said about «لباس». As for «لبوس», they did not make it clear whether it has fatḥa on the lām, so that it is like His saying, Exalted is He: {وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ لَّكُمْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 80], or ḍamma on the lām as a plural, which is problematic; the most that can be imagined for it is that it is the plural of لِبْس with kasra on the lām, meaning "what is worn".
His saying: «ذلك مِنْ آيات الله» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar; the reference by it is to all that preceded, the sending down of the garment, the adornment (ريش) and the garment of piety. It was also said: rather it refers to the nearest thing mentioned, namely the garment of piety only.

semin-durr:27-27.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: {لاَ يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ}: In form it is a prohibition addressed to Satan, but what is meant is forbidding those addressed from following him and listening to him. The meaning of that has been given at His saying {فَلاَ يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ} [al-Aʿrāf: 2]. Ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm read: «لا يُفْتِنَنَّكم» with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from أفتنه, meaning "he drove him into temptation". Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «لا يَفْتِنْكم» without the nūn of emphasis.
His saying: {كَمَآ أَخْرَجَ} is the adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: let him not tempt you with a temptation like the temptation of expelling your parents. The implied form may also be: let him not expel you by his temptation with an expulsion like his expelling your parents. His saying «يَنْزِع» is a clause in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). There are two possibilities for its owner. The first: that it is the pronoun in «أخرج» referring to Satan; the second: that it is the parents. Both views are allowed because the meaning is sound on either construction, and the grammatical craft supports that, for the clause contains a pronoun of the parents and a pronoun of Satan. The Shaykh said: "Had it been نازعاً instead of «ينزع», the first would have been required, because then, were the second allowed, it would be an adjective applied to someone other than its owner, and the pronoun would have to be made explicit; that is according to the position of the Basrans." I say: he means that a distinction is made between the noun and the verb when they are applied to something other than what they belong to in meaning: if it is a noun, the Basrans' position is as he mentioned; if it is a verb, it does not need that. The discussion of this question has been given to you before, and that Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn ibn Mālik made the two equal, and that Makkī has a problematic statement on it.
As for {يَنْزِعُ}, it was brought in the imperfect form as a narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl), as though it had occurred and been completed. النَّزْع is pulling a thing forcefully from its place; from it is {تَنزِعُ الناس كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 20], and from it is drawing (نَزْع) the bow. It is used for non-physical things; from it is removing enmity and love from the heart; and نُزِع فلانٌ كذا means he was stripped of it; and from it is {والنازعات غَرْقاً} [al-Nāziʿāt: 1], because they pull out the souls of the unbelievers violently. From it is المنازعة, which is disputing; النَّزْع عن الشيء is refraining from it; النزوع is intense longing; from it is نَزَع إلى وطنه ("he longed for his homeland") and نَزَع إلى مذهب كذا نَزْعَةً ("he inclined to such a doctrine"); أنزع القومُ: their camels longed for their home grounds; رجل أَنْزَعُ: a man whose hair has receded; النَّزْعتان are the two bare patches flanking the forelock; النَّزْعة is also the place [of baldness] on the head of the أنزع; one does not say امرأة نَزْعاء when she has that, but she is called زَعْراء; and بئر نَزُوع is a shallow well, because water is drawn from it by hand.
His saying: {إِنَّهُ يَرَاكُمْ هُوَ وَقَبِيلُهُ}: «هو» is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the attached [latent] pronoun so that conjunction to it becomes permissible; such is the wording of some. Al-Wāḥidī said: "He repeated the pronoun so that the conjunction would be good, as in His saying: {اسكن أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ} [al-Baqara: 35]." I say: there is no need for emphasis in a form like this for the conjunction to be sound, since the separator here exists [i.e. «كم»], and it suffices for the soundness of the conjunction; so it is not a parallel to {اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ}.
A discussion of {اسْكُنْ أَنْتَ وَزَوْجُكَ} has been given to you before, namely that it is not of the type of conjunction to the pronoun, because of an impediment mentioned there.
As for {وَقَبِيلُهُ}, the well-known reading is in the nominative, conjoined to the latent pronoun. It may also be conjoined to the ism of «إنَّ» according to its position, for those who allow that, especially for those who say it is allowed after the khabar by consensus. It may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with its khabar (predicate) omitted. So three views result for its nominative. Al-Yazīdī read «وقبيلَه» in the accusative, and it has two explanations. The first: that it is accusative, conjoined to the ism of إنَّ in form, if we say that the pronoun refers to Satan, which is the apparent view. The second: that it is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), i.e.: he sees you in company with his tribe. Concerning the pronoun in «إنه» there are two views; the apparent one, as stated, is that it is for Satan. The second: that it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); al-Zamakhsharī held this, but no need calls for it.
القبيل is a group of three or more from various origins; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayd. القبيلة is a group from one father; so القبيلة is not the feminine of القبيل, because of this difference.
His saying: {مِنْ حَيْثُ لاَ تَرَوْنَهُمْ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent of seeing; «حيث» is an adverb for the place of the absence of seeing; and «لا تَرَوْنهم» is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. This is the apparent i'rab of this verse.
There is a problematic statement transmitted from Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj], which I thought fit to mention lest anyone who sees it imagine it to be correct. Abū Isḥāq said: "What follows «حيث» is a ṣila (relative clause) for it and not annexed to it." Al-Fārisī said: "This is not right. What follows «حيث» cannot be a ṣila for it, because if it were its ṣila, there would have to be in it a mention [pronoun] of the relative, just as in all other ṣilas of relatives there is a mention of the relative. So the clause after «حيث» being free of any pronoun referring to «حيث» is proof that it is not a ṣila for حيث; and if it is not a ṣila, it is annexed. If it is said: we construe the referring pronoun in this as we construe the referring pronoun in relatives — so if you say «رأيتك حيث زيد قائم» ('I saw you where Zayd is standing'), the implied form is: where he stands in it; and if you say «رأيتك حيث قام زيد», the implied form is: where Zayd stood in it; then the preposition was dropped by extension, so the pronoun became attached and was then dropped, as it is dropped in your saying «زيد الذي ضربت», i.e. الذي ضربته — it is said in reply: had that been intended, using this original form would have been permissible; their abandoning this usage is proof that it is not an original form for it."
[Translator's note: The construction «حيث قائمه» is as written in the source; the sense required is "where [Zayd] is standing in it".]
I say: Abū Isḥāq did not believe that it is a relative meaning الذي — no one says that. He merely claims that it is not annexed to the clause after it, so that the clause became like a ṣila for it, i.e. like an addition; and that is an incoherent statement. So the reply to him should be from this standpoint, not from the standpoint of his believing it to be a relative. It may be that what he meant is that since the clause is part of the completion of its meaning, in the sense that it needs it as the relative needs its ṣila, this expression was applied to it. What indicates what I have said is that Makkī mentioned, among the reasons for its indeclinability: "and because what follows it is part of its completion, like the ṣila and the relative" — yet he accepts that it is annexed to what follows it.
It was read {مِنْ حَيْثُ لاَ تَرَوْنَهُ} in the singular. That admits two views. The first: that the pronoun refers to Satan alone, without his tribe, because he is their head and they are his followers, and because he is the one forbidden at the beginning of the speech. And [the second:] that it refers to him and his tribe, the pronoun being singular because it is treated like the demonstrative in His saying, Exalted is He: {عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذلك} [al-Baqara: 68]. A parallel to this reading is the saying of Ruʾba:
2181 - فيها خطوطٌ من سَوادٍ وبَلَقْ ... كأنه في الجلد توليعُ البَهَقْ
(In it are streaks of black and piebald white, as if it were, in the skin, the blotching of leprosy.)
This verse has been given before, with the anecdote about it, in al-Baqara.
His saying: {إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا} may have the meaning of "made into", i.e.: We made the devils allies. Al-Zahrāwī said: "جعل here has the meaning of 'described'." This is not known for «جعل»; it is as though it were an escape from attributing to Allah the Exalted the making of the devils allies of those who do not believe, and it seems to be a Muʿtazilī inclination. «للذين» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أولياء because it has the meaning of a verb; it may also be attached to something omitted because it is an adjective of أولياء.

semin-durr:111-111.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَرْجِهْ}: In this word, here and in al-Shuʿarāʾ, there are six readings among the well-known mutawātir ones, and no regard is to be paid to anyone who denied some of them, nor to anyone who objected to their transmitter. The way to organise them is to say: three with the hamza and three without it. As for the three with the hamza: the first is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, and of Hishām from Ibn ʿĀmir: أَرْجِئْهو, with a hamza carrying sukūn and a hāʾ joined to a wāw. The second is the reading of Abū ʿAmr: أَرْجِئْهُ, as above, except that he does not join it with a wāw. [Translator's note: the Arabic text repeats the sentence "The second is the reading of Abū ʿAmr: أَرْجِئْهُ, as above, except that he does not join it with a wāw" twice; it is translated once here.] The third is the reading of Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir: أَرْجِئْهِ, with a hamza carrying sukūn and a hāʾ with kasra, without a joining letter. As for the three without the hamza: the first is the reading of ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza: أَرْجِهْ, with kasra on the jīm and sukūn on the hāʾ, in both continuous reading and pause. The second is the reading of al-Kisāʾī: أَرْجِهي, with the hāʾ joined to a yāʾ. The third is the reading of Qālūn, with a hāʾ carrying kasra and no yāʾ.

As for the ḍamma and the kasra of the hāʾ, they are already known from what preceded. As for the hamza and its absence, they are two well-known dialects: one says أَرْجَأْته and أَرْجَيْتُه, meaning "I postponed him"; and the saying of Allah the Exalted {تُرْجِي مَن تَشَآءُ} [al-Aḥzāb: 51] has been read both with the hamza and without it. This is like their saying تَوَضَّأْتُ and تَوَضَّيْتُ. And are the two separate original roots, or is the substituted one a derivative of the hamzated one? There are two possibilities.

A group have attacked the reading of Ibn Dhakwān. al-Fārisī said: "A ḍamma on the hāʾ together with the hamza is the only permissible form, and the transmission of Ibn Dhakwān from Ibn ʿĀmir is a mistake." Ibn Mujāhid said: "This is not permissible, because the hāʾ is not given a kasra except after a kasra or a quiescent yāʾ." al-Ḥawfī said: "Among the readers are some who give a kasra together with the hamza, and it is not good." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is also read with a kasra on the hāʾ together with the hamza, and it is weak, because the hamza is a sound quiescent letter, so there is nothing before the hāʾ that requires a kasra."

I say: People have excused this reading, by way of concession, in two ways. One: the hamza is quiescent, and a quiescent letter is a barrier that is not impregnable, and there are attested examples of this mentioned in their proper place; so it is as if the hāʾ immediately followed the jīm with its kasra, and for that reason it was given a kasra. The second: the hamza is often subject to change, and here it is liable to be replaced by a quiescent yāʾ because of its quiescence after a kasra; so it is as if it immediately followed a quiescent yāʾ, and for that reason it was given a kasra.

Abū Shāma objected to these two answers on three grounds. First: the hamza is counted as a barrier by consensus in {أَنبِئْهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 33] and {نَبِّئْهُمْ} [al-Qamar: 28], and the ruling is the same for the plural and the singular pronoun as regards the kasra and the ḍamma. Second: it would then be necessary to join the hāʾ (with a long vowel), since in effect it directly follows the jīm. Third: even if the hamza were turned into a yāʾ, the preferred form would be a ḍamma on the hāʾ together with the explicit yāʾ, considering that its origin is a hamza; so what is to be thought of the one who gives the hāʾ a kasra with the explicit hamza! The full treatment of this will come in the chapter on the pausing of Ḥamza and Hishām. So a ḍamma on the hāʾ with the hamza is the (correct) form.

Abū l-Baqāʾ considered the reading of Ibn Kathīr and Hishām weak, for he said: "أَرْجِئْهُ is read with the hamza and a ḍamma on the hāʾ without lengthening, and that is the good one; and with lengthening, which is weak, because the hāʾ is faint, so the wāw after it is as though it followed the hamza directly, which is close to combining two quiescent letters; and from here their saying عليهي مال with lengthening is weak." I say: This weakening is nothing, because it is an established dialect from the Arabs, I mean lengthening the vowel of the hāʾ after any quiescent letter, and it has already been mentioned that this is a principle of Ibn Kathīr not restricted to this word, but his rule is: every pronominal hāʾ after a quiescent letter has its vowel lengthened until a long-vowel letter is generated from it, such as مِنْهو and عَنْهو and أرجِئْهو, except before a quiescent letter, where the lengthening is dropped because two quiescent letters would meet, apart from one place which al-Bazzī transmitted from him, namely {عَنْهُ تلهى} [ʿAbasa: 10] with a doubled tāʾ. Likewise al-Zajjāj considered the reading of Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim weak. After citing the poet's verse he said:

2259 - لمَّا رأى أن لا دَعَهْ ولا شِبَعْ ... مالَ إلى أَرْطاةِ حِقْفٍ فالْطَجَعْ
(When he saw that there was no rest and no satiety, he turned to an arṭā tree on a sand-dune and lay down.)

"This is a verse whose author is not known and it is worthless; and had a named poet said it, he would be told: you erred, because a poet may err, and this is a doctrine not to be relied upon." I say: It has already been mentioned that making the pronominal hāʾ quiescent is an established dialect, and its attestations have been given, so there is no need to repeat that.

As for his saying {وأخاه}: the best is that it is conjoined (nasaqan) to the hāʾ in {أَرْجِهْ}; and taking it as accusative as an object of accompaniment is weak, because conjunction is possible without any weakness in wording or meaning.

His saying: {فِي المدآئن} is attached to أَرْسِلْ, and {حاشرين} is a direct object, and the object of {حاشرين} is omitted, i.e. "gatherers of the magicians", as indicated by what follows. And المدائن is the plural of مدينة, and there are three views about it. The first, which is the sound one, is that its pattern is فَعيلة, so its mīm is original and its yāʾ is extra, derived from مَدَنَ يَمْدُنُ مُدُوناً, meaning "he stayed". Evidence for this view is the agreement of the readers on pronouncing مدائن with a hamza, like صحيفة and صحائف, and سفينة and سفائن; whereas if it were مَفْعِلة it would not be hamzated, like معيشة and معايش; and also because they pluralised it too as مُدُن, as they say سفينة and سُفُن, صحيفة and صُحُف. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What makes it certain that it is فَعيلة is that they pluralised it on فُعُل: they said مُدُن, as they said صُحُف for صحيفة."

I say: al-Zajjājī said: "مُدُن is in reality the plural of مَدِين, because مدينة is not pluralised as مُدُن but is pluralised as المدائن; and similar to this is سُفُن, as if they pluralised سفينة as سفين and then pluralised that as سُفُن." I do not know what led him to make مُدُن the plural of مدين, and مدين the plural of مدينة, given that فُعُل is regular for فعيلة not in the sense of مفعولة; unless he had perceived in مدينة that it is a فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة, since the meaning of مدينة is that people "settle" in it, i.e. stay; and this is supported by what will come later, that the original pattern of مدينة is مَدْيُوْنة according to some.

The second view: its pattern is مَفْعِلة from دانَه يَدينُه, i.e. "he governed it, he rules it", so the meaning of مدينة is "owned" and "governed", i.e. its people are governed, from دانهم مَلِكُهم when he governed them; and it ought then to be pluralised as مداين with an explicit yāʾ, like معايش in the well-known dialect of the Arabs.

The third: that its pattern is مَفْعولة, and this is the doctrine of Abū l-ʿAbbās (al-Mubarrad). He said: "It is from دانَه يَدينُه when he possessed and subdued it; and if its origin is مَدْيونة, it was subject to weakening-change as مَبِيع, the passive participle of البيع, is changed; then the disagreement proceeds over the letter dropped: is it the original yāʾ or the extra wāw? The first is the view of al-Akhfash, and the second is the view of al-Māzinī, and it is the doctrine of the majority of the grammarians." And the مدينة is well known: it is the walled place over which a king has taken control.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذَا فَعَلُواْ}: This conditional clause has no grammatical position, because it is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and this is the apparent view. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that it falls within the scope of the ṣila (relative clause), by conjunction to it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "So that the rebuke may fall upon the attribute of a people who have been made similar to the believers, since their deed resembles the deed of those they are likened to." And his saying «وَجَدْنا» may be understood as the verb of knowing, i.e., "we knew that their way is this", or it may mean "we met (laqīnā)". On the first reading «عليها» is the second object; on the second it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
And his saying {لاَ يَأْمُرُ بالفحشآء}: the first object is omitted because it is known, i.e., "He does not command anyone", or "He does not command you with a command of ... that."
And his saying {مَا لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ} is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and this is a singular in the force of a sentence, because what they do not know, of what they ascribe falsely to Allah the Exalted, is a great deal of speech, from their saying {والله أَمَرَنَا بِهَا}, such as slitting the ears of the baḥīra camels, letting the sāʾiba camels loose, their circumambulating the House naked, and other things. Likewise the object is omitted from His saying {أَمَرَ رَبِّي بالقسط}.
[Translator's note: the source text has an ellipsis (". . .") after "بأمر" in the first paragraph; I have rendered it as written.]

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَقِيمُواْ}: There are two views on it. The more evident is that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the implied command, i.e., the one into which the maṣdar (verbal noun) «بالقسط» resolves. That is because «القسط» is a maṣdar, and it resolves into a maṣdar particle and a verb. So the implied form is: "Say: My Lord has commanded that you act justly (an aqsiṭū) and that you establish ...". Just as the maṣdar resolves into «أَنْ» plus the past verb, as in "I marvelled at Zayd's standing up and going out", i.e., "at his having stood up and gone out", and into «أَنْ» plus the imperfect verb, as in her saying:
2182 - To wear a cloak while my eye is cooled ... . . . . . . . . . . . .
i.e., "than that I wear (a cloak) and my eye be cooled", so too it resolves into «أَنْ» plus an imperative verb, because it combines with all three forms, the past, the imperfect and the imperative, on condition that the verb is inflected (taṣarruf). We have already treated this question, its difficulty and its answer. This is unlike «ما», for it is not joined to the imperative, and unlike «كي», for it is joined only to the imperfect. Hence the maṣdar does not resolve into «ما» plus an imperative verb, nor into «كي» plus a past or imperfect verb. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «وأقيموا وجوهكم»: "and say: Set your faces", i.e., "direct yourselves to His worship." This statement of Abū l-Qāsim admits two interpretations. One: that by his "say" he meant an implied "say" other than the one pronounced, so «أقيموا» would be governed by an implied saying, a command; and (the other) that it is conjoined to His saying «أَمَر ربي», for that is governed by «قل». Al-Zamakhsharī made «قل» explicit alongside «أقيموا» only to confirm that it is conjoined to «أَمَر ربي». It is also possible that his saying «وأقيموا» is conjoined to an omitted command, its implied form being: "Say: Turn (to Him) and establish ...".
Al-Jurjānī, author of «al-Naẓm», said: "He conjoined the command upon the genitive, and that is permissible because His saying {قُلْ أَمَرَ رَبِّي} is a saying; for a command is nothing but speech, and speech is saying; as if He had said: 'Say: My Lord says: Act justly and establish'." He means that it is a conjunction upon the meaning.
And {مَسْجِدٍ} here may be a place or a time. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "At the time of every prostration and in the place of every prostration." By right «مسجد» should have had a fatḥa on the ʿayn, since it has a ḍamma in the imperfect; and he has many sisters of this irregularity mentioned in morphology (taṣrīf).
And his saying {مُخْلِصِينَ} is a ḥāl from the agent of «ادعُوه», and «الدّين» is a direct object of the active participle. And «له» is attached to «مخلصين»; it is also possible that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «الدين».
His saying: {كَمَا بَدَأَكُمْ}: The kāf is in the position of accusative as an adjective (naʿt) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being: "You will return a return like what He began you", and it was said the implied form is "you will come forth a coming forth like what He began you". Makkī mentioned both, and the first is more fitting to the wording of the noble verse. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "The position of the kāf in «كما» is accusative by «تعودون»; and this follows the Arabs' practice of putting the object of the verb before it, i.e., 'you will return as He began your creation'."
Al-Fārisī said: «كما بدأكم تعودون» is not on its apparent sense, since the apparent sense is "you will return like the beginning", and the meaning is not to liken them to the beginning; rather the meaning is on the repetition of the creation as it was begun. So the implied form of «كما بدأكم تعودون» is "as He began your creation", i.e., He will bring your creation to life again as a return like its beginning. And just as He did not intend the beginning in its apparent sense without omission of the muḍāf ilayhi (the genitive), so He did not intend the return without omission of the muḍāf, which is the "creation". When He omitted it, the muḍāf ilayhi stood in place of the agent, so those who do the act became addressed, just as when He omitted the muḍāf from "as He began your creation", those addressed became objects in wording. I (al-Samīn) say: he means that the original is "as your creation began, your creation returns", and the "creation" was omitted in both places; so those addressed in the first became objects after having been genitive by annexation, and in the second became agents after having been genitive by annexation too.
And «بدأ» with the hamza means "originated and invented"; it is used with this meaning in the triliteral form and in the quadriliteral form on the pattern afʿala. The triliteral is as in this verse, and both usages are combined in the saying of the Exalted: {أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ الله الخلق} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 19], which is from abdaʾa, and then He said: {كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الخلق} [al-ʿAnkabūt: 20]. This is for what is transitive by itself. As for what is transitive by means of the bāʾ, as in "I began with such-and-such", meaning I put it first and made it the first of things, one says of it "badaʾtu bihi" and "ibtadaʾtu bihi". Al-Rāghib also reported that from this one says "abdaʾtu bihi" on the pattern afʿala, which is rare. And their saying "abdaʾtu min arḍi kadhā" means "I began my departure from it". And «al-badʾ» is the chief; it is said to be so called because he is begun with in the count when chiefs are counted. They cited for it his saying:
2183 - So I came to their graves as a chief, though I was not yet ... and I called to the graves, but they did not answer.
i.e., I came to the graves of my people as a chief, when I had not been a chief, but through their death I became a chief. And this looks to the saying of another:
2184 - The abodes are empty, so I became master, though not made master ... and among the hardships is my being alone in lordship.
And «ما» is a maṣdar particle, i.e., "like your beginning".
[Translator's note: verse 2182 and the first hemistich of 2183 are partly elided or textually uncertain in the source; I have glossed only what is written. The word "ولمَّا" in 2183 is left without its complement as in the source.]

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَرِيقاً هدى وَفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الضلالة}: There are two views on the accusative of «فريقاً». The first is that it is governed by «هدى» after it, and the second «فريقاً» is accusative by an implied verb which is explained, in terms of meaning, by His saying {حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الضلالة}; the implied form being: "and He led astray a group upon whom (misguidance) became due". Al-Zamakhsharī implied it as "and He forsook a group", for a purpose of his in that. The two verbal clauses are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «بدأكم», i.e., "He began you while guiding a group and leading another astray", and «قد» is implied according to some. On this view it is also possible that the two verbal clauses are resumptive. Then the pause at «يعودون» is complete on this construal, unlike when he makes them two ḥāls, in which case the pause is at His saying «الضلالة».
The second view: that «فريقاً» is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تَعُودون», i.e., "you will return as a group guided and a group upon whom misguidance became due". On this view the two verbal clauses are in the position of accusative as an adjective (naʿt) of «فريقاً» and «فريقاً», and then an omitted pronoun referring back to the qualified noun is necessary after «هَدَى», i.e., "a group He guided (hadāhum)". Had you implied it as «هداه», in the singular, it would be permissible, taking into account the wording of «فريق»; except that the first is better, for its agreement with His saying {وَفَرِيقاً حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ}. The pause is then at His saying «الضلالة». What supports parsing it as a ḥāl is the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: «تعودون فريقَيْن: فريقاً هدى وفريقاً حقَّ عليهم الضلالة». Here «فريقَيْن» is accusative as a ḥāl, and «فريقاً» and «فريقاً» are badal (substitute) or accusative by an implied "I mean (aʿnī)" in the manner of qaṭʿ (cutting off). It is also possible that the first «فريقاً» is accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of «تعودون», and the second «فريقاً» accusative by an implied verb explained by «حقَّ عليهم الضلالة», as was verified earlier for each of them.
All of these views were mentioned by Ibn al-Anbārī, who spoke well. May Allah have mercy on him, he said: "«فريقاً» and «فريقاً» are accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «تعودون»; he means: 'you will return as your creation began, differing, some of you wretched and some of you blessed'. So «فريق», being indefinite, was connected to the pronoun in «تعودون», which is definite, and was thereby cut off from its wording, and the second was conjoined to it." He said: "It is also possible that the first is accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun, and the second is accusative by «حقَّ عليهم الضلالة», because it has the meaning 'He led them astray', as someone might say: 'ʿAbd Allāh, I honoured him, and Zayd, I treated him well', so «زيداً» is accusative by «أحسنت إليه» in the sense 'I benefited him'." And he cited:
2185 - Is it Thaʿlaba of the horsemen or Riyāḥ ... that you have put Ṭuhayya and al-Khishāb on a par with them?
He said that «ثعلبة» is accusative by «عَدَلْتَ بهم طهية», because it has the meaning "you slighted them", i.e., "you equated with them one who is below them". He also cited his saying:
2186 - Would that your guest al-Zubayr and your neighbour ... had mingled his rope with my ropes, me!
So «إياي» is accusative by his saying «لَبَّس حبله بحبالي», since its meaning is "he mingled with me and sought me out". I (al-Samīn) say: he means that it is accusative by an implied verb from the meaning of the second, not from its wording; this is the point of the comparison. Al-Farrāʾ held that «فريقاً» is accusative by «هدى» and «فريقاً» accusative by «حَقَّ», and he made it comparable to the saying of the Exalted: {يُدْخِلُ مَن يَشَآءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ والظالمين أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ عَذَاباً أَلِيماً} [al-Insān: 31].
And his saying: {إِنَّهُمُ اتخذوا} runs in the course of a causal clause, even if it is resumptive in wording. What indicates this is the reading of ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Faḍl and Sahl ibn Shuʿayb: «أنهم» with fatḥa on the hamza, which is explicit about causation, i.e., "misguidance became due upon them because of their taking the devils as allies". He did not ascribe the leading astray to His holy Self, though He is the doer of it, for the beautification of the wording and to teach His servants proper manners; on this basis: {وعلى الله قَصْدُ السبيل وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ} [al-Naḥl: 9].
[Translator's note: the source repeats the sentence "فالوقفُ على «يعودون» على هذا الإِعرابِ تامٌّ بخلاف ما إذا جَعَلهما حالَيْن" twice in the first paragraph; I translated it once. Also, the verse numbers of 2182-2186 are the book's running poetry numbers.]

semin-durr:58-58.t:
Al-balad (the land, the town) is applied to every part of the earth, whether inhabited or ruined. They recited as evidence for this the words of al-Aʿshā:
2221 - Many a land, like the back of a shield, desolate, ... for the jinn at night in its borders there is a murmuring sound.
{بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ}: it is possible that the bāʾ is causal or ḥāl (circumstantial). As for his words «إلا نَكِداً»: there are two views. The first is that it is accusative as a ḥāl, meaning "difficult, slow"; one says from it nakida yankadu nakadan (with fatḥa) and it is nakid (with kasra). The second is that it is accusative as the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), meaning: "except a scanty growth/emergence (khurūjan nakadan)". He described the emergence as scanty (nakad) just as others are described by it. This is supported by the reading of Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ «إلا نَكَداً» with fatḥa on the kāf. Al-Zajjāj said: "It is the reading of the people of Medina." Ibn Muṣarrif read «إلا نَكْداً» with sukūn; both are maṣdars. Makkī said: "It is a lightened form of nakid with kasra, like katf for katif." One says: a man nakid and ankad. Al-mankūd is the meagre gift, and they recited on this:
2222 - Give what you give with a good heart, ... there is no good in the grudging gift or in the grudging giver.
They also recited:
2223 - Do not fulfil the promise if you promise, and if ... you give, you give something paltry and miserly?
His words: {كذلك نُصَرِّفُ}: as already discussed in its parallel. Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Abū Ḥaywa and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «يُخْرَج» in the passive, with «نباتُه» in the nominative as it stands in the place of the fāʿil, who is Allah the Exalted. His words {والذي خَبُثَ} are a ṣifa (descriptive qualifier) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e. "and the land which is bad"; it was omitted only because what precedes it indicates it, just as the preposition and its genitive noun were omitted from it in his words «بإذن ربه», since the implied form is: "and the land which is bad does not bring forth, by the leave of its Lord, except scantily." An omitted muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) is necessary: either from the first, its implied form being "and the case of that which is bad does not come forth", or from the second, its implied form being "and that which is bad, its vegetation does not come forth except scantily." He varied between the two relatives, using the definite article in the first, while in the second he used alladhī, and linked it with a past verb.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His words, the Exalted: {لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا}: the answer to an omitted oath, its implied form being: "By Allah, we have indeed sent". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why do they scarcely pronounce this lām except with «قد», and rarely do they say:
2224 - I swore to her by Allah, the oath of a sinner, ... 'they would have slept' . . . . . . . . . . .
I say: that is because the oath clause is brought only to corroborate the clause sworn upon, which is its answer, so it is a likely place for the sense of expectation, which is the meaning of «قد», when the addressee hears the word 'oath'." As for grammarians other than Abū l-Qāsim, they said: "When the answer to the oath is a past, affirmative, conjugated verb: either it is close to the present time, so you bring «قد», or else you bring the lām alone." The apparent sense of this statement is that both options are permissible on two different considerations.
He said here «لقد» without a conjunction, whereas in Hūd and al-Muʾminūn it is «ولقد» with a conjunction. Al-Kirmānī answered that in Hūd the mention of the messenger had come several times earlier, and in al-Muʾminūn Nūḥ was mentioned implicitly in the words «وعلى الفلك», because he was the first to build it, [so it was fitting to bring the conjunction on what preceded], unlike in this sūra.
His words «غيره»: al-Kisāʾī read it with kasra on the rāʾ throughout the Quran, and the rest with ḍamma. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «غيرَه» in the accusative. The genitive is as naʿt (adjective), or badal (substitute), for «إله» in form. The nominative is as naʿt, or badal, for the position of «إله», because «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida) in it and its position is nominative: either as mubtadaʾ (subject) or as fāʿil (agent). Makkī ruled out, on the genitive reading, that it is a badal for «إله» in form, saying: "just as it is not permissible for «مِنْ» to enter if you removed the thing replaced, because it does not enter in the affirmative"; and this is an incoherent statement. The accusative is on the basis of exception (istithnāʾ). The first two readings are preferable, because whenever the speech is non-affirmative, following (ittibāʿ) is preferred over the accusative of exception, and the rule of «غير» is the rule of the noun occurring after «إلا». As for «من إله», if you make it a mubtadaʾ, you have two views for the khabar (predicate). The more evident is that it is «لكم»; the second is that it is omitted, i.e. "you have no god in existence or in the world other than Allah", and on this «لكم» is for specification and clarification.
The conjunctive fāʾ was brought here where it says «فقال», and likewise in al-Muʾminūn, while in the story of Hūd, Ṣāliḥ and Shuʿayb here it is without a fāʾ. The original is with the fāʾ; it was omitted only for lightness, for latitude, and being content with the semantic link, and the later ones, and those after them, were more deserving of omission. As for Hūd, before his words «إني لكم» one implies: "so he said", with the fāʾ, as is original. Here it came {مَا لَكُمْ مِّنْ إله غَيْرُهُ} and he did not conjoin this negated clause with a fāʾ or anything else, because it explains and draws attention to Allah the Exalted's exclusive right to worship and the rejection of everything besides Him, and it was in the utmost connection.

semin-durr:60-60.t:
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Ibn ʿĀmir read «المَلَوُ» with a wāw, and so it is in the Syrian codices; but this reading is not well known from him."
His words {لَنَرَاكَ}: it may be the verb of the heart (qalbiyya), so it takes two objects, the second being «في ضلال»; or it may be the verb of sight (baṣariyya), though that is not evident, in which case the preposition and its genitive noun is a ḥāl. He made error a container (ẓarf) for him, as exaggeration in their description of him with this, and they added to the exaggeration by emphasizing it, placing «إنَّ» at the head of the clause and the lām in its khabar.

semin-durr:61-61.t: His words, the Exalted: {لَيْسَ بِي ضَلاَلَةٌ}: among the finest and most eloquent of replies, because he denied that even a single error should attach to him, let alone that error should encompass him; had he said "I am not astray" it would not have conveyed this meaning. His words «ولكني»: «لكن» came here in the best possible way, because it is between two opposites, since a person is free of neither of two things: error or guidance, and messengership does not coexist with error. «من رب» is a ṣifa of «رسول», and «مِنْ» is for figurative beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أُبَلِّغُكُمْ}: it may be a resumptive clause (mustaʾnafa) brought to explain his being a messenger, and it may be a ṣifa of «رسول», but he took into account the preceding pronoun, which is the speaker's, so he said «أُبَلِّغُكُمْ»; had he taken into account the overt noun after it, he would have said "yubalighukum". Both usages are permissible with every overt noun preceded by a present pronoun of speaker or addressee, so two options are established for you: taking into account the preceding pronoun, which is more frequent, and taking into account the overt noun. So you say: "anā rajulun afʿalu kadhā" (I am a man who do such and such), taking account of anā; and if you wish, "anā rajulun yafʿalu kadhā", taking account of rajul; similarly: "anta rajulun tafʿalu wa-yafʿalu", with the second person and third. His words {بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ} [النمل: 47] came on the more frequent form. Similar is what occurs when a relative noun follows the pronoun, such as: "anā alladhī faʿaltu wa-faʿala" and "anta alladhī faʿala wa-faʿalta". From this:
2225 - We are those who pledged allegiance to Muḥammad ... to wage jihad for as long as we remain, ever.
He combined both usages. This has already been discussed here more clearly.
Abū ʿAmr read «أُبْلِغُكم» in the lightened form, and the rest in the intensified form; this disagreement runs here in both places and in al-Aḥqāf. The doubling and the hamza are both for transitivization, like anzala and nazzala. «رسالة» is put in the plural with regard to its kinds: command, prohibition, exhortation, rebuke, warning and excuse. The past tense occurred in the pattern afʿala in his words {فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ} [هود: 57], which is evidence for Abū ʿAmr's reading, and in the pattern faʿʿala in his words { فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ} [المائدة: 67], which is evidence for the reading of the majority.

semin-durr:63-63.t: His words, the Exalted: {أَن جَآءَكُمْ}: i.e. min an jāʾakum ("because it came to you"); when the particle was omitted, the well-known disagreement applied. The disagreement over this hamza preceding the wāw has already been discussed. Al-Zamakhsharī, following his principle, implied an omitted word it is conjoined to, its implied form being: "Did you deny and wonder?" «مِنْ ربكم» is a ṣifa of «ذِكْر». His words «على رجل»: it is possible that there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "upon the tongue of a man". It was also said that «على» means "with" (maʿa), i.e. "with a man", so there is no omission. It was also said: there is no need for omission or for implying a particle (tadmīn), because the meaning is: "a reminder was sent down to you upon a man", and this is preferable, since implication (tadmīn) in verbs is better than in particles, because of the strength of the former and the weakness of the latter.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فِي الفلك}: it may be attached to «أنجيناه», i.e. "we saved him in the ship". In that case «في» may be causal, i.e. "because of the ship", like "A woman entered the Fire because of a cat" (fī hirra). It may also be attached to what the circumstantial phrase occurring as a ṣila is attached to, i.e. "those who were settled in the ship with him". «عَمِين» is the plural of ʿamin, and the discussion of this root has already preceded. It was said here: ʿamin when he is blind of insight, not knowing his affairs, and aʿmā meaning blind of sight. Zuhayr said:
2226 - I know the knowledge of today and yesterday before it, ... but of the knowledge of what lies in tomorrow I am blind.
This is the statement of al-Layth. It was also said: ʿamin and aʿmā have the same meaning, like khaḍir and akhḍar. Some said: «عَمٍ» indicates the permanence and settledness of the attribute, like fariḥa and ḍayyiq; had occurrence (ḥudūth) been intended, one would have said ʿāmin, as one says fāriḥ and ḍāʾiq. «قوماً عامين» has also been read, as related by al-Zamakhsharī.

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أَخَاهُمْ هُوداً}: «أخاهم» is accusative by the first «أَرْسَلْنَا», as though it were said: "We sent Nūḥ, and We sent to ʿĀd their brother"; likewise what comes later, His words {وإلى ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ} [الأعراف: 73], {وإلى مَدْيَنَ أَخَاهُمْ شُعَيْباً} [الأعراف: 85], {وَلُوطاً} [الأعراف: 80]; and what follows «أخاهم» is a badal or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Makkī allowed the accusative to be by an implied "udhkur" (mention), but it is worthless, since the meaning is as I stated, with no need for it.
«عاد» is a name for the clan (ḥayy), and therefore he made it fully declinable; some made it a name for the tribe, and therefore treated it as diptote. He said:
2227 - Had he witnessed ʿĀd in the time of ʿĀd, ... he would have plundered it, blessed in battle.
ʿĀd was originally the name of the great forefather, ʿĀd ibn ʿAwṣ ibn Aram ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ, and the tribe or clan was named after him. Likewise similar names such as «ثمود»: if you make it the name of a masculine you make it fully declinable, and if you make it the name of a feminine you treat it as diptote. Sībawayh devoted a chapter to it. As for Hūd, it became well known on the tongues of the grammarians that it is Arabic, but there is room for doubt, since the apparent sense of Sībawayh's words, when he counted it with Nūḥ and Lūṭ, is that it is non-Arabic (aʿjamī); and because Abū l-Barakāt the genealogist, the noble, related that the people of Yemen claim that Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān ibn Hūd was the first to speak Arabic and the Arabs were called ʿarab after him; on this basis Hūd would be non-Arabic, and it is fully declinable only for the reason mentioned about its two fellows Nūḥ and Lūṭ. Hūd's name was ʿĀbir ibn Shāliḥ ibn Arfakhshad ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ; so the meaning of «أخاهم» is that he was from among them. For whoever says that he was of ʿĀd by lineage, the brotherhood is evident.
Here «قال» is without a fāʾ, and it was already stated that it is intended. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why is the conjunction omitted from «قال يا قوم» and he did not say 'fa-qāla' as in the story of Nūḥ? I say: it is on the assumption of a questioner's question, who said: 'So what did Hūd say to them?' and it was said to him: «قال يا قوم»." End of quotation. On this basis this fāʾ is not to be implied at all.

semin-durr:66-66.t: It was said here: {قَالَ الملأ الذين كَفَرُواْ}, so he described the chiefs (al-malaʾ) as disbelieving, whereas they were not so described in the story of Nūḥ. It was said: because this is a distinguishing attribute, since some of them believed, such as Marthad ibn Saʿd, unlike the people of Nūḥ, none of whom believed. Al-Zamakhsharī and others said this. There is room for doubt in it, because of His words, the Exalted {لَن يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إِلاَّ مَن قَدْ آمَنَ} [هود: 36] and {وَمَآ آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ} [هود: 40]. It is possible that when Nūḥ addressed a people, none of them had yet believed, and then they believed; unlike the story of Hūd, for at the time of address there was a believer among them. It is also possible that it is an attribute of mere censure, with no intention of distinguishing by it.

semin-durr:152-152.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَكَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي المفترين}: that is, "and in the same way as that — the attainment of disobedience and humiliation — We recompense the fabricators."

semin-durr:153-153.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين عَمِلُواْ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is His saying "إن ربك" to the end. The returning pronoun is omitted, and the implied form is: "Forgiving to them, Merciful to them," like His saying: {وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الأمور} [al-Shūrā: 43], that is, "of it."
His saying: {مِن بَعْدِهَا}: it is permissible for the pronoun to refer back to «السيئات», and that is the obvious reading; and it is permissible that it refer back to repentance, which is indicated by His saying «ثم تابوا», that is, "after the repentance." The Shaykh said [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān]: "And this is preferable, because the first requires the omission of a muḍāf (head of a genitive construct) together with what is conjoined to it, since the implied form would be: after the doing of evil deeds and the repentance from them."
His saying: {وآمنوا}: it is permissible that the wāw be for conjunction, so it is asked: repentance comes after belief, so how did it come before it? It is answered: the wāw does not impose order. And it is permissible that the wāw be for ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "they repented while having believed."

semin-durr:154-154.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَماَّ سَكَتَ}: al-sukūt and al-sukāt mean the cutting off of speech, and here it is a wonderful metaphor. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is a figurative expression, as though anger had been urging him on in what he did and saying to him: 'Say such-and-such to your people, and throw down the tablets, and drag your brother by the head toward you,' and then he left off speaking this and left off the urging to it. Every person of sound nature and correct taste finds this expression elegant and eloquent only for this reason, and because it belongs to the branches of rhetoric. Otherwise, what of the reading of Muʿāwiya ibn Qurra «ولمَّا سكن» with a nūn — does one not find in it any of that stir, and a measure of that awe?"
It was also said: he likened the abating of anger to the breaking off of a speaker's speech. Yūnus said: "The valley flowed, then fell silent (sakata)" — and this too is a metaphor. Al-Zajjāj said: "The maṣdar (verbal noun) of sakata al-ghaḍabu is al-sakta, and the maṣdar of sakata al-rajulu is al-sukūt." This implies that «سكت الغضب» is a verb in its own right. It was also said: this is a case of inversion (qalb) and the original is: "and when Moses fell silent from the anger," like "I put the cap into my head" [Translator's note: i.e., "I put my head into the cap"]. But this should not be allowed, for there is no need for it, in addition to the disagreement about inversion which I have mentioned to you more than once.
His saying: {وَفِي نُسْخَتِهَا هُدًى}: this clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الألواح» or from the pronoun of Moses, and the first is better.
His saying: {لِّلَّذِينَ}: attached to an omitted element, because it is an adjective of «رحمة», that is: "a mercy existing for those who…". It is also permissible that the lām be the lām of mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), as if it were said: "guidance and mercy for the sake of these"; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ, «يرهبون» is its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
His saying: {لِرَبِّهِمْ يَرْهَبُونَ}: there are four views concerning this lām. The first: that the lām is a reinforcer of the verb, because when its object is put first the verb is weakened and is strengthened by the lām, like His saying: {إِن كُنتُمْ لِلرُّؤْيَا تَعْبُرُونَ}. It has already been mentioned that the lām serves as a reinforcer where the governor is placed later or is derivative, as in {فَعَّالٌ لِّمَا يُرِيدُ} [Hūd: 107]; and it is not added in anything other than these two cases except by necessity, according to some, as in his saying:
2305 - ولمَّا أن تواقَفْنا قليلاً ... أَنَخْنا للكلاكل فارْتَمَيْنا
(When we had stood facing one another for a little while, we made our camels kneel, chests down, and we hurled ourselves) — or, according to others, in rare cases, as in His saying, the Exalted: {رَدِفَ لَكُم} [al-Naml: 72]. The second: that the lām is the lām of cause, and on this view the object of «يرهبون» is omitted, its implied form being: "they fear His punishment for His sake"; this is the position of al-Akhfash. / The third: that it is attached to an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being: "those whose fear is toward their Lord"; this is the saying of al-Mubarrad, and it does not run according to the principles of the Basrans, because it requires the omission of the maṣdar while its complement remains, which is prohibited except in poetry; moreover it is an implied form that takes the speech out of its eloquent manner. The fourth: that it is attached to an implied verb as well, its implied form being: "they are humble before their Lord." Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is preferable to what precedes it.

semin-durr:113-113.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {قالوا إِنَّ لَنَا}: There are two views about this sentence. The more evident is that it has no grammatical position, because it is a resumption answering an implied question, and for that reason it is not conjoined with فـ to what precedes. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was it not said وجاء السحرة فرعون فقالوا? I say: it rests on the supposition of someone asking, 'What did they say when they came to him?', and so it is answered by his saying: قالوا أإن لنا لأجراً." al-Wāḥidī had preceded him to this, except that he said: "He did not say فقالوا because the meaning is 'when they came, they said', so adding the fāʾ is not sound on this view." The second view: that it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of {جاؤوا}; so said al-Ḥawfī.

The two Ḥaramī readers (Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr) and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «إنَّ» with a single hamza, and the rest read with two hamzas, as an interrogative. They follow their own principles regarding verification and facilitation of the hamza, and the insertion of an alif between the two or not. The reading of the two Ḥaramīs is declarative, but al-Fārisī allowed that it be with the intention of a question, which the reading of the others indicates; and they made that like the saying of Allah the Exalted {وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 22] and the poet's saying:

2260 - أفرحُ أَنْ أُرْزَأَ الكرام وأنْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Shall I rejoice that the noble are bereaved, and that … [the rest of the verse is elided in the source])

and another's saying:

2261 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . وذو الشيب يلعبُ
(… [first half elided in the source] … and the grey-haired one plays?)

The full treatment of this has already been given, and that it is the doctrine of Abū l-Ḥasan (al-Akhfash). He made «أجراً» indefinite to express magnitude. al-Zamakhsharī said: "like their saying: إنَّ له لإِبلاً وإن له لغنماً (he has indeed camels, he has indeed sheep)."

His saying: {إِن كُنَّا} is a condition whose apodosis is omitted, being indicated, according to the majority; or else it is what preceded, according to those who allow the apodosis to come before the condition. As for «نحن», it may be an emphasis (tawkīd) for the nominative pronoun, or it may be a faṣl (separating pronoun), in which case it has no position according to the Basrans; its position is nominative according to al-Kisāʾī and accusative according to al-Farrāʾ.

semin-durr:114-114.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِنَّكُمْ لَمِنَ المقربين}: This sentence is conjoined (nasaq) to the omitted sentence for which «نعم» stands in the reply, for the implied form is: He said: "Yes, you will have a reward, and you will be among those brought near."

semin-durr:115-115.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِمَّآ أَن تُلْقِيَ}: «إمَّا» here is for choice, and it is figuratively called a conjunction. As to the position of «أَنْ تلقي وإما أَنْ نكون» there are three views. The first is accusative, by an implied verb, i.e. "do either your casting or our casting"; the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) implied it thus. There is something to consider in this, because he would not be the one to do their casting, so one ought to imply a verb suited to that, namely "choose", i.e. "choose either your casting or our casting". Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ implied it differently, saying: "either you do the casting". Makkī said: "like his saying:

2262 - قالوا الركوبَ فقلنا تلك عادتنا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(They said: 'Riding!' and we said: 'That is our habit' … [rest elided in the source])

except that he made the accusative the doctrine of the Kufans." The second: nominative, as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, whose implied form is: "your affair is either your casting or our casting". The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being: "either your casting is what is begun with, or our casting is what is begun with". The maṣdar particle «أَنْ» was brought before the verb here, unlike His saying, the Exalted: {وَآخَرُونَ مُرْجَوْنَ لأَمْرِ الله إِمَّا يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ} [al-Tawba: 106], because «أَنْ» and what follows it here is either an object or a mubtadaʾ, and an object or a mubtadaʾ cannot be a bare verb; rather a maṣdar particle must be attached to it to put it in the interpretation of a noun. As for the verse of al-Tawba, the verb after «إمَّا» is either a second khabar of آخرون or an adjective of it, and a khabar and an adjective can be a verbal sentence without a maṣdar particle.

The object of the casting is omitted because it is known, the implied form being: "either you cast your ropes and your staffs", because they believed that he would do as they did, "or we cast our ropes and our staffs".

semin-durr:116-116.t: His saying, the Exalted: {واسترهبوهم}: It is possible that اسْتَفْعَلَ here has the sense of أَفْعَلَ, i.e. "they terrified them", which is close to their saying قرَّ and استقرَّ, عَظَّم and استعظم; this is the view of al-Mubarrad. It is also possible that the sīn is on its usual meaning, i.e. "they sought to make people fear them"; this is the view of al-Zajjāj.

semin-durr:117-117.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنْ أَلْقِ}: It may be the explicative «أن» (explaining the meaning of the inspiration), or it may be a maṣdar particle, in which case it and what follows it are the object of the inspiration.

His saying: {تَلْقَفُ}: The majority read «تَلَقَّفُ» with tashdīd, from تلقَّفَ يتلقَّفُ, the original being «تَتَلَقَّفُ» with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped, either the first or the second; this was already discussed in cases such as {تَذَكَّرُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 80]. al-Bazzī follows his own principle of assimilating it into what follows, so he reads {فإذا هي تَّلقَّفُ} with a doubled tāʾ as well, and its verification was given at His saying: {وَلاَ تَيَمَّمُواْ الخبيث} [al-Baqara: 267]. Ḥafṣ read «تَلْقَف» with a light qāf, from لَقِفَ, like عَلِم يعلم and رَكِب يركب. One says لَقِفْتُ الشيء أَلْقَفُه لَقْفاً ولَقَفاناً, and تَلَقَّفْتُه أَتَلَقَّفُه تَلَقُّفاً when you seize it quickly and eat or swallow it. In the exegesis: that it swallowed everything they had made. They cited, for لَقِف يلقَف like عَلِم يَعْلَم, the poet's saying:

2263 - أنت عصا موسى التي لم تَزَلْ ... تَلْقَفُ ما يَصْنَعُه السَّاحر
(You are the staff of Moses, which has never ceased to swallow what the magician makes.)

One also says: رجلٌ ثَقْفٌ لَقْفٌ and ثقيف لقيف, meaning clearly skilled and quick-witted. One says لَقِفَ and لَقِمَ with one meaning; so said Abū ʿUbayd. And one says لَقِف and لَقِم and لَهِم with one meaning.

The fāʾ in «فإذا هي» may be the conjunction, and a sentence must be omitted before it so that what follows the fāʾ is consequent upon it, the implied form being: "so he cast it, and lo, it...". And whoever allows the fāʾ to be redundant in a case like خرجت فإذا الأسدُ حاضر ("I went out, and lo, the lion was present") allows its redundancy here. On that view this sentence was revealed to Moses like the one before it; whereas on the first view, I mean the fāʾ being a conjunction, the sentence is not something revealed to him.

As for «ما يأفِكون»: «ما» may mean «الذي» (that which), with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "that which they falsify"; or «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, the maṣdar then standing in the place of the direct object, and this is unnecessary.

semin-durr:118-118.t: Likewise His saying, the Exalted: {مَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونَ}: it may mean «الذي», or be a maṣdar particle, i.e. "and that which they used to do came to nothing", or "their deed"; and this maṣdar may be on its usual sense or may stand in the place of the direct object, unlike «ما يَأفِكون», which must stand in the place of the direct object for the meaning to be sound, since swallowing requires a concrete thing over which it can take effect. al-Farrāʾ said about these verses: "How was it sound for Moses to command them with his saying {أَلْقُواْ مَآ أَنتُمْ مُّلْقُونَ} [Yūnus: 80], when their casting was magic and disbelief? And he answered that the meaning is: cast, if you are in the right; and cast what is sound and permissible." End of quotation. The apparent position is that he commanded them thus only to show their incapacity, to cut short their disputation and arrogance, and so that they could not say: "had we been left to do it, we would have done it"; and because a command does not entail intent.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {قُلْ مَنْ حَرَّمَ}: an interrogative whose meaning is rebuke and denial (inkār). When it is for denial it has no answer, since no information is sought by it; for that reason Makkī was charged with error in claiming that His saying «قل هي للذين آمنوا» up to the end is its answer.
And His saying {مِنَ الرزق} is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الطيبات». His saying «خالصة»: Nāfiʿ read it in the nominative, and the rest in the accusative. The nominative has two aspects. One: that it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) which is «هي», and «للذين آمنوا» is attached to «خالصة», as is «يوم القيامة». Makkī said: "And His saying «للذين» is a clarification." I (al-Samīn) say: on this it is attached to an omitted element, like their saying "saqyan laka" (may you be given drink) and "jadʿan lahu" (may he be mutilated). And «في الحياة الدنيا» is attached to «آمنوا», and the meaning is: "Say: the good things are exclusively for the believers in this world, on the Day of Resurrection", i.e., they become exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection for those who believed in this world, even though in this world they are shared between them and the disbelievers; and this is a fine meaning. It was also said that what is meant by their being exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection is that they will not be punished for them; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr inclined to this interpretation.
Second: that it is a khabar after a khabar, the first khabar being His saying «للذين آمنوا»; «في الحياة الدنيا» on this is attached to what the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to, namely the implied "being established (istiqrār)", and «يوم القيامة» is governed by «خالصة» as in the preceding aspect. The implied form is: "Say: the good things are established for, or exist for, those who believed in the life of this world, and they are exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection, even though in this world the disbelievers share them." When the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] mentioned this aspect, he attached «في الحياة» only to the "establishment"; had he attached it to «آمنوا» as in the preceding aspect, it would have been good. That «خالصة» is a second khabar is the view of al-Zajjāj, and al-Fārisī approved of it, then said: "And it is permissible in my view", and then mentioned the first aspect as I have set it out, but in more concise wording.
The accusative is from one aspect, namely the ḥāl; and «للذين آمنوا» is the khabar of «هي», so it is attached to the implied "establishment"; it will come that, in some of the implied forms, some hold that it is attached to a specific "establishment".
And {فِي الحياة الدنيا}, as preceded, is attached either to «آمنوا» or to the "establishment" to which «للذين» is attached. And «يوم القيامة» is likewise attached to «خالصة». The implied form is: "Say: the good things exist or are established for the believers in life, while their exclusivity to them is foreordained for the Day of Resurrection." Al-Farrāʾ called its accusative qaṭʿ (cutting off), saying: "«خالصةً» is accusative by qaṭʿ", and he made the khabar of «هي» in the lām in His saying «للذين». I say: by qaṭʿ he means ḥāl.
Abū ʿAlī allowed {فِي الحياة الدنيا} to be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, the governor in it being what governs in «للذين آمنوا».
Al-Fārisī allowed, and Makkī followed him, that «في الحياة» be attached to «حرَّم», the implied form being: "Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah in the life of this world?" He also allowed it to be attached to «الطيبات», and al-Fārisī alone allowed it to be attached to «الرزق». Makkī prevented that, saying: "Because you have separated between them by His saying {قُلْ هِي لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ}", meaning that «الرزق» is a maṣdar, so what is attached to it belongs to its completion just as it belongs to the completion of the relative noun, and you have separated it from what it governs by an alien sentence. An answer to this will come, to an objection that was raised against al-Akhfash.
Al-Akhfash allowed «في الحياة» to be attached to «أخرج», i.e., "He brought them forth in the life of this world".
