People rejected this from him, since it entails separating the parts of the ṣila (relative clause) by an alien element, namely His saying {وَالْطَّيِّبَاتِ مِنَ الرزق} and His saying {قُلْ هِي لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ}. That is because nothing is conjoined to the relative noun except after its ṣila is complete, and here it has been conjoined to what the relative noun qualifies before the completion of its ṣila; for «التي أَخْرَجَ» is an adjective of «زينة», and «الطيبات» is conjoined to «زينة». And His saying «قل هي للذين» is another sentence, which on this construal has separated by two things.
Al-Fārisī said, as if answering al-Akhfash: "That is permissible even if the ṣila and the relative noun are separated by His saying {هِي لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ}, because that is speech which strengthens the ṣila and is not by definition alien to it, as in His saying: {والذين كَسَبُواْ السيئات جَزَآءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ} [Yūnus: 27]; His saying {وَتَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ} is conjoined to «كَسَبُوا» and enters into the ṣila." I say: this, even if it helps in what he mentioned, does not help against the first objection, namely the conjunction to what the relative noun qualifies before the completion of its ṣila, since that is alien to it. Moreover, we do not concede that this verse is a counterpart of the verse of Yūnus, for the apparent sense in the verse of Yūnus is that there is no separation between the parts of the ṣila. [The objector says:] His saying {جَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا} is parenthetical and «ترهقهم» is conjoined to «كَسَبوا». We say: that is not conceded; rather {جَزَاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ بِمِثْلِهَا} is the khabar of the relative noun, and it is objected that there is no connecting link between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar; this is answered by saying that it is omitted, and it is among the best of omissions, because it is genitive by the partitive «مِنْ», and the grammarians have stated explicitly that what is of this kind is often omitted and is good. The implied form is: "And those who earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed from them is the like of it". So «جزاءُ سيئةٍ» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» is its adjective, «بمثلها» is its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of the relative noun. This is parallel to their saying "al-samn manawāni bi-dirham" (clarified butter, two manns for a dirham), i.e., two manns of it. More explanation of this verse will come.
Makkī prevented {فِي الحياة الدنيا} from being attached to «زينة», saying: "Because it has been qualified by an adjective, and the maṣdar and the active participle, whenever they are qualified by an adjective, do not govern, because of their distance from resemblance to the verb." He said: "And because it would separate between the ṣila and the relative noun, for the adjective of the relative noun is not part of its ṣila."
I say: because «زينة» is a maṣdar, it is in the force of a relative particle and its ṣila, and it is established that the relative noun is not followed by anything except after its ṣila is complete. So there result, in the attachment of «للذين آمنوا», three aspects: either it is attached to «خالصة», or to an omitted element as the khabar, or to an omitted element as clarification (bayān). And in the attachment of {فِي الحياة الدنيا} there are seven aspects. First: that it is attached to «آمنوا». Second: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl. Third: that it is attached to what «للذين آمنوا» is attached to. Fourth: that it is attached to «حرَّم». Fifth: that it is attached to «أخرج». Sixth: that it is attached to His saying «الطيبات». Seventh: that it is attached to «الرزق». And «يوم القيامة» has one attachment only, namely «خالصة». The meaning is: though the two groups share in them in this world, they are exclusive to the believers alone in the other.
If it is asked: if the matter is as you claimed, in the sense of their sharing in this world, how does His saying {قُلْ هِي لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ} come, when this apparently signals the absence of sharing? I say: they have answered that in several ways. First: that there is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: "Say: they are for those who believed, and for others, in the life of this world, exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection." Abū l-Qāsim al-Kirmānī said this; it is as if His saying afterwards {خَالِصَةً يَوْمَ القيامة} pointed to the omitted element, for if they were exclusively theirs in both abodes, He would not have singled out one of them. The second: that «للذين آمنوا» is not attached to an unrestricted being but to a restricted being, which the meaning indicates, the implied form being: "Say: they are not exclusively for those who believed, because the polytheists are their partners in them; they are exclusively theirs on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and what points to this restricted being is its counterpart, His saying {خَالِصَةً يَوْمَ القيامة}. The third: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, and al-Tabrīzī preceded him in it. He said: "If you say: why was it not said '[they are] for those who believed and for others'? I say: to draw attention that they were created for those who believed in the way of primacy, and that the disbelievers are subordinate to them, as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلاً} [al-Baqara: 126]." And al-Tabrīzī said: "He did not mention the sharing between them and those who associated others with Allah in this world, to draw attention that He created them for those who believed in the way of primacy, and the disbelievers are subordinate to them; and for that reason He addressed the believers by His saying {هُوَ الذي خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض جَمِيعاً} [al-Baqara: 29]." And this third is in reality not a third answer; it merely explains the beauty of omitting the conjoined element and not mentioning it together with what it is conjoined to.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ}: This has been treated at the end of the sūra before this one. And His saying «والإِثم»: the apparent sense is that it means sin. It was also said that here it means wine; al-Faḍl said this and cited:
2187 - The Messenger of Allah forbade us to approach adultery ... and to drink al-ithm, which brings a burden of sin.
And al-Aṣmaʿī cited:
2188 - I went off grieving, bewildered in mind after them ... as if I had drunk al-ithm or madness had touched me.
He said: wine is sometimes called ithm, and he cited:
2189 - I drank al-ithm until my mind went astray ... thus al-ithm takes away the minds.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī that they said: "Al-ithm: wine." Al-Ḥasan said: "The confirmation of that is His saying: {قُلْ فِيهِمَآ إِثْمٌ كَبِيرٌ} [al-Baqara: 219]." But what the discerning scholars said is that ithm is not among the names of wine. Ibn al-Anbārī said: "Ithm cannot be a name for wine, because the Arabs did not call wine ithm, in the Jāhiliyya or in Islam; and the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan does not contradict that, because wine is a cause of sin, indeed the greater part of it, for it kindles discord. And how could it be so, when wine at the time this sūra was revealed was lawful, since this sūra is Meccan and the prohibition of wine came only in Medina after Uḥud; a group of the Companions drank it on the day of Uḥud and died as martyrs with it in their bellies. As for what al-Aṣmaʿī cited, 'I drank al-ithm', they have stated explicitly that it is fabricated; as for the other, Allah knows best."
And {بِغَيْرِ الحق} is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is a confirming one (muʾakkida), because oppression (baghy) is only ever without right. And «أَنْ تُشْرِكوا» is accusative in position, conjoined to the object of «حَرَّمَ», i.e., "and He forbade you to associate partners". The object of associating is {مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَاناً}, and its explanation has preceded in al-Anʿām. And {أَن تقولوا} is likewise conjoined to what precedes, i.e., "and He forbade your saying about Him without knowledge". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "{مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَاناً}: mockery of them, because it is not possible that He would send down a proof that something else be associated with Him."

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ}: a fronted khabar (predicate). There is no need to omit a muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct), as some claimed that the implied form is "and for every individual of a nation there is a term (ajal), i.e., a lifespan", as if he imagined that each individual has an independent lifespan and that this is what the noble verse intends; yet what the verse intends is more general than that. And His saying {فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ}: some said: "In every place in the Qur'an with a construction like this, the fāʾ is attached to «إذا», except in Yūnus; as for Yūnus, its ruling will come; and as for the other places, he said: because it conjoins one sentence to another with connection and immediate sequence between them, so the place was the place of the fāʾ." Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn read «آجالهم» as a plural.
His saying: {لاَ يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ}: the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا». When the imperfect negated by «لا» occurs as the apodosis of «إذا» in appearance, it may either be met with the fāʾ or not be met with it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "One should hold that between the fāʾ and the verb after it there is a noun as a mubtadaʾ, so the sentence becomes nominal, and whenever it is so, it must be met with the fāʾ or with the «إذا» of surprise." And «ساعة» is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and it is a proverbial term for the shortness of time.
His saying: {وَلاَ يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ}: this is resumptive, its meaning being the report that they do not precede their term appointed for them, but must complete it, just as they do not fall behind it by the least time. Al-Ḥūfī and others said: "It is conjoined to «لا يستأخرون»", and this is not permissible, because the future matters, not past ones, are what follow «إذا» and what comes after it, and "precedence" relative to the coming of the term is prior to it, so how can it follow from it? This would become a case of reporting the self-evident, whose meaning no one is ignorant of, thus equivalent to your saying "If you stand in the future, your standing in the past will not have come earlier", and it is known that your standing in the future has not preceded this standing of yours.
Al-Wāḥidī said: "If it is said: what is the meaning of this, given the impossibility of advancing the term at the time of its arrival? And how can advancing be good with this term? It is said: this is on the sense of nearness, because the Arabs say 'the thing came' when its time drew near, and with the nearness of the term, advancing can be imagined, though it cannot be imagined with its expiry; and the meaning is: they do not fall behind their terms when they have expired, nor do they advance upon them when they have drawn near to expiry." I say: this is a construction by him on the basis that it is conjoined to «لا يستأخرون», and it is the apparent sense of the exegetes' statements.

semin-durr:188-188.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِنَفْسِي}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it is attached to أملك. The second is that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نفعاً», because originally it is an adjective of it, had it come later. It is also possible that «لنفسي» is governed by «نفعاً», the lām being redundant (zāʾida) in the direct object to strengthen the governor, since the latter is derivative; the implied sense then being: "I do not have the power to benefit myself, nor to harm it." That is a fine possibility.

His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ الله}: there are two possibilities in this exception. The more apparent is that it is connected (muttaṣil), i.e. "except what Allah wills to enable me to have of it, for I then possess it." The second, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya held, preceded in it by Makkī, is that it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ); but nothing calls for it to be disconnected.

His saying: {وَمَا مَسَّنِيَ السواء} is conjoined to the apodosis of «لو». It came here in the finest usage, in that he affirmed the lām in the apodosis of the affirmative «لو» (although otherwise is permissible, as has preceded) and omitted the lām from the negated one, because it is not allowed there. The Shaykh said: "The negative «ما» was not accompanied, i.e. by the lām, although the eloquent usage is that it not accompany it, as in {وَلَوْ سَمِعُواْ مَا استجابوا لَكُمْ} [Fāṭir: 14]." There is room for objection in this, because they have stated explicitly that the lām may not enter its negated apodosis.

His saying: {لِّقَوْمٍ}: this belongs to the chapter of tanāzuʿ (competition between two governors). According to the Basrans its attachment to «بشير» is preferred, because it is the second; according to the Kufans, to the first, because it comes first. It is also possible that what is attached to «النذارة» is omitted, i.e. "a warner to the disbelievers", indicated by the mention of its counterpart; this is close to the omission of the conjoined element (maʿṭūf), as in {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81].

semin-durr:35-35.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ}: its counterpart has preceded in al-Baqara. And «منكم» is an adjective of «رسل», and likewise «يَقُصُّون»; the preposition and its genitive noun were put before the clause because it is closer to the singular than the clause is. And His saying «فَمَنْ»: «مَنْ» may be conditional or relative. If the first, it and its apodosis are the apodosis of the first condition, and it is independent in the apodosis, without the clause after its apodosis, which is «والذين كَذَّبوا»; if the second, it and its apodosis and the clause referred to are both the apodosis of the condition, as if He divided the apodosis of His saying «إمَّا يأتينَّكم» into the God-fearing and the one who denies, and the recompense of each. The verification of this has preceded in al-Baqara.
He omitted the two objects of «اتَّقى وأصلحَ» for brevity because they are known, i.e., "he feared his Lord and set right his deed", or for restriction (iqtiṣār), i.e., "whoever is of the people of piety and righteousness", without regard to an object, as in His saying: {وَأَنَّهُ هُوَ أغنى وأقنى} [al-Najm: 48]. But a link must be implied between this clause and the conditional clause, the implied form being: "whoever among you fears (Allah), and those among you who deny".
Ubayy and al-Aʿraj read «تأتينَّكم» with a tāʾ of two dots from above, with regard to the meaning of the group of messengers; so His saying, the Exalted, «يَقُصُّون» with a yāʾ from below is by construal according to the meaning; for had it been construed according to the wording, he would have said «تَقُصُّ», feminine as well.

semin-durr:189-189.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {حَمْلاً}: the well-known rule is that ḥaml with fatḥa is what is in a belly or on the top of a tree, and ḥiml with kasra is what is on a back or on the top of something other than a tree. Abū Saʿīd reported, for the pregnancy of a woman, both ḥiml and ḥaml. Yaʿqūb reported the kasra for the fruit-load of a palm. The ḥaml in the verse may be intended as the maṣdar (verbal noun), and then it is accusative as a maṣdar is; or it may be intended as the foetus itself, which is the apparent sense, and then it is accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is, as in your saying "ḥamaltu Zaydan" (I carried Zayd).

His saying: {فَمَرَّتْ}: the majority read it with shaddah on the rāʾ, and its meaning is "she carried on with it", i.e. she stood up and sat down. It was also said that it is by inversion, i.e. "it passed on with her", that is, it continued and persisted.

Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū l-ʿĀliya, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar and Ayyūb read «فَمَرَتْ» with a light rāʾ, and there are two derivations of it. The first is that its origin is with shaddah, but they disliked the doubling in a repeated letter and dropped it; this is like the reading «وقَرْن» with fatḥa on the qāf if we take it from qarār. The second is that it is from al-miryah, which is doubt, i.e. "she doubted because of it: is it a pregnancy or an illness?"

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and al-Jaḥdarī read «فمارَتْ» with an alif and a light rāʾ. Here too there are two possibilities. The first is that it is from māra yamūru, i.e. "came and went"; one says "the wind mārat", i.e. came and went and moved about in every direction. Its pattern is then faʿalat and the origin is mawarat, then the wāw was turned into alif, so it is like ṭāfat taṭūfu. The second is that it is also from al-miryah, as al-Zamakhsharī said; on this its pattern is fāʿalat and the origin is mārayat, like ḍārabat; the weak letter was vowelled with a fatḥa before it, so it was turned into alif, then it was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it is like bārat and rāmat.

Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, also Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «فاسْتَمَرَّتْ به», which is clear. Ubayy read «فاستمارَتْ», in which are the two possibilities mentioned for «فمارَتْ», i.e. it may be from al-miryah, the origin being «اسْتَمْرَيَتْ», or from al-mawr, the origin being istamwarat.

His saying: {أَثْقَلَتْ}, i.e. she became possessed of heaviness, like their saying "albana l-rajulu" and "atmara", i.e. he became possessed of milk and dates. It was also said: she entered into heaviness, like their saying "aṣbaḥa" and "amsā", i.e. entered the morning and the evening. «أُثْقِلَتْ» was also read, in the passive.

His saying: {دَّعَوَا الله}: the object of the supplication is omitted, as the oath clause indicates it, i.e. "they supplicated Him that He give them a righteous child."

And His saying: {لَئِنْ آتَيْتَنَا}: concerning this oath and its answer there are two possibilities. The more apparent is that it explains the clause of supplication, as if it were said: "What was their supplication?" Their supplication was thus and thus; for that reason I said that this clause indicates the object of the supplication. The second is that it is governed by an implied saying, its implied form being: "so they said: «لئن آتيتنا»." And «لنكونَنَّ» is the answer to the oath, while the apodosis of the condition is omitted, as established. As for «صالحاً» there are two views. The more apparent is that it is a second direct object, i.e. "a righteous child". The second, which Makkī held, is that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a righteous giving". There is no need of this, since it is necessary to supply "the dead ones" for them [Translator's note: the source text reads «الموتى» here, apparently a misprint or obscure expression; translated as written].

semin-durr:190-190.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {جَعَلاَ لَهُ}: it was said that there is an omitted muḍāf (first term of a genitive construct) here, i.e. "their children made partners for Him", otherwise Allah forbid that Adam and Eve should do that; and if the pronoun is made not to refer to Adam and Eve, there is no need to supply it. It was also said that there are views on the verse which require that the pronoun refer to Adam and Eve without any omitted muḍāf, by an interpretation mentioned in the books of tafsīr.

Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «شِرْكاً» with kasra on the shīn, sukūn on the rāʾ and tanwīn on the kāf. The rest read it with ḍamma on the shīn, fatḥa on the rāʾ and a lengthened hamzated kāf without tanwīn, the plural of sharīk (partner). Shirk is thus a maṣdar, and an omitted muḍāf is necessary, i.e. "possessors of shirk" in the sense of ishrāk (associating); so in reality it is an ism maṣdar (noun of action). It was also said that by shirk is meant a share, namely what the two made out of their provision for him, which he would eat with them, whereas the two used to eat and drink by themselves. Then the pronoun in «له» refers to the righteous child. It was also said that the pronoun in «له» refers to Iblīs, though no mention of him has preceded. These two views have no sense. Makkī, Abū l-Baqāʾ and others said: the implied form may be: "they made for other than Him a share". I say: of what these people supposed, Abū l-Ḥasan said: "Whoever reads «شِرْكاً» ought to say that the meaning is: they made for other than Him a share [in what He gave them], for they do not deny that the origin is for Allah; so the association is only in making it for someone else."

His saying: {فَتَعَالَى الله عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ}: it was said that this is a resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) clause, the pronoun in «يشركون» refers to the disbelievers, and the speech was complete before it. It was also said that it refers to Adam, Eve and Iblīs, the meant association being their naming a third child ʿAbd al-Ḥārith, Iblīs having hinted at that; so the association is in the naming only. It was also said that Adam had not known. The first view is supported by the reading of al-Sulamī «عَمَّا تشركون» with tāʾ of address, and likewise «أَتُشرِكون» also with address, which is an iltifāt (shift of person).

semin-durr:191-191.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ}: it may refer back to «ما» in terms of meaning, what is meant by it being the idols; they were expressed by «هم» because of the disbelievers' belief about them of what they believe about rational beings, or because they are mixed with those of the rational beings who are worshipped, such as the Messiah and ʿUzayr; or it may refer to the disbelievers, i.e. "the disbelievers are created", so had they reflected on that they would have believed.

semin-durr:119-119.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَغُلِبُواْ هُنَالِكَ}: «هنالك» may be a place, i.e. "they were defeated in the place where their magic took place", and this is the apparent sense. It is said that it may also be a time, though that is not its basic sense, and some have established this meaning for it from His saying, the Exalted, {هُنَالِكَ ابتلي المؤمنون} [al-Aḥzāb: 11] and from another's verse:

2264 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فهناك يَعْترفون أين المَفْزَعُ
(… [first half elided in the source] … and there they will confess: where is the refuge?)

There is no proof in either, because the place is clear in both.

His saying: {صَاغِرِينَ} is a ḥāl from the agent of «انْقَلبوا», and the pronoun in «انقلبوا» may refer to the people of Pharaoh, and also to the magicians if we make the turning back occur before the magicians' belief, or if we take انقلبوا in the sense of "they became", as al-Zamakhsharī explained it, i.e. "they became abased, stupefied, bewildered"; and it may refer to them (Pharaoh's people) to the exclusion of the magicians if that was after their belief and انقلبوا is not taken in the sense of "became", because Allah does not describe them (the magicians) as abased after their belief.

semin-durr:121-121.t: His saying, the Exalted: {قالوا}: i.e. "they were cast down prostrating and saying that". It may be a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «ساجدين». On both views they are engaged in prostration to Allah the Exalted. It may also be a resumption with no grammatical position. Abū l-Baqāʾ made it a ḥāl from the agent of «انقلبوا», for he said: "It may be a ḥāl, i.e. 'so they turned back abased, having said'." This is not good, because of the separation by His saying: {وَأُلْقِيَ السحرة}.

semin-durr:122-122.t: His saying, the Exalted: {رَبِّ موسى}: It may be an adjective (naʿt) of «رب العالمين», or a badal (substitute), or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The benefit of that is to remove the misconception of anyone who imagines that "Lord of the worlds" might be applied to other than Allah the Exalted, because of Pharaoh's saying {أَنَاْ رَبُّكُمُ الأعلى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 24]. They mentioned Moses before Aaron, although Aaron was older than he, because of Moses' greater rank, or because it fell at the verse-end here; and for that reason He said in Sūrat Ṭā Hā {بِرَبِّ هَارُونَ وموسى} [Ṭā Hā: 70], because Moses fell at the verse-end there; or else each group among them said one of the two statements, so He attributed the act of some to the whole in one sūra and the act of others to the whole in another.

semin-durr:123-123.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {آمَنتُمْ}: The readers differed over this word here, in Ṭā Hā and in al-Shuʿarāʾ. Some followed a single reading, and some read in one place in a way they did not read in another. I say: the readers fall into four categories in this:

The first: the reading of the two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza) and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, which is: verifying both hamzas in the three sūras, without inserting an alif between them, and it is an interrogative of denial. As for the third alif, all read it thus, because it is the fāʾ of the word, replaced (by alif) due to its quiescence after a fatḥa-bearing hamza. The origin of this word is أَأَأْمَنْتم with three hamzas: the first for the interrogative, the second the hamza of the form أَفْعَلَ, and the third the fāʾ of the word. The third must be turned into an alif, for the reason you learned at the beginning of this topic. As for the first, it is verified, nothing else; and the second is the one over which there is disagreement regarding verification and facilitation.

The second: the reading of Ḥafṣ, which is «آمنتم» with a single hamza followed by the alif referred to, throughout the Quran. This reading may be a pure declarative containing rebuke, or it may be the interrogative mentioned, but with the interrogative omitted because the meaning is understood and because of the reading of the rest.

The third: the reading of Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Bazzī from Ibn Kathīr, which is verification of the first, facilitation of the second between the two (bayna bayna), and the alif mentioned. It is an interrogative of denial, as above.

The fourth: the reading of Qunbul from Ibn Kathīr, which distinguishes between the three sūras. He read in this sūra, when beginning with آمنتم, with two hamzas, the first lightened and the second facilitated bayna bayna, and an alif after it, like his companion al-Bazzī; and in continuous reading he read: «قال فرعون وامنتم», replacing the first with a wāw, facilitating the second bayna bayna, and an alif after it. That is because when a hamza carries fatḥa after a ḍamma it may be replaced by a wāw, whether the ḍamma and the hamza are in one word, as in جُوَن and يُؤاخذكم and مُوَجَّلاً, or in two words, as in this verse. He did the same in Sūrat al-Mulk in His saying: {وَإِلَيْهِ النشور وأَمِنتُمْ} [al-Mulk: 15-16], replacing the first hamza with a wāw because of the ḍamma before it in continuous reading; and in beginning he lightens it, since the cause for its change has gone, except that in Sūrat al-Mulk there are not three hamzas. This will be treated, Allah willing, in its place.

In Sūrat Ṭā Hā he read like the reading of Ḥafṣ, I mean with one hamza followed by an alif; and in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ like his companion al-Bazzī, for there is no ḍamma before it that he would replace with a wāw in continuous reading. I have also read for Qunbul three ways in this sūra in continuous reading: making the hamza quiescent after the substituted wāw, or giving it a vowel, or replacing it with an alif, in which case it is pronounced for the length of two alifs. None of the readers inserted a lengthening between the two hamzas here, whether he verified or facilitated, so that four similar letters would not come together.

The pronoun in «به» refers to Allah the Exalted, because of His saying: {قالوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ العالمين}; and it may refer to Moses. As for the one in Ṭā Hā and al-Shuʿarāʾ, in His saying {آمنتم له}, the pronoun is Moses', because of His saying {إنَّه لكبيرُكم}.

His saying: {فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ}: the object of "knowing" is omitted because it is known, i.e. "you will know what will befall you"; then he explained this vagueness by His saying:
{لأُقَطِّعَنَّ}

semin-durr:124-124.t:
{لأُقَطِّعَنَّ}: He brought it in an oath-sentence as emphasis of what he would do. Mujāhid ibn Jabr, Ḥumayd al-Makkī and Ibn Muḥayṣin read «لأقْطَعَنَّ» lightened, from the triliteral قَطَعَ, and likewise «ولأَصْلُبَنَّكُمْ» from the triliteral صلب. Both ḍamma and kasra on the lām (i.e. of the imperfect stem) are transmitted, and they are two dialects in the imperfect: one says صَلَبَه يَصْلُبُه and يَصْلِبُه.

His saying: {مِّنْ خِلاَفٍ}: it may mean that he would cut off from each side a limb, i.e. cut off the right hand and the left foot, and so it is in the exegesis; then the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, as if he said "alternately". It may also mean: "I shall cut you off because of your opposing me", so «مِنْ» is causal and is attached to the verb itself, which is far-fetched. «أجمعين» is an emphasis (tawkīd) with «به» (sic) without «كل», although it is more often preceded by كل. [Translator's note: the Arabic reads "أي به دون كل", the phrase "i.e. with it" is translated literally; the wording appears slightly garbled in the source.] «ثم» is brought here, while in the other two sūras it is «ولأصلبنَّكم» with wāw, because wāw is suited to a delay, so there is no contradiction between the verses.

semin-durr:125-125.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّآ إلى رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ}: They allowed two views about this pronoun. The first: that it is specific to the magicians, and what supports it is His saying after that: {وَمَا تَنقِمُ مِنَّآ}, for the pronoun in «مِنَّا» is specific to them. They also allowed that it refers to them and to Pharaoh, i.e. "we and you will return to Allah, and He will requite each according to his deed"; and although that is what will happen, it is not from this wording.

semin-durr:126-126.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا تَنقِمُ}: It has already been mentioned, in Sūrat al-Māʾida, that it has two dialects, and how it is made transitive with «من», and that this is by implication (taḍmīn). And His saying: {إِلاَّ أَنْ آمَنَّا} may be in the position of accusative as a direct object, i.e. "you blame us for nothing except our belief". It may also be an object of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), i.e. "you do not take vengeance on us and punish us for any reason except our belief". On both views it is an incomplete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh).

His saying: {لَمَّا جَآءَتْنَا} may be temporal, as is the view of al-Fārisī and one of the two statements of Sībawayh, and the operator in it on this view is «آمنَّا», i.e. "we believed when the signs came"; or it may be a particle of "occurrence due to occurrence" (ḥarf wujūb li-wujūb), and on this view it must have an apodosis, which is omitted, its implied form being: "when they came to us, we believed in them without hesitation".

semin-durr:155-155.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {واختار موسى}: «اختار» takes two objects: the first directly, and the second by means of a preposition, though the preposition may be omitted. You say «اخترت زيداً من الرجال» ("I chose Zayd from among the men"), then the construction is extended, so you omit «مِنْ» and say «زيداً الرجال». He said:
2306 - اخْتَرْتُكَ الناسَ إذ رثَّتْ خلائِقُهُمْ ... واعتلَّ مَنْ كان يُرجى عنده السُّؤلُ
(I chose you from among the people when their characters grew worn, and he from whom requests were hoped for fell ill/failed.)
And al-Rāʿī said:
2307 - فقلْتُ له اخترها قَلوصاً سمينة ... ونابٌ علينا مثل نابِكَ في الحيا
(So I said to him: "Choose from them a fat young she-camel, and an old she-camel among us like your old she-camel in fertility.")
And al-Farazdaq said: 2308 - منا الذي اختير الرجالَ سماحةً ... وجوداً إذا هَبَّ الرياح الزعازعُ
(Among us is the one who was chosen from among men for munificence and generosity when the violent winds blow.)
This type is confined to what is heard from the Arabs; the grammarians have restricted it to certain words, namely: «اختار»; and «أَمَر», as in his saying:
2309 - أمرتك الخيرَ فافعلْ ما أُمِرْتَ به ... فقد تَرَكْتُك ذا مالٍ وذا نَشَبِ
(I commanded you [to do] good, so do what you were commanded, for I have left you possessing wealth and property.)
and «استغفر», as in his saying:
2310 - أستغفرُ اللهَ ذنباً لستُ محصيَه ... ربَّ العبادِ إليه الوجهُ والعملُ
(I seek Allah's forgiveness for a sin I cannot count — the Lord of the servants, to whom are directed the face and the deed.)
and «سمَّى» [such as:] «سَمَّيْتُ ابني بزيد» ("I named my son Zayd"), or, if you wish, «زيداً». And «دعا» in its sense, he said:
2311 - دَعَتْني أمُّ عمرو أخاها ولم أكن ... أخاها ولم أَرْضَعْ لها بلَبانِ
(Umm ʿAmr called me her brother, though I was not her brother and had not suckled at her breast.)
and «كَنَى»: you say «كَنَيْته بفلان» ("I gave him the kunya of so-and-so"), or, if you wish, «فلاناً». And «صَدَق», the Exalted said: {وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ الله وَعْدَهُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 152]. And «زوَّج», the Exalted said: {زَوَّجْنَاكَهَا} [al-Aḥzāb: 37]. The Shaykh did not add anything to these. Among them also are «حدَّث وأنبأ ونبّأ وأخبر وخبَّر» when they are not made to include the meaning of «أَعْلَمَ» ("to inform"). The Exalted said: {مَنْ أَنبَأَكَ هذا} [al-Taḥrīm: 3] and He said: {فَلَمَّا نَبَّأَهَا بِهِ} [al-Taḥrīm: 3]. And you say «حَدَّثْتك بكذا», or, if you wish, «كذا». He said:
2312 - لَئِنْ كان ما حُدِّثْتُه اليومَ صادقاً ... أَصُمْ في نهارِ القيظِ للشمس باديا
(If what I was told today is true, I shall fast in the day of the scorching heat, exposed to the sun.)
And «قومه» is a second object, taking precedence over the first, and the implied form is: "and Moses chose seventy men from his people." Abū l-Baqāʾ reported from some that «قومَه» is the first object and «سبعين» is a badal (substitute), that is, a partial substitute for the whole; then he said: "I see that the substitution is permissible, though weak, and that the implied form is: seventy men of them." I say: it is prohibited, or weak, only because it involves the omission of two things. One of them is that from which the choice is made, for choosing necessarily requires one chosen and one chosen from; whereas on the badal analysis only the one chosen is mentioned, not the one chosen from. The second: that a link is necessary between the badal and the mubdal minhu (the thing substituted for), and that is «منهم» as Abū l-Baqāʾ supposed; moreover the badal is in the intention of being discarded.
The origin of «اختار» is «اختَيَرَ», of the pattern ifʿala (Form VIII), from the word «الخير», like «اصطفى» from «الصفوة». And «لميقاتنا» is attached to it, that is: "for the sake of Our appointed time." It is also permissible that its meaning be specification, that is: "he chose them, assigning the appointed time to them," as in your saying «اختير لك هذا» ("this was chosen for you").
His saying: {لَوْ شِئْتَ}: the object of the willing is omitted, that is: "if You had willed our destruction"; «أهلكتهم» is the apodosis (jawāb) of «لو». It is most common to bring the lām in this kind of construction, and for that reason it does not come bare of it except here, and in His saying {أَن لَّوْ نَشَآءُ أَصَبْنَاهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 100] and in His saying: {لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً} [al-Wāqiʿa: 70]. And the meaning of «من قبل» is: before the choosing and the seizure by the quake.
His saying: {وَإِيَّايَ}: whoever holds that it is permissible to use the detached pronoun when the attached one is possible may cling to it, since it would have been possible to say «أهلكتنا». But that is an extremely flimsy clinging, because his aim, peace and blessings be upon him, was to state explicitly the destruction of each one separately, as a magnification of the matter; moreover Moses had not engaged in anything that would call for his destruction, unlike his people, and he said that only as submission to his Lord, so he conjoined his own pronoun to draw attention to that. A similar case has already been given to you in His saying {وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الذين أُوتُواْ الكتاب مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 131] and His saying {يُخْرِجُونَ الرسول وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 1].
His saying: {أَتُهْلِكُنَا}: it is permissible that it be in its normal sense, that is: "Will You encompass us all in destruction, or single out the foolish among us for it?" / And it is permissible that it carry the meaning of negation, that is: "You do not destroy one who has not sinned for the sin of another." Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī said this; he said: "It is like your saying: 'Would you humiliate one who honours you?'" And from al-Mubarrad: it is a question of appeal for compassion. And «منا» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from «السفهاء», and it may be explicative (lil-bayān).
His saying: {تُضِلُّ بِهَا}: two views are permissible concerning it. The first: that it is resumptive, so it has no grammatical position. The second: that it is a ḥāl from «فتنتك», that is: "while it leads astray by means of it." It is also permissible that it be a ḥāl from the kāf, because it is nominative in implication as agent; Abū l-Baqāʾ prohibited it, saying: "because of the absence of a governor in it." The discussion with him on this has already been presented more than once.

semin-durr:156-156.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {هُدْنَآ}: the majority read with ḍamma on the hāʾ, from hāda yahūdu meaning "to incline." He said:
2313 - قد عَلِمَتْ سَلْمى وجاراتُها ... أني مِنَ الله لها هائدُ
(Salmā and her neighbour women know that I, toward Allah on her account, am one who inclines/repents.)
Or "to repent," from his saying:
2314 - إني امرؤٌ مما جَنَيْتُ هائِدُ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I am a man who repents of what I have committed … [Translator's note: the rest of the verse is elided in the source].)
And from the speech of one of them: «يا راكبَ الذنب هُدْهُدْ، واسجد كأنك هُدْهُد» ("O rider of sin, repent, and prostrate as though you were a hoopoe"). Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Abū Wajza read «هِدْنا» with kasra [on the hāʾ], from hāda yahīdu, meaning "to move." Al-Zamakhsharī allowed, in both «هُدنا» and «هِدْنا», with ḍamma and with kasra, that the verb be active or passive in each, meaning "we inclined" or "someone else made us incline," or "we moved ourselves" or "someone else moved us"; but this is open to objection, because some of the grammarians have stated that whenever ambiguity arises, a vowel that removes the ambiguity must be brought. So one says of «عقتُ» (from al-ʿawq) if someone else hindered you: «عِقت» with kasra only, or with ishmām; and of «بعتَ يا عبد» if what is meant is that someone else sold him: «بُعْت» with ḍamma only, or with ishmām. But Sībawayh allowed the three forms in «قيل» and «بيع» and the like, without reservation.
And «هي» is a pronoun explained by the context of the speech, since the implied form is: "It is only Your trial of them" (in fatatuhum illā fitnatuka). It was also said: it refers back to the request for seeing, from {أَرِنَا الله جَهْرَةً}, that is: "it is only the request for the vision."
His saying: {عذابي أُصِيبُ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. The majority read «مَنْ أشاء» with the dotted shīn. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Ṭāwūs and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid read «أساء» with the undotted sīn, from isāʾa (doing wrong). Al-Dānī said: "This reading is not authentic from al-Ḥasan or from Ṭāwūs, and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid is a wicked man. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna once read it and approved of it, so ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ stood up to him and shouted at him and made him hear it. Sufyān said: 'I was not aware of what the people of innovation say.'" I say: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān means that the Muʿtazila clung to this reading to argue that the servant's act is created by him, and Sufyān excused himself for that.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His words, the Exalted: {إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ}: there are two views on «إذ». The first: it is a ẓarf (adverbial) accusative by the verbal sense contained in «الآلاء», as though it were said: "and remember Allah's favours upon you at this time". The object of «اذكروا» is omitted, as indicated by His later words: «فاذكروا آلاءَ الله», and because His words «إذ جعلكم خُلَفاء» and "He increased you in such and such" are themselves the favours; this is the apparent sense of al-Ḥawfī's statement. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «إذ» is the object of «اذكروا», i.e. "remember this time, which comprised weighty blessings."
His words {فِي الخلق}: it is possible that the maṣdar (verbal noun) is meant, in the sense of "in the stretch of your stature, in the beauty of your forms and the greatness of your bodies"; and it is possible that the sense of the direct object (mafʿūl bihi) is meant, i.e. "among the created", meaning: "He increased you among people, the like of you, in stature over them", for there was no one like them in their time in the greatness of bodies. It is reported in tafsīr that the shortest of them was sixty cubits. The disagreement over «بَسْطة» was discussed in al-Baqara.
His words: {آلآءَ الله}, i.e. His favours; it is a plural whose singular is «إلْيٌ» with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the lām, like ḥiml and aḥmāl; or «أُلْي» with ḍamma on the hamza and sukūn on the lām, like quful and aqfāl; or «إلَى» with kasra on the hamza and fatḥa on the lām, like ḍilaʿ and aḍlāʿ, or ʿinab and aʿnāb; or «أَلَى» with fatḥa on both, like qafā and aqfāʾ. Al-Aʿshā said:
2228 - ... white, he does not fear emaciation, nor
does he cut my kinship, nor betray (ilā) ... It is recited with kasra on the hamza, which is the well-known form, and with fatḥa. Similar is «الآناء», plural of iny, uny, inā or anā. Al-Akhfash said: "inw". «الآناء» means times, as in His words: {وَمِنْ آنَآءِ الليل} [طه: 130], which will come.

semin-durr:70-70.t: His words, the Exalted: {لِنَعْبُدَ}: attached to the coming which they rejected in him. His words «إن كنتَ»: its apodosis is omitted or precedes, and it is «فَأْت به».

semin-durr:71-71.t: His words, the Exalted: {مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ}: it is either attached to «وَقَع», with «مِنْ» for the figurative beginning of the extent; or it is attached to an omitted word, as a ḥāl, since originally it was a ṣifa of «رجس». His words «سَمَّيْتُموها» are a ṣifa of «أسماء», and likewise the clause «ما نَزَّل الله»; «مِنْ سلطان» is the object of «نَزَّل», and «مِنْ» is redundant. «من المنتظرين» is the khabar of «إني». As for «معكم», what was said before applies to it, in His words {إِنِّي لَكُمَا لَمِنَ الناصحين} [الأعراف: 21]. It is possible, though weak, that «معكم» is the khabar and «من المنتظرين» a ḥāl, the implied sense being: "I am your companion while being among those awaiting victory and relief from Allah the Exalted". But it is not so, because what is intended in the speech is the waiting, in correspondence with His words «فانتظروا», so it should not be made a superfluous element (faḍla).

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وإلى ثَمُودَ}: Thamūd is the name of a man, Thamūd ibn Jāthir ibn Iram ibn Sām, brother of Jadīs; so Thamūd and Jadīs were brothers, and then this tribe was named after him. The more common practice is to treat it as diptote, in view of what I mentioned; some made it the name of the clan and so treated it as fully declinable, and this is the reading of al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb throughout the Quran; a disagreement among the seven readers will come to you in Sūrat Hūd and elsewhere. It was also said: they were named Thamūd because of the scarcity of their water, thamd being little water. Al-Nābigha said:
2229 - Judge as the girl of the clan judged when she looked ... at the doves in flight coming to the little water (thamad).
Ṣāliḥ is an Arabic name; he is Ṣāliḥ ibn Āsif. It was said: ibn ʿUbayd ibn Āsif ibn Kāshiḥ ibn Arūm ibn Thamūd ibn Jāthir.
His words: {قَدْ جَآءَتْكُمْ بَيِّنَةٌ}: this word has often been followed by operators (ʿawāmil), so it runs in the manner of al-abṭaḥ and al-abraq in not mentioning its qualified noun. His words «من ربكم» may be attached to «جاءتكم», with «مِنْ» for the figurative beginning of the extent, or attached to an omitted word, as it is a ṣifa of «بَيِّنة». An omitted muḍāf is necessary, i.e. "from the proofs of your Lord", so that the qualified noun and its ṣifa agree. His word «آية» is accusative as ḥāl, because it means a sign. The operator in it is either the sense of alerting or the sense of pointing, as though he said: "I alert you to it" or "I point to it in this state". It is also possible that the operator is implied, its implied form being: "Look at it in this state"; and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is like the answer to an implied question, as though they said: "Where is your sign?" and he said: "This is the she-camel of Allah"; he attributed it to Allah as an honour, like "House of Allah" and "Spirit of Allah", because it was not born between a male camel and a she-camel but emerged from a hard rock, as is well known.
His words {لِكُمْ}, i.e. "I mean, for you"; they were singled out for this because they were the ones who asked for it, or those who would benefit from it among all people had they obeyed. It is possible that «هذه ناقة الله» is explicative of His words «بيِّنة», because the proof calls for something by which the claim is made clear, so the clause would be in the position of nominative as a badal; and it is permissible to substitute a clause for a singular because it is equivalent to it in force.
His words: {في أَرْضِ الله}: the apparent view is that it is attached to «تأكل»; it was said that it may be attached to His words «فَذَرُوها», and on this the matter is one of tanāzuʿ (rivalry of two operators), with the second being operative; had the first been made operative, he would have placed a pronoun in the second and said: "taʾkulu fīhā fī arḍi llāh". «تأكل» is jussive as the answer to the command. The disagreement about its jussive-causing element has already been discussed: is it the request clause itself or an implied particle? Abū Jaʿfar read «تأكلُ» with the verb nominative, as a ḥāl; this is parallel to {فَهَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنْكَ وَلِيّاً يَرِثُنِي} [مريم: 6], read nominative and jussive.

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَبَوَّأَكُمْ فِي الأرض}: bawwaʾahu means "He lodged him in a dwelling". Al-mabāʾa is the dwelling; this root was discussed in Āl ʿImrān. It takes two objects; the second is omitted, i.e. "He lodged you in dwellings". «في الأرض» is attached to the verb, and it is mentioned so that what comes after it, His words «تَتَّخذون», may be built upon it. His words «تَتَّخذون»: it may be the one that takes one object, in which case «من سهولها» is attached to the taking, or to an omitted word as a ḥāl from «قصوراً», since it was originally a ṣifa of it had it come later, meaning that the material of the palaces is from the soft plains of the earth, such as gypsum, mud brick and baked brick, like His words: {واتخذ قَوْمُ موسى مِن بَعْدِهِ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ} [الأعراف: 148], i.e. its material was of their ornaments. It was said: «مِنْ» means "in" (fī). In tafsīr: they lived in palaces in summer and in the mountains in winter. Or it may be the one that takes two objects, the second being «من سهولها».
His words: {وَتَنْحِتُونَ الجبال بُيُوتاً}: «الجبال» may be on the dropping of the preposition, i.e. "from the mountains", like His words: {واختار موسى قَوْمَهُ} [الأعراف: 155], in which case «بيوتاً» is its object. It is also possible that «تَنْحِتون» is made to imply a verb taking two objects, i.e. "you take the mountains as houses by carving, or you make them houses by carving". It is also possible that «الجبال» is the direct object and «بيوتاً» an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), like your saying: "Sew this cloth into a jubba", i.e. destined for that. «بيوتاً», even though it is not derived, is in the sense of a derived word, i.e. "inhabited".
Al-Ḥasan read «تَنْحَتون» with fatḥa on the middle letter. Al-Zamakhsharī added that he read «تنحاتون» with the fatḥa lengthened into an alif, and recited:
2230 - It gushes from behind the ear of a furious, strong she-camel ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
Yaḥyā ibn Muṣarrif and Abū Mālik read it with the yāʾ (third person), as a shift of person (iltifāt), except that Abū Mālik put fatḥa on the ḥāʾ like al-Ḥasan's reading. Al-sahl of the earth is what is soft and easy to benefit from, the opposite of al-ḥazn. Al-suhūla means ease. Al-quṣūr is the plural of qaṣr, which is the lofty house; it was so called because people fall short (quṣūr) of ascending to it, or because most people fall short of building the like of it, unlike their elite, or because it is confined (yuqtaṣar) to one plot of land, unlike hair tents and tent poles, which are not confined to a particular plot because their people move on, or because it confines (yaqṣur) those within it, i.e. holds them, from which: {وحُورٌ مَّقْصُورَاتٌ فِي الخيام} [الرحمن: 72]. Al-naḥt is carving into something hard, such as stone and wood. He said:
2231 - As for the day, it is in shackle and chain, ... and the night in the belly of a hewn teak (box).
Al-Aʿmash read «ولا تِعْثُوا» with kasra on the imperfect prefix letter; it was already stated that this is a dialect. «مفسدين» is an emphasizing ḥāl, since its meaning is understood from its operator. «في الأرض» is attached to the preceding verb or to «مفسدين».

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His words, the Exalted: {قَالَ الملأ}: Ibn ʿĀmir alone read «وقال» with a conjunctive wāw, conjoining this clause to what precedes, in agreement with the Syrian codices, in which it is written. The rest omit it: either being content with the semantic link, or because it is the answer to an implied question as the like of it was explained earlier, in agreement with their codices. This is as was said before regarding His words: {وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهْتَدِيَ} [الأعراف: 43], except that there it is he who omitted the wāw.
His words: {لِلَّذِينَ استضعفوا}: the lām is for conveying. It is weak to take it as causal. The sīn in «استكبروا» and «استضعفوا» may be in its usual sense of seeking, i.e. those people sought arrogance from themselves, and weakness from the believers. It is also possible that istafʿala is in the sense of faʿala, like ʿajiba and istaʿjaba.
His words: {لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ} is a badal from «الذين اسْتُضْعِفُوا» with repetition of the operator, and it has two views. The first: it is badal kull min kull (whole for whole) if the pronoun in «منهم» refers back to his people, and the oppressed are believers only, as though it were said: "The arrogant said to the believers from the people of Ṣāliḥ." The second: it is badal baʿḍ min kull (part for whole) if the pronoun refers back to the oppressed, and the oppressed are of two kinds, believers and disbelievers, as though it were said: "The arrogant said to the believers among the weak, not the disbelievers among the weak."
His words: {أَتَعْلَمُونَ} are in the position of accusative as the object of the saying. «من ربه» is attached to «مُرْسَل». «مِنْ» is for the figurative beginning of the extent, and it may be a ṣifa, in which case it is attached to an omitted word.
His words: {بِمَآ أُرْسِلَ بِهِ} is attached to «مؤمنون», fronted for restriction, emphasis and the verse-ending rhyme. «ما» is a relative. Here it is not permissible to omit the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid), even though the preposition is the same for the relative and its returning pronoun, because the operator differs in the two prepositional phrases. Likewise His words: { بالذي آمَنتُمْ بِهِ كَافِرُونَ} [الأعراف: 76].

semin-durr:77-77.t:
Al-ʿaqr originally means severing the hamstrings of camels, which is striking the legs of the camel or she-camel so that it falls; this was their custom in slaughtering. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
2232 - And the day I hamstrung my mount for the maidens, ... how wondrous was its carried howdah!
Then it was applied to every slaughter even if there was no severing of hamstrings, naming a thing after what usually accompanies it, applying the cause to what it causes. This is al-Azharī's statement. Ibn Qutayba said: "Al-ʿaqr is killing however it be; ʿaqartuhā, so she is maʿqūra." It was also said: al-ʿaqr is wounding. On this is Imruʾ al-Qays's saying:
2233 - She says, while the saddle leaned with us both: ... "You have injured (ʿaqarta) my camel, O Imruʾ al-Qays, so get down."
She means: you have wounded it with your weight and your leaning. Al-ʿuqr and al-ʿaqr, with fatḥa; and with ḍamma is the original; from it, ʿaqartuhu means "I struck its ʿaqr", i.e. its root, like their saying kabadtuhu and raʾastuhu, i.e. "I struck his liver and his head"; and ʿaqarta l-nakhl means "you cut the palm from its root". The "biting dog" (al-kalb al-ʿaqūr) is from it. A woman is ʿāqir (barren), and she has been ʿuqirat. Al-ʿuqr with ḍamma is the last of offspring and the last egg; one says ʿuqira l-bayḍ. Al-ʿaqār with fatḥa is property in buildings, and from it: "No people were ever attacked in the heart (ʿuqr) of their home but they were humiliated"; some restrict it to palm trees. Al-ʿuqār with ḍamma is wine, because it is like a barren-maker (ʿāqira) of the mind. "He raised his ʿaqīra" means his voice, and its origin is that a man had his foot hamstrung and raised his voice, so it was borrowed for every one who cries out. Al-ʿuqr with ḍamma also means dowry.
His words: {وَعَتَوْاْ}: al-ʿutuww and al-ʿutiyy mean recoiling, i.e. rising above obedience; one says from it ʿatā yaʿtū ʿutuwwan and ʿutiyyan, with both wāws turned into yāʾs; the better practice when it is a maṣdar is to keep the two wāws sound, as in His words: {وَعَتَوْا عُتُوّاً كَبِيراً} [الفرقان: 21]. When it is a plural, the weakening change is used, as in qawm ʿutiyy, because the plural is heavier, and by analogy it takes the change for lightness. And His words: {أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرحمن عِتِيّاً} [مريم: 69]. And His words: {وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الكبر عِتِيّاً} [مريم: 8], i.e. a state in which it is impossible to treat me, and it is like his saying:
2234 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... and among hardships is training an old man.
It was said: al-ʿātī is the hardened, i.e. the dry. One also says ʿathā yaʿthū ʿuthuwwan with the thāʾ of three dots, from another root, since one says ʿathiya yaʿthā ʿithiyyan and ʿathā yaʿthū ʿuthuwwan; in one of its two dialects it shares with «عتا» (with the two-dotted tāʾ) the form and the meaning, and is close to it in its letters. Al-ʿayth, with the yāʾ placed before the thāʾ, is also corruption, so it may be an original, or may be a transposition. Some make al-ʿayth the corruption perceived by the senses and al-ʿithiyy that perceived by judgment; a portion of this has already preceded you.
His words: {يَا صَالِحُ ائتنا}: on the narration of those who ease the hamza, namely Warsh and al-Sūsī, you may change the hamza into a wāw, pronouncing it in the form yā ṣāliḥu wtinā, in continuous reading only, replacing the hamza by the vowel of what precedes it even though it is separate, in another word. ʿĀṣim and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read: «أُوْتنا» with the hamza and a full ḍamma; perhaps this is ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī, not Ibn Abī l-Najūd. This reading is not far from error, because the hamzat al-waṣl in such a pattern is with kasra, so whence came the ḍamma of the hamza, except through supposition? His words: {بِمَا تَعِدُنَآ}: the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "taʿidunāhu"; it is not permissible to imply that «تَعِدُنا» governs it with the bāʾ, even though the original is for it to govern it with the bāʾ, so as not to necessitate omitting a returning pronoun governed by a preposition without the two attachments being the same, because «بما» is attached to the coming and «به» to the promise.

semin-durr:127-127.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَيَذَرُكَ}: The majority read «ويَذَرَك» with a third-person yāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ. There are two views about the accusative. The more evident: that it is conjoined to «ليُفْسدوا». The second: that it is accusative as the answer to the interrogative, as it is made accusative in answer to it after the fāʾ, like the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:

2265 - ألم أكُ جارَكُم ويكونَ بيني ... وبينكمُ المودةُ والإِخاءُ
(Was I not your neighbour, and may there be between me and you affection and brotherhood?)

The meaning: how can there be a combination of your leaving Moses and his people to cause corruption and their leaving you and the worship of your gods? That is, the occurrence of that is not possible.

al-Ḥasan, in a transmission from him, and Nuʿaym ibn Maysara read «ويذرُك» with ḍamma on the rāʾ. There are three views about it. The most evident: that it is conjoined (nasaq) to «أتذر», i.e. "will you let him have that?". The second: that it is a resumptive statement of that. The third: that it is a ḥāl, and a mubtadaʾ must be implied, i.e. "while he leaves you".

al-Ḥasan also, and al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, read «ويذرْك» jussive. There are two views about it. One: that it is jussive by conjoining on a fancied form, as if he had fancied «يُفْسدوا» jussive in the answer to the interrogative and so conjoined to it with the jussive, like His saying {فأصَّدَّق وأكنْ} [al-Munāfiqūn: 10], with «وأكن» jussive. The second: that it is a lightening, like the reading of Abū ʿAmr «يَنْصُرْكم» and its like.

Anas ibn Mālik read: «ونذرُك» with the nūn of the group and ḍamma on the rāʾ; they were threatening him with that, or the matter would end up at that, so it would be a pure statement. ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) and al-Aʿmash read in a way that differs from the written copy (rasm), so there is no need to mention it.

The majority read «وآلهتكَ» in the plural. In the exegesis: that he used to worship several gods, such as cattle, stones and stars; or his gods whose worship he had legislated for them while making himself the highest god, in the saying {أَنَاْ رَبُّكُمُ الأعلى}. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Ibn Masʿūd, Anas and a great number read: «وإلاهتك». There are two views about it. One: that «إلاهة» is a name for the object of worship, and what is meant is Pharaoh's object of worship, which is the sun; in the exegesis he used to worship the sun, and the sun is called «إلاهة» as a proper name for it, and for that reason it is diptote for being a proper name and feminine. The second: that «إلاهة» is a maṣdar meaning worship, i.e. "and leaves your worship", because his people used to worship him. Ibn al-Anbārī reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he used to reject the reading of the majority and read «وإلاهتك», and he would say: Pharaoh was worshipped and did not worship.

His saying: {سَنُقَتِّلُ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr read «سَنَقْتل» lightened, and the rest with tashdīd for intensification, because of the multiplicity of those killed. It will come that the group read «يُقَتِّلُون أبناءكم» with tashdīd except Nāfiʿ, who lightens it. So the result is that Nāfiʿ reads both verbs lightened; Ibn Kathīr lightens «سنقتل» and doubles «يقتلون»; and the rest double both.

semin-durr:128-128.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُورِثُهَا}: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. There are two views about its owner (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl). One: the Majestic Name, i.e. "it belongs to Him while He causes whomever He wills to inherit it". The second: that it is the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, i.e. "the earth is established as belonging to Allah while being bequeathed from Allah to whom He wills". It is also possible that «يورثها» is a second khabar, or the khabar alone, with «لله» being the ḥāl, and «مَنْ يشاء» a second object; and it may be a resumptive sentence.

al-Ḥasan read, and it is transmitted from Ḥafṣ, «يُوَرِّثُها» with tashdīd for intensification. It has also been read «يُوْرَثُها» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, passive, the deputy agent being «مَنْ يشاء». The alif and lām in «الأرض» may be of familiarity (ʿahd), meaning the land of Egypt, or generic.

Ibn Masʿūd read «العاقبة» accusative, conjoined to «الأرض», with «للمتقين» as its khabar, so he conjoined noun to noun and khabar to khabar, which is a conjunction of sentences. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why is this sentence free of the wāw, while it was brought in on the one before it? I say: it is a newly begun resumptive sentence; whereas {وَقَالَ الملأ} [al-Aʿrāf: 127] is conjoined to what precedes it, His saying: {وَقَالَ الملأ مِن قَوْمِ فِرْعَونَ}."

semin-durr:130-130.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بالسنين}: the plural of سَنَة. It has two dialects. The more famous: that it is treated like the sound masculine plural, so it is nominative with wāw and accusative and genitive with yāʾ, and its nūn is dropped in the genitive construct. The grammarians said: it is treated so by way of compensation for what it lost, namely its dropped lām; something will be said about its lām. The second dialect: the case ending is placed on the nūn, but only with the yāʾ. Abū Zayd and al-Farrāʾ reported this dialect. Then in it you have two dialects: one with its tanwīn retained, the other without it. al-Farrāʾ said: "In this dialect it is triptote according to Banū ʿĀmir and diptote according to Banū Tamīm." The reason for dropping the tanwīn is lightening, and then the nūn is not dropped in the genitive construct; and on that came his saying:

2266 - دَعَانيَ مِنْ نَجْدٍ فإنَّ سنينَه ... لَعِبْنَ بنا شِيْباً وشَيَّبْنَنَا مُرْدا
(Leave me from Najd, for its years played with us as grey-haired men and turned us grey when we were beardless youths.)

The ḥadīth also came: «اللهم اجعلها عليهم سنين كَسِني يوسف» and «سنيناً كسنينِ يوسف», in both dialects. ("O Allah, make them years upon them like the years of Joseph.")

For the lām of «سَنَة» there are two views. One: that it is a wāw, from their saying سنوات, سانَيْتُ and سُنَيَّة. The second: that it is a hāʾ, from their saying سانَهْتُ, سَنَهات and سُنَيْهَة. This ruling mentioned, I mean its being treated like the masculine plural or its inflection by vowels, is not restricted to the word سنين, but applies to every triliteral feminine noun whose lām has been dropped and replaced by the tāʾ of feminine and which has not been pluralised as a broken plural, such as ثُبة and ثبين, قُلة and قُلين. By my saying "whose lām was dropped" I exclude those whose fāʾ was dropped, like لِدة and عِدَة; and by my saying "and which has not been pluralised as a broken plural" I exclude ظُبَة and ظُبَى. Their saying «لِدُون» for a noun with dropped fāʾ is irregular, and so is ظِبون for the broken plural. He said:

2267 - يرى الراؤون بالشَّفَراتِ منها ... وُقودَ أبي حُباحبَ والظُّبينا
(Onlookers see in the blades of it the fire of Abū Ḥubāḥib, and the sword-edges.)

Know that when this type is treated like الزيدين: if its first letter has kasra it remains and is not changed, such as مئة and مئين, فئة and فئين. If its first letter has fatḥa, it takes kasra, such as سنين; and its retention of fatḥa has been transmitted but is very rare. If its first letter has ḍamma, both ways are allowed for it: retention and kasra, such as ثُبين and قُلين.

السَّنَة has come to predominate for the time of drought, and العام for the time of plenty, until they became like proper names by predominance. For this reason they derived from the word سنة and said: أَسْنَتَ القومُ ("the people suffered drought"). He said:

2268 - عمروُ الذي هَشَمَ الثَّريدَ لقومِه ... ورجالُ مكةَ مُسْنِتونَ عجافُ
(ʿAmr is the one who crumbled the tharīd for his people, while the men of Mecca were in drought, gaunt.)

And Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī said:

2269 - وإنَّا نُهيْنُ المالَ في غيرِ ظِنَّةٍ ... وما يَشْتكينا في السنين ضريرُها
(We treat wealth with contempt, without any suspicion, and the one in distress does not complain of us in the years of drought.)

What I have mentioned is supported by what is in Sūrat Yūsuf: {تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعُ سِنِينَ} [Yūsuf: 47], then He said: {سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ} [Yūsuf: 48], which concerns drought. And He said: {ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِن بَعْدِ ذلك عَامٌ فِيهِ يُغَاثُ الناس} [Yūsuf: 49]. And His saying: {مِّن الثمرات} is attached to {نَقْصٍ}.

semin-durr:193-193.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن تَدْعُوهُمْ}: the apparent sense is that the address is to the disbelievers and the accusative pronoun refers to the idols; the meaning is: "if you call your gods to seek guidance and right direction, as you seek it from Allah, they will not follow you in what you want." It is also possible that the pronoun (the subject) refers to the Messenger and the believers and the accusative pronoun to the disbelievers: "and if you [believers] call these disbelievers to faith." It is not permissible that «تَدْعوا» be attributed to the pronoun of the Messenger alone with the accusative pronoun also referring to the disbelievers, because the wāw ought then to be dropped on account of the jussive particle; and it cannot be said that he intended an implied dropping of the vowel with the weak letter remaining, as in his saying:

2358 - هَجَوْت زَبَّان ثم جِئْتَ مُعْتذراً ... مِنْ هَجْو زبَّانَ لم تهجو ولم تَدَعِ
(You satirised Zabbān, then came apologising for the satire of Zabbān: you neither satirised nor left off.)

and to be like the saying of the Exalted {إِنَّهُ مَن يَتَّقي وَيِصْبِرْ} [Yūsuf: 90], {فَلاَ تنسى}, and {لا تَخَفْ دَرَكاً ولا تخشى} [Ṭā Hā: 77], because that is a poetic necessity, while the verses are interpreted otherwise, as will come, and a good deal of it has already passed.

His saying: «لا يَتَّبِعكم»: Nāfiʿ read it with a light tāʾ, and likewise in al-Shuʿarāʾ «يَتْبَعُهم»; the rest read it with shaddah. It was said that they are two dialectal forms, which is why in the story of Adam {فَمَن تَبِعَ} [al-Baqara: 38] occurs, and in another place {اتبع} [Ṭā Hā: 123]. It was also said that tabiʿa means he followed his track, while ittabaʿa with shaddah means he took him as a model. The first is more apparent.

His saying: {أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ}: this is a nominal clause conjoined to a verbal one because it has the meaning of a verbal clause, the implied form being "or have you fallen silent". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "A nominal clause in the place of a verbal one, the implied form being: have you called them or have you been silent?" Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "He conjoined the noun to the verb, since the implied form is «أم صَمَتُّم»; like it is the poet's saying:

2359 - سواءٌ عليك الفقرُ أم بِتَّ ليلةً ... بأهل القباب مِنْ نميرِ بن عامرِ
(Poverty is the same for you as spending a night among the people of the domed tents of Numayr ibn ʿĀmir.)"

The Shaykh said: "It is not the conjoining of a verb to a noun; it is only the conjoining of a nominal clause to a verbal one. As for the verse, there is no conjoining of a verb to a noun in it, but rather the conjoining of a verbal clause to a noun that is interpreted as verbal, since the original is: 'It is the same for you whether you became poor or spent the night'. The second clause in the verse was brought as nominal only because the verb indicates occurrence (ḥudūth), and because it is the end of a verse-ending (fāṣila)."

Al-ṣamt means stillness; one says ṣamata yaṣmutu, with fatḥa in the past and ḍamma in the imperfect; and also ṣamita with kasra, yaṣmatu with fatḥa; the maṣdar is al-ṣamt and al-ṣumāt. And «إصْمِت» with kasra on the hamza and the mīm is the name of a well-known desert; it is transferred from the imperative of this root. Some have refuted this, saying that if it were transferred from the imperative its hamza would have to be a hamzat waṣl, and its mīm would have to have ḍamma if from yaṣmut, or fatḥa if from yaṣmat, and that it ought not to be feminised with tāʾ, whereas they said iṣmita. The answer is that the hamza of an imperative verb must be a hamzat qaṭʿ when it is used as a name, as in «إشرب», since among nouns we have none whose hamza is of waṣl except ten nouns [and the pattern of inṭilāq from every maṣdar exceeding five (letters)], which is few, so attaching it to the many is preferable; as for the kasra on the mīm, it is because change is companion to change, and likewise the answer concerning its feminisation with tāʾ.

semin-durr:194-194.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ الذين}: the majority read «إنَّ» with shaddah, so the relative noun is its subject (ism) and «عباد» its predicate (khabar). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read the light «إنْ» with accusative «عباد» and «أمثالكم». Abū l-Fatḥ Ibn Jinnī and others derived it as the negative «إنْ», acting as the Hijazi «ما» does; this is the school of al-Kisāʾī and most of the Kufans other than al-Farrāʾ, and among the Basrans Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Fārisī and Ibn Jinnī held it; the report from Sībawayh and al-Mubarrad differs. The sound view is that its acting is an established dialectal usage, in verse and prose, and they recited:

2360 - إنْ هو مستولياً على أحد ... إلا على أَضْعف المجانين
(He is not prevailing over anyone except over the weakest of the mad.)

But they found this reading problematic in that it negates their being servants like them, whereas the famous reading affirms it, and contradiction in the speech of Allah the Exalted is impossible. They answered that this reading conveys the belittling of the affair of what is worshipped besides Allah and the stupidity of its worshipper: for the worshippers are more complete in state and more able to harm and benefit than their gods, which are inanimate and do none of that, so how does the perfect worship one who is beneath him? So it agrees with the mutawātir reading a fortiori.

Abū Jaʿfar rejected this reading on three grounds. The first: its opposition to the written skeleton of the muṣḥaf. The second: Sībawayh prefers the nominative for the predicate of the light «إنْ», saying «إنْ زيد منطلق», since the action of «ما» is weak and «إنْ» in its sense is weaker still. The third: al-Kisāʾī does not hold that it may mean «ما» unless an affirmation follows it. What al-Naḥḥās rejected it with is nothing, because it is a slight divergence. The Shaykh said: "It is possible that the accusative was written according to the dialect of Rabīʿa, which stops on an accusative tanwīn without an alif, so there is no divergence from the skeleton in it." As for Sībawayh, people differ in understanding him on that. As for al-Kisāʾī, this restriction is not known from him. The Shaykh derived the reading as the light «إنْ» (a lightened form of inna), saying: "The light «إنْ» acts in the mutawātir reading, as in the reading «وإنْ كلاً», and moreover it is established for it to put both parts in the accusative," and he recited:

2361 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . إنَّ حُرَّاسنا أُسْدا
(… indeed our guards are lions.)

He said: "It is an established dialect." Then he said: "If we interpret what has come of that, such as:

2362 - يا ليت أيامَ الصِّبا رواجعا ... أي: تُرى رواجعا
(Would that the days of youth were returning — i.e. 'seen returning'.)

then likewise the interpretation of this reading is: 'Those whom you call upon besides Allah, We created them as servants like you.'" I say: this derivation is then built on two positions. One: the acting of the light form, and a group of grammarians have stated that it is rarer than its not acting; the expression of some is "it is rare", and I do not approve of it because it occurs in the mutawātir. The other: that inna and its sisters put both parts in the accusative, which is a weaker school. So three derivations have resulted for this reading: «إنْ» being negative and acting; or the light one putting both parts in the accusative; or the accusative by an implied verb that is its predicate in meaning.

Some read light «إنْ», «عباداً» accusative and «أمثالُكم» nominative. Its derivation is that it is the light one and not acting, «الذين» being the mubtadaʾ (subject), «تدعون» its ṣila, the returning pronoun omitted, «عبادٌ» a ḥāl from that omitted returning pronoun, and «أمثالكم» its khabar (predicate). The implied form is: "Those whom you call, while they are servants like you in being created and owned — how then are they worshipped?" It is weak that the relative noun be accusative in position, because, as preceded, the acting of the light form is rare.

Abū l-Baqāʾ also reported a fourth reading, with shaddah on «إنَّ», accusative «عباد» and nominative «أمثالكم», its derivation being as the preceding.

semin-durr:195-195.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يَبْطِشُونَ}: the majority read with kasra on the ṭāʾ, from baṭasha yabṭishu. Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ in a report from him read «يَبْطُشون» with ḍamma on it; they are two dialectal forms. Al-baṭsh means seizing with force.

His saying: {ثم كيدوني}: Abū ʿAmr read «كيدوني» with the yāʾ affirmed in continuation (waṣl) and dropped in pause (waqf). Hishām affirms it in both cases. The rest drop it in both cases, and from Hishām there is a well-known disagreement. The Shaykh said: "Abū ʿAmr and Hishām, with a disagreement from him, read «فكيدوني» with the yāʾ affirmed in continuation and pause." I say: Abū ʿAmr does not affirm it in pause at all, for his rule concerning the additional yāʾs is what I have mentioned to you. In the recitation «فكيدوني» occurs in three places: this one, whose ruling is now known; in Hūd [verse 55] {فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعاً}, where all the readers affirm it in both cases; and in al-Mursalāt [verse 39] {فَإِن كَانَ لَكمُ كَيْدٌ فَكِيدُونِ}, where all drop it in both cases. This is the like of what you have met in the word {واخشوني} [al-Baqara: 150], which is affirmed for all in al-Baqara in continuation and pause, omitted at the beginning of al-Māʾida, and disputed in its second occurrence.

semin-durr:157-157.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الذين يَتَّبِعُونَ}: there are several views on its position. The first: genitive, as an adjective (naʿt) of His saying «الذين يتقون». The second: that it is a badal (substitute) for it. The third: that it is accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off, i.e., a new construction). The fourth: that it is nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, which is also the meaning of qaṭʿ. The fifth: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and then there are two views about the khabar. One: that it is the verbal clause in His saying «يأمرهم بالمعروف». The other: the nominal clause in His saying {أولئك هُمُ المفلحون}. Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned that, and there is weakness in it — indeed, a prohibition: how can «يأمرهم» be made a khabar when it is part of the completion of the description of the Messenger ﷺ, or else is, according to some, governed by the verb of finding, as will be pointed out? And how can «أولئك هم المفلحون» be made the khabar of this relative noun, when the second relative noun, His saying {فالذين آمَنُواْ بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ}, demands it as its khabar? The mind does not turn to anything other than that, and were it to turn, it would not be considered.
His saying: {الأمي}: the majority read with ḍamma on the hamza, as a nisba (relational adjective): either to the umma, meaning the nation of the Arabs, because the Arabs neither reckon nor write — and from this is the ḥadīth: "We are an unlettered nation (umma ummiyya); we neither write nor reckon"; or a nisba to al-amm, which is the maṣdar of amma yaummu, that is, "to aim at, to head for," and the meaning on this view is that this noble Prophet is aimed at by everyone. There is an objection in this, because it ought to have been said al-ammī with fatḥa on the hamza. It may be said that it is one of the alterations of the nisba. It will come that this is the reading of some of them. Or a nisba to Umm al-Qurā, which is Mecca; or a nisba to al-umm (the mother), as though the one who neither reads nor writes is in the state of his birth from his mother.
Yaʿqūb read «الأَمِّيّ» with fatḥa on the hamza, and some explained it as one of the alterations of the nisba, as they say for the nisba to Umayya: amawī. / Some explained it as a nisba to al-amm, which is aiming, that is: the one who is on the right aim and straight course; this too has been mentioned before regarding the famous reading. So it results that each of the two readings may be an alteration of the other.
His saying: «تجدونه»: the obvious is that this verb takes one object, because it is al-luqba (finding of a lost thing); the implied form is: "you encounter him," that is, you encounter his name and description written, because it has the sense of finding a stray; so «مكتوباً» would be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «تجدونه». Abū ʿAlī said: "It takes two objects, the first being the hāʾ and the second «مكتوباً»." He said: "And it is necessary to omit this muḍāf, I mean his saying 'his mention' or 'his name.'" Sībawayh said: "You say, when you look in this book: 'This is ʿAmr,' and the meaning is only: 'This is the name of ʿAmr,' 'this is the mention of ʿAmr.'" He said: "And this is allowed through the breadth of speech."
His saying: {عِندَهُمْ فِي التوراة}: this adverbial and its counterpart are both attached to «تَجدون»; and it is permissible — and it is the clearer — that they be attached to «مكتوباً», that is: "his name and description were written with them in their Torah and Gospel."
His saying: {يَأْمُرُهُم}: there are six views on it. The first: that it is resumptive, so it has no position then; this is a saying of al-Zajjāj. The second: that it is a khabar of «الذين»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it, and it has been mentioned; I say: what is wrong with it has been mentioned there. The third: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «تجدونه», but figurative usage is necessary here, in that it is made an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara). Abū ʿAlī prohibited that it be a ḥāl from this pronoun; he said: "because the pronoun refers to the name and the mention, and the name and the mention do not command" — he means that the speech involves the omission of a muḍāf, as has passed, for its implied form is: "you find his name or his mention," and the mention and the name do not command; only the one mentioned and named commands. The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «النبيّ». The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «مكتوباً». The sixth: that it is an explication of «مكتوباً», that is, of what was written; al-Fārisī said it. He said: "just as His saying {وَعَدَ الله الذين آمَنُواْ} is explained by His saying: {لَهُمْ مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ} [al-Māʾida: 9], and just as «المَثَل» in the saying of the Exalted {إِنَّ مَثَلَ عيسى عِندَ الله كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 59] is explained by {خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرَابٍ}."
And al-Zajjāj said here: "It is permissible that the meaning be: they find it written with them that he commands them to the good; and on this basis the command to the good and what is mentioned with it of his description, which was mentioned in the two Books." Abū ʿAlī took exception to this statement and said: "There is no justification for his saying 'they find it written with them that he commands them to the good,' if he means that that is intended, because nothing indicates its omission, and because we do not know that they were truthful in anything; and the explanation of the verse is that {وجدت} in it takes two objects" — and he mentioned something like what I gave from him earlier.
I say: this rebuttal is unfair to him, because he wanted to explain the meaning, and it is a good explanation.
His saying: {إصرهم}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «آصارهم» in the plural on the pattern afʿāl, so the hamza that is the fāʾ of the word turned into an alif because of being preceded by another like it; the rest read it in the singular, and it is a plural in respect of its connected matters and kinds, which are many. As for whoever made it singular, it is because it is a generic noun. Some read «أَصرهم» with fatḥa on the hamza, and some «أُصْرهم» with ḍamma. The explanation of this root was given earlier near the end of al-Baqara.
And «الأغلال» is the plural of ghull, and here it is a figurative likeness for what they were charged with. The explanation of the root was also given earlier in Āl ʿImrān: {وما كان لنبي أن يَغُلَّ}, and likewise the explanation of taʿzīr in al-Māʾida.
The majority read {وعزَّروه} with shadda. Al-Jaḥdarī, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Sulaymān al-Taymī read it without shadda, and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad read «وعَزَّزوه» with two dotted zāys.
