His saying: {أُنزِلَ مَعَهُ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of «أُنْزِلَ معه», when it was sent down only with Jibrīl? I say: its meaning is: it was sent down along with his prophethood, because his being made a prophet was accompanied by the Qurʾān and coupled with it.
It is permissible that it be attached to «اتَّبعوا», that is: 'and follow the Qurʾān sent down, along with following the Prophet, and acting by his sunna and by what he commanded and forbade; or follow the Qurʾān as he followed it, accompanying him in following it.'" By this last view he means that it is a ḥāl from the agent of «اتبعوا». / And it was said: «مع» has the meaning of «على», that is: "was sent down upon him." The Shaykh allowed that «معه» be an adverbial in the position of ḥāl. He said: "And the governor of it is omitted, its implied form being: 'it was sent down, being with him'; and it is an anticipated ḥāl, like their saying: 'I passed by a man with a falcon with him, hunting with it tomorrow'; so at the time of sending down it was not with him, but it became with him afterwards, just as the hunting did not exist at the time of passing."

semin-durr:158-158.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلَيْكُمْ}: attached to «رسول», and «جميعاً» is a ḥāl from the noun governed by «إلى».
His saying: {الذي لَهُ مُلْكُ}: nominative, accusative and genitive are all permissible in it. The nominative and accusative are by qaṭʿ (cutting off), which has been mentioned more than once. The genitive is in two ways: either as an adjective of the Majestic Name, or as a badal (substitute) from it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is permissible that it be genitive as a description, even though a separation intervenes between the adjective and the qualified noun, namely His saying «إليكم جميعاً»." Abū l-Baqāʾ judged this weak, together with the badal view, and said: "It is remote that it be an adjective of Allah or a substitute for it, because of the separation between them by «إليكم» and by a ḥāl, which is attached to «رسول»."
His saying: {لا إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}: this clause has no grammatical position, since it is a badal of the ṣila (relative clause) before it, and it clarifies it, because whoever owns the world is the God in reality. Likewise His saying «يحيي ويميت» is a clarification of {لا إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}; it was brought to explain His exclusive claim to divinity, because none but He is able to give life and cause death. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh said: "The substitution of clauses for clauses that do not share a governor is something we do not know." Al-Ḥawfī said: "«يحيي ويميت» is in the position of the khabar of «لا إله»." He said: "because «إله» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «إلا هو» is a badal upon the position." He said: "and the clause is also in the position of ḥāl from the name of Allah." I say: by "the clause" he means His saying {لا إله إِلاَّ هُوَ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ}, and by "the name of Allah" he means the pronoun in «له مُلْك», that is: "the dominion is established for Him while He is alone in divinity." The Shaykh said: "The better is that these be independent clauses as regards i'rab, even if some of them are connected to others in meaning." And of the earlier i'rab of al-Ḥawfī he said: "it is forced," and it is as he said.
Mujāhid and ʿĪsā read «وكلمة» in the singular, and the genus is intended by it, as in the saying: "The truest word (kalima) a poet ever uttered is the word of Labīd," and they call the entire ode a "word"; the explanation of this has already been given to you.
His saying: {فَآمِنُواْ بالله وَرَسُولِهِ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said: 'so believe in Allah and in me' after His saying {إِنِّي رَسُولُ الله إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعاً}? I say: it turned from the pronoun to the overt noun so that the attributes which are applied to him may be applied to him, and for the eloquence in the way of iltifāt (shift of person), and to make known that the one in whom belief and whom following are obligatory is this independent person, the unlettered Prophet who believes in Allah and His words, whoever he may be — I or another — as a show of fairness and avoidance of partisanship for himself."

semin-durr:37-37.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنَ الكتاب}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نصيبهم», i.e., "while being established from the Book"; and «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the limit.
His saying: {حتى إِذَا}: «حتى» here is a terminal particle (ghāya), and «إذا» and what lies within its scope — discussion of them has preceded for you more than once: is it a preposition (jārra) or a particle of commencement (ibtidāʾ)? Al-Zamakhsharī's wording about it has also preceded. They differed about it also when it is a particle of commencement: is it then a preposition attached to what precedes it with the attachment of prepositions in meaning, not in wording, with the sentence after it in the position of genitive; or is it not a preposition but only a particle of commencement, not a preposition, though its meaning is the terminal limit, as in his saying:
3190 - I travelled with them until their mounts grew weary ... and until the thoroughbreds were no longer led by halters.
and the saying of another:
2191 - The slain kept spewing out their blood ... in the Tigris, until the water of the Tigris was mixed with red.
There is a disagreement. The first is the view of Ibn Durustawayh, and the second is the view of the majority. The author of «al-Taḥrīr» said: "«حتى» here is not for the terminal limit but is a commencement and its khabar", and this is an error, since the terminal limit is a meaning that does not leave it; and his saying "but it is a mubtadaʾ and a khabar" is a looseness of expression; he means: rather the sentence after it. Then the sentence after it in this place is not a mubtadaʾ and khabar but a verbal sentence, namely «قالوا», and «إذا» is governed by it. Among those who held that it is not here for the terminal limit is al-Wāḥidī, who reported several views on the meaning of the verse and then said: "On this view the meaning of «حتى» is the end and limit, whereas on the first two views «حتى» in this verse is not for the limit but is the one after which sentences occur and the speech after it turns to commencement, like «أمَّا» and «إذا». And there is no attachment of «حتى إذا» to what precedes it; rather this is the commencement of a report, informing about them, as in his saying:
2192 - What a wonder! Even Kulayb insults me ... as if their father were Nahshal or Mujāshiʿ!"
I say: this is not approved of him, for contradicting the majority. And his saying "it has no attachment to what precedes it" is not conceded on all the views he mentioned, and were it not for fear of prolixity I would have set out what he imagined to be preventing what he mentioned, and I would have mentioned the escape from it; the apparent sense is that it is attached only to His saying {يَنَالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُم}.
And His saying: {يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ} is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. «أينما» is written joined, though its right is to be separated, because «ما» is a relative noun, not a redundant one, since the implied form is "Where are those whom you used to call upon?" For that reason {إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ لآتٍ} [al-Anʿām: 134] is written separated and {إِنَّمَا الله} [al-Nisāʾ: 171] joined. And their saying «ضلُّوا» is an answer in meaning, not in wording, because the question was about the place of those whom they used to call upon besides Allah; so had the answer come in line with the question, it would have been said: "They are in such-and-such a place". The meaning is rather: "What has become of your object of worship and those you used to call upon?" So they answered that they were lost to them and absent.
His saying: {وَشَهِدُواْ}: it may be conjoined to «قالوا», which occurred as the answer to the messengers' question, so that it too enters into the answer. It may also be resumptive, cut off from what precedes it, not entering within the scope of the answer. So said the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], and there is something to consider in it, in that he made this sentence an answer by its conjunction to «قالوا», whereas «قالوا» is in reality not the answer; the answer is rather the content of this saying, namely «ضلُّوا عنا». So «ضَلُّوا عنا» is the real answer from which the speech is understood. Its counterpart is that one says: "I asked Zayd what he did, and he said: I fed and I clothed" — the very words "I fed and I clothed" are the answer. Once this is established, he ought to have said that it is conjoined to «ضلوا عنا»; but then, had he said so, it would be problematic from another side, namely that the sentence structure would then have been «ضلُّوا عنا وشهدنا على أنفسنا أنَّا كنَّا» ("they were lost to us and we testified against ourselves that we were"), unless it is said that the second answer is reported according to meaning; that is possible, though very remote.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {في أُمَمٍ}: it is possible that His saying «في أمم» and His saying «في النار» are both attached to «ادخلوا». Then the well-known objection arises: how can two prepositions identical in wording and meaning be attached to one governor? It is answered in one of two ways. Either the first «في» is not for containment (ẓarfiyya) but for accompaniment, as if it were said: "Enter with nations", i.e., accompanying them in entering; and «في» sometimes comes with the meaning of «مع» (with), as in His saying, the Exalted: {وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَن سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ في أَصْحَابِ الجنة} [al-Aḥqāf: 16], and the poet's saying:
2193 - Spirited yet affectionate, in modesty and chastity ... soft in the echo of her voice, sweet of fragrance.
Or [the answer is] that «في النار» is a badal (substitute) for His saying «في أمم», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), as in His saying, the Exalted: {أَصْحَابُ الأخدود، النار} [al-Burūj: 4], for «النارِ» is a substitute for «الأخدود»; likewise «في النار» is a substitute for «أممٍ», with repetition of the governor, as a badal of inclusion; and the containment in the first «في» is figurative, because the nations are not in reality containers for them; the meaning is rather: "Enter among the sum of nations and their throng." It is also possible that «في أمم» be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, i.e., "being among the sum of nations", and «في النار» is attached to «خَلَتْ», i.e., "that preceded you in the Fire".
It is also possible that it be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «أمم», so that «أمم» is qualified by three descriptions: the first, the verbal clause, His saying «قد خَلَتْ»; the second, the preposition and its genitive noun, His saying {مِّن الجن والإنس}; and the third, His saying «في النار». The implied form is: "among nations that passed before you, being of the jinn and mankind, and established in the Fire."
It is also possible that «في النار» be attached to an omitted element otherwise than in the way mentioned, namely as a ḥāl from «أمم»; this is permissible even though it is indefinite, because it has been specified by the two descriptions referred to. It is also possible that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خَلَتْ», since this is the pronoun of the nations. The jinn were put before mankind because they are the origin in misleading.
And His saying «حتى» here is the terminal limit of what precedes it. The meaning is that they enter group after group, each cursing the other, until the end of their overtaking one another in it. The majority read «إذا ادَّاركوا» with the connecting alif and a doubled dāl; the original is «تداركوا», and when its assimilation was desired, what was done to «ادَّارَأْتم» was done to it. Its morphology has been verified in al-Baqara.
Makkī said: "It is not possible to pronounce its pattern with the connecting alif, because you would turn the additional letter into a radical, saying «افَّاعلوا», so the tāʾ of tafāʿala would become the fāʾ of the verb, through its assimilation into the fāʾ of the verb, and that is not permissible; but if you weigh it on the original and say «تَفَاعلوا», it is permissible." I say: this which he mentioned, that its pattern cannot be given except by the original, which is «تفاعلوا», is not conceded. His saying "because you would turn the additional into a radical": we say: that does not follow, because we weigh it by its wording with the hamzat al-waṣl and bring the tāʾ of tafāʿul in its own form, saying: the pattern of «ادَّاركوا» is «اتْفاعَلوا», so the tāʾ is pronounced in consideration of its origin, not of what it became on assimilation.
Grammarians have stated a counterpart of this question: when the tāʾ of ifʿitāl is changed into a letter homogeneous with what precedes it. . . it is changed into ṭāʾ or dāl in such words as «اصطبر» and «اضطرب» and «ازدجر» and «ادَّكر»; when what it is in is weighed, they said: the original tāʾ of ifʿitāl is pronounced in the weighing, not what it became of ṭāʾ or dāl; so one says that the pattern of «اصطبر» is «افتعل» not «افطعل», and the pattern of «ازدَجَر» is «افتعل» not «افدعل». Likewise you say here that the pattern of «ادَّاركوا» is «اتْفاعلوا» not «افَّاعلوا», so there is no difference between the tāʾ of ifʿitāl and of tafāʿul in that.
Ibn Masʿūd and al-Aʿmash read, and it was also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr: «تداركوا», which is the origin of the common reading. And Abū ʿAmr read «إذا ادَّاركوا» with a detached (qaṭʿ) hamza in place of the connecting one. Ibn Jinnī said: "This is problematic, and one does not do the like of that extemporaneously; it is as if he paused with the pause of one who disapproves, then began and detached." I say: this is what is to be held about Abū ʿAmr, otherwise how would he read what is established only in poetic necessity in nouns? So said Ibn Jinnī, meaning that detaching the connecting alif in necessity occurs only in nouns.
Ḥumayd read «أُدْرِكوا», with ḍamma on the detached hamza, sukūn on the dāl and kasra on the rāʾ, like «أُخْرِجوا»; he made it passive, meaning "they were made to enter into its depths (darakāt) or its lower levels (adrāk)". Two readings are reported from Mujāhid ibn Jabr: Makkī related from him «ادَّارَكوا» with the connecting alif and fatḥa on the doubled dāl and fatḥa on the rāʾ, whose origin is «ادْتَرَكوا» on the pattern ifʿalū, active, then assimilated as «ادَّان» from «الدَّيْن» was assimilated. Others related from him «أَدْرَكوا» with fatḥa on a detached hamza, sukūn on the dāl and fatḥa on the rāʾ, i.e., "some of them overtook others". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "And it was read «إذا ادَّاركوا» with one silent alif followed by a doubled dāl, which is a combination of two silent letters, and it is permissible in the separate as it is in the joined; some have even said «اثنا عْشر» with the alif retained and the ʿayn silent." I say: by the joined he means such as «الضالِّين» and «جانّ», and the meaning of the separate is that the alif of «إذا» belongs to one word and the second silent letter to another word. And «ادَّاركوا» means "they caught up with one another"; the explanation of this root has preceded.
And {جَمِيعاً} is a ḥāl from the agent of «ادَّاركوا». And «أُخْراهم» and «أُولاهم»: it may be that «أُخرى» is the feminine of afʿal, the one of comparison, and the meaning on this, as al-Zamakhsharī said: "the last of them in rank, namely the followers and the lowly, say to the first of them in rank, namely the masters and the leaders"; it may also be that «أخرى» has the meaning of «آخِرة», the feminine of «آخِر», the opposite of «أوَّل», not the feminine of «آخَر» which is for comparison, as in His saying: {وَلاَ تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أخرى} [Fāṭir: 18].
The difference between «أخرى» meaning «آخِرة» and «أخرى» the feminine of «آخَر» of the pattern afʿal for comparison is that the one for comparison does not indicate the end, just as its masculine does not indicate it, and for that reason its like are conjoined to it within one kind; you say: "I passed by a woman and another and another", as you say "by a man and another and another"; whereas this one indicates the end just as its masculine does, and for that reason its like are not conjoined to it; and because the former gives the sense of «غير» (other than), while this one does not give the sense of «غير».
And the apparent sense in this noble verse is that the two are not for comparison but are as I have mentioned to you.
And His saying: {لأُولاَهُمْ}: the lām is causal, i.e., "on account of"; it cannot be the lām of communication (tablīgh), as in your saying "I said to Zayd: do". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because their address is to Allah, not to them." Al-Zajjāj elaborated on this before him, saying: "The meaning is: the last of them said: 'Our Lord, these misled us', about the first of them", and he mentioned something like it. I say: on this, the second lām in the saying «أُولاهم لأخراهم» may be for communication, because their address is to them, by the evidence of His saying: «فما كان لكم علينا مِنْ فضلٍ، فذوقوا بما كنتم تَكْسِبون».
And His saying «ضِعْفاً»: Abū ʿUbayda said: "Ḍiʿf is the like of a thing once." Al-Azharī said: "What Abū ʿUbayda said is what people use in the figurative sense of their speech, and al-Shāfiʿī said something close to it, saying about a man who bequeathed: 'Give him double (ḍiʿf) what my son receives', 'he is given the like of it twice.'" Al-Azharī said: "In bequests, custom and what people understand among themselves is applied; but as for the Book of Allah, it is clear Arabic, and its interpretation is referred to the language of the Arabs and the basis of their speech, which is the craft of their tongues. And ḍiʿf in the speech of the Arabs is the like and upward; it is not restricted to two likes, rather you say: 'this is its ḍiʿf', i.e., twice it and three times it, because ḍiʿf originally is an unlimited increase. Do you not see the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {فأولئك لَهُمْ جَزَآءُ الضعف} [Saba': 37]? He did not mean by it one like or two likes, and the most fitting thing is to make it ten times, as in His saying, the Exalted: 'Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like of it'. So the least of ḍiʿf is limited, namely the like, and its most is unlimited." Al-Zajjāj said the like of this statement too, for he said: "i.e., a doubled punishment, because ḍiʿf in the speech of the Arabs is of two kinds: one, the like; the other, that it be in the sense of multiplication of a thing", i.e., increasing it to what has no end. Part of this has preceded in al-Baqara.
And «ضِعْفاً» is an adjective of «عذاباً». And «من النار» may be an adjective of «عذاباً» and may be an adjective of «ضِعْفاً»; and it is possible that «ضعفاً» is a badal of «عذاباً».
And His saying «لكلٍّ» i.e., for each group of the last and the first. And His saying: «ولكن لا تعلمون»: the common reading has the tāʾ of address, either addressing the questioners, or addressing the people of the world, i.e., "but you do not know what has been prepared of punishment for each group". Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read it in the third person, and it may be that the pronoun refers to the group asking for a doubling of punishment, or to both groups, i.e., "they do not know the measure of what has been prepared for them of punishment."

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَمَا}: this fāʾ conjoins this negated sentence to the saying of Allah, the Exalted, to the lowly: «لكلٍ ضعف». So "it is established that you have no superiority over us, and that we are equal in deserving the double; so taste". The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said, after reporting some of al-Zamakhsharī's words: "What appears is that the meaning is the negation of there being any superiority over them from the lowly in the world on account of their following them and agreeing with them in disbelief, i.e., your following us and your not following us are the same, because you were in the world, in our view, too little for you to have any superiority over us by your following, rather you disbelieved by choice, not that we forced you to disbelief; and that His saying «فما كان» is a sentence conjoined to an omitted sentence after the saying, which the preceding speech indicates, the implied form being: 'The first of them said to the last of them: your calling upon Allah that we misled you, and your asking what you asked is of no use; so you had no superiority over us through your misguidance'; and that His saying «فذوقوا» is from the speech of the first, addressing the last by way of gloating, and that the tasting of punishment is because of what you earned, not because we misled you. It was also said: «فذوقوا» is from Allah's address to them."
And «بما»: the bāʾ is causal, and «ما» is a maṣdar particle or has the meaning of «الذي», with the pronoun omitted, i.e., "which you earn (taksibūnahu)".

semin-durr:131-131.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَإِذَا جَآءَتْهُمُ الحسنة}: In the case of the good, He used «إذا», which is for what is certain. The good (الحسنة) was made definite because of the breadth of Allah the Exalted's mercy and because it is a beloved matter that everyone wishes for; and in the case of the evil He used «إنْ», which is for what is doubtful, and the evil (سيئة) was made indefinite because it is a matter that everyone guards against. al-Zamakhsharī made that clear, saying: "If you ask: how is it that {فَإِذَا جَآءَتْهُمُ الحسنة} is said with «إذا» and with الحسنة definite, and {وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ} with «إن» and سيئة indefinite? I say: because the genus of its occurrence is like something obligatory and extensive, whereas evil occurs only rarely and only something of it occurs." End of quotation. This is among the beauties of the science of rhetoric (ʿilm al-bayān).

His saying: {يَطَّيَّرُواْ}: the original is يتطيَّروا, and the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ because of their closeness. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «تطيَّروا» with a tāʾ of two dots above, as a past verb; and according to Sībawayh and his followers this is a poetic necessity, since the protasis cannot be imperfect and the apodosis past except by necessity, like the saying:

2270 - مَنْ يَكِدْني بِسَيِّءٍ كنتُ منه ... كالشَّجا بين حَلْقِه والوريد
(Whoever plots against me with evil, I shall be to him like a bone stuck between his throat and his jugular vein.)

and the saying:

2271 - وإن يَرَوا سُبَّة طاروا بها فَرَحاً ... مني وما سمعوا مِنْ صالحٍ دَفَنُوا
(If they see a disgrace in me they fly off with it in joy, and any good they hear of me they bury.)

The disagreement over that has already been given, so it need not be repeated.

التطيُّر is taking an ill omen. Its origin is that wealth was divided and flew (طار) among a people, so that to each one flew his share and what was specific to him; then it came by predominance to be applied to a bad share and portion. They cited the verse of Labīd:

2272 - تطير عَدائِدُ الأشراكِ شَفْعاً ... ووِتْراً والزَّعامةُ للغلام
(The counted shares fly, in pairs and singly, and the leadership goes to the young man.)

الأَشْراك is the plural of شِرْك, meaning share; i.e. the divided wealth flew, in pairs for the male and singly for the female. And الزَّعامة, i.e. leadership, is for the male. So its meaning is "was dispersed, and each person got his share", and it has nothing to do with ill omen; then it came to predominate in what I mentioned to you. The meaning of {طَائِرُهُمْ عِندَ الله} is their lot and what flew to them in the decree and predestination; or their ill omen, i.e. the cause of their ill fortune is with Allah, namely what He sends down upon them.

semin-durr:132-132.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَهْمَا}: «مهما» is a conditional noun that jussively governs two verbs, like «إنْ». This is the view of the majority of the grammarians. It sometimes comes for interrogation, but this is very rare, like his saying:

2273 - مهما لي الليلةَ مهما لِيَهْ ... أَوْدَى بنعلَيَّ وسِرْباليَهْ
(What is the matter with me tonight, what is the matter with me? It has made off with my sandals and my shirt.)

He means: ما لي الليلة ما لي? and the hāʾ is for pausing.

Some grammarians claimed that the jussive-governing one comes as an adverb of time, and he cited:

2274 - وإنك مهما تُعْطِ بطنك سُؤْلَه ... وفَرْجَكَ نالا منتهى الذمِّ أجمعا
(Whenever you give your belly its desire and your private part its desire, they both reach the utmost blame.)

and the saying of another:

2275 - ... عوَّدْتَ قومَك أن كلَّ مُبَرَّرٍ
مهما يُعَوَّدْ شيمةً يَتَعوَّدِ ...
(You have accustomed your people that every pious one, whatever habit he is accustomed to, becomes accustomed to it.)

and the saying of another:

2276 - نُبِّئْتُ أن أبا شُتَيْمٍ يَدَّعي ... مهما يَعِشْ يُسْمِعْ بما لم يُسْمَعِ
(I was told that Abū Shutaym claims that, as long as he lives, he will hear what has not been heard.)

He said: "So مهما here is an adverb of time." The majority hold the opposite. What he cited is open to interpretation; indeed in some of it no meaning of adverbiality is apparent.

al-Zamakhsharī denounced the one who says that, saying: "This word is among the words that are distorted by one who has no hand in the science of Arabic, so he puts them in the wrong place, and thinks «مهما» is in the sense of «متى», and says: مهما جئتني أعطيتك, and this is from his own speech and not from the founder of Arabic; then he goes and explains {مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِ مِن آيَةٍ} in the sense of time, thereby deviating from Allah's verses without realising it; and this and the like of it are what make it necessary to kneel before the one who studies the book of Sībawayh." I say: He (the one who said it) is excused for taking it as time, for that is a weak view that only an isolated group has held, and Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik said: "All the grammarians say that «مهما» and «ما» are like «مَنْ» in the necessity of being devoid of adverbiality, although their use as adverbs is established in the poetry of the eloquent Arabs," and he cited some of the verses above. I say: his saying "all the grammarians" is enough as evidence of the weakness of the view that they are adverbial.

It is a noun, not a particle, as shown by the pronoun returning to it, and a pronoun does not return to a particle, as in His saying {مَهْمَا تَأْتِنَا بِهِ}: the hāʾ in «به» returns to «مهما». al-Suhaylī was isolated in claiming that it sometimes comes as a particle.

The grammarians differed about «مهما»: is it simple or compound? Those who say it is compound differed. Some said: it is compounded of ماما: the conditional «ما» was repeated for emphasis, the succession of two identical forms was felt to be heavy, and the alif of the first «ما» was replaced by a hāʾ. Others said: «ما» was added to the conditional «ما», as it is added to «إنْ» in His saying: {فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم} [al-Baqara: 38], and the said operation was performed because of the resulting heaviness. This is the view of al-Khalīl and his followers among the Basrans. A group said: "It is compounded of مَهْ, which is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) meaning rebuke, and the conditional ما; then the two words were compounded and became one thing." Some said: "There is no compounding here; rather it is as if they said to him: مَهْ, then said: ما تَأْتِنا به". These two possibilities are ascribed to al-Kisāʾī, and it is nothing, because that sometimes occurs where there is no rebuke, and because its being written joined negates each of the two being an independent word.

A group said: it is compounded of مَهْ meaning "desist" and the conditional مَنْ, by the evidence of the poet's verse:

2277 - أماوِيَّ مَهْ مَنْ يَسْتمعْ في صديقه ... أقاويلَ هذا الناسِ ماوِيَّ يندمِ
(O Māwiyya, desist! Whoever listens, regarding his friend, to the tales of these people, O Māwiyya, will regret.)

so the nūn of «مَنْ» was replaced by an alif, as the light nūn is replaced after a fatḥa, and tanwīn by alif. This is nothing; rather «مَهْ» is on its normal sense, from "desist", and then he said: مَنْ يستمع. A group said: "Rather it is compounded of مَنْ and ما, and the nūn of مَنْ was replaced by a hāʾ, as they replaced the alif of the first «ما» by a hāʾ, because of the brotherhood of «مَنْ» and «ما» in things, though they differ in one thing." Makkī mentioned it.

Its position is accusative or nominative. Nominative is as a mubtadaʾ with what follows as the khabar, and in this is the well-known disagreement: is the khabar the protasis verb, the apodosis verb, or both together? Accusative is in two ways: the more evident is by occupation (ishtighāl), the verb being implied after the conditional noun, the implied form being: مهما تُحْضِر تأتِنا به, where «تَأْتِنا» explains «تُحضر» because it is of its meaning. The second: accusative as an adverb according to those who hold that, and the refutation of this view has already been given. The two pronouns in «به» and «بها» return to «مهما»; the first returned to the wording and the second to the meaning, since its meaning is the verse (sign) mentioned. Like it is the saying of Zuhayr:

2278 - ومهما تكنْ عند امرئٍ من خَليقةٍ ... وإن خالها تَخْفَى على الناسِ تُعْلَمِ
(Whatever trait a man has, even if he supposes it hidden from people, will be known.)

and similar to it in that is His saying: {ما نَنْسَخْ من آيةٍ أو نَنْسَأْها نأْتِ بخيرٍ منها أو مثلها} [al-Baqara: 106], where he returned the pronoun to «ما» in the feminine because it is in the sense of the verse (āya).

And His saying: {فَمَا نَحْنُ}: «ما» may be Ḥijāzī or Tamīmī, and the bāʾ (i.e. of «بمؤمنين») is redundant on both views, and the sentence is the apodosis of the condition, so its position is jussive.

semin-durr:196-196.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ الله}: the majority read «وليي» with shaddah, annexed to the first-person yāʾ with fatḥa; this is a clear reading. He annexed the walī (protector) to himself.

Abū ʿAmr, in some of his transmissions, read «إن وليَّ» with a single yāʾ, with shaddah and fatḥa, and there are two derivations of it. The first, Abū ʿAlī said: "The yāʾ of faʿīl is assimilated into the yāʾ of the speaker, and the yāʾ which is the lām of the word is omitted, and the reverse is prevented." The second is that «وليَّ» is its ism (subject of inna) and is an indefinite noun not annexed to the speaker's yāʾ, the original being «إن ولياً الله»: «ولياً» is its ism and «الله» its khabar, and then the tanwīn was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in his saying:

2363 - فالفيته غيرَ مُسْتَعْتِبٍ ... ولا ذاكرَ اللهَ إلا قليلا
(So I found him not one who seeks to please, nor one who remembers Allah, save little.)

and as in the reading of one who read {قُلْ هُوَ الله أَحَدُ الله الصمد} [al-Ikhlāṣ: 1-2]. Nothing remains but predicating a definite noun of an indefinite one, which is attested; the poet said:

2364 - وإنَّ حراماً أن أَسُبَّ مجاشعاً ... بآبائي الشمِّ الكرام الخضارم
(Indeed it is forbidden that I should revile Mujāshiʿ with my proud, noble, generous fathers.)

Al-Jaḥdarī in one report read «إن وليِّ الله» with kasra on a doubled yāʾ. Its origin is that he made the speaker's yāʾ quiescent, so it met the lām of definiteness and was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, the kasra remaining to indicate it, as in «إنَّ غلامِ الرجلُ». In another report he read «إن وليَّ الله» with a doubled yāʾ and the divine name in the genitive, which Abū ʿAmr al-Dānī transmitted from him: he annexed the walī to the divine name. Al-Akhfash and Abū Ḥātim mentioned this reading from him, without mentioning the fatḥa on the yāʾ. People derived it in three ways. The first is the view of al-Akhfash, that «وليّ الله» is its ism and «الذي نزَّل الكتاب» its khabar, what is meant by "the One who sent down the Book" being Jibrīl, as indicated by the saying of the Exalted {نَزَلَ بِهِ الروح الأمين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193] and {قُلْ نَزَّلَهُ رُوحُ القدس} [al-Naḥl: 102]; except that al-Akhfash said, regarding His saying «وهو يتولى الصالحين», that it is of the attributes of Allah definitely and not of the attributes of Jibrīl; and in the necessity of that there is room for objection. The second: that the one described as sending down the Book is Allah the Exalted, and what is meant by the relative noun is the Prophet ﷺ, there being an omitted returning pronoun understood from the meaning; the implied form is: "the walī of Allah is the Prophet upon whom Allah sent down the Book", so «عليه» is omitted, although it does not fulfil the conditions of omission; but it has occurred rarely, as in his saying:

2365 - وإن لساني شُهْدةٌ يُشْتفى بها ... وهُوَّ على مَنْ صَبَّه الله عَلْقَمُ
(My tongue is honey by which one is healed, but to him upon whom Allah has poured it, it is colocynth.)

i.e. «صَبَّه الله عليه». Another said:

2366 - فأصبح من أسماء قيسٍ كقابضٍ ... على الماء لا يدري بما هو قابضُ
(Qays became, with regard to Asmāʾ, like one grasping water, not knowing what he is grasping.)

i.e. «بما هو قابض عليه». Another said:

2367 - لعلَّ الذي أَصْعَدْتِني أن يَرُدَّني ... إلى الأرض إن لم يَقْدِرِ الخيرَ قادرُهْ
(Perhaps the One by whom you raised me up will return me to the earth, if the One able to decree good does not decree it.)

i.e. «أَصْعَدْتني به». Another said:

2368 - ومِنْ حَسَدٍ يجورُ عليَّ قومي ... وأيُّ الدهر ذو لم يحسُدوني
(Out of envy my people wrong me; and in which period of time did they not envy me?)

Another said:

2369 - فقلت لها لا والذي حَجَّ حاتمٌ ... أخونُكِ عهداً إنني غيرُ خَوَّانِ
(I said to her: No, by the One to whom Ḥātim made pilgrimage, I will not betray your covenant; I am no betrayer.)

i.e. «حجَّ إليه». Another said:

2370 - فَأَبْلِغَنَّ خالدَ بنَ عَضْلَةٍ ... والمَرْءُ مَعْنِيٌّ بلومِ مَنْ يثقْ
(So convey to Khālid ibn ʿAḍla … and a man is concerned with blaming the one he trusts.)

i.e. «يثق به». Once it is established that the pronoun is omitted in places like these even where the condition of omission is not fulfilled, this reading has in the stated derivation a precedent. The third: that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: "the walī of Allah is the righteous one", or "whoever is righteous", and it is omitted because His saying «وهو يتولَّى الصالحين» indicates it; and like His saying {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ بالذكر} [i.e. "they are punished"], and like His saying {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ وَيَصُدُّونَ} [al-Ḥajj: 25].

semin-durr:200-200.t: Al-nazgh is the slightest movement that can be; most often it is attributed to Satan because he is the quickest at it. It was also said: al-nazgh is entering into a matter in order to corrupt it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-nazgh and al-nasgh are goading and pricking; and he made the nazgh a nāzigh (a goader), as it was said «جَدَّ جَدُّه»", meaning that by this he intended emphasis.

semin-durr:201-201.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {طَائِفٌ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «طَيْفٌ», and the rest «طائف» on the pattern of fāʿil. As for ṭayf, there are three possibilities. The first is that it is a maṣdar of ṭāfa yaṭīfu, like bāʿa yabīʿu, and Abū ʿUbayda recited:

2371 - أنَّى ألمَّ بك الخيالُ يَطيفُ ... ومَطافُه لك ذُكْرَةٌ وشُعُوفُ
(How did the phantom visit you, wandering, its wandering being for you a remembrance and a passion?)

The second is that it is a lightened form of fayʿil, the origin being ṭayyif with shaddah on the yāʾ, the middle letter of the word being dropped, as they say mayt for mayyit, layn for layyin, hayn for hayyin. Then ṭayyif, which is the origin, may be from ṭāfa yaṭīfu or from ṭāfa yaṭūfu, the origin being ṭaywif, which was inverted and assimilated; this is the view of Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī. The third is that its origin is ṭawf from ṭāfa yaṭūfu, the wāw being turned into yāʾ. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The wāw was turned into yāʾ though quiescent, as it was in ayd, and that is remote." I say: they also said ḥayl for ḥawl, but this is such an irregularity that it cannot be taken as a measure. His saying "though quiescent" does not require preventing its conversion into yāʾ; rather it ought to have been said: "though what precedes it is not kasra'd."

As for ṭāʾif, it is an active participle; it may be from ṭāfa yaṭūfu, so it is like qāʾim and qāʾil, or from ṭāfa yaṭīfu, so it is like bāʾiʿ and māʾil. Some claimed that ṭayf and ṭāʾif have one meaning, and this is ascribed to al-Farrāʾ; so it is possible that he returns ṭāʾif to ṭayf, making both maṣdars (fāʿil has occurred as a maṣdar, as in their saying «أقائماً وقد قعد الناس», "standing, when people have sat?"), or that he returns ṭayf to ṭāʾif, i.e. making it a descriptive noun on the pattern faʿl.

Al-Fārisī said: "Al-ṭayf is like the passing thought (khaṭra), and al-ṭāʾif is like the one who passes (khāṭir)", thus distinguishing between them. Al-Kisāʾī said: "Al-ṭayf is the slight touch (lamam), and al-ṭāʾif is what goes around a person." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "How can this be, when al-Aʿshā said:

2372 - وتُصْبح مِنْ غِبِّ السُّرَى وكأنما ... ألمَّ بها من طائفِ الجنِّ أولقُ
(After the night journey she is, as it were, touched by madness from a visiting jinn?)

and I do not know what his astonishment is." It is as if he took his saying "what goes around a person" as restricted to a person, whereas he (al-Aʿshā) made it go around the she-camel; and this is a slip, since al-Kisāʾī said it incidentally, not as a restriction. Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī said: "Ṭāfa: he approached and withdrew, yaṭūfu ṭawfan and ṭawāfan; aṭāfa: the people encircled from their sides; and ṭāfa l-khayāl: it visited, yaṭīfu ṭayfan." Abū Zayd thus distinguished between the wāw-root and the yāʾ-root, assigning each root a meaning; and he also distinguished between faʿala and afʿala, as you have seen.

Al-Suhaylī claimed that no active participle is used from «طاف الخيال», saying: "because it is an imagination with no reality." He said: "As for His saying, the Exalted {فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ} [al-Qalam: 19], one does not say ṭayf in it because it is truly an active participle." Ḥassān said:

2373 - جِنِّيَّةٌ أرَّقَني طيفُها ... تَذْهَبُ صُبْحاً وتُرى في المنامْ
(A jinn-woman whose phantom kept me sleepless; she goes at morning and is seen in sleep.)

Al-Suddī said: "Al-ṭayf is madness and al-ṭāʾif is anger." From Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him: they have one meaning, which is al-nazgh.

semin-durr:78-78.t:
Al-rajfa is the violent earthquake; one says rajafat al-arḍu tarjufu rajfan, rajīfan and rajafānan. It was also said: al-rajfa is the calamity that shakes a person and unsettles him; hence the sea is called rajjāf for its turbulence. It was also said that its origin is from rajafa bihi l-baʿīr when it moves him in its travel. Ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
2235 - When I saw that the time of Hajj had come ... and the camels of the people in the tribe were shaking (tarjufu).
Al-irjāf is the causing of rajfa; its plural is al-arājīf, and from it: "Rumours are the impregnators of tribulations." His words: {يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الراجفة} [النازعات: 4] are like His words: {إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الأرض زِلْزَالَهَا} [الزلزلة: 1], and from it:
2236 - It revives the shaking bones from decay ... yet for the ailment of the two knees there is no physician.
Al-juthūm is clinging to the ground, from the crouching of a bird or hare, which presses its belly to the ground; from it comes "a man juthama and jaththāma", a figure for the sleepy lazy one; and a person's juthmān is his figure when seated. Abū ʿUbayd said: "Al-juthūm is for people and birds as al-burūk is for camels." He recited from Jarīr:
2237 - I recognized the place and recognized of her ... the cooking-pot's mounts like crouching kites.
Al-Kirmānī said: "Where rajfa is mentioned the dār (home) is in the singular, and where ṣayḥa (cry) is mentioned it is in the plural, because the cry was from heaven, so its reach is greater and more far-reaching than the earthquake; so He mentioned each in the manner most fitting to it." It was said of «دارهم»: i.e. their land. It was also said that the genus is meant. The fāʾ in «فَأَخَذَتْهم» is for immediate sequence. It may be conjoined to the clause «فَأْتِنا», on the supposition that the time of destruction was near the time of the request to bring it. It is also possible to imply something to which the conjunction with fāʾ is valid, the implied form being: "He promised them the punishment after three days, which elapsed, then it seized them."
No attention is paid to what some heretics mentioned about His words {فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ الرَّجْفَةُ} and in another place: {الصيحة} [هود: 67], and in another place {بالطاغية} [الحاقة: 5], believing something impermissible, since there is no contradiction between these: the rajfa follows from the ṣayḥa, because when they were cried at, their hearts shook and they died; so it is permissible to attribute the destruction to each of them. As for «بالطاغية», the bāʾ is causal. Al-ṭāghiya is al-ṭughyān, a maṣdar like al-ʿāqiba; a tyrannical king is also called ṭāghiya; so the meaning of «أُهْلِكوا بالطاغية» is "by their transgression", like His words: {كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْوَاهَآ} [الشمس: 11], i.e. because of their transgression.
His words «فأصبحوا»: it may be the deficient verb (nāqiṣa), with «جاثمين» its khabar and {في ديارهم} attached to it; it is not permissible for the preposition and its genitive noun to be the khabar and «جاثمين» a ḥāl, for lack of benefit in saying "they became in their home", although both views are possible in your saying "Zayd became in the house sitting". It may also be the complete verb (tāmma), i.e. "they entered the morning", with «جاثمين» a ḥāl; the first is more evident.

semin-durr:79-79.t: His words, the Exalted: {وَلَكِن لاَّ تُحِبُّونَ}: it was said that «كان» is omitted here because it is a narration of a past state, i.e. "but you did not love (kuntum lā tuḥibbūn)".

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَلُوطاً}: there are two views. The first: it is accusative by the first «أَرْسَلْنا», and «إذا» is a ẓarf of the sending. The second: it is accusative by an implied "udhkur" (mention). Then, as to the operator in the ẓarf, there are two views. The first, the statement of al-Zamakhsharī: it is a badal from «لوطاً»; he said: "meaning: and mention the time when he said to his people", and this is on granting that «إذ» can be used freely. The second: that the operator in it is implied, its implied form being: "and mention the message of Lūṭ when he said"; so «إذ» is accusative by «رسالة». Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and the badal then is badal ishtimāl.
His words: {مَا سَبَقَكُمْ بِهَا مِنْ أَحَدٍ}: there are two views on this clause. The first: it is resumptive, with no grammatical position. On resumption it may be the answer to a question or not. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the position of this clause? I say: it has no position, because it is resumptive; he first rebuked them with {أَتَأْتُونَ الفاحشة}, then reproached them for it, saying: you are the first to have done it. Or it is the answer to an implied question, as though they said: 'Why should we not do it?' and he said: no one preceded you in it, so do not do what you have not been preceded in."
In the bāʾ of «بها» there are two views. The more evident: it is circumstantial, i.e. "no one preceded you accompanying it, i.e. in connection with it". The second: it is for transitivization. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The bāʾ is for transitivization, from your saying 'sabaqtuhu bi-l-kura' when you hit the ball before him. From it the words of the Prophet, peace be upon him: 'ʿUkkāsha has beaten you to it (sabaqaka bihā).'" The Shaykh said: "Transitivization here is very shaky, because the transitivizing bāʾ in a verb that takes one object consists in making the first object perform that act upon what the bāʾ enters, so it is like the hamza. To illustrate: when you say 'ṣakaktu l-ḥajara bi-l-ḥajar', its meaning is 'aṣkaktu l-ḥajara', i.e. I made the stone strike the stone; likewise 'dafaʿtu Zaydan bi-ʿAmr ʿan Khālid' means 'adfaʿtu Zaydan ʿAmran ʿan Khālid', i.e. I made Zayd repel ʿAmr from Khālid; so the first object has an effect on the second. This meaning is not valid here, since it is not valid to imply 'asbaqtu Zaydan al-kura', i.e. I made Zayd beat the ball, except by a strained figure of speech, which is that you make your hitting of the ball the first making of a blow that preceded it, i.e. came earlier in time, so the two did not coincide." The first «مِنْ» is for emphasizing comprehensiveness, and the second for partition.
The second of the two views on the clause: it is a ḥāl, and for its owner there are two views. The first: it is the fāʿil, i.e. "do you come to it as initiators of it?" The second: it is the object, i.e. "do you come to it as something begun with, not preceded by anyone other than you?"

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أإنكم}: Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim read «إنكم» as a resumptive statement (khabar), which is an explanation of that abomination. The rest read it as a question implying rebuke.
His words: {شَهْوَةً}: there are two views. One: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. "for the sake of desire; nothing impels you to it but mere desire and nothing else". The second: it is a maṣdar occurring in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "desiring", or remaining a maṣdar, with «أتَأْتُون» as its governor, because it means "do you desire?" One says shahiya yashhā shahwatan, and shahā yashhū shahwatan. He said:
2238 - Many a dishevelled one who desires sleep, I said to him "Depart," ... when the stars were turning aside and stretching out.
That was discussed in Āl ʿImrān.
His words: {مِّن دُونِ النسآء}: three views. One: it is attached to an omitted word because it is a ḥāl from «الرجال», i.e. "do you come to them apart from women?" The second: it is attached to «شهوة», as al-Ḥawfī said. It is not evident, since you would say "I desired from such", except in a sense not fitting here. The third: it is a ṣifa of «شهوة», i.e. "a desire that is apart from them".
His words: {بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ}: «بل» is for turning away (iḍrāb), and the well-known view is that it is a turning from story to story to story; it was said: from something mentioned, namely the report of their exceeding the limit in this abomination, or from rebuking them, making them confess, and denouncing them. It was also said: «بل» is a turning away from something omitted. There is disagreement about it: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "its implied form is: 'You have not been just; rather you are'". Al-Kirmānī said: «بل» is a rejection of an answer they claimed would be an excuse for them, i.e. "you have no excuse; rather".
The active participle «مُسْرفون» came here as the description of the people, because it is more indicative of permanence and for conformity with the verse endings, which are nouns. In al-Naml, «تَجْهَلُون» came, indicating that their ignorance renews at every time and for conformity with the verse endings, which are verbs.

semin-durr:82-82.t: His words, the Exalted: {وَمَا كَانَ جَوَابَ}: the majority read «جواب» accusative as the khabar of kāna, with the ism being «أنْ» and what is in its scope, which is the most eloquent, since it makes the more definite the ism. Al-Ḥasan read «جوابُ» nominative, it being its ism, with the khabar «إلا أَنْ قالوا»; that has been discussed. He brought «وما» here, and in al-Naml and al-ʿAnkabūt «فما»; the fāʾ is the original in this chapter because what is meant is that their answer was not delayed after his counsel. As for the wāw, immediate sequence is one of its senses, so here it is determined to be for immediate sequence on account of an external matter, and the Arabic form in the two mentioned sūras is that they required that by their placement.

semin-durr:83-83.t:
His words, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ امرأته}: an exception from «his family» who were saved. His words: {كَانَتْ مِنَ الغابرين} are the answer to an implied question. This is as discussed in al-Baqara and at the beginning of this sūra in the story of Iblīs.
Al-ghābir means the one who stays. This is the well-known usage in the language, and they recited the words of Abū Dhuʾayb al-Hudhalī:
2239 - So I stayed (ghabartu) after them in a wearisome life, ... and I think that I am to follow, to be pursued.
From it are ghubbar al-laban, for what remains of it in the udder, and ghubbar al-ḥayḍ too. Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī said, and it is also attributed to Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
2240 - Free of every remnant of menses, ... and of the corruption of a nursing woman and of baffling disease.
The meaning of «من الغابرين» in the verse is: of those who remain in destruction. Some said: "ghabara means passed and went", and the meaning of the verse supports it, and he recited from al-Aʿshā:
2241 - He bit with what the razors left him ... of his mother in the bygone (al-ghābir) time.
i.e. the past time. Some said: ghabara means ghāba (was absent), from which their saying: "He was absent from us for a time." Abū ʿUbayda said: "Ghabara: he lived a long period until he grew old", and it is indicated by: {إِلاَّ عَجُوزاً فِي الغابرين} [الصافات: 135]. The upshot is that ghubūr is either a homonym like ʿasʿasa, or literal and figurative, and that is the preferred view. Al-ghubār is what remains of raised-up dust. From it {وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ} [عبس: 40], as an image of their change and darkening. Al-ghabrāʾ is the earth. Ṭarafa said:
2242 - I saw the sons of the dust-coloured earth, they do not disown me, ... nor the people of that extended tent.

semin-durr:84-84.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَأَمْطَرْنَا}: Abū ʿUbayd said: "One says muṭira for mercy and umṭira for punishment." Abū l-Qāsim al-Rāghib said: "One says muṭira for good and umṭira for punishment; the Exalted said: {وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ حِجَارَةً} [الحجر: 74]." This is refuted by His words, the Exalted: {هذا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا} [الأحقاف: 24], for they meant mercy by that, and it is from the quadriliteral amṭara. Maṭara and amṭara have one meaning and take one object; one says maṭaratthum al-samāʾ and amṭaratthum. His words, the Exalted, here «وأَمْطَرْنا» are made to imply the sense of "we sent" (arsalnā), and therefore it is transitivized with «على»; on this «مَطَراً» is the direct object, because stones are meant by it and the maṣdar is not meant at all, since if it were, it would be said "amṭār". A "rainy day" (yawm maṭīr) means a rained-upon day. Yawm māṭir and mumṭir are figurative, like His words: {فِي يَوْمٍ عَاصِفٍ} [إبراهيم: 18]; and a wādin maṭīr only, with no figurative use. Maṭīr means mumṭir. He said:
2243 - O dove of the belly of the two valleys, sing, ... may the morning bright clouds' rain water you.
Faʿīl here is in the sense of fāʿil, because the cloud rains on other than her. He made «مطراً» indefinite to express magnitude.

semin-durr:85-85.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وإلى مَدْيَنَ}: There is disagreement about Madyan. It was said: it is non-Arabic, so treating it as diptote is for non-Arabic origin and being a proper name; he is Madyan ibn Khalīl al-Raḥmān (the Friend of the Merciful), and the tribe was named after him. It was said: it is Arabic, the name of a town; al-Farrāʾ said this and recited:
2244 - The monks of Madyan, and those whom I knew, ... weep, sitting, from fear of the punishment.
If they heard her words as I heard them, ... they would fall down for ʿAzza, bowing and prostrating.
So treating it as diptote is for being a proper name and feminine, and an omitted muḍāf is then necessary, i.e. "to the people of Madyan"; therefore he returned the pronoun in «أخاهم» to the people. It is also possible that the place is meant with its inhabitants, so that was taken into account in regard to the pronoun returning to it. On the supposition that it is Arabic, they said: it is irregular (shādhdh), since it should by right have the weak-letter change, like matāʿ and maqām, but they deviated in it as they deviated in Maryam and makwaza. It is not irregular to al-Mubarrad, because it does not follow the verb; this is right, even though the majority hold otherwise.
Shuʿayb: it may be the diminutive of shiʿb or shaʿb, so they said; but the proper manners are not to say that; rather this was placed on this pattern. As for the names of the prophets, no diminutive enters them at all, except what the Quran has pronounced in a form resembling it, such as Shuʿayb, peace be upon him, who is Arab, not non-Arab.
His words: {وَلاَ تَبْخَسُواْ}: the meaning of this word was discussed earlier in His words: {وَلاَ يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً} [البقرة: 282]. It takes two objects, namely the people and their things, i.e. "do not diminish for them their things".

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His words, the Exalted: {بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ}: the bāʾ may remain in its sense of attachment or accompaniment, or it may mean "in" (fī). «تُوْعِدون», «تَصُدُّون» and «تبغون»: these clauses are ḥāls, i.e. "do not sit threatening, barring and seeking". The thing threatened with was not mentioned so that the mind may go every way. The object of «تصدُّون» is «مَنْ آمن». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: «مَنْ آمن» is the object of «تصدُّون», not of «توعدون», since if it were the object of the first, he would have said «تَصُدُّونهم». He means that if it were so, the matter would be one of tanāzuʿ, and if it were tanāzuʿ and you made the first operative you would place a pronoun in the second and say «تَصُدُّونهم»; but the Quran is not so, which shows that «توعدون» is not operative on it. His statement admits that it is a case of tanāzuʿ with the second operative, which is the choice of the Basrans, and that it is omitted from the first, or that it is not, which is the evident view.
The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's statement is that it is tanāzuʿ with the first operative, for he said: "If you ask: to what does the pronoun in «مَنْ آمن به» return? I say: to «كل صراط», its implied form being: 'you threaten whoever believes in it and you bar from it', so he placed the overt, 'the path of Allah', in the place of the pronoun, to increase the ugliness of their conduct."
The Shaykh said: "This is arbitrary and forced, with no need for fronting, delaying and placing the overt in the place of the pronoun, since the original is contrary to all that, and no necessity calls for it; also it is a case of the first being operative, which is the weaker school; and had it been the first being operative, a pronoun would have been obligatory in the second, and omitting it is not permitted except in poetic necessity according to some, such as his saying:
2245 - At ʿUkāẓ it dazzles the onlookers ... when they glance, its radiance
He made «يُعْشي» operative and made «شعاعُه» nominative by it, and omitted the pronoun from «لمحوا», its implied form being «لمحوه». Some allowed it, rarely, outside poetry. The pronoun in «به» is either for «كل صراط», as was reported before from Abū l-Qāsim, or for Allah because it is known, or for the path of Allah, and that is permissible because it is both masculine and feminine; on this he combined both usages here, saying «به» masculine and «وتَبْغُونها عِوَجاً» feminine; similar is {قُلْ هذه سبيلي} [يوسف: 108]. The like of «تَبْغونها عِوَجاً» has been discussed in Āl ʿImrān, which spares repeating it."
His words: {واذكروا}: either its object is omitted, in which case this ẓarf is governed by that object, i.e. "remember His favour upon you at that time", or the ẓarf itself is made the direct object. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The hāʾ in «به» may return to Shuʿayb, according to one who holds that sitting on the roads was to turn people away from Shuʿayb." This is remote, because the one saying «ولا تَقْعدوا» is Shuʿayb, and the construction would then have been «مَنْ آمن بي»; and the claim that it is a case of iltifāt is very remote, since it is not good to say: "O you, I tell you: do not humiliate whom he honoured", i.e. whom I honoured.
His words «كيف» and what is within its scope: it suspends the looking from operating, so it and what follows are in the position of accusative on the dropping of the preposition. Looking here is reflection. «كيف» is the khabar of kāna, obligatorily fronted.

semin-durr:40-40.t:
Abū ʿAmr read {لا تُفْتَح} with ḍamma on the tāʾ of two dots from above and without doubling; the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with the yāʾ from below and without doubling; and the rest with the feminine and the doubling. The feminine and the masculine are by considering plural and collective; the lightening and the doubling are by considering intensification or its absence, and the doubling here is clearer because of the multiplicity of what is connected with it. In these readings it is passive. Abū Ḥaywa and Abū l-Burhasam read «تَفَتَّح» with fatḥa on the tāʾ from above and doubling; the original is «لا تتفتَّح» with two tāʾs, one of which was omitted, as has preceded in «تذكَّرون» and the like. So «أبواب» on the reading of Abū Ḥaywa is an agent, and on what preceded it is a deputy agent (mafʿūl lam yusamma fāʿiluhu). It was also read «لا تَفْتَحُ» with the tāʾ and the accusative of «الأبواب», on the basis that the verb belongs to the signs (āyāt), and with the yāʾ on the basis that the verb belongs to Allah; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it.
And His saying {فِي سَمِّ الخياط} is attached to «يَلِجُ». «Samm al-khiyāṭ» is the eye of the needle, which is the khurt; its sīn takes three vowels, and every narrow hole is a samm. It was also said: every hole in the body; and it was said: every hole in a nose or an ear is a samm, and its plural is sumūm. Al-Farazdaq said:
2194 - So I relieved its two holes until it breathed ... and I said to it: fear nothing behind me.
And «al-summ» is the deadly poison; it is so called for its subtlety and its effect on the pores of the body until it reaches the heart. It is originally a maṣdar, then the sense of the agent was intended by it, because it enters the interior of the body; one says «sammahu» when he put it into it. From it comes «al-sāmma» for the elite who enter into the interiors of matters and their pores, and for that reason they are called «al-dukhlul». And «al-samūm» is the hot wind, because it has an effect like the deadly poison. And «al-khiyāṭ» and «al-mikhyaṭ» are the tool with which one sews, on the patterns fiʿāl and mifʿal, like izār and mizar, and liḥāf and milḥaf, and qināʿ and miqnaʿ. And a camel is not called jamal unless it has reached bāzil age. It was also said: it is not called that unless it has reached four years. And the first that comes out of the she-camel's young, when its maleness or femaleness is not yet known, is called salīl; if it is male it is saqb, and the female is ḥāʾil; then it is ḥuwār until weaning, and after that faṣīl until a year; in the second year ibn makhāḍ and bint makhāḍ; in the third ibn labūn and bint labūn; in the fourth ḥiqq and ḥiqqa; in the fifth jadhaʿ and jadhaʿa; in the sixth thaniyy and thaniyya; in the seventh rabāʿ and rabāʿiya, lightened; in the eighth sadīs for both, and it was said sadīsa for the female; in the ninth bāzil and bāzila; in the tenth mukhlif and mukhlifa. There is no age after buzūl and ikhlāf, but one says "bāzil of a year or two years" and "mukhlif of a year or two years" until it grows decrepit and is called fawd.
And «al-wulūj» is entering with intensity, and for that reason it is said: it is entering a narrow place, so it is more specific than entering. And «al-walīja» is everything on which a person relies; and «al-walīja» is also one who enters among a people who are not of them.
And «الجَمَل» is the common reading, and it is a simile of the utmost beauty, because the camel is the greatest animal in the Arabs' view and the largest in body, so that he said:
2195 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... the bodies of camels and the minds of sparrows
and his saying:
2196 - The camel has grown big without intellect ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
And the eye of the needle is the utmost in narrowness. So since the proverb is struck with the hugeness and bigness of this and the narrowness of that, until it was said "narrower than the eye of a needle" (and from it comes «al-khirrīt», the one skilled in narrow roads), it is as if it were said: they will not enter Paradise until the greatest and largest of things in the Arabs' view plunges into the narrowest and smallest of things; as if it were said: "they will not enter until this impossible is found". Similar in meaning is the saying of another:
2197 - When the raven turns grey I will come to my family ... and pitch will become like fresh milk.
Ibn ʿAbbās in the narration of Ibn Ḥawshab, and Mujāhid, Ibn Yaʿmar, Abū Mijlaz, al-Shaʿbī, Mālik ibn al-Shikhkhīr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Abū Rajāʾ, Abū Razīn and Abān from ʿĀṣim read «الجُمَّل» with ḍamma on the jīm and doubled fatḥa on the mīm, which is the qals. The qals is a thick rope assembled from many ropes and twisted; it is the ship's rope; and it was said: the rope by which a palm tree is climbed. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: "Allah is finer in simile than to liken to the camel", as if he thought, if it is authentic from him, that what is fitting for the eye of the needle is something that suits the thread passed through it. Al-Kisāʾī said: "The one who narrated that from Ibn ʿAbbās was a non-Arab, so he doubled the mīm." Ibn ʿAṭiyya weakened al-Kisāʾī's statement because of the many who narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbās as a reading. I say: likewise it is a reading well known among people. Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās ḍamma on the jīm and a light fatḥa on the mīm, and that is the reading of Ibn Jubayr, Qatāda and Sālim al-Afṭas.
Ibn ʿAbbās also read, in the narration of ʿAṭāʾ: «الجُمُل» with ḍamma on the jīm and the mīm, light, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Ḥajdarī read it so. ʿIkrima and Ibn Jubayr read it with ḍamma on the jīm and sukūn on the mīm; al-Mutawakkil and Abū l-Jawzāʾ with fatḥa and sukūn; and all are dialectal forms of the qals mentioned. Ibn Masʿūd was asked about the camel (jamal) in the verse, and he said: "the mate of the she-camel", as if he understood what the questioner meant and thought him stupid. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd], Qatāda, Abū Razīn and Ṭalḥa read «سُمّ» with ḍamma on the sīn; Abū ʿImrān al-Ḥūfī, Abū Nahīk and al-Aṣmaʿī from Nāfiʿ read «سِمّ» with kasra. It has already preceded that these are dialectal forms. ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Razīn and Abū Mijlaz read «المِخْيَط» with kasra on the mīm, sukūn on the khāʾ and fatḥa on the yāʾ; Ṭalḥa with fatḥa on the mīm. This is contrary to the written copy (al-sawād).
His saying: {وكذلك}: i.e., "and like that recompense We recompense the criminals"; so the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {لَهُمْ مِّن جَهَنَّمَ مِهَادٌ}: The sentence may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) or resumptive. It is then possible for «مهاد» to be an agent of «لهم», so that the ḥāl is of the class of single words; and it may be a mubtadaʾ, so that it is of the class of sentences. And «من جهنم» is a ḥāl from «مِهاد», for if it had come after it, it would have been an adjective; or it is attached to what the preceding preposition and its genitive noun are attached to.
And «غَواشٍ» is the plural of «غاشية». The grammarians differ concerning a plural on the pattern mafāʿil when it is defective (manqūṣ) by rule: is it declinable or diptote? Some said: it is declinable, because the pattern of the ultimate plural has disappeared from it, so its pattern became the pattern of janāḥ and qadhāl, so it is declined. The majority said: it is a diptote, and the tanwīn is a compensatory tanwīn. They differed about what is compensated for: the majority hold that it is a compensation for the omitted yāʾ; al-Mubarrad held that it is a compensation for its vowel. And the kasra is not a kasra of declension; so too «جَوارٍ» and «مَوالٍ». Some put it in the genitive with fatḥa, saying:
2198 - Had ʿAbd Allāh been a client I would have satirized him ... but ʿAbd Allāh is the client of clients.
and another said:
2199 - She marvelled at me and at Yuʿaylī ... when she saw me worn and lying on my back.
This ruling is not specific to the pattern mafāʿil, rather every diptote, when it is defective, has the ruling mentioned, such as «يُعَيْلٍ», the diminutive of «يَعْلى», and «يَرْمٍ», the name of a man, and on this basis is his saying «ومن يُعَيْلِيا». Some of the Arabs decline «غواشٍ» and the like with the vowels on the letter before the omitted yāʾ, saying: "These are jawārun". It was read {وَمن فوقهم غواشٌ} with ḍamma on the shīn, which is like the reading of ʿAbd Allāh {وله الجوارُ} [al-Raḥmān: 24] with ḍamma on the rāʾ. I have treated this question and the schools and dialects in it in a place other than this.
His saying: {وكذلك}: its like has preceded. And His saying {الظالمين} may be a case of the overt noun being put in the place of the pronoun, the wrongdoers meant being the criminals; it may also be that they are others, and that they are recompensed like their recompense.

semin-durr:133-133.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الطوفان}: There are two views about it. One: that it is the plural of طُوْفانة, i.e. it is a generic noun, like قمح and قمحة, شعير and شعيرة. It is also said that it is a maṣdar, like النُّقْصان and الرُّجْحان, and this is the view of al-Mubarrad among others. The first is the view of al-Akhfash, who said: "It is فُعْلان from الطَّواف (going round), because it goes round until it covers all, and its singular by analogy is طُوْفانة." He cited:

2279 - غَيَّرَ الجِدَّةَ من آياتها ... خُرُقُ الريحِ وطوفانُ المَطَرْ
(What has changed the freshness of its traces is the violence of the wind and the flood of rain.)

الطُّوفان is abundant water; so said al-Layth, and he cited for al-ʿAjjāj:

2280 - وعَمَّ طُوفانُ الظلامِ الأَثْأَبا ...
(And the flood of darkness covered the athʾab trees.)

He likened the darkness of the night to water that overspreads places. And Abū l-Najm said:

2281 - ومَدَّ طوفانٌ مبيدٌ مَدَدا ... شهراً شآبيبَ وشهراً بَرَدا
(And a destroying flood extended its extent, a month of downpours and a month of hail.)

It is also said: الطُّوفان is, of anything, whatever is abundant, encompassing and enveloping a group from every side, such as abundant water, widespread killing and sweeping death; so said Abū Isḥāq. The Prophet ﷺ has explained it sometimes as death and sometimes as a command from Allah, and he recited His saying, the Exalted: {فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ} [al-Qalam: 19]. Although this root has been treated under «طائفة», this form has a specificity for these meanings mentioned.

His saying: {والجراد}: the plural of جَرادة; the male and female are the same in it. One says جرادة ذََكَرٌ and جرادة أنثى, like نملة and حمامة. The lexicographers said: it is derived from الجَرْد (stripping); they said that derivation among generic nouns is very rare. One says أرض جَرْداء, i.e. smooth, and ثوب جَرْد when its nap is gone.

His saying: {والقمل}: it is said that it is ticks (القِرْدان); and it is said: creatures resembling them but smaller; and it is said: the weevil that comes out of wheat; and it is said: a kind of locust smaller than it; and it is said: الحِمْنان, singular حِمْنانة, a kind of tick; and it is said: it is the well-known lice (القُمَّل) found on a person's body and clothes. The reading of al-Ḥasan «والقَمْل» with fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the mīm supports this, so there are two dialects: القُمَّل as in the reading of the majority and القَمْل as in the reading of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. It is also said: القمل are fleas; and it is said: dung beetles (الجِعلان).

His saying: {والضفادع}: the plural of ضِفْدَع, on the pattern of دِرْهم, and a kasra on its dāl is also permitted, making it on the pattern of زِبْرِج; and the ʿayn of its plural is sometimes replaced by yāʾ, as in the verse:

2282 - ومَنْهَلٍ ليس له حَوازِق ... ولِضفادي جَمِّه نقانِقُ
(Many a watering place with no [ḥawāziq], and in its abundant water the frogs croak.)

Its plural as ضِفْدَعان is also irregular. الضِّفدع is feminine and not masculine. On this, the masculine and feminine are distinguished by an adjective: one says ضفدع ذَكَر and ضفدع أنثى, as we said of what is marked by the feminine tāʾ, such as حمامة, جرادة and نملة.

His saying: {آيَاتٍ} is accusative as a ḥāl from those things mentioned earlier, i.e. "We sent upon them these things while they were signs, each distinguished from the others."

semin-durr:134-134.t: His saying, the Exalted: {بِمَا عَهِدَ}: Two views are possible for this bāʾ. One, which is the apparent: that it is attached to ادْعُ, i.e. "call upon Him with the supplication which He taught you to call upon Him with". The second: that it is the bāʾ of oath. al-Zamakhsharī mentioned these two views, saying: "The bāʾ is either attached to «ادْعُ», in two ways: one, 'Help us to what we ask of you in the way of supplication for us, by virtue of the covenant of Allah that you have and His honouring of you with prophethood'; or, 'Call upon Allah for us, seeking nearness to Him by His covenant with you'; or it is an oath answered by «لنؤمِنَنَّ», i.e. 'we swear by Allah's covenant with you'."

semin-durr:135-135.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إلى أَجَلٍ}: There are two views about it. One: that it is attached to كَشَفْنا, and this is the well-known one among the grammarians. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) found a difficulty with it, namely that what «لمَّا» enters upon has its apodosis arranged on the beginning of its occurrence, and a limit (ghāya) conflicts with being linked to the beginning of occurrence; so the beginning and the continuation must both be conceived until the limit is realised. For this reason a limit does not occur with a verb that is not prolonged; one does not say: «لَمَّا قتلت زيداً إلى يوم الخميس جَرَى كذا» ("when I killed Zayd until Thursday, such-and-such happened"), nor «لَمَّا وثبتُ إلى يوم الجمعة اتفق كذا» ("when I leapt until Friday, such-and-such occurred"). This is his statement, and it is good. It may be answered that what is meant by the term (أجل) here is the time of their belief and their sending the Children of Israel with him, and what is meant by the removal is the continued lifting of the plague, as if it were said: "when it went on, We removed it from them until a term". As for whoever explained the term as death or drowning, he needs an omitted muḍāf, the implied form being: "when We removed the plague from them until near a term which they were to reach", and he needed that because between their death or drowning, a breaking of the covenant occurred on their part, so how could the breach be imagined to be from them after their death or drowning?

The second: that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl from «الرِّجز», i.e. "when We removed from them the plague, being until a term". The meaning is that the punishment was deferred. The Shaykh said: "What strengthens this interpretation is that the apodosis of «لمَّا» came with the sudden «إذا», i.e. 'when We removed from them the punishment appointed for them until a term, they suddenly broke it'; and on the meaning of setting the removal a limit by the reached term, suddenness is not possible except on the interpretation of the removal as a continued limited one, so suddenness in the breach is then possible." End of quotation.

His saying: {هُم بَالِغُوهُ} is in the position of genitive as an adjective of أَجَل. Describing with this sentence is more eloquent than describing with a single word, because of the repetition of the pronoun, which signals magnification.

And His saying: {إِذَا هُمْ يَنكُثُونَ}: this is the sudden «إذا», which has been discussed shortly before; «هم» is the mubtadaʾ and «ينكثون» its khabar, and «إذا» is the apodosis of «لَمَّا», as above, by the interpretation mentioned. al-Zamakhsharī said: "«إذا هم ينكُثون» is the apodosis of «لَمَّا», meaning: when We removed the punishment from them, they suddenly broke it and hastened to it and did not delay it, but when He removed it from them, they broke it." The Shaykh said: "No; a limit is not possible with the apparent form of this implied meaning." End of quotation. He means that the removal must be interpreted as continuing, as above, for that to be sound. This verse refutes the doctrine of whoever claims that «لَمَّا» is an adverb, since then it would need an operator, and what follows «إذا» does not operate on what precedes it. This has been treated carefully in its place.

Abū Ḥaywa and Abū Hāshim read «تنكِثون» with kasra on the kāf, and the majority with ḍamma; they are two dialects in the imperfect. النَّكْثُ is breaking; its origin is from unravelling spun wool so that it may be spun a second time, and that unravelled stuff is called نِكْثٌ, like ذِبْح and رِعْي, and the plural is أَنْكاث. It was borrowed for breaking a covenant after it was made firm and strong, as with the threads of cloaks when they are unravelled after having been twisted tight; and this is among the finest metaphors.

semin-durr:136-136.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فانتقمنا}: this fāʾ is causal, i.e. vengeance resulted from the breach. Then, if what is meant by vengeance is the drowning itself, the second fāʾ is explicative, according to whoever establishes that for it; otherwise the implied form is: "we intended vengeance".

His saying: {فِي اليم} is attached to «أَغْرَقْناهم». اليَمُّ is the sea. The well-known view is that it is Arabic. Dhū l-Rumma said:

2283 - داوِيَّةٌ ودُجَى ليلٍ كأنهما ... يَمٌّ تراطَنَ في حافاتِه الرومُ
(A desert and the darkness of night, as if they were a sea on whose shores the Byzantines jabber.)

Ibn Qutayba said: "It is the sea in Syriac." It is also said: in Hebrew. The well-known view is that it is not restricted to a particular sea. al-Harawī said of its being Arabic: "اليَمُّ is the sea called Isāf, in which Pharaoh drowned." This is not good, because of His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي اليم} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 7], where what is meant is the Nile of Egypt, which is not the one in which Pharaoh drowned.

His saying: «بأنهم»: the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "We drowned them because of their denying Our signs and their being heedless of Our signs." The pronoun in «عنها» refers to the signs. This is the apparent sense, and al-Zajjāj and others said it. It is also said that it may refer to the vengeance indicated by «انتقمنا»; this is ascribed to Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is as if the one who says that imagined that heedlessness of the signs was an excuse for them, since heedlessness is not something a person earns.

The majority said: they engaged in the causes of heedlessness and so were blamed for it, as a forgetful person is blamed for his forgetting because he engaged in its causes.

semin-durr:160-160.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَقَطَّعْنَاهُمُ اثنتي عَشْرَةَ}: the obvious is that «قطعناهم» takes one object, because it is not made to include the meaning of a verb that takes two. On this basis «اثنتي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «قطَّعناهم», that is: "We divided them, being counted by this number." Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that «قَطَّعْنا» have the meaning of "We made," and that «اثنتي» be a second object, and al-Ḥawfī was decisive about that.
The tamyīz (specification) of «اثنتي عشرة» is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being: "twelve groups (firqa)," and «أسباطاً» is a badal (substitute) from that specification. I said the specification is omitted, and did not make «أسباطاً» the specifier, for two reasons. One: that the thing counted is masculine, since «أسباطاً» is the plural of sibṭ, so the construction would have been «اثني عشر». The second: that the specification of the compound numeral, which is from eleven to nineteen, is a singular accusative, and this, as you see, is a plural. Al-Zamakhsharī made it the specification and justified it, saying: "If you say: the specifier of what is beyond ten is singular, so what is the reason for its coming in the plural? Why was it not said 'twelve sibṭan'? I say: had that been said, it would not have conveyed the exact meaning, because what is meant is: 'We divided them into twelve tribes,' and each tribe is asbāṭ, not one sibṭ; so he put «أسباطاً» in the place of 'tribe.' Its like is:
2315 - ...
بين رماحَيْ مالكٍ ونَهْشَلِ
(between the two sets of spears of Mālik and Nahshal)."
The Shaykh said: "What he holds, that each tribe is asbāṭ, / is contrary to what people have mentioned: they mentioned that the asbāṭ among the Children of Israel are like the tribes among the Arabs, and they said: al-asbāṭ is the plural of [sibṭ], and they are the groups; and the asbāṭ among the descendants of Isaac are like the tribes among the descendants of Ishmael. On his claim, the saying of the Exalted {وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إلى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ والأسباط} would mean: 'and the tribe.' And his saying that it is the like of the saying 'between the two spears of Mālik and Nahshal' is not its like, because that is a case of dualising a plural, which is permissible only by necessity; it is as if he is pointing out that were it not for observing in the plural that a kind of spears is meant, the dual would not be sound, and likewise here it is observed in «الأسباط», though a plural, the meaning of 'tribe,' so it is specified by it as it is specified by a singular."
Al-Ḥawfī said: "It is possible that it rests on omission, the implied form being: 'twelve groups, asbāṭan,' with «أسباطاً» an adjective of «فرقة», then the qualified noun was omitted and the adjective put in its place. And «أمم» is an adjective of «أسباط»; and he made the numeral feminine though it applies to the asbāṭ, which is masculine, because it has the meaning of a group (firqa) or a nation (umma), as he said:
2316 - ثلاثة أنفس. . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(three persons …) meaning a man. [And he said:]
2317 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . عشرُ أَبْطُنْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(ten clans …) with regard to the tribe. And an example of describing a singular specification with a plural, regarding the sense, is the poet's saying: 2318 - فيها اثنتان وأربعون حَلوبةً ... سُوداً كخافيةِ الغراب الأَسْحَمِ
(In it are forty-two milch camels, black like the covert feather of the dusky raven.)
He described «حلوبة», which is singular in form, by «سُوداً», which is a plural, regarding its meaning, since the plural is what is intended."
Al-Farrāʾ said: "He said «اثنتي عشرة» though sibṭ is masculine because what follows are nations (umam), so the feminine went to the nations; and had it been «اثني عشر» for the masculinity of sibṭ it would have been permissible." The grammarians cited as evidence for this the poet's saying:
2319 - وإنَّ قريشاً هذه عشرُ أبطنٍ ... وأنت بريءٌ من قبائلها العشرِ
(Indeed these Quraysh are ten clans, and you are free of its ten tribes.)
He took baṭn to mean the tribe and the clan; for that reason he made it feminine, though baṭn is masculine.
Al-Zajjāj said: "The meaning is: 'We divided them into twelve groups, asbāṭan,' as an attribute of firqa, as though He said: 'We made them asbāṭ and We divided them as asbāṭ.'" He also allowed that «أسباطاً» be a badal from «اثنتي عشرة», and al-Fārisī followed him in that.
Some of them said: "The implied wording is: 'We divided them into groups, twelve,' and then there is no need for anything else." Others said: He made each one of the twelve into asbāṭ, as you say: "Zayd has dirhams, so-and-so has dirhams, so-and-so has dirhams, so these are twenty dirhams" — meaning that the sense is of twenties of dirhams. Had you said "so-and-so, so-and-so and so-and-so have twenty dirhams," with «درهم» in the singular, it would have led to all sharing in a single twenty, whereas the meaning is the opposite. A group of them, among them al-Baghawī, said: "There is a transposition (taqdīm and taʾkhīr) in the speech; its implied form is: 'We divided them into asbāṭ, nations, twelve.'"
