And His saying {أُمَماً}: it is either an adjective of «أسباطاً» or a badal from it following a badal, on our view that «أسباطاً» is a badal from that omitted specification. Al-Zamakhsharī made it a badal from «اثنتي عشرة», saying: "meaning: 'We divided them into nations,' because each of the asbāṭ was a great nation and a dense-numbered community, and each one aims at something different from what the other aims at, scarcely harmonising." End. The discussion about «الأسباط» has already been given.
Abān ibn Taghlib read «وَقَطَعْناهم» with a light ʿayn; the famous reading is better because the context is for multiplicity, though this one also allows it. Al-Aʿmash, Ibn Wathāb and Ṭalḥa ibn Sulaymān read «عَشِرة» with kasra on the shīn, and fatḥa on it has also been reported from them; Abū Ḥaywa and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif agreed with them on the kasra only. The verification of this was given earlier in al-Baqara, namely that the kasra is the dialect of Tamīm and the sukūn the dialect of the Hijaz.
His saying: {أَنِ اضرب}: it is permissible that «أَنْ» be the explicative for the revelation, and permissible that it be the maṣdar-forming particle. And His saying «فانبجسَتْ» is like His saying {فانفجرت} [al-Baqara: 60] in i'rab, implied form and meaning, and all that was given earlier in al-Baqara. It was also said: al-inbijās is sweating. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: / "inbajasat: it sweated; infajarat: it flowed," so he distinguished between them with what was mentioned; and in the exegesis, when Moses, upon him be peace, struck the rock, there appeared on it something like a woman's breast, which would sweat and then flow; and the two are close to the distinction mentioned between naḍkh and naḍḥ. Al-Rāghib said: "It is said bajasa l-māʾu and inbajasa: it burst forth; but inbijās is most often said of what comes out of something narrow, whereas infijār is used for that and for what comes out of something wide; therefore the Exalted said: {فانبجست مِنْهُ اثنتا عَشْرَةَ عَيْناً}, and in another place {فانفجرت} [al-Baqara: 60], so both words were used where the outlet was narrow." He means he distinguished between them by generality and specificity: every inbijās is an infijār, without the converse.
Al-Harawī said: "It is said inbajasa, tabajjasa, tafajjara and tafattaqa in one sense." And in the ḥadīth of Ḥudhayfa: "There is none of us but a man with an āmma which the fingernail could open (yabjusuhā), except two men" — meaning ʿUmar and ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them. The āmma is the head wound that reaches the umm al-raʾs (the brain membrane); this is a figure, meaning that the āmma among us is filled with pus, such that what is in it can be drained with a fingernail without need of an iron instrument such as a lancet; so he expressed a man's slip in this way, saying it has grown worse until it resembled a wound of this description.
His saying: {كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ}: the promise to discuss the word «أناس» here was made earlier in al-Baqara. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Unās is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) that is not a broken plural, like rukhāl, tunāʾ, tuʾām and their sisters. It may be said that the origin is kasra and a broken plural, and the ḍamma is a substitute for the kasra, as the ḍamma is substituted for the fatḥa in such as sukārā and ghuyārā." The Shaykh said: "What he said is not permissible for two reasons. One: that «إناس» with kasra on the hamza is not uttered, so as to be a broken plural for which the ḍamma could be a substitute for the kasra; unlike sukārā and ghuyārā, where the analogy is faʿālā with fatḥa on the first letter, which is heard in both. The second: that in sukārā, ghuyārā, ʿujālā and what comes like them, the ḍamma is not a substitute for the fatḥa; rather Sībawayh stated in his Book that it is an original broken plural, just as faʿālā is an original broken plural, even though the ḍamma is not analogically productive as the fatḥa is.
Sībawayh said, in defining the breaking of adjectives: 'They sometimes break some of these on fuʿālā, and that is the saying of some of them: ʿujālā and sukārā.' And Sībawayh said in the chapter on noun patterns also: 'And fuʿālā occurs in nouns such as ḥubārā, sumānā and lubādā, and it is not an adjective unless the singular is broken on it for the plural, as in sukārā and ʿujālā.' These are two statements of Sībawayh that it is a broken plural, and if it is an original broken plural, it is not tenable to claim that its origin is faʿālā and that the vowel was substituted in it. Al-Mubarrad held that it is a collective noun, I mean fuʿālā with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and not a broken plural. So al-Zamakhsharī did not adopt what Sībawayh adopted, nor what al-Mubarrad adopted, because for al-Mubarrad it is a collective noun, so the ḍamma on its first letter is original, not a substitute for the fatḥa; rather he introduced a third view." End.
His saying: {كُلُواْ مِن طَيِّبَاتِ}: the discussion of this clause and of what precedes and follows it has been given earlier in al-Baqara, and it is as though this story is an abridgment of that one, for that one is fuller than this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The advancing and delaying in «وقولوا وادخلوا» is equivalent, whether they put ḥiṭṭa before entering the gate or after it, for they combine the two in carrying out." The Shaykh said: "His saying 'whether they put it before or after' is a non-Arabic construction; its correction is: 'whether they put it before or after (a-qaddamū am akhkharū),' as the Exalted said:
{سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْنَآ أَجَزِعْنَآ أَمْ صَبَرْنَا} [Ibrāhīm: 21]." I say: he means that he brought the word «سواء» with «أو» instead of «أم», and did not bring the hamza of equalisation after «سواء»; and it has been mentioned earlier that this is permissible even though what he mentioned is the more frequent, and that {سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم أو لم تُنْذِرْهم} was read; so rebuttal by the like of this is of no use.
ʿĪsā al-Hamdhānī read «ما رَزَقْتُكم» in the singular [first-person], and a disagreement among the Seven in the like of this will come in Sūrat Ṭā Hā.
His saying: {نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ}: the disagreement over «يغفر» has been given earlier. As for «خطاياكم», Ibn ʿĀmir read it «خطيئتكم» in the singular and nominative, as passive (what the agent is not named), the premise being that he reads «تُغْفَر» with the tāʾ from above. Nāfiʿ read «خطيئاتكم» in the sound plural, nominative, as passive, because he reads «تُغْفَر» like the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir; and Abū ʿAmr read «خطاياكم», the broken plural, and he reads «نغفر» with the nūn of magnification; and the rest read «نَغْفر» like Abū ʿAmr, «خطيئاتكم» in the sound plural, accusative with the kasra, per the rule. And in Sūrat Nūḥ Abū ʿAmr / read «خطاياهم» in the broken plural also, and the rest in the sound plural. Ibn Hurmuz read «تُغْفَر» with a ḍamma tāʾ, passive, like Nāfiʿ, «خطاياكم» like Abū ʿAmr. And from him also: «يَغْفر» with the yāʾ of third person; and from him: «تَغْفِر» with fatḥa on the tāʾ from above, in the sense that ḥiṭṭa is a cause of forgiveness so forgiveness is attributed to it.

semin-durr:163-163.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {عَنِ القرية}: an omitted muḍāf is necessary, that is: "about the news of the town," and this muḍāf is the governor in the accusative of this adverbial, His saying «إذ يعدون». It was also said: rather, it is accusative by «حاضرة». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He allowed that because it existed at that time and then fell into ruin." Al-Zamakhsharī supposed the muḍāf to be «أهل», that is: "about the people of the town," and made the adverbial a badal (substitute) of the omitted «أهل», for he said: "«إذ يَعْدون» is a badal from «القرية», the town being meant as its people, as though it were said: 'and ask them about the people of the town at the time of their transgression on the Sabbath'; and it is a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute)."
The Shaykh said: "This is not permissible, because «إذ» is among the adverbs that are not declinable and no preposition enters upon them, and making it a badal would permit «عن» to enter upon it, because a badal is in the intention of repeating the governor, and were you to enter «عن» upon it, it would not be permissible. Rather it is used flexibly only by annexing to it some of the time adverbs, as in «يوم إذ كان كذا». As for the saying of whoever held that it is the object of «اذكر», it is the saying of one who was unable to interpret it as it should be, keeping it an adverbial."
Al-Ḥawfī said: "«إذ» is attached to «سَلْهم»." The Shaykh said: "This is inconceivable, because «إذ» refers to the past, and «سَلْهم» is future; and if it were a future adverbial, the meaning would not be sound, for the transgressors, who are the people of the town, are gone, so asking them is not possible; so the one asked is other than the transgressing people of the town."
Shahr ibn Ḥawshab and Abū Nahīk read «يَعَدُّون» with fatḥa on the ʿayn and shadda on the dāl, and this resembles the reading of Nāfiʿ in «لا تَعَدُّوا في السبت»; the origin is «تَعْتَدُّوا», so the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl because of its proximity to it. «تُعِدُّون» was also read, with ḍamma on the tāʾ, kasra on the ʿayn and shadda on the dāl, from aʿadda yuʿiddu iʿdādan: "when he prepared its implements." In the exegesis: they were commanded on the Sabbath and would leave it and prepare the implements of fishing.
His saying: {إِذْ تَأْتِيهِمْ}: the governor in it is «يَعْدُون», that is: "when they transgressed, when they [the fish] came to them," because the past adverbial turns the imperfect to the past. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وإذ تأتيهم» is a badal from «إذْ يَعْدُون», a badal following a badal," meaning that it is a second badal from «القرية» according to what he established. The Shaykh's rebuttal of him has been given there, and it applies here as well.
And «حِيتان» is the plural of ḥūt; the wāw was changed to yāʾ only because of its being sukūn and the kasra before it. Like it: nūn and nīnān. And al-nūn is the fish.
His saying: {شُرَّعاً}: a ḥāl from «حِيتانهم», and shurraʿ is the plural of shāriʿ. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz read «يوم إسْباتهم», a maṣdar of asbata when he entered into the Sabbath.
ʿĀṣim, with a disagreement from him, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «لا يَسْبُتون» with ḍamma on the bāʾ. ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim, with disagreement from him, read «يُسْبِتون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the bāʾ, from asbata, that is, he entered into the Sabbath. «يُسْبَتُون» was also read, with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the bāʾ, passive, which al-Zamakhsharī transmitted from al-Ḥasan; he said: "that is: the Sabbath is not made to come round for them and they are not commanded to keep the Sabbath."
The governor in «يوم لا يَسْبتون» is His saying «لا تَأْتيهم», that is: "they do not come to them on the day they do not keep the Sabbath," and this indicates the permissibility of putting before «لا» the object of what is negated by «لا». I have given earlier three positions on it: permissible absolutely, as in this verse; prohibited absolutely; and the distinction between its being the answer to an oath, in which case it is prohibited, and otherwise permissible.
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ نَبْلُوهُم}: al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Anbārī mentioned two views concerning this kāf and its genitive noun. The first: al-Zajjāj said: "That is: 'in the same way as this severe testing We test them,' so the position of the kāf is accusative by «نَبْلوهم»." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "«ذلك» is a pointer to what follows it; he means: 'We test them through their wrongdoing, in the same way as the trial that befell them in the matter of the fish,'" and the speech breaks off at His saying «لا تأتيهم».
The second view: al-Zajjāj said: "It is possible, though remotely, that it be: 'and on the day they do not keep the Sabbath they do not come to them thus,' that is: 'they do not come to them in plenty (shurraʿan),' and «نَبْلوهم» would be resumptive." Abū Bakr said: "On this view, «كذلك» refers back to the plenty (al-shurūʿ) in the saying of the Exalted {يَوْمَ سَبْتِهِمْ شُرَّعاً}, and the implied form is: 'and on the day they do not keep the Sabbath they do not come to them in the same coming, with plenty,' and the position of the kāf on this view is accusative, by the coming, as a ḥāl, that is: 'they do not come in the like of that coming.'" /
And His saying: {بِمَا كَانُوا}: the bāʾ is causal and «ما» is maṣdarī (verbal-noun-forming), that is: "We test them because of their wrongdoing"; it is weak that it have the meaning of «الذي» ("that which") for the artificiality of omitting the returning pronoun by degrees. Makkī mentioned here a question over which the grammarians differ, which has no connection with this place, saying: "The most eloquent usage is that the adverbial be accusative with the Sabbath and Friday, so you say: «اليومَ السبتُ» and «اليومَ الجمعة», putting «اليوم» in the accusative as an adverbial, and nominative with the rest of the days, so you say «اليومُ الأحد» and «اليومُ الأربعاء», because there is no verbal meaning in them, so the mubtadaʾ is the khabar, and you make it nominative." I say: this question has disagreement among the grammarians. The majority, as he mentioned, require the nominative, because it is like your saying «اليومُ الأولُ، اليومُ الثاني». Al-Farrāʾ and Hishām allowed the accusative; they said: "because «اليوم» is like «الآن»; and «الآن» is more general than Sunday and Tuesday, as though it were said: 'Now it is Sunday; now it is Monday,'" that is, they occur within "now." And this question is not specific to Friday and the Sabbath; rather the rule in it is that when «اليوم» is mentioned with something that includes an act and an event, the accusative and the nominative are both permissible, as in their saying «اليوم العيد»، «اليوم الفطر»، «اليوم الأضحى», as though you said: "today there takes place a gathering, breaking of the fast and sacrifice."

semin-durr:164-164.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مَعْذِرَةً}: the majority read «معذرة» in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "our admonition is an excuse." Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «معذرةً» in the accusative. There are three views about it. The clearest: that it is accusative as mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose), that is: "we admonished him for the sake of excuse." Sībawayh said: "If a man were to say to another: «معذرةً إلى الله وإليك من كذا», it would be accusative." The second: that it is accusative as a maṣdar, by an implied verb of its own wording, its implied form being: "we excuse ourselves with an excuse." The third: that it is accusative in the manner of the direct object, because the excuse includes speech, and a singular that includes speech, when it occurs after "saying," is put in the accusative as a direct object, as in «قلت خطبة» ("I said a sermon"). Sībawayh prefers the nominative; he said: "because they did not intend to make a fresh excuse, but it was said to them: 'Why do you admonish?' and they said: 'Our admonition is an excuse.'" And al-maʿdhira is an ism maṣdar, being al-ʿudhr. Al-Azharī said: "It has the meaning of al-iʿtidhār," and al-ʿudhr is the disclaiming of a sin.

semin-durr:202-202.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِخْوَانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الغي}: in this verse there are several possibilities. The first: the pronoun in «إخوانهم» refers to the satans, as the word "satan" indicates them, or to Satan himself, since the individual is not meant but the kind. The accusative pronoun in «يَمُدُّونهم» refers to the disbelievers, and the nominative one (the subject) refers to the satans or Satan as preceded. The implied form is: "the brothers of the satans — the satans extend them [in error]". On this possibility the predicate runs on something other than what it belongs to in meaning: do you not see that the extending is attributed in meaning to the satans, while in wording it is a predicate of «إخوانهم»? Like it is:

2374 - قوم إذا الخيلُ جالُوا في كواثبها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(A people who, when the horses roam about their withers …)

A discussion and investigation of this with Makkī and others has already preceded you, regarding the verb running on other than the one it belongs to without a pronoun being made overt. This interpretation which I mentioned is the view of the majority and most of the commentators. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is the most sound, because «إخوانهم» stands against «الذين اتقوا»."

The second: that by the brothers the satans are meant, and by the pronoun to which it is annexed, the ignorant or the non-God-fearing; because a thing points to its opposite. The wāw refers to the brothers, and the accusative pronoun refers to the ignorant or the non-God-fearing. The meaning: "the satans who are the brothers of the ignorant, or the non-God-fearing, extend the ignorant or the non-God-fearing in error." The predicate on this possibility runs on the one it belongs to, in wording and meaning; and this is the exegesis of Qatāda.

The third: that the genitive and accusative pronouns refer to the satans, and the nominative to the brothers, who are the disbelievers. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The meaning is then: the brothers of the satans in error — as opposed to brothers in Allah — extend [the satans], i.e. by obeying them and accepting from them; and this interpretation does not work out if «في الغيّ» is attached to the extending, because humans do not lead the satans astray." I say: he means that «في الغيّ» is then a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "their brothers, while being settled in error"; and in the coming of a ḥāl from the mubtadaʾ there is disagreement. The better is that it be attached to what «إخوانهم» contains of the meaning of fraternity and brotherhood; the Shaykh has a discussion of it coming.

The Shaykh said: "On this interpretation «في الغيّ» can be attached to «يمدُّونهم» in the sense of causation, i.e. 'they extend them because of their error', as in «دخلت امرأة النار في هرة», i.e. because of a cat. It is also possible that «في الغيّ» is a ḥāl, being attached to an omitted element, i.e. 'being in error'; so «في الغيّ» is in its place and is not attached to «إخوانهم», and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that. In my view there is room for objection in this: if you said «مُطْعِمُك زيدٌ لحماً», meaning 'the one who feeds you meat is Zayd', separating the mubtadaʾ from its governed element by the khabar, there would be room for objection in its permissibility; because you separated the governor from its governed element by something foreign to both, even though it is not foreign to one of them, namely the mubtadaʾ."

I say: there is no apparent reason to prevent this at all, because of its not being foreign.

Nāfiʿ read «يُمِدونهم» with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from amadda; the rest read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the mīm, from madda. Discussion of this root has already preceded, and whether the two have one meaning or there is a difference between them, near the beginning of this subject. Al-Jaḥdarī read «يُمادُّونهم», from mādda-hu on the pattern fāʿala-hu.

The majority read «يُقْصِرُون», from aqṣara. The poet said:

2375 - لعَمْرك ما قلبي إلى أهله بحُرّْ ... ولا مُقْصِرٍ يوماً فيأتيني بقُرّْ
(By your life, my heart is not free toward its people, nor does it ever desist one day so as to bring me coolness.)

And Imruʾ al-Qays said:

2376 - سما لك شوقٌ بعدما كان أَقْصَرا ... وحَلَّتْ سُلَيْمى بَطْنَ قَوٍّ فعَرْعرا
(Longing rose for you after it had desisted, and Sulaymā alighted in the valley of Qawwin, then Ghar'ar.)

i.e. "nor one who desists from what he is in"; and "your longing rose after it had left off and ceased." ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ثم لا يَقْصُرون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the ṣād, from qaṣara, i.e. "then they do not diminish from their extending." As for this sentence, I mean «وإخوانهم يمدُّونهم», al-Zajjāj claimed that it is connected with the sentence of His saying {وَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ لَهُمْ نَصْراً}, which is a remote affectation.

And His saying {فِي الغي}: it has preceded that it may be attached to the verb, or to «إخوانهم», or to an omitted element as a ḥāl: either of «إخوانهم», or of the wāw of «يمدُّونهم», or of its object.

semin-durr:203-203.t:
Al-inṣāt is stillness for the sake of listening, al-Farrāʾ said. One says naṣata and anṣata with one meaning, and anṣata has occurred as transitive; al-Kumayt said:

2377 - أبوك الذي أجْدَى عليك بنصره ... فأنصت عني بعده كلَّ قائل
(Your father is the one who benefited you with his help; so after him he silenced for me every speaker.)

And His saying {هذا بَصَآئِرُ}: baṣāʾir is the plural of baṣīra; baṣāʾir is applied to the Quran, either as hyperbole, or because it is the cause of insights, or on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessor of insights". «لعل» may be for hope relative to those addressed, or it may be for giving a reason.

semin-durr:204-204.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَهُ}: it is attached to «استمعوا», in the sense of "for its sake", and the pronoun refers to the Quran. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be in the sense of «لله», i.e. 'for His sake'", thus returning the pronoun to «الله»; and in that is remoteness. He also allowed that the lām be redundant, i.e. "so listen to it"; and you have learned that this is not permissible according to the majority except in two places: either the fronting of the governed element, or the governor being derivative. He also allowed that it be in the sense of «إلى», and there is no need of it.

Al-ijtibāʾ is iftiʿāl from jabāhu yajbīhi, i.e. he gathered it, choosing it; for this reason the usage «اجتبيتُ الشيء», "I chose the thing", came to predominate. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Ijtabā l-shayʾ: in the sense of jabāhu for himself, i.e. he gathered it, as you say ijtamaʿahu; or it was collected for him and he took it, i.e. took it, as in «جَلَيْتُ إليه العروس فاجتلاها» (I displayed the bride to him and he took her in view). The meaning: 'Why did you not gather it, a contrivance from yourself?', because they used to say {إِنْ هذا إِلاَّ إِفْكٌ افتراه} [al-Furqān: 4]."

semin-durr:205-205.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تَضَرُّعاً وَخِيفَةً}: there are two possibilities for their being accusative. The more apparent is that both are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose), since remembrance is caused by them. The second: that they are accusative as maṣdars standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "humbling yourself and fearing", or "possessing humility and fear". «وخفية» was also read, with the fāʾ fronted. It was also said that they are two maṣdars of the verb in meaning but not in wording; Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it, and it is remote.

His saying: {وَدُونَ الجهر}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is conjoined to «تضرُّع», the implied form being 'and being moderate'." This is weak, because «دون» is an adverb that is not declined, according to the well-known view; so what ought to be done is to make it an adjective of an omitted thing, that omitted thing being the ḥāl, as al-Zamakhsharī supposed, saying: "«ودونَ الجهر»: and speaking speech below the loud; because concealment is more fitting for sincerity and closer to good reflection."

His saying: {بالغدو والآصال} is attached to «اذكر», i.e. "remember Him in these two times", which stand for night and day. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«بالغُدُوِّ» is attached to «ادعوا»", which is a slip of tongue and pen, since the arrangement of the Quran is not so.

Al-ghudūw is either the plural of ghudwa, like qamḥ and qamḥa, and on this the plural is set against a plural in meaning. It was also said that it is a maṣdar, so a time is supplied as annexed to it so that a plural time is set against its like; the implied form: "at the times of al-ghudūw". Al-āṣāl is the plural of uṣul, and uṣul is the plural of aṣīl, so it is a plural of a plural. It is not permissible that it be a plural of aṣīl directly, because faʿīl is not pluralised on afʿāl. It was also said: rather it is a plural of aṣīl, and faʿīl is pluralised on afʿāl, such as yamīn and aymān. It was also said: āṣāl is the plural of uṣul and uṣul is singular, this being established from their language, and it is the evening; and fuʿul is pluralised on afʿāl, as they said ʿunuq and aʿnāq; on this there is no need to claim that it is a plural of a plural. It is also pluralised on uṣlān, like raghīf and rughfān, and it is diminutive in its own form, as in his saying:

2378 - وَقَفْتُ فيها أُصَيْلالاً أسائلُها ... عَيَّتْ جواباً وما بالرَّبْعِ مِنْ أحدِ
(I stood in it at a little eventide, questioning it; it was at a loss for answer, and there was no one in the encampment.)

The Kufans used their saying «أُصَيْلان» as evidence, in this verse, for the permissibility of diminutive of a plural of multitude; the Basrans interpreted it as singular, its nūn being changed into lām; and it is also transmitted as «أصيلالاً».

Abū Mijlaz, whose name is Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd al-Sadūsī al-Baṣrī, read «والإِيصال», a maṣdar of āṣala, i.e. "he entered the evening (aṣīl)".

semin-durr:137-137.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وأَوْرَثْنَا}: it takes two objects, because before being transitivised by the hamza it takes one object, as in وَرِثْتُ أبي ("I inherited from my father"); by the transfer it acquired another. The first of them is «القوم», and «الذين» with its ṣila is in the position of accusative as its adjective. As for the second object, there are three views about it. The most evident: that it is {مَشَارِقَ الأرض وَمَغَارِبَهَا}. On this, there are two views about {التي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا}: one, that it is an adjective of «مشارق» and «مغارب»; the second, that it is an adjective of «الأرض». There is weakness in the latter because of the separation, by the conjoined element, between the adjective and the described, and it is like your saying: «قام غلامُ هندٍ وزيدٌ العاقلةِ». Abū l-Baqāʾ said here: "There is weakness in it, because in it there is a conjunction on the described before the adjective." This is a slip of the tongue or pen, because the conjunction is not on the described but on what is annexed to the described. [Translator's note: the author is correcting Abū l-Baqāʾ's wording.]

The second of the three views: that the second object is {التي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا}, i.e. "We caused them to inherit the land which We blessed". In His saying, the Exalted, {مَشَارِقَ الأرض وَمَغَارِبَهَا} there are two views: one, that it is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf) of «يُسْتَضْعفون»; the second, that its implied form is: "they were oppressed in the easts of the land and its wests", and when the particle was dropped the verb reached it directly and made it accusative. So said Abū l-Baqāʾ. I do not know how these can be two views, since the adverbial view is the very same as the view that it is on the implication of «في», because every adverbial is implied with «في»; so how does he make one thing into two?

The third view: that the second object is omitted, its implied form being: "We caused them to inherit the land" or "the dominion" or the like. And «يُستضعفون» may be on its usual sense of seeking, i.e. weakness was figuratively sought from them; or استفعل in the sense of "he found it to be such". What is meant by the land is the land of Syria; it is also said: the land of Egypt.

al-Ḥasan, and it is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim, read «كلمات» in the plural. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its like is {لَقَدْ رأى مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّه الكبرى} [al-Najm: 18]", meaning in the plural being described by a singular. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What he mentioned is not necessarily so in «الكبرى», for the implied form may be: 'he saw the greatest sign', in which case it is the description of a singular and not of a plural, and that is more eloquent." I say: In some places what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned is necessary, as in {مَآرِبُ أخرى} [Ṭā Hā: 18] and this verse; so he chose from them what is necessary elsewhere.

His saying: {بِمَا صَبَرُواْ} is attached to «تَمَّت», and the bāʾ is causal, «ما» a maṣdar particle, i.e. "because of their patience". What the patience was directed at is omitted, i.e. "at the harm of Pharaoh and his people".

His saying: {وَدَمَّرْنَا مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ}: Several views are possible in this verse. One: that «فرعون» is the subject (ism) of كان, and «يصنع» a preposed khabar, the kāna-clause being the ṣila of «ما», with the returning pronoun omitted, the implied form being: "and We destroyed what Pharaoh used to make".

Abū l-Baqāʾ considered this view weak, saying: "because «يصنع» is able to govern «فرعون», so its postposing is not to be implied, just as the postposing of the verb is not implied in your saying قام زيد." I say: he means that your saying «قام زيد» must be of the category of verb and agent, and one may not claim in it that «قام» is a verb with its agent and the sentence a preposed khabar and «زيد» a postposed mubtadaʾ, because of the confusion with the agent construction; so likewise here, because «يصنع» can act upon «فرعون» and make it nominative as agent, so preposing is not claimed in it. Makkī had preceded him to this and said: "Whoever allows this must allow «يقوم زيد» as mubtadaʾ and khabar with preposing and postposing, and no one has allowed it." This question and what is in it, and whether it can be of the category of competition (tanāzuʿ) or not, has already been given. What the two of them mentioned, though it appears impossible at first thought, is like the category of mubtadaʾ and khabar; but the answer to that is that the obstacle in «قام زيد» is the confusion, and that is absent here.

[Translator's note: the Arabic text here reads «القثاني», an evident misprint for «الثاني» ("the second"); translated as "the second".]

The second: that the subject of «كان» is a pronoun returning to the relative «ما», and «يصنع» is predicated of فرعون, the sentence being the khabar of كان, and the returning pronoun also omitted, the implied form being: "and We destroyed what he, Pharaoh, used to make".

The third: that «كان» is redundant and «ما» a maṣdar particle, the implied form being: "and We destroyed what Pharaoh makes", i.e. his making. Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it. I say: this view should also apply if «ما» is a relative noun, with the returning pronoun omitted, the implied form being: "and We destroyed that which Pharaoh makes".

The fourth: that «ما» is also a maṣdar particle, and «كان» is not redundant but defective, its subject being the pronoun of the affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn), and the sentence «يصنع فرعون» the khabar of كان, so it explains the pronoun. Abū l-Baqāʾ said here: "It is also said: «كان» is not redundant, but the defective «كان» does not separate «ما» from its ṣila, and we have mentioned that at His saying {بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ} [al-Baqara: 10]; and on this view «كان» needs a subject. It is weak that its subject be the pronoun of the affair, because the sentence after it is the ṣila of «ما», so it is not suited to explanation, and clarification is not achieved by it, whereas the completion of the noun and the explainer must be independent; so need calls for making «فرعون» the subject of كان, and in «يصنع» a pronoun returning to it." I say: after supposing it defective, it follows that the sentence «يصنع فرعون» is the khabar of «كان», and it is impossible that it be the ṣila of «ما». And his saying "so need calls" means: that very view with which I began and which he weakened, he needed in this place, in flight from making the subject the pronoun of the affair, because of what he imagined to be an obstacle.

التدمير is destruction, and it is transitive by itself. As for His saying {دَمَّرَ الله عَلَيْهِمْ}, its object is omitted, i.e. "He ruined upon them their dwellings and houses".

His saying: {يَعْرِشُونَ}: Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read here and in al-Naḥl «يَعرُشون» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, and the rest with kasra in both. They are two dialects: عَرَش الكرمَ يعرِشُه ويعرُشُه ("he trellised the vine"), and the kasra is the Ḥijāzī dialect. al-Yazīdī said: "It is the most eloquent." It has also been read anomalously with a dotted ghayn and an undotted sīn, from غَرْس الأشجار (planting trees), and I think it is nothing but a scribal distortion. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «يُعَرِّشون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the ʿayn and a doubled kasra on the rāʾ, for intensity and multiplicity.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying, the Exalted: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject). There are two views on its khabar (predicate). One: that it is the sentence from His saying {لاَ نُكَلِّفُ نَفْساً}, and on this a returning pronoun is necessary, which is implied, its implied form being "a soul of them". The second: it is the sentence from His saying {أولئك أَصْحَابُ}, and this negated sentence is then parenthetical between the two; and this view is the more fitting in i'rab.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {مِّنْ غِلٍّ}: «مِنْ» may be for clarifying the class of «ما», and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), so that it is attached to an omitted element, i.e., "being of rancour". And His saying: «تجري من تحتهم الأنهار»: in this sentence there are three views. One: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «صدورهم»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and he made the governor in this ḥāl the meaning of annexation (iḍāfa). The second: that it is a ḥāl, the governor in it being «نزعنا»; al-Ḥūfī said this. The third: that it is a resumptive report about the description of their states.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected the first two views. As for the second, because {تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِهِمُ الأنهار} is not a description of the agent of «نَزَعْنا» nor of its object, which are «نا» and «ما»; so how can it be accusative as a ḥāl from them? This is plain. As for the first, because the meaning of annexation governs only when it is possible to strip the muḍāf and make it govern what follows it, in the nominative or accusative. I say: it has been said more than once that the ḥāl comes from the muḍāf ilayhi when the muḍāf is a part of the muḍāf ilayhi, for another reason, not for what Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned, that the governor is the meaning of annexation; rather the governor in the ḥāl is the governor in the muḍāf, even if the ḥāl is not from it; because, since the two are in an annexation relation and are at the same time one thing, that is allowed.
And «al-ghill» is rancour, spite and hatred, and so too «al-ghulūl». The plural of «al-ghill» is «ghilāl». And «al-ghulūl» is taking in secret, and the best of what was said is that it comes from the word «al-ghilāla» (an undergarment), as if he wrapped himself in and put on rancour and treachery until it became to him like the garment worn.
His saying: {لولا أَنْ هَدَانَا}: «أَنْ» and what lies in its scope are in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, as I have implied more than once; and the apodosis of «لولا» is indicated by His saying «وما كنا», its implied form being: "Had there not been a guidance of us existing, we would have been wretched, or we would not have been guided." And «لقد جاءت» is the apodosis of an implied oath. And «بالحق»: the bāʾ may be for transitivity, so «بالحق» is an object in meaning; and it may be circumstantial, i.e., "they came accompanied by the truth".
His saying: {أَن تِلْكُمُ}: it may be the explicative (mufassira), explaining the call, which is the apparent sense, with what follows it. And it may be the lightened one (mukhaffafa), its noun being the pronoun of the matter, omitted, with «أن» and what follows it in the position of accusative or genitive; for the original is «بأن تلكم». It is pointed to with the demonstrative of the far because they were promised it in this world. The wording of some, "it is a pointing to something absent", has looseness in it, because pointing is only to something present, but the scholars apply "absent" figuratively to the far.
And «أُورِثتموها»: this sentence may be a ḥāl, as in His saying: {فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةً} [al-Naml: 52]; it may be a khabar of «تلكم»; and «الجنة» may be a badal (substitute) or an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān), with «أُورثتموها» the khabar. Abū l-Baqāʾ forbade it to be a ḥāl from «تلكم», because of the separation by the khabar and because the mubtadaʾ does not govern a ḥāl. Abū ʿAmr and the two brothers assimilated the thāʾ into the tāʾ, and the rest made it clear.
And {بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ} has preceded more than once. The group read «وما كنا» with the wāw, and so it is in the codices of the regions other than Syria. There are two views on it, the more apparent being that it is the wāw of resumption, and the sentence after it is resumptive. The second: that it is circumstantial. Ibn ʿĀmir read «وما كنا» without the wāw, and the sentence is, as preceded, either resumptive or circumstantial; and it is so in the codex of the Syrians; so each read according to what is in his own codex.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن قَدْ وَجَدْنَا}: «أَنْ» may be explicative of the call, and it may be the lightened form of the heavy «أنَّ», its noun being the pronoun of the matter and affair, with the sentence after it its khabar; and when the verb is inflected (mutaṣarrif) and not an invocation, the best is separation by «قد», as in this verse, or by something else. Its verification has preceded in al-Māʾida. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it not said «ما وعدكم ربكم», as it was said «ما وَعَدنا ربنا»? I say: that was omitted for lightness because «وَعَدْنا» indicates it. And one might say: it was left unrestricted so as to include everything Allah promised of resurrection, reckoning, punishment, reward and all the states of the Resurrection, because they were denying all of that, and because the whole of what was promised is of what grieved them, and the bliss of the people of Paradise is nothing but punishment for them, so it was left unrestricted for that." I say: his saying "One might say..." to the end, this answer does not match his question, because what is claimed is the omission of the first object, which is the pronoun of those addressed, whereas the answer came with the second object, which is the reckoning, the punishment and the other states; so this would be fitting only if he had been asked about the omission of the second object, not the first.
And {نَعَمْ} is a particle of answer, like ajal, iy, jayr and balā. Its opposite is «lā». «Naʿam» is used to confirm a report, or to inform in answer to an inquiry, or as a promise to a petitioner. A negation joined to an interrogative may also be answered with it, which is very rare, as in his saying:
2200 - Does not the night bring together Umm ʿAmr ... and us? That is our nearness to each other.
Yes, and you see the crescent as I see it ... and the day rises over her as it rose over me.
So he answered his saying «أليس» with «naʿam», though by right he should have said «balā»; for that reason it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās on His saying, the Exalted: {أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُواْ بلى} [al-Aʿrāf: 172]: "Had they said 'naʿam' they would have disbelieved." There is a discussion in it which will come soon, if Allah the Exalted wills.
Its ʿayn is also pronounced with kasra; al-Kisāʾī, al-Aʿmash and Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb read it so, and it is the dialect of Kināna. Abū Ḥātim criticized it and said: "The kasra is not known." Al-Kisāʾī argued for his reading with what is related of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that he asked some people and they said «naʿam» with fatḥa, so he said: "As for al-naʿam, it is the camels; so say «naʿim»", i.e., with kasra. Abū ʿUbayd said: "We have not seen the Arabs know what they narrated from ʿUmar, and we regard it as post-classical." I say: this is a criticism of a mass-transmitted reading, so it is not accepted. Its ʿayn is also changed into ḥāʾ, which is a widespread dialect, just as the ḥāʾ of «ḥattā» is changed into ʿayn.
And His saying: {بَيْنَهُمْ}: may be accusative by «أذَّن» or by «مؤذِّن», and may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «مؤذِّن». Makkī said, when he allowed this view: "But «مُؤَذِّن» does not govern «أَنْ», since he has qualified it by an adjective", meaning that His saying «أَنْ لعنةُ» cannot be governed by «مؤذن» because it is qualified, and the active participle does not govern whenever it is qualified.
I say: this gives the impression that if we do not make «بينهم» an adjective of «مؤذِّن», it could govern «أن»; but it is not so, [because if you said] "A striker struck Zayd" you make «زيداً» accusative by «ضرب», not by «ضارب». But I have seen that al-Wāḥidī [allowed what] Makkī allowed, [that] «مؤذِّن» governs «أَنْ», and if you qualify it that is prevented, and in it is what has preceded, and it is good.
[Translator's note: in the Arabic text above, the square brackets in the last paragraph and the preceding one are in the source itself, which appears to be corrupted or reconstructed at these points; I have translated what is written.]
And «أَنْ» may be the explicative, and may be the lightened, with the nominal sentence after it the khabar, and there is no need here for a separator. The two brothers, Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Bazzī read «أنَّ» with fatḥa on the hamza and doubling the nūn and accusative of «اللعنة», as its noun, with «على الظالمين» its khabar; likewise in al-Nūr «أن لعنةُ الله عليه»; Nāfiʿ alone lightened «أَنْ» and read «اللعنة» in the nominative, and the rest with the doubling and the accusative. ʿIṣma from al-Aʿmash read «إنَّ» with kasra and doubling, and that is either by implying "saying", according to the Basrans, or by treating the call as saying, according to the Kufans.

semin-durr:45-45.t: And His saying, the Exalted: {الذين}: it may be in the position of nominative or accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off) in both, and genitive as an adjective (naʿt), a badal (substitute) or an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān). The object of «يَصُدُّون» is omitted, i.e., "they bar people". It is also possible that no object be implied for it, the meaning being: "those whose characteristic is barring", like their saying "he gives and withholds". It is also possible that «يَصُدُّون» have the meaning "they turn away", from «ṣadda ṣudūdan», so that it is intransitive.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَبَيْنَهُمَا}: i.e., between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, and this is the apparent sense because of His saying {فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُم بِسُورٍ}. It was also said: between Paradise and the Fire, and with this al-Zamakhsharī began. And His saying {وَعَلَى الأعراف}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "i.e., on the heights of the veil", as if he made the «al» a compensation for the annexation, which is a Kufan view, and its verification has preceded. Some made the Aʿrāf itself the very veil mentioned earlier, expressed sometimes as the veil and sometimes as the Aʿrāf. Al-Wāḥidī said, and he did not mention another: "For that reason the Aʿrāf are definite, because he meant by it the veil."
And «al-aʿrāf» is the plural of «ʿurf» with ḍamma on the ʿayn, which is every elevated place of ground or other, by metaphor from the ʿurf (crest) of the rooster and the ʿurf (mane) of the horse, as if it is known by its elevation, unlike low things, which are generally unknown. Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt said:
2201 - And others on the heights have set their hopes ... on a garden fenced by pomegranate and greenery
and similarly his saying:
2202 - Every one compact of flesh and tall ... like a mountain towering over the heights.
And another, who is al-Shammākh, said:
2203 - So she stayed on the heights rushing, as if she were ... spears which a planter has set facing the wind.
And His saying: {يَعْرِفُونَ} is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «رجال». And «كُلاًّ» i.e., each group of the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire. And His saying {أَن سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ} is like His saying {أَن لَّعْنَةُ الله عَلَى الظالمين} [al-Aʿrāf: 44], except that here it was read only with the light «أَنْ».
His saying: {وَنَادَوْاْ}: this pronoun and what follows it refer to «رجال». And His saying {لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا}: in this sentence there are several views. One: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «نادوا», i.e., "the people of the Aʿrāf called out while not entering Paradise". And His saying «وهم يطمعون» may be a ḥāl from the agent of «يدخلوها»; then you have two considerations after that. The first: that the meaning is "they did not enter it hoping to enter it, but entered it in despair of entering it". The second: that the meaning is "they did not enter it while hoping", i.e., they have not yet entered, and at the time of not entering they are hoping; and it may be resumptive, reporting about them that they are hoping to enter.
The second view: that it is a ḥāl from the object of «نادوا», i.e., "they called out to them while the latter were not entering". And His saying «وهم يَطْمَعون» is as preceded just now. The third view: that it is in the position of nominative as an adjective of «رجال»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. There is weakness in it in that it separates between the qualified noun and its adjective by the sentence «ونادَوا», which is not a parenthetical sentence. The fourth view: that it has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to a questioner who asked about the people of the Aʿrāf, saying: what was done with them? So it was said: they did not enter it, while they hope to enter it.
Makkī said a strange thing, which is that he said: "If you take the meaning to be that they entered it, then «وهم يطمعون» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of ḥāl from the latent nominative pronoun in «يدخلوها»; its meaning is that they despaired of entering, so they had no hope of entering, but they entered while in despair of that. If you take its meaning to be that they have not yet entered but hope to enter through Allah's mercy, it is a resumptive mubtadaʾ and khabar."
Some said: "The sentence of His saying «لم يدخلوها» is from the speech of the people of Paradise, and the sentence of His saying «وهم يطمعون» is from the speech of the angels." ʿAṭāʾ said from Ibn ʿAbbās: "The people of the Aʿrāf call out to the people of Paradise with the greeting of peace, and they return the greeting to them. Then the people of Paradise say to the keepers: what of our companions on the heights of Paradise, why have they not entered it? And the angels say to them, in answer, «وهم يطمعون»." It is unlikely that this is sound from Ibn ʿAbbās, since it does not suit the eloquence of the Qur'an.
And «al-ṭamaʿ» here may be in its normal sense, and may be with the meaning of certainty. They said: because of the saying of the Exalted, relating from Ibrāhīm, upon our Prophet and upon him the best of prayers and peace: {والذي أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 82]; and he said:
2204 - And I do hope that God is able ... by the goodness of my certainty, my certainty.
[Translator's note: the final verse (2204) is garbled in the source (the word «يقيني» is repeated); the gloss follows what is written.]

semin-durr:165-165.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَلَماَّ نَسُواْ مَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهِ}: the pronoun in «نَسُوا» refers to those who were forbidden. «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي», that is: "when they forgot the admonition with which the righteous reminded them." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that the reminder itself is meant by it, and it is possible that what contained the reminder is meant." The Shaykh said: "These two possibilities are not clear to me." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya means by "the reminder itself" that the relative noun itself is meant as the maṣdar, as though He said: "when they forgot the reminder with which they were reminded"; and by "what contained the reminder" the very thing with which they were reminded, which is what the reminding is connected to; because when Ibn ʿAṭiyya made «ما» mean «الذي» he said: "it admits of applying to these two differing things."
His saying: {بِعَذَابٍ بَئِيسٍ}: Nāfiʿ, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read «بِيْسٍ» with a quiescent yāʾ. Ibn ʿĀmir read it with a quiescent hamza, and there are four views regarding both. The first: that this is originally a past verb which was used as a name and so inflected, like his saying, upon him be peace: "I forbid you «قيلٍ وقال»," with inflection and with citation form; likewise their saying «مُذْ شَبَّ إلى دَبَّ» and «مُذْ شَبٍّ إلى دَبٍّ»; so when it was moved to nominal status it became an adjective like niḍw and niqḍ. The second: that it is an adjective set on the pattern fiʿl, like ḥilf. The third: that its origin is «بَئيس» like the famous reading, then the hamza was softened, so two yāʾs met, then the bāʾ was given kasra by assimilation, as in righīf and shahīd; then the succession of two yāʾs after a kasra was found heavy, so the vowelled yāʾ was dropped and the word became «بِئْسٍ»; this is al-Kisāʾī's analysis. The fourth: that its origin is «بَئِس» on the pattern of katif, then the bāʾ was made to follow the hamza in kasra, then the hamza was made quiescent, then changed to yāʾ. As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, it may be a transferred verb and it may be an adjective like ḥilf.
Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read «بَيْئَسٍ» with a quiescent yāʾ between a bāʾ and a hamza both with fatḥa, and it is an adjective on the pattern fayʿal, like ḍayghan and ṣayraf, and it is frequent among adjectives. / Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿĀbis al-Kindī said:
2320 - كلاهما كان رئيساً بَيْئَساً ... يَضْرِبُ في يومِ الهياجِ القَوْنَسا
(Each of them was a chief, fierce, who struck the crown of the helmet on the day of battle.)
The rest of the Seven read «بَئِيْسٍ» on the pattern raʾīs. There are two views on it. One: that it is an adjective on the pattern faʿīl, like shadīd, and it is for intensification, and its origin is fāʿil. The second: that it is a maṣdar used descriptively, that is: "with a punishment possessing a severe severity (baʾs)," a maṣdar like nadhīr, nakīr and ʿadhīr; and similar in admitting both views is the saying of Abū l-Iṣbaʿ al-ʿAdwānī:
2321 - حَنَقَاً عَلَيَّ ولا أَرَى ... ليَ منهما شَرَّاً بئيساً
(Enraged at me, and I see from the two of them no severe evil for myself.)
It is also the reading of ʿAlī and Abū Rajāʾ.
Yaʿqūb the reader read «بَئِسَ» on the pattern of shahida, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Zayd ibn ʿAlī also read it. Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim read «بَأَس» on the pattern of ḍaraba, as a past verb.
Al-Aʿmash and Mālik ibn Dīnār read «بَأْس» as a past verb, and its origin is «بئِس» with kasra on the hamza, which he made quiescent for lightness, like «شَهْد» in his saying:
2322 - لو شَهْدَ عادَ في زمانِ تُبَّعِ
(Had he witnessed ʿĀd in the time of Tubbaʿ…)
Ibn Kathīr and the people of Mecca read «بِئِسٍ» with kasra on the bāʾ and a light hamza, and it was not made clear whether the hamza is kasra'd or quiescent.
Ṭalḥa and Khārija from Nāfiʿ read «بَيْسٍ» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and a quiescent yāʾ, like kayl, and its origin is «بَيْئَس» like ḍayghan; so he softened the hamza by turning it into yāʾ and assimilating the yāʾ into it, then lightened it by dropping, as in mayt for mayyit.
ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «بَيْئِسٍ» like the reading of Abū Bakr from him, except that he put kasra on the hamza. People have rejected this one, because fayʿil with kasra on the ʿayn is for the weak (muʿtall) roots, just as fayʿal with fatḥa is for the sound, like sayyid and ḍayghan; though it is irregular: ṣayqil with kasra, and ʿayyal with fatḥa.
Naṣr, in the transmission of Mālik ibn Dīnār from him, read «بَأَسٍ» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and hamza and genitive sīn, on the pattern jabal.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «بِئَسٍ», like kabid and ḥadhir. ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qays said:
2323 - ليتني أَلْقَى رُقَيَّةَ في ... خَلْوةٍ من غير ما بَئِسِ
(Would that I met Ruqayya in a solitude, without any harm.)
Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, in one transmission, read «بَيِّسٍ» with shadda on the yāʾ, like mayyit, and there are two analyses of it. One: that it is from al-buʾs, with no hamza in its origin, the origin being «بَيْوِس» like «مَيْوِت», and so was done to it what was done to that. The second: that its origin is with hamza, which he changed to yāʾ and then assimilated the bāʾ into the yāʾ.
[Translator's note: the source says "assimilated the bāʾ into the yāʾ"; the sense appears to require the first yāʾ into the second.]
He also read, in one transmission, «بَأَّس» with a doubled hamza; they said: he changed the yāʾ into a hamza and assimilated it into its like, as a past verb like shammara.
Another group: «بَأَسَ», like the one before it, except that the hamza is light.
Another group: «باسٍ» with an explicit alif between the bāʾ and the genitive sīn.
The people of Medina read «بِئيس» like raʾīs, except that they put kasra on the bāʾ, and this is the dialect of Tamīm in fa'īl whose ʿayn is a guttural, such as biʿīr, shiʿīr and shihīd, whether a noun or an adjective.
Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿmash read «بِئْيَسٍ» with a kasra'd yāʾ, then a quiescent hamza, then a fatḥa'd yāʾ, on the pattern of ḥidhyam and ʿithyar.
[Translator's note: the source's description says "a kasra'd yāʾ" first, where the vocalised word has a kasra'd bāʾ; translated as written.]
Al-Ḥasan read «بِئْسَ» with kasra on the bāʾ, quiescent hamza and fatḥa on the sīn, making it the one of censure, as in «بئس الرجل زيد» ("Evil is the man, Zayd"), and it was reported from Abū Bakr.
Al-Ḥasan also read likewise except with an explicit yāʾ, and its analysis is like the one before it, and it is reported from Nāfiʿ. Abū Ḥātim rejected this reading and the one before it, saying that one does not say «مررت برجلٍ بئس» ("I passed by a man evil") until it is said «بئس الرجل» or «بئس رجلاً». Al-Naḥḥās said: "This is rejected — meaning the saying of Abū Ḥātim: the grammarians have reported: 'If you do such-and-such, then fa-bihā wa-niʿmat,' that is, 'and excellent is the quality,' and the implied form is: 'evil is the punishment.'" I say: Abū Ḥātim is excused in [rejecting] the reading, for the agent is not mentioned overtly, and the agent is a pillar that may not be omitted; but it has come in the ḥadīth: "Whoever performs ablution, fa-bihā wa-niʿmat, and whoever bathes, the bath is better," so the agent of «نعمت» here is latent, / explained by the context of the speech. The Shaykh said: "So these are twenty-two readings, and the summary of their classification is that it was read with three-letter and four-letter wording: the triliteral as a noun: «بِيْسٍ، بِئْسٍ، بَيْسٍ، بَاْسٍ، بَأَسٍ، بِئِسٍ، بَئِسٍ».
And as a verb: «بِئْسَ، بِيْسَ، بَئِسَ، بَأَسَ، بَأْسَ، بَيَسَ». And the quadriliteral as a noun: «بَيْئَسٍ، بِيْئِسٍ، بَيْئِسٍ، بَيِّسٍ، بَئِيْسٍ، بِئَيْسٍ، بِئْيَسٍ». And as a verb: «بَأَّسَ».
I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ added four other readings: «بَيِسٍ» with fatḥa'd bāʾ and kasra'd yāʾ. He said: "Its origin is a kasra'd hamza, which was changed to yāʾ"; and «بَيَس» with fatḥa on both; he said: "its origin is a quiescent yāʾ and a fatḥa'd hamza, except that the vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the yāʾ and it was dropped, and the yāʾ was not turned into an alif because its vowel is incidental." And «بَأْيَسٍ» with fatḥa on the bāʾ, quiescent hamza and fatḥa on the yāʾ; he said: "and it is remote, as there is no faʿyal in the language." And «بَيْآس» on the pattern fayʿāl was read, which is strange. So these are twenty-six readings in this word, and I have verified their wording and their analyses, praise be to Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:167-167.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ}: there are several views regarding «تَأَذَّن». The first: that it has the meaning of «آذَنَ», that is, "to inform." Al-Wāḥidī said: "Most of the people of the language hold that taʾadhdhun has the meaning of īdhān, which is informing. Al-Fārisī said: 'ādhana means to inform, and adhdhana means to call out and shout for the sake of informing; and from it is the saying of the Exalted {فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ بَيْنَهُمْ} [al-Aʿrāf: 44].' He said: 'Some of the Arabs treat ādhantu as taʾadhdhantu, so they make ādhana and taʾadhdhana one in meaning; and if adhdhana means "to inform" in the dialect of some of them, then taʾadhdhana is the tafaʿʿala form of this.' It was also said that its meaning is: He decreed and made obligatory." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«تأذَّن»: your Lord resolved; and it is the tafaʿʿala form of īdhān, which is informing, because one who is resolved on a matter speaks of it to himself and informs himself of his doing it; and it was made to run in the course of a verb of oath, like «علم الله» and «شهد الله»; for that reason it was answered with what an oath is answered with, namely «ليبعثَنَّ»." Al-Ṭabarī and others said: "«تَأَذَّن» means 'He informed,'" and this is shaky from the standpoint of morphology, since the relation of «تأذَّن» to the agent differs from the relation of «أعلم», and between them there is a difference between transitivity and its absence.
His saying: {إلى يَوْمِ القيامة}: there are two views. One: that it is attached to «يَبْعَثَنَّ», and this is the sound one. The second: that it is attached to «تأذَّن»; Abū l-Baqāʾ reported it. It is not permissible that it be attached to «يُسومهم», because «مَنْ» is either relative or qualified, and the ṣila and the qualifier do not govern what precedes the relative noun and the qualified noun.

semin-durr:168-168.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أُمَماً}: it is either a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object of «قطَّعناهم», or a second object, according to what preceded, that «قَطَّعَ» includes the meaning of «صَيَّر». And «منهم الصالحون» is an adjective of «أمم». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "or a badal from it, that is, from «أمم»," meaning that it is a ḥāl from the object of «قطَّعناهم», that is: "We divided them while among them are the righteous."
His saying: {وَمِنْهُمْ دُونَ ذلك}: «منهم» is a fronted khabar, and «دون ذلك» is an adjective of an omitted qualified noun which is the mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "and among them are people or a group below that." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its meaning is: 'and among them are people who fall short of righteousness,' and like it: {وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلاَّ لَهُ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 64], meaning: 'there is none among us but has a known station.'" He means that the qualified noun was omitted and the descriptive clause put in its place, as the descriptive adverbial takes its place. And in apportioning with «مِنْ», omission of the qualified noun and putting the adjective in its place is permissible, as in their saying «منا ظَعَن ومنَّا أقام» ("among us is one who departed and among us is one who stayed"). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "If by righteousness belief is meant, then «دون» has the meaning of «غير» ('other than'), and the unbelievers are meant by it." The Shaykh said: "If he means that «دون» is synonymous with «غير», this is not correct; and if he means that it follows that whoever is below something is other than it, it is correct."
And «ذلك» is either pointing to the righteousness or pointing to the group. If it points to the righteousness, then an omitted muḍāf is necessary for the meaning to be sound, its implied form being: "and among them are those below the people of that righteousness," so that the division be balanced; and if it points to the group, that is: "and among them are those below those righteous," then there is no need to suppose / a muḍāf, because the division is balanced without it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«ودون ذلك» is an adverbial or a khabar, according to what we mentioned in His saying {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94]." There is an objection in this, in that «دون» is not a khabar.

semin-durr:138-138.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَجَاوَزْنَا ببني إِسْرَآئِيلَ}: like His saying {فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ البحر} [al-Baqara: 50], in that the bāʾ may be for transitivisation or for the ḥāl, as in the verse:

2284 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
تَدوسُ بنا الجماجمَ والتَّريبا
(… [first half elided in the source] … trampling with us the skulls and the breast-bones.)

This has already been given. جاوز is in the sense of جاز, so فاعَل is in the sense of فَعَل. al-Ḥasan, Ibrāhīm, Abū Rajāʾ and Yaʿqūb read جَوَّزنا with tashdīd, which is also in the sense of the plain فَعَل, like قَدَر and قدَّر.

His saying: {يَعْكُفُونَ} is an adjective of «قوم». The two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza) read «يعكفون» with kasra on the ʿayn, and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr; the rest with ḍamma; they are two dialects in the imperfect, like يَعْرشون. The meaning of العكوف and its derivation were given in al-Baqara.

His saying: {كَمَا لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ}: the kāf is in the position of accusative as an adjective of إلهاً, i.e. "a god like their god". About «ما» there are three views. The first: that it is a particle-type relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī), i.e. interpreted as a maṣdar; on this its ṣila is omitted, and when the ṣila of the maṣdar «ما» is omitted, the dependent of its ṣila must remain, as in their saying: «لا أكلِّمكَ ما أنَّ حِراءَ مكانَه», i.e. "as long as it is established that Ḥirāʾ is in its place". So also here, the implied form being: "as it is established for them that they have gods", so آلهة is the agent of the implied «ثبت». Abū l-Baqāʾ said of this view: "The sentence after it is its ṣila, and what makes that good is that the adverbial phrase is implied by the verb." I say: his statement as it stands is not good, because the maṣdar «ما» is not joined to a nominal sentence according to the well-known view, and according to those who allow it, it is mostly required that it convey time, as in the verse:

2285 - واصِلْ خليلَكَ ما التواصلُ ممكنٌ ... فلأَنْتَ أَوْ هُوَ عن قريبٍ ذاهبُ
(Keep up with your friend as long as keeping up is possible, for either you or he will soon be gone.)

But what he means is that the preposition and its genitive noun is implied by a verb, and so it reverts to a verbal sentence, i.e. "as there is established for them gods".

The second: that «ما» is a preventer (kāffa) of the comparative kāf from operating, for it is a preposition. This is as «رُبَّ» is prevented, so that nominal and verbal sentences follow it; but that is not obligatory; rather with the kāf and «رب», when the redundant «ما» follows them, two options are allowed: operation and non-operation; and on that is the poet's verse:

2286 - ونَنْصُرُ مولانا ونعلمُ أنَّه ... كما الناسُ مجرومٌ عليه وجارِمٌ
(We support our patron and know that he, like people, is wronged and a wrongdoer.)

and another's verse:

2287 - رُبَّما الجامِلُ المُؤَبَّلُ فيهمُ ... وعناجيجُ بينهنَّ المَهارى
(How often among them are the herd of camels set aside and excellent steeds with fine riding camels among them.)

It is transmitted with «الناس» and «الجامل» both nominative and genitive. This is when operation is possible; as for when it is not possible, it must be a preventer, as in this verse if «ما» is said to be redundant.

The third: that «ما» is in the sense of «الذي», and «لهم» is its ṣila, with a latent nominative pronoun in it, and «آلهة» a badal from that pronoun. The implied form is: "like that which is established, it, for them as gods". Abū l-Baqāʾ said of this view: "The returning pronoun is omitted and «آلهة» is a badal from it, the implied form being: like that which is, it, for them." His calling this omission is a looseness, because nominative pronouns, when they are agents, are not described as omitted but as latent.

semin-durr:139-139.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ هؤلاء مُتَبَّرٌ مَّا هُمْ فِيهِ}: «هؤلاء» points to those who devoted themselves to the idols, and about «مُتَبَّر» there are two views. One: that it is the khabar of إنَّ, and «ما» a relative in the sense of «الذي», and «هم فيه» a nominal sentence as its ṣila with its returning pronoun, and this relative is nominative by the passive participle, so you have predicated with a single word by which you have made something nominative. The second: that the relative is a mubtadaʾ and «مُتَبَّر» its khabar preposed to it, the sentence being the khabar of إنَّ. al-Zamakhsharī said: "In making «هؤلاء» the subject of «إنَّ», and preposing the khabar of the mubtadaʾ from the sentence that serves as its khabar, there is a branding of the idol-worshippers' expression, that they are the ones exposed to destruction and that it will certainly not pass them by, and that it is a fixed lot for them, so as to warn them of the outcome of what they asked for and make hateful to them what they loved." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "What he said, that he preposed the khabar of the mubtadaʾ from the sentence that serves as khabar, is not necessary, because the better analysis of the like of this is that «مُتَبَّر» is the khabar of إنَّ and what follows it is nominative", and he mentioned what I have established, and likened it to your saying: «إنَّ زيداً مضروب غلامه». He said: "The better is that «غلامه» be nominative by «مضروب»."

Then he mentioned the second view, which is that «مُتَبَّر» is a preposed khabar of the sentence, and he made it the weaker, and it is as he said, because the basic rule for khabars is that they be single words, so what is possible in them is not departed from. However, al-Zamakhsharī did not mention that as a definite choice but as one of the two views. This may be preferable in his view on the strength of the meaning he mentioned; and when the matter turns between a verbal preponderance and a semantic one, taking the semantic into account is preferable, and I do not think that anything led al-Zamakhsharī to that except what I have mentioned.

And His saying: {وَبَاطِلٌ مَّا كَانُواْ} is like {مُتَبَّرٌ مَّا هُمْ فِيهِ} in the permissibility of the two views and what was mentioned about them.

التَتْبير is destruction, and from it comes «التِّبْر», which is gold fragments, because of people's perishing over it. It is also said: التتبير is breaking and smashing, and from it comes التِّبْر, because it is gold fragments.

semin-durr:140-140.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَغَيْرَ الله}: the hamza is for denial and rebuke. About the accusative of «غير» there are two views. One: that it is a direct object of «أبغيكم» with the lām omitted, the implied form being: أبغي لكم غيرَ الله, i.e. "I seek for you"; so when the particle was dropped the verb reached it directly, and this is not regular. On this, about «إلهاً» there are two views: one, which is the apparent, that it is a tamyīz (specification) of «غير»; the second, that it is a ḥāl, mentioned by the Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān), and there is something to consider in it. The second of the two views about «غير»: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from «إلهاً», and «إلهاً» is the direct object of «أَبْغيكم» as established, the original being: أبغي لكم إلهاً غير الله, so «غير الله» is an adjective of «إله», and when the adjective of an indefinite noun was preposed to it, it became accusative as a ḥāl. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "«غير» is accusative by an implied verb; this is the apparent; and it may be a ḥāl." This implying of a verb that he mentioned is not needed; and if he means that it is by occupation (ishtighāl), that is not sound, because its condition is that the explainer operate on the pronoun of the first or on something related to it.

His saying: {وَهُوَ فَضَّلَكُمْ} may be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl: either from «الله» or from those addressed, because the sentence contains both of their pronouns; and it may have no position, being a resumption.

semin-durr:141-141.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِذْ أَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ}: The majority read it with the verb attributed to the One who magnifies Himself (the plural "We"). Ibn ʿĀmir read «أنجاكم», attributed to the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, following His saying «وهو فَضَّلكم». It is also read «نَجَّيناكم» with tashdīd. The disagreement over doubling «يقتلون» and lightening it was given a little before this. The i'rab of this entire verse was given in al-Baqara, so there is no need to repeat it.

semin-durr:142-142.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَوَاعَدْنَا موسى ثَلاَثِينَ}: The disagreement over وَعَدْنا and واعَدْنا has been given. The adverbial after it came as a second object with an omitted muḍāf; it cannot be an adverbial because of the corruption of the meaning, in al-Baqara and so likewise here, i.e. "We promised him the completion of thirty (nights)", or "the course of them", or "the intimate converse of them".

His saying: {وَأَتْمَمْنَاهَا بِعَشْرٍ}: about this pronoun there are two views. One: that it refers to the appointment understood from «واعَدْنا», i.e. "and We completed his appointment with ten". The second: that it refers to thirty; so said al-Ḥawfī. The Shaykh said: "It does not appear so, because the thirty were not deficient so as to be completed with ten." The tamyīz of «عشر» is omitted because the speech indicates it, i.e. "We completed it with ten nights". In the copy (muṣḥaf) of Ubayy it is «تَمَّمناها» with doubling, transitivised by the doubling.

His saying: {فَتَمَّ مِيقَاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ}: The difference between الميقات and الوقت: الميقات is that in which an action of some kind has been fixed, whereas الوقت is the time of a thing without fixing or determining an action. About the accusative of «أربعين» there are several views. One: that it is a ḥāl. al-Zamakhsharī said: "{أربعين} is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. 'it was completed, reaching this number'." The Shaykh said: "On this the ḥāl is not «أربعين»; rather the ḥāl is this omitted element, which contradicts his statement." I say: There is no contradiction in it, because the grammarians have continually attributed the ruling to the remaining dependent after the omission of its operator for which it stands, and it has witnesses, among them: «زيد في الدار أو عندك», where they say the preposition phrase and the adverbial are the khabar, whereas the khabar in reality is the implied event that operates in them. So also they say: «جاء زيد بثيابه», «بثيابه» is a ḥāl, whereas the ḥāl is really what operates in it, and so on. al-Fārisī implied it as «معدوداً», saying: "like your saying «تمَّ القوم عشرين رجلاً», i.e. counted at this number", and it is a fine implication.

The second: that «أربعين» is accusative as a direct object. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because its meaning is 'reached', like their saying بَلَغَتْ أرضك جَرِيبَيْن", i.e. he implies in «تَمَّ» the meaning of «بلغ». The third: that it is accusative as an adverbial. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is sound that «أربعين» be an adverbial insofar as it is a number of periods of time." There is something to consider in this: how can it be an adverbial of the completion, when completion occurs only with the last part of those periods? Unless by a far-fetched figurative sense: that every part of the parts of the time, whether first or last, if it falls short, the completion goes. The fourth: that it is accusative as a tamyīz. The Shaykh said: "The original is: فتمَّ أربعون ميقاتُ ربه; then completion was attributed to ميقات, and «أربعون» became accusative as tamyīz, so it is transferred from being an agent," meaning that it is like His saying: {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [Maryam: 4]. This that he said, and made the apparent view, is problematic given what he himself mentioned in refuting al-Ḥawfī, where he said: "the thirty were not deficient so as to be completed"; likewise it should be said here that the forty were not deficient so as to be completed; so how does he imply «فتمَّ أربعون ميقات ربه»? If he gives an answer here, it is an answer there to the one who objected to him.

And His saying: {فَتَمَّ مِيقَاتُ رَبِّهِ أَرْبَعِينَ}: about this sentence there are two views. The more evident: that it is for emphasis, because from His saying before that «وأَتْمَمْناها بعشر» it was understood that it was forty nights. It is also said: rather it is for establishing a new meaning, lest someone imagine ten hours or something else, which is very far-fetched.

His saying «ربِّه» and He did not say "Our appointment", following «واعَدْنا», because in showing this noble name there is an acknowledgement of Allah's lordship over him and His putting him right.

His saying «هارونَ»: the majority have fatḥa on its nūn, and there are three views about it. The first: that it is genitive as a badal from «أخيه». The second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān of it. The third: that it is accusative by an implied "I mean" (aʿnī). It is also read anomalously «هارونُ» with ḍamma, and there are two views about it: one, that it is a vocative from which the vocative particle was dropped, i.e. "O Aaron", like {يُوسُفُ أَعْرِضْ} [Yūsuf: 29]; the second, that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "he is Aaron", and this in meaning is like the earlier view that it is accusative by an implied "I mean", for both are a cutting off (qaṭʿ). Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Were it read with the nominative", and he mentioned both, as if he were not aware that it is a reading.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {تِلْقَآءَ}: accusative as an adverbial of place (ẓarf makān). Makkī said: "Its plural is talāqiyy." I say: because the pattern of «tilqāʾ» is tifʿāl, like timthāl, and timthāl and its class are pluralized on tafāʿīl, so the additional yāʾ met the yāʾ which is the lām of the word and they were assimilated, becoming «talāqiyy». «Al-tilqāʾ» is originally a maṣdar, then it was made to denote place, i.e., the direction of meeting and facing. They said: no maṣdar has come on tifʿāl with kasra on the tāʾ except two words, «al-tilqāʾ» and «al-tibyān»; all other maṣdars have fatḥa, such as «al-tardād» and «al-takrār», while among nouns it takes kasra, such as «timthāl», «timsāḥ» and «tiqṣār».
And in His saying {صُرِفَتْ أَبْصَارُهُمْ} is a weighty benefit, namely that they did not turn toward the Fire except compelled to it, not by their own choice, because the place of evil is to be avoided. The disagreement of the readers on such as «تلقاء أصحاب», regarding dropping one of the two hamzas, keeping it or softening it, has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara. Al-Aʿmash read «وإذا قُلِبَتْ», which is contrary to the written copy (al-sawād), like the reading «لم يدخلوها وهم ساخطون» or «وهم طامِعُون», though this is closer. And «قالوا» is the apodosis of «إذا» and the governor in it.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying, the Exalted: {مَآ أغنى}: it may be interrogative, for rebuke and reproach, and this is the apparent sense; and it may be negative. And His saying: «وما كنتم»: «ما» is a maṣdar particle, so that a maṣdar be conjoined to its like, i.e., "your gathering and your being arrogant did not avail you". It was also read «تستكثرون» with the thāʾ of three dots, from abundance (kathra).

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أهؤلاء الذين أَقْسَمْتُمْ}: in this sentence there are two views. One: that it is in the position of accusative by the preceding saying, i.e., "they said: 'What availed...' and they said: 'Are these those who...'". The second: that it is an independent sentence not entering within the scope of the saying. On the first view, those pointed to are the people of Paradise, those who say it are the people of the Aʿrāf, and those spoken to are the people of the Fire. The meaning: the people of the Aʿrāf said to the people of the Fire: "Are these who are in Paradise today the ones you used to swear would not enter Paradise? By Allah's mercy and bounty, enter Paradise", i.e., they said to them, or it was said to them: "Enter Paradise."
On the second view, which is the resumptive, there is disagreement about the one pointed to. It was said: they are the people of the Aʿrāf, and the speaker is an angel whom Allah commands with this saying, and those spoken to are the people of the Fire. It was said: those pointed to are the people of Paradise, the speakers are the angels, and those spoken to are the people of the Fire. It was said: those pointed to are the people of the Aʿrāf and they are also the ones saying it, and those spoken to are the disbelievers, and His saying «ادخلوا الجنة» is also from the saying of the people of the Aʿrāf, i.e., they turn back and address one another, saying: "Enter Paradise." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "His saying «أهؤلاء الذين أَقْسَمْتم لا ينالهم الله برحمة» is from the speech of the people of the Aʿrāf, and His saying «ادخلوا» is from the speech of Allah, the Exalted, and this is by implying a saying, i.e., 'Then Allah said to them: Enter it'; its counterpart is His saying, the Exalted: {يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِّنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 35], this being from the speech of the council, and «فماذا تأمرون؟» being from the speech of Pharaoh, i.e., 'Then he said: What do you command?'."
Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn read «أَدْخِلوا الجنة» as an imperative from adkhala, and there are two interpretations of it. One: that those commanded to cause entry are the angels, i.e., "Cause these to enter, O angels." Then He addressed mankind after addressing the angels, saying: "There is no fear upon you", and the sentence of «لا خوف» then has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The second: that those commanded to do so are the people of the Aʿrāf, the implied form being: "Cause yourselves to enter", so the object is omitted in both views. Similar to this reading here is His saying, the Exalted: {أَدْخِلُوا آل فرعون} [Ghāfir: 46], which will come, if Allah wills, except that the object there is expressed in one of the two readings.
The sentence of «لا خوف» on this is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., "cause yourselves to enter, not fearing". ʿIkrima read «دَخَلوا» as an active past verb. Ṭalḥa, Ibn Wathāb and al-Nakhaʿī read «أُدْخِلوا», from udkhila, a passive past verb in the declarative; on both of these the negated sentence is in the position of accusative by an implied saying, that saying itself being accusative as a ḥāl, i.e., "being told: there is no fear upon them".

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَنْ أَفِيضُواْ}: like its other occurrences, it admits explicative and maṣdar readings. And «من الماء» is attached to «أفيضوا» in one of two ways: either by omitting an object, i.e., "something of the water", so it is partitive — they asked of them a small part; or by implying in «أفيضوا» the meaning of what is made transitive with «مِنْ», i.e., "bestow upon us from it by pouring." And His saying: {أَوْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ}: «أو» here is in its normal sense of requiring one of two things, either as option or permission or otherwise as befits it. On this it may be asked: how was it said «حرَّمهما» with the pronoun returning in the dual, when the right of one who says that it is for one of two things is that it return in the singular, as established more than once? They answered that the meaning is: He forbade each of the two. It was also said that «أو» has the meaning of «و», so the return of the pronoun is plain on it.
And «ممّا»: «ما» may be a relative noun, which is the apparent sense, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e., "or from that which Allah has provided you with (razaqakumūhu)"; it may also be a maṣdar particle, and there are two figurative aspects in it: one, that they asked of them the pouring of the very provision, as an exaggeration in that; the second, that the passive participle is intended by the maṣdar, as in His saying: {كُلُواْ واشربوا مِن رِّزْقِ الله} [al-Baqara: 60] in one of its two views. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "or from what Allah has provided you of other drinks, since it enters into the ruling of pouring. It is also possible that the meaning is: 'or throw to us from what Allah has provided you of food and fruit', as in his saying:
2205 - I fed her chopped straw and cold water ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ."
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "His saying 'and throw to us from what Allah has provided you of food and fruit' has two possibilities.
