One: that His saying «أفيضوا» is made to imply the meaning of «ألقوا» 'throw to us' from the water or from what Allah has provided you, so the conjunction is sound; and it may be, and this is the apparent sense of his words, that he implied a verb after «أو» which reaches «مما رزقكم الله», namely «ألقوا». These are two views among the grammarians regarding what is conjoined to something by a conjunction when the verb does not reach it, and the sound one of them is implication of meaning (taḍmīn), not implying a verb." I say: al-Zamakhsharī means that «ifāḍa» in origin is used for water and what runs like it among liquids; so his saying "or from other drinks" is a correction to make «ifāḍa» govern it; for if «مما رزقكم الله» were taken as food and fruit, ascribing «ifāḍa» to them would not be good except figuratively; so he mentioned the way of figurative use by his saying «ألقوا», then the Shaykh explained it as he mentioned, and it is as he said; for feeding is not ascribed to water. His saying "either by taḍmīn", i.e., "so I nourished her", and similarly:
2206 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... and they lined the eyebrows and the eyes
and his saying:
2207 - Would that your husband had set out ... girding on a sword and carrying a spear
and His saying, the Exalted: {والذين تَبَوَّءُوا الدار والإيمان} [al-Ḥashr: 9]; a good number of such cases has preceded. Some claimed that His saying {أَوْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ الله} is general, with the water mentioned earlier falling under it; it is remote, or impossible, because of the conjunction by «أو».
And «tahrīm» here is prevention, as in his saying:
2208 - It is forbidden to my eyes to be given sleep ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

semin-durr:51-51.t: His saying, the Exalted: {الذين}: it may be in the position of genitive, which is the apparent sense, as an adjective (naʿt) or badal (substitute) of «الكافرين»; and it may be nominative or accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off). And His saying «وغَرَّتْهم» is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause). And His saying «فاليومَ» is accusative by what follows it. And His saying «كما» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e., "He forgets them with a forgetting like their forgetting the meeting of", i.e., by their abandoning; and «ما» is a maṣdar particle. It is also possible that the kāf is causal, i.e., "We abandoned them on account of their forgetting the meeting of their Day". And «يومهم» may be extended in usage (muttasaʿ fīhi), so that the maṣdar is annexed to it as it is annexed to the direct object; it may also be that the object is omitted, with the annexation to the adverbial of the event, i.e., "the meeting of the punishment in their Day". And His saying «وما كانوا»: «ما» is a maṣdar particle conjoined to its sister governed in the genitive by the kāf, i.e., "and as they used to reject Our signs", and the causal sense in it is plain.

semin-durr:87-87.t:
His words, the Exalted: {وَطَآئِفَةٌ لَّمْ يْؤْمِنُواْ}: conjoined to the first «طائفة», which is the ism of kāna; «لم يؤمنوا» is conjoined to «آمَنوا», which is the khabar of kāna; so a noun is conjoined to a noun and a khabar to a khabar. Similar is if you said: "ʿAbd Allāh was going and Bakr leaving": you conjoin a nominative to its like, and likewise an accusative. The qualifier of the second «طائفة» is omitted because the qualifier of the first indicates it, the implied form being: "and a group of you who did not believe"; the object of belief is also omitted in the second because the first indicates it, the implied form being: "did not believe in that with which I was sent". The qualification by «منكم», overt or implied, is what made it valid for «طائفة» to occur as the ism of kāna, in that the ism in this chapter is like the mubtadaʾ, and the mubtadaʾ is not indefinite except with a justifier, as was pointed out earlier.
His words: {فاصبروا}: the pronoun may be for the believers among his people, or for the disbelievers among them, or for both groups, and this is the evident view: the believers were commanded to be patient so that victory and triumph may be theirs, and the disbelievers are commanded to it so that Allah may give the believers victory over them, per His words, the Exalted: {قُلْ تَرَبَّصُواْ} [الطور: 31]; or by way of contention with them, i.e. "be patient, for you will know who is victorious and who prevails", while knowing that the triumph is his. «حتى» means only «إلى» (until). In his words «بيننا» the speaker's pronoun predominates over the addressee's, since what is meant is "between us all, believer and disbeliever", and there is no need to claim an omitted conjoined word, its implied form being "between us and between you".

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His words, the Exalted: {والذين آمَنُواْ}: conjoined to the kāf, and «يا شعيبُ» is a parenthetical clause between the two conjoined elements.
His words: «أو لَتَعُودُنَّ» is conjoined to the answer of the first oath, since the implied form is: "By Allah, we will drive you out, and the believers, or you will return." The returning is attributed to the pronoun of the prophet and those who believed with him. «عاد» has two usages in their tongue: one, which is the original, is returning to what one was upon in the first state. The second is its use in the sense of ṣāra (became), and then it raises the ism and puts the khabar in the accusative, so it is not content with a nominative and needs an accusative; this is according to some. Others forbade its being in the sense of ṣāra. Among its occurrences in the sense of ṣāra, according to some, is the poet's saying:
2246 - I raised him until, when I left him ... a brother to the people, his moustache needing no wiping,
and with pure milk, until he became a tall, lanky man, ... when he stood, his withers matched the withers of the stallion.
He made the pronoun of the first nominative by «عاد» and put «جَعْداً» in the accusative by it; and whoever forbids that makes the accusative a ḥāl. But they found a difficulty in it being in its original sense, namely that Shuʿayb, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was never upon their religion nor in their creed. How then is it good to say «أو لتعودُنَّ», i.e. "you will return to your first state", with the address to him and his followers? Three answers were given: First: this statement was from their chiefs, by which they intended to deceive the common people and give them the impression that he had been on their religion and in their creed. Second: his returning means his returning to his state of silence before his mission, because before he was sent to them he used to conceal his faith and was silent about them, seeing something other than Allah among their objects of worship. Third: the group predominates over the individual, because when they accompanied him in the expulsion, the ruling of returning to the creed was drawn onto him and onto them, giving them predominance over him. As for if we make it in the sense of ṣayyara (made/became), there is no difficulty in that, since the meaning is: "you will become part of our creed after you were not"; so «في مِلَّتنا» is a ḥāl on the first view, a khabar on the second; and he transitivized «عاد» with «في» of containment, as though the creed were for them like a vessel surrounding them.
His words: {أَوَلَوْ كُنَّا كَارِهِينَ}: the interrogative is for denial, the implied form being: "Is either of these two things found among you: I mean expelling from the town and returning to the creed, in every circumstance, even when we dislike that?" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The hamza is interrogative and the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, its implied form being: 'Will you return us to your creed while we dislike it?'" The Shaykh said: "This is not the wāw of ḥāl but the wāw of conjunction, conjoining this ḥāl to an omitted ḥāl, like his saying, peace be upon him: 'Turn back the beggar, even with a burnt hoof (wa-law bi-ẓilfin muḥraq)'; the meaning is not 'turn him back in the state of giving him alms with a burnt hoof', but 'turn him back accompanied by alms, even accompanied by a burnt hoof'." I say: this matter has already preceded, namely that it is valid to call it wāw of ḥāl and wāw of conjunction, and its verification; and were it not for its repetition, I would not have repeated it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«لو» here means «إنْ» because it is for the future; it is also possible that it is in its original sense, and the meaning is: 'even if we were disliking in this state.'" His statement "because it is for the future" is disputed.

semin-durr:89-89.t:
His words, the Exalted: {إِنْ عُدْنَا}: a condition whose apodosis is omitted according to the majority, i.e. "then we have forged", omitted because what precedes indicates it; according to Abū Zayd, al-Mubarrad and the Kufans it is His words «فقد افترَيْنا», but this is rejected because, had it been an apodosis by itself, the fāʾ would have been obligatory in it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«قد افترَيْنا» is in the sense of the future because it has not occurred, but it stands in the place of the apodosis of «إنْ عُدْنا», and it was valid for «قد» to enter here because they treated forging, upon returning, as though occurring, and so paired it with qad; the sense is as though: 'We have forged now, if we intend to return.'"
On this clause there are two views. The first: it is a resumptive statement with the sense of wonder, as al-Zamakhsharī said, as though it were said: "How much we lie against Allah if we return to disbelief!" The second: it is the answer to an omitted oath from which the lām has been omitted, the implied form being: "By Allah, we have indeed forged"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this as well. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it a possibility and recited:
2247 - I kept my wealth and turned away from the heights ... and met my guests with a frowning face.
He said: "as you say 'I have forged against Allah if I speak to so-and-so'." Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not recite the verse after this one, which is the place of the benefit because it contains the condition, namely:
If I do not launch a raid on Ibn Hind, ... may it never be without the plunder of lives one day.
His words: {بَعْدَ إِذْ نَجَّانَا} is accusative by «نعود», i.e. "it is not for us, nor is it right for us, to return after we have been rescued from it".
His words: {إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ}: there are two views on this exception. One: it is connected (muttaṣil). The other: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). Then those who say connected differ: some said it is an exception from general times, the implied form being: "It is not for us to return to it at any time except at the time of Allah's willing that", and this is conceivable for everyone other than Shuʿayb, for Allah does not will that for the prophets, because He has protected them. Some said it is an exception from general states. The implied form being: "It is not for us to return to it in any state except in the state of the willing of Allah the Exalted." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It is possible that he intends an exception of what Allah may enjoin on the believers as worship, of the acts of devotion done by the disbelievers; for when he said to them 'we shall not return to your creed', he then feared that Allah might enjoin some act of the disbelievers, so that a heretic would object and say: 'this is a return to our creed', so he excepted the will of Allah regarding what might be enjoined."
The Shaykh said: "This possibility is not valid, because His words «بعد إذ نجَّانا اللهُ منها» only mean salvation from disbelief and sins, not from acts of piety." I say: Ibn al-Anbārī related this statement from the Muʿtazila who do not believe in divine will (irāda), then said: "This statement's import is remote, because it entails dividing the creed." It was also said: this is an exception in the way of submission and courtesy.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This interpretation is shaky on account of the futurity of the exception; had the words been 'illā in shāʾa', this interpretation would be strong." What he said is an oversight, because the past is made future after the conditional «إنْ», as the imperfect is made pure future by the maṣdar-forming «أَنْ».
It was also said: the pronoun in His words «فيها» does not refer back to the creed but to the forgery, the implied form being: "It is not for us to return to the forgery unless our Lord wills." It is good were it not for its remoteness. He repeated here His words «بيننا وبين قومنا», unlike {حتى يَحْكُمَ الله بَيْنَنَا} [الأعراف: 87], to increase the emphasis on distinguishing him and those of his people who followed him. It has already been explained that al-fatḥ means judgment in the language of Ḥimyar; it was said in the language of Murād, and he recited:
2248 - Let a messenger convey to the Banū ʿIṣm ... that I am independent of your judging (fatāḥatikum).
His words: «عِلْماً» is accusative as tamyīz, transferred from the agent, the implied form being: "the knowledge of our Lord encompassed everything", like His words, the Exalted: {واشتعل الرأس شَيْباً} [مريم: 4].

semin-durr:90-90.t:
His words, the Exalted: {إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً لَّخَاسِرُونَ}: idhan is a particle of answer and consequence; it has been discussed at length, along with people's disagreement about it. Here it is parenthetical between the ism and the khabar. Some imagined and made this «إذاً» the temporal «idhā» in the future, as in your saying: "I will keep to you idhā jiʾtanī" (when you come to me), i.e. the time of your coming. He said: "Then the clause to which it is annexed was omitted; the original is: 'You, idhā ittabaʿtumūhu (when you follow him), are losers'; so idhā is a ẓarf and the operator in it is «لخاسرون»; then the clause annexed to it, namely 'ittabaʿtumūhu', was omitted, and tanwīn was given as compensation for it; when the tanwīn, which is sukūn, was introduced, two sukūns met, it and the alif before it, so the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the form remained 'idhan' as you see. This speaker claimed that this is permissible by analogy with the idhā of the past in their sayings 'ḥīnaʾidhin' and 'yawmaʾidhin': just as the tanwīn there is compensation for a clause according to the majority, so also here." The Shaykh rejected this, saying that this ruling is not established for the future idhā anywhere else, so that this could be analogized to it. I say: this is not binding, since that speaker could say: "I have found another place, namely His words, the Exalted: {إِنَّآ إِذاً لَّظَالِمُونَ} [يوسف: 79]."
I have seen the words of Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn al-Qarāfī on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ when they asked him about selling fresh dates for dried dates, and he said: "Do fresh dates shrink when they dry?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then no, idhan": that this «idhan» is the temporal «idhā»; he said: like that in His words, the Exalted: {إِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الأرض} [الزلزلة: 1], so the clause was omitted, and he mentioned it to the end. When I saw it I was astonished beyond measure how this could come from him, until I saw it in the Shaykh's book at this place from someone, unnamed, and my astonishment at him went away; if that speaker was not al-Qarāfī, then he has a predecessor in the matter, otherwise the source is one; the apparent view is that he is someone else.
His words «إنكم»: it is the answer to the oath prepared for by the lām. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the answer to the oath prepared for by the lām in His words «لئن اتبعتم شعيباً», and the answer to the condition? I say: His words {إِنَّكُمْ إِذاً لَّخَاسِرُونَ} fill the place of both answers." The Shaykh said: "What the grammarians say is that the answer to the condition is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it, and therefore the verb of the condition must be past. If he meant by 'filling the place of both' that mentioning it sufficed in place of mentioning the answer to the condition, that is close. If he meant it from the standpoint of the grammatical craft, it is not as he claimed; because it is impossible for a clause both to have no grammatical position and to have one." I say: this matter has been discussed repeatedly, with the Shaykh's objection to him and the answer to it, so I do not repeat it, being content with what preceded. By his words "because it is impossible for a clause to have a position..." to the end, the Shaykh means that, from the aspect of being the answer to the condition, it calls for a grammatical position, namely the jussive; and from the aspect of being the answer to the oath, it calls for there being none, since the clause which is the answer to the oath has no position, because it is among the resumptive clauses that are begun with, and it is established that an initial clause has no position.

semin-durr:92-92.t:
His words, the Exalted: {الذين كَذَّبُواْ شُعَيْباً}: there are five views. The first: this relative is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is the comparative clause after it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In this inchoative there is the sense of specification, as though it were said: 'Those who denied Shuʿayb are the ones specifically destroyed and uprooted, as if they had never dwelt in their home, because those who followed Shuʿayb Allah the Exalted had saved.'" I say: his statement "it gives specification" is the meaning of the jurists' statement "it gives restriction", with disagreement among them on that, if you say "Zayd is the knower"; the disagreement about your saying "the knower is Zayd" is better known than about what is said in the fronted mubtadaʾ.
The second: the khabar is the second relative itself and its khabar, since the second relative is a mubtadaʾ and the clause {كَانُواْ هُمُ الخاسرين} is in the position of nominative as its khabar, and it and its khabar are the khabar of the first, with {كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْاْ} either parenthetical or a ḥāl from the agent of «كذَّبوا». The third: the second relative is a khabar after a khabar for the first relative, the first khabar being the comparative clause as before. The fourth: the relative is a badal from His earlier words {الذين كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوْمِهِ} [الأعراف: 90], as though He said: "The chiefs who disbelieved among them, who denied Shuʿayb, said", and His words {لَئِنِ اتبعتم شُعَيْباً} are governed by the saying, so it is not foreign. The fifth: it is a ṣifa of it, i.e. of {الذين كفروا من قومه}. This is Abū l-Baqāʾ's expression, and the Shaykh followed him on it. It is better to say: a badal from «الملأ» or a naʿt of it, because it is the one being spoken of and the relative is a ṣifa of it, and the comparative clause on these two views is a ḥāl from the agent of «كذَّبوا».
As for the second relative, it has already been stated that it may be a khabar from two perspectives, namely its being first or second; it may also be a badal from the agent of «يَغْنَوا», or accusative by an implied "aʿnī" (I mean), or a mubtadaʾ with what follows as khabar. This is the evident view, so that each clause is independent in itself. On this view al-Zamakhsharī also mentioned that the inchoative gives specification; he said: "i.e. they are the ones specified with the great loss, not his followers", and this has been explained earlier.
His words: {كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْاْ}: yaghnawn means "to dwell"; one says ghaniya bi-l-makān yaghnā fīhi, i.e. he dwelt a long time. Some restricted it to dwelling in a life of ease, so it is more specific than mere dwelling. Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur said:
2249 - They indeed dwelt (ghanaw) in it in the softest of lives ... in the shade of a king with firm tent-pegs.
It was said: the meaning of the verse here is from ghinā (wealth), which is the opposite of poverty; al-Zajjāj said this, saying: "ghaniya in such a place: when his stay in it is long, being independent through it of others."

semin-durr:93-93.t: His words, the Exalted: {فَكَيْفَ آسى}: «كيف» here is like «كيف» in {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ} [البقرة: 28], and the discussion of «أَسي» and its chapter has preceded. Ibn Waththāb, Ibn Muṣarrif and al-Aʿmash read «إيسَى» with kasra on the hamza which is the imperfect prefix; it was already stated that this is the dialect of Banū Akhyal, and the report of Laylā al-Akhyaliyya in al-Fātiḥa. Necessarily the fāʾ (the initial radical) after it turns into yāʾ, because the original is "aʾsā" with two hamzas.

semin-durr:94-94.t: His words, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَخَذْنَا}: this is a vacated exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), and «أَخَذْنا» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. The implied form is: "We did not send except seizing its people". A past verb does not occur after «إلا» except under one of two conditions: either a preceding verb, like this verse, or that it be accompanied by «قد», such as: "mā Zaydun illā qad qāma"; if both conditions are absent it is impossible, so "mā Zaydun illā qāma" is not permissible.

semin-durr:95-95.t:
His words, the Exalted: {ثُمَّ بَدَّلْنَا مَكَانَ السيئة الحسنة}: there are two views on «مكان». The more evident: it is a direct object, not a ẓarf, the meaning being: "We exchanged, in place of the bad state, the good state"; so the good is what is taken and attained, and "the place of the bad" is what is left and departed, and it is what the bāʾ accompanies in a construction like this, if one said in its parallel: "baddaltu Zaydan bi-ʿAmr", where Zayd is taken and ʿAmr left. This verification has already been given in al-Baqara in two places, the first: {فَبَدَّلَ الذين ظَلَمُواْ} [الأعراف: 59] and the second: {وَمَن يُبَدِّلْ نِعْمَةَ الله} [الأعراف: 211]; so «مكان» and «الحسنة» are two objects, except that the verb reached one of them by itself, namely «الحسنة», and the other with omission of the preposition, namely «مكان». The second: it is accusative as a ẓarf, the implied form being: "Then We exchanged in the place of the bad the good"; but this should be rejected because baddala needs two objects, one of them with the bāʾ dropped.
His words: {حتى عَفَوْاْ}: «حتى» here denotes a limit; whoever implies it as «إلى» only intends to explain the meaning, not the grammar, because the prepositional «حتى» is joined only to an imperfect made accusative by an implied «أن», since it is in the implied form entering the maṣdar formed from it and the verb; as for the past, the omission of «أن» with it is not regular, so it is not implied with it as a preposition entering the maṣdar-forming «أن», i.e. "ḥattā an ʿafaw"; and this is what Abū l-Baqāʾ's statement should be taken to mean: "ḥattā ʿafaw: ilā an ʿafaw."
The meaning of «عَفَوا» here is "they multiplied", from ʿafā l-siʿr when it increased, and from it "and let the beards grow (aʿfū l-liḥā)"; one says ʿafāhu and aʿfāhu, triliteral and quadriliteral. Zuhayr said:
2250 - Is that she, or a lean-bellied, wild ass ... on which is the ʿafāʾ (abundant hair) of his ʿaqīqa?
In the ḥadīth: "When the fur grows abundant (ʿafā l-wabar) and the saddle sore heals, ʿumra becomes lawful for whoever intends it." Al-Zamakhsharī recited on it the words of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
2251 - By a lion-haunted lowland whose vegetation is abundant (ʿāfin) ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
and the words of Labīd:
2252 - But we bite the sword into them, ... in the legs of the fat-abundant (ʿāfiyāt al-shaḥm), humped camels.
This root was verified in al-Baqara.
His words: {فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ}: Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is conjoined to «عَفَوا»." He means: and to what is conjoined to it as well, I mean that the seizing is not caused only by their abundance, but by it and by their saying that ignorant statement; because the meaning is not that He seized them suddenly merely because of their multitude and the growth of their wealth, but by the two things together; rather the evident view is that it was by their saying that alone.
His words: {وَهُمْ لاَ يَشْعُرُونَ} is also a ḥāl, and it is in force emphasizing, because «بغتة» gives the same benefit, whether we parse «بغتة» as a ḥāl or a maṣdar.

semin-durr:96-96.t: It was already stated that Ibn ʿĀmir reads «لفتَّحنا» with intensification, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar al-Thaqafī and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī agreed with him here.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أَفَأَمِنَ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the thing conjoined to, and why was the first conjoined with fāʾ and the second with wāw? I say: what it is conjoined to is His words «فَأَخَذْناهم بغتةً», and His words «ولو أنَّ أهل القرى ... يكسبون» came as a parenthetical clause between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to. It was conjoined with fāʾ only because the meaning is: 'they did and made, so We seized them suddenly; after that, did the people of the towns feel safe that Our might would come upon them by night, and did the people of the towns feel safe that Our might would come upon them in the forenoon?'" The Shaykh said: "What he mentioned is a retreat from his school in the like of this to the school of the group; for his school regarding a hamza at the head of a conjunction particle is to imply something conjoined to between the hamza and the conjunction particle, while the school of the group is that the conjunction particle is intended to come first, and was merely delayed, with the interrogative hamza preceding it by the strength of its right to precede at the start of speech." The verification of this has been given more than once, and al-Zamakhsharī here did not imply anything conjoined to between them, but made what is after the fāʾ conjoined to the preceding clauses, namely His words «فأخذناهم بغتة».
His words {بَيَاتاً}: it was stated at the beginning of the sūra that it may be a ḥāl and may be a ẓarf.
His words: {وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ} is a circumstantial clause, and the evident view is that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «بَيَاتاً», because it carries a pronoun by occurring as a ḥāl, so the two ḥāls are nested.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His words, the Exalted: {ضُحَىً}: accusative as a temporal ẓarf, and it may be mutaṣarrif (flexible) or non-mutaṣarrif. The mutaṣarrif is whatever does not refer to the time of a specific day, such as: "Your forenoon is a blessed forenoon". If you say: "I came to you on Friday in the forenoon (ḍuḥan)", this is not flexible but necessarily accusative as a ẓarf. This expression is better than the Shaykh's expression, where he said: "a flexible ẓarf if indefinite, and non-flexible if of a specific day", because he imagined that whenever it is definite, by any kind of definiteness, it is not flexible, and that is not so. The Exalted said: {والضحى} [الضحى: 1], using it in the genitive by the oath though it is definite with the article; and the Exalted said: {والشمس وَضُحَاهَا} [الشمس: 1], making it genitive by the oath particle also though it is made definite by annexation; and it is the extension of the sun and the extension of the day.
One says ḍuḥan and ḍaḥāʾ; if you give it ḍamma you shorten, and if fatḥa you lengthen. Some said: al-ḍuḥā, with ḍamma and shortening, is for the first rising of the sun, and al-ḍaḥāʾ, with fatḥa and lengthening, is for the strength of its rising before noon. Al-ḍuḥā is feminine; they deviated in its diminutive to ḍuḥayy without tāʾ, like ʿurayb and its sisters. Al-ḍaḥāʾ is also the food of the forenoon, as al-ghadāʾ is the food at the time of ghudwa (early morning); one says from the two: yuḍaḥḥī ḍaḥāʾan and taghaddā ghadāʾan. Ḍaḥiya yaḍḥā means he went out into the sun at the forenoon, then it was used generally for being struck by the sun, and from it His words {وَلاَ تضحى} [طه: 119], i.e. you will not be exposed to the sun. One says: laylatun uḍḥiyānatun, with ḍamma on the hamza, and ḍaḥyāʾ with lengthening, i.e. lit with the light of the forenoon. Al-uḍḥiya, plural aḍāḥin, and al-ḍaḥiyya, plural ḍaḥāyā, and al-aḍḥāt, plural aḍḥan, is the animal slaughtered on the Day of Sacrifice, so called because it is slaughtered at that time, per his saying, peace be upon him: "Whoever slaughters before this prayer of ours, let him repeat." And ḍawāḥī l-balad are its exposed outskirts.
His words: {وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ} is a ḥāl, and this strengthens that «بياتاً» is a ẓarf, not a ḥāl, so that the two clauses correspond, with each having a time and a state; and he brought the first ḥāl containing an active participle because it indicates stability and settledness, which suits sleep, and the second containing a verb, because it indicates renewal and occurrence, which suits play and jesting.
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ibn Kathīr read «أو» with sukūn on the wāw, and the rest with fatḥa. In the first reading «أو» as a whole is a conjunction particle, and its meaning is then division. Some claimed that it is for permission and choice, but that is not evident. In the second reading it is the conjunctive wāw which the interrogative hamza entered, preceding it in pronunciation though it is after it in implied order according to the majority. The school of al-Zamakhsharī in that is known. The meaning of the interrogative here is rebuke and reproach. Some, like Abū Shāma and others, said: "It is in the sense of negation."

semin-durr:169-169.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَرِثُواْ}: in the position of nominative as an adjective of «خَلْفٌ», and «يأخذون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «ورثوا». As for al-khalf and al-khalaf, with the lām quiescent or with fatḥa, are they one in meaning, so that each is applied to the generation that succeeds another, whether righteous or wicked; or is the one with a quiescent lām for the wicked and the one with fatḥa for the righteous? This is a well-known disagreement among the lexicographers. Al-Farrāʾ said: "A generation is called khalf, meaning with quiescent lām, and one whom you appoint as successor khalaf, meaning with vowelled lām." Al-Zajjāj said: "The generation that comes after a generation is called khalf." Thaʿlab said: "All people say «خَلَف صدق» for the righteous and «خَلْف سوء» for the wicked," and he recited:
2324 - ذهب الذين يُعاشُ في أكنافِهم ... وبَقِيتُ في خَلْف كجِلْدِ الأجرب
(Gone are those in whose shelter one lived, and I remain among a generation like the skin of the mangy.)
And they said in the proverb: «سكت أَلْفاً ونطق خَلْفاً» ("he kept silent for a thousand and spoke foolishness"), and this too is ascribed to al-Farrāʾ; and they recited:
2325 - خَلَّفْتَ خَلْفاً ولم تَدَعْ خَلفَا ... ليت بهم كان لا بك التَّلَفَا
(You left behind a bad successor and did not leave a [good] successor; would that ruin had been with them and not with you.)
Some of them said: "Khalaf with fatḥa may come for the bad, and khalf with sukūn for the good. As for the coming of the first, his saying:
2326 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إلى ذلك الخَلَفِ الأعور
(… to that one-eyed successor)
and as for the coming of the second, Ḥassān's saying:
2327 - لنا القَدَمُ الأُوْلى عليهم وخَلْفُنا ... لأولِنا في طاعة الله تابعُ
(Ours is the first precedence over them, and our successors follow our predecessors in obedience to Allah.)
And a poet combined the two in his saying:
2328 - إنَّا وَجَدْنا خَلْفَنا بِئْسَ الخَلَفْ ... عبداً إذا ما ناء بالحِمْل وَقَفْ
(We have found our successors an evil successor, a slave who, when he staggers under the load, stops.)
So he used the quiescent and the vowelled for the bad; for this reason al-Naḍr said: "Vowelling and sukūn are both permissible for the bad; as for the good, with vowelling only," and a group of the people of the language agreed with him, except al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbayd, who allowed the sukūn in khalf where the righteous is meant.
And al-khalf with sukūn has two views. One: that it is a maṣdar, and for that reason it is not dualised, pluralised or feminised, and on this is what preceded of his saying "We have found our successors an evil successor." Or an ism jamʿ (collective noun) of khālif, like rakb for rākib and tajr for tājir; Ibn al-Anbārī said so. They rejected it from him, since if it were a collective noun it would not apply to the singular, yet it has applied to it. Its derivation is either from khilāfa, that is, every successor succeeds the one before him; or from khalafa l-nabīdhu yakhlufu, that is, it spoiled; it is said khalafa l-nabīdhu yakhlufu khalfan when it spoils, khalfan and khulūfan, and likewise the mouth when its smell changes. From that is the ḥadīth: "The odour (khulūf) of the mouth of the fasting person…" Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «وُرِّثوا» with ḍamma on the wāw and shadda on the rāʾ, passive. It is permissible that «يأخذون» be resumptive, reporting that of them. The discussion of the word «الأدنى» and its derivation has been given earlier.
His saying: {وَيَقُولُونَ}: joined to «يأخذون» in both views, and «سيُغْفَر» is its object. Regarding the one standing in the place of its agent there are two views. One: the preposition and noun after it, namely «لنا». The second: that it is the pronoun of the taking indicated by His saying «يأخذون», that is: "the taking of the lower goods will be forgiven us."
His saying: {وَإِن يَأْتِهِمْ عَرَضٌ}: concerning this conditional clause there are two views. One — and it is the obvious — that it is resumptive with no grammatical position. The second: that the wāw is for ḥāl, and what follows it is accusative on that basis. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The wāw is for ḥāl, that is: they hope for forgiveness while they persist, returning to their deed, not repenting; and forgiveness of sins is not sound except through repentance, and the persister has no forgiveness." End. He made the wāw for ḥāl only for this purpose that he mentioned, that forgiveness is conditional on repentance, and that is the view of the Muʿtazila; as for the Ahl al-Sunna, it is possible without repentance because the Agent is free to choose.
His saying: {عَرَضَ}: al-ʿaraḍ with fatḥa on the rāʾ is what has no permanence, and from it the theologians borrowed "accident" (al-ʿaraḍ) as opposed to substance. Abū ʿUbayda said: "Al-ʿaraḍ with fatḥa is all the goods of this world except the two coins (gold and silver)." And al-ʿarḍ with sukūn is the dirhams and dīnārs which are the values of what is destroyed and the capital sums. On the first it was said: "The world is a present good, from which the pious and the wicked eat."
His saying: {أَن لاَّ يِقُولُواْ}: there are [views] / The first: that its position is nominative as a badal from «ميثاق», because speaking the truth is the covenant of the Book. The second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it, and it is close to the first. The third: that it is accusative as mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If the covenant of the Book is explained by what was mentioned earlier, then «أن لا يقولوا» is an object of purpose, and its meaning: 'so that they should not say.'" He had explained the covenant of the Book by what is in the Torah: whoever commits a great sin, it is not forgiven him except through repentance. And «أنْ» is explicative of the covenant of the Book because it has the meaning of speech; «لا» is prohibitive and what follows it is jussive by it; and on the [first] views «لا» is negating and the verb is accusative by the maṣdar-forming «أنْ». And «الحق» may be a direct object and may be a maṣdar; and the covenant is annexed to the Book because it is mentioned in it.
His saying: «دَرَسُواْ»: there are three views on it. The clearest is what al-Zamakhsharī said, that it is conjoined to His saying «ألم يُؤْخَذْ» because that is an affirmation, as though it were said: "the covenant of the Book was taken from them and they studied," and it is the like of the saying of the Exalted {أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيداً وَلَبِثْتَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 18], whose meaning is: "We have raised you, and you stayed." The second: that it is conjoined to «وَرِثوا». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "And His saying «ألم يُؤْخَذْ» would be parenthetical between them"; and this view was anticipated by al-Ṭabarī and others.
The third: that it rests on an implied «قد», the implied form being: "and they had studied." I say: on this it is accusative as a ḥāl, joined to the conditional clause, that is: "they say: 'It will be forgiven us' in this state"; and it is permissible that it be a ḥāl from the agent of «يأخذوه», that is: "they take the goods while studying what is in the Book that forbids taking bribes."
On both suppositions the interrogative is parenthetical.
Al-Jaḥdarī read «أن لا تقولوا» with the second-person tāʾ, and it is a fine iltifāt (shift of person). ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read «وادَّارسوا» with shadda on the dāl, the origin being «تدارسوا», and its morphology is like the morphology of {فادارأتم فِيهَا} [al-Baqara: 72], which has been verified earlier.
His saying: {أَفَلاَ تَعْقِلُونَ}: the discussion of this hamza and fāʾ has been given more than once. Ibn ʿĀmir, Nāfiʿ and Ḥafṣ read «تعقلون» in the second person, and the rest in the third person. The second person admits of two views. One: that it is an iltifāt from third person to second, the pronouns then meaning one and the same thing. The second: that the address is to this Umma, that is: "Do you not understand the state of these people and what they are upon, and wonder at their state?" As for the third person, it follows what preceded of the pronouns. The Shaykh reported that the reading in the third person is that of Abū ʿAmr and the people of Mecca, and the reading in the second person is that of the rest.

semin-durr:170-170.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين يُمَسِّكُونَ}: there are two views. The clearer: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and about its khabar then there are [views]. One: the clause in His saying: «إنَّا لا نُضيع أَجْرَ المُصْلحين», and then regarding the link there are sayings. One: that it is an omitted pronoun because the meaning is understood, the implied form being "the reformers among them"; this is according to the principles of the majority of the Basrans, whereas the principles of the Kufans require that the article «أل» stand in the place of the pronoun, the implied form being "the reward of their reformers," like His saying: {فَإِنَّ الجنة هِيَ المأوى} [al-Nāziʿāt: 41], that is, "its abode"; and His saying: {مُّفَتَّحَةً لَّهُمُ الأبواب} [Ṣād: 50], that is, "its gates"; and His saying: {في أَدْنَى الأرض} [al-Rūm: 3], that is, "their land," and so on. The second: that the link is the repetition of the mubtadaʾ in its meaning, like "Zayd — Abū ʿAbd Allāh stood," which is the opinion of al-Akhfash, and as he allows it with the relative noun, like "Abū Saʿīd is the one from whom I narrated, al-Khudrī," and "al-Ḥajjāj, whom I saw, is Ibn Yūsuf"; I have given many attestations of that earlier. The third: that the link is the generality in «المُصْلحين»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said so. He said: "If you wish you may say: since the reformers are a genus and the mubtadaʾ is one of it, you dispense with a pronoun." I say: generality is one of the five links, and on it is his saying:
2329 - ألا ليت شعري هَلْ إلى أمِّ سالمٍ ... سبيلٌ فأمَّا الصبر عنها فلا صبرا
(Would that I knew whether there is a way to Umm Sālim; as for patience away from her, there is none.)
and from it «نِعْم الرجل زيد» on one view.
The second of the two views on the khabar is that it is omitted, its implied form being: "those who hold fast are rewarded" or "recompensed" and the like, and His saying «إنَّا لا نضيع» is a parenthetical clause; al-Ḥawfī said so, and there is no need to claim the like of this.
The second of the two views on «والذين يُمْسكون»: that it is in the position of genitive, joined to «للذين يتقون», that is: "the abode of the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing and for those who hold fast"; al-Zamakhsharī said so, except that he said: "and His saying «إنَّا لا نُضيع» would be parenthetical." There is an objection to this because it did not occur between two inseparable things nor between / two things with a connection in meaning, so he should have said: "and on this it would be resumptive."
The majority read «يُمَسِّكون» with shadda, from massaka meaning tamassaka; the morphologists reported it, that is, faʿʿala has the meaning of tafaʿʿala; and on this the bāʾ is instrumental, as in "I held fast to the rope." Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, and it was transmitted from Abū ʿAmr and Abū l-ʿĀliya, read «يُمْسِكون» with a quiescent mīm and light sīn, from amsaka; they are two dialects, one says masaktu and amsaktu, and Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr combined them in his saying:
2330 - ولا تُمَسِّكُ بالعَهْدِ الذي زَعَمَتْ ... إلا كما يُمْسِكُ الماءَ الغرابيلُ
(She does not hold fast to the covenant she professed, any more than sieves hold water.)
But amsaka is transitive. The Exalted said: {وَيُمْسِكُ السمآء}. On this its object is omitted, the implied form being: "they hold their religion and their deeds by the Book," so the bāʾ may be for ḥāl and may be instrumental, that is: "accompanying the Book," that is, its commands and prohibitions. Al-Aʿmash read — and it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh — «استمسكوا», and Ubayy «تَمَسَّكوا», both past tense.

semin-durr:171-171.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَوْقَهُمْ}: there are two views. One: that it is attached to an omitted element, as a ḥāl from «الجبل», and it is an anticipated ḥāl, because at the time of the uprooting it was not above them, but through the uprooting it came to be above them. The second: that it is an adverbial of «نَتَقْنا»; al-Ḥawfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ said so. The Shaykh said: "That is not possible unless the verb is made to include the meaning of a verb that can govern «فوقهم», that is: 'We raised the mountain above them by uprooting,' so that it would be like His saying: {وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ الطور} [al-Nisāʾ: 154]."
As for al-nataq, the expressions of the lexicographers differ about it. Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is uprooting a thing from its place and throwing it, and from it «نَتَق ما في الجِراب» when he shook it out and threw what was in it. A woman nātiq and mintāq: when she bears many children. And in the ḥadīth: 'Marry virgins, for they are more fertile in their wombs (antaq arḥāman), sweeter in their mouths and more content with little.'" It was also said: al-nataq is pulling forcefully; and from it «نَتَقْتُ السِّقاء» when you pull it in order to pull the butter from its mouth. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is raising." Ibn Qutayba said: "shaking," and Mujāhid explained it so. Al-Nābigha said:
2331 - لم يُحْرَموا حُسْنَ الغِذاءِ وأمُّهُمْ ... طَفَحَتْ عليك بناتقٍ مِذْكار
(They were not deprived of good nourishment, while their mother overflowed upon you with a fruitful, male-bearing child-bearer.)
All these meanings are close. You have known that «فوقهم» may be accusative by «نَتَق» because it has the meaning of raising and uprooting.
His saying: «كأنه ظُلَّة» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from «الجبل» also, so the ḥāl is multiple. Makkī said: "It is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: 'it is as though it were a canopy,'" and there is remoteness in it.
His saying: {وظنوا}: there are several views. One: that it is in the position of genitive, joined to «نَتَقْنا» which is in the genitive in implication by the adverbial. The second: that it is a ḥāl, with «قد» implied according to some, and the owner of the ḥāl is either the mountain, that is: "as though it were a canopy while it was thought to be about to fall on them" — and it is weak that its owner be «هم» in «فوقهم». The third: that it is resumptive, with no position. The thinking (ẓann) here is in its normal sense, and it may mean certainty; and the bāʾ is in its normal sense also. It was said: it may have the meaning of «على».
His saying: {واذكروا}: the majority read without shadda, an imperative from dhakara yadhkuru. Al-Aʿmash read «واذَّكِروا» with shadda on the dhāl, from iddikār, the origin being «اذْتَكِرُوا», and iddikār, whose morphology has been given earlier. Ibn Masʿūd read «تذكَّروا» from tadhakkara, with shadda on the kāf. «وتَذَّكَّروا» was also read, with shadda on the dhāl and the kāf, the origin being «وَلْتَتَذَكَّروا», so the tāʾ was assimilated into the dhāl and the lām of command was dropped, as in his saying:
2332 - محمدُ تَفْدِ نفسَك كلُّ نفسٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . .
(Muḥammad, may every soul ransom your soul…) [Translator's note: the verse is incomplete in the source.]

semin-durr:143-143.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِمِيقَاتِنَا}: this lām is for specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), and likewise in His saying, the Exalted, {لِدُلُوكِ الشمس} [al-Isrāʾ: 78]; it is not in the sense of «عند», as some imagined mistakenly.

His saying: {أرني}: its second object is omitted, the implied form being: "show me Yourself" or "Your holy Essence"; it is omitted only as a refinement of courtesy, in that he did not address Him with an explicit mention of the object. The origin of أَرِني is أَرْ إني, and the vowel of the hamza was transferred. This has already been treated.

His saying: {لَن تَرَانِي}: it has already been mentioned that the negation by «لن» does not necessarily imply perpetuity, although some understood that, so that Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "If we remained with this negation by itself, it would imply that Moses will never see Him, not even in the Hereafter; but from another direction the mutawātir ḥadīth came that the people of Paradise will see Him." I say: Even supposing that «لن» does not require perpetuity, the statement of Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others who say that the negation of the future after it covers all future times is sound, but on a different ground: that the verb is indefinite, and an indefinite in the context of negation is general; and there is room for discussion on that.

The rectification (istidrāk) in His saying «ولكن انظر» is clear. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how does the rectification connect in His saying «ولكن انظر» [with what precedes it]? I say: it connects on the sense that looking at Me is impossible, so do not ask for it, but ask for another looking, which is that you look at the mountain." This is on his view that vision is impossible absolutely, in this world and the next.

His saying: {جَعَلَهُ دَكّاً}: the two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza) read «دَكّاء» with madd on the pattern of حَمْراء, and the rest «دَكّاً» short with tanwīn. The reading of the two allows two views. One: that it is taken from their saying ناقةٌ دكَّاء, i.e. with a flattened hump, not high; or else from their saying أرضٌ دكاء for a raised ground. In the exegesis: that not all of it vanished but its top vanished, and this fits it. As for the reading of the group, «دَكٌّ» is a maṣdar standing in the place of a direct object, i.e. "pounded" or "crumbled", with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "possessing crushing". About its accusative in the two readings there are two views. The well-known: that it is a second object of «جعل» in the sense of "made". The second, which is the view of al-Akhfash: that it is a maṣdar by meaning, since the implied form is: دَكَّه دَكّاً.

As for the first reading, it is only an object, i.e. "He made it like a flat-humped she-camel or a raised ground". الدكُّ and الدقُّ are in one meaning, namely pulverising and crushing a thing. It is also said: levelling it with the ground. Ibn Wathāb read «دُكَّا» with ḍamma on the dāl and short, and it is the plural of دَكَّاء with madd, like حُمر for حمراء and غُرّ for غَرَّاء, i.e. He made it pieces.

His saying: «صَعِقاً» is a concurrent ḥāl; and الخُرور is falling; so the Shaykh stated it unrestricted, while al-Rāghib restricted it to a fall which is heard with a murmur, and الخرير is said of the sound of water and wind and the like that fall from a height. الإِفاقة is the return of understanding and reason to a person after madness or intoxication, and from it comes the recovery of the sick, which is the return of his strength; and إفاقة الحَلْب, which is the return of the milk-flow to the udder; one says: استَفِقْ ناقَتَك, i.e. leave her until her milk returns; and الفُواق is the interval between two milkings of the milker. Its explanation will come, Allah willing.

semin-durr:144-144.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِرِسَالاَتِي}: i.e. "because of". The two Ḥaramī readers (Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr) read «برسالتي» in the singular, and what is meant is the maṣdar, i.e. "by My sending you"; and it may be with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "by conveying My message". الرسالة is the thing itself sent to another. The rest read the plural, taking account of the kinds; this was given in al-Māʾida and al-Anʿām. The majority read «وبكلامي», which allows that the maṣdar is meant, i.e. "by My speaking to you", so it would be like {وَكَلَّمَ الله موسى تَكْلِيماً} [al-Nisāʾ: 164] and the verse:

2288 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنَّ كلامَها شفاءٌ لِما بيا
(… [first half elided in the source] … for her speech is a cure for what afflicts me.)

i.e. "by his speaking to her"; and it may be that the Torah and what He revealed to him is meant, from their calling the Quran "the speech of Allah", naming the thing by the maṣdar. He put the message before the speech because it is earlier, or so as to ascend to the nobler. He repeated the preposition to draw attention to the difference of the choosing. al-Aʿmash read: «برسالاتي وبكَلِمِي», the plural of كلمة; and al-Mahdawī also transmitted from him «وتكليمي» on the pattern of تفعيل, which supports the view that الكلام is a maṣdar. Abū Rajāʾ read «برسالتي» singular and «بكَلِمي» plural, i.e. "and by hearing My words".

semin-durr:145-145.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُ فِي الألواح مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مَّوْعِظَةً}: «أل» in الألواح may be for defining the essence, or for familiarity (ʿahd), since it is transmitted in the story that he was the one who cut and split them. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «أل» is a substitute for the pronoun, the implied form being "in his tablets", and this is like {فَإِنَّ الجنة هِيَ المأوى}, i.e. "his abode". As for «أل» being a substitute for the pronoun, the Basrans do not recognise it. As for {فَإِنَّ الجنة هِيَ المأوى}, we need in it a link tying the subject and the predicate; the Kufans make «أل» a substitute for the pronoun, while the Basrans imply it, i.e. "it is the abode for him"; but in this verse there is no necessity calling for that.

About the object of «كَتَبْنَا» there are three views. The first: that it is «موعظة», i.e. "We wrote for him an admonition and a detailed account". Then about «من كل شيء» there are two views: one, that it is attached to «كتبنا»; the second, that it is attached to an omitted element, because originally it is an adjective of «موعظة», and when it was preposed to it, it became accusative as a ḥāl; and «لكلِّ شيء» is an adjective of «تفصيلاً». The second: that it is «من كل شيء». al-Zamakhsharī said: "«من كل شيء» is in the position of accusative as the object of «كتبنا», and «موعظة وتفصيلاً» a badal from it, and the meaning: We wrote for him everything the Children of Israel needed in their religion of admonitions and detailed rulings." The third: that the object is the place of the genitive phrase. The Shaykh, after relating the first view from al-Ḥawfī and the second from al-Zamakhsharī, said: "There is a third view in my opinion, that the object of «كتبنا» is in the position of the genitive phrase, as you say «أكلت من الرغيف», and «مِنْ» is partitive, i.e. We wrote for him things from everything, and «مَوْعِظة وتفصيلاً» are accusative as objects of purpose (mafʿūl li-ajlihi), i.e. We wrote for him those things for admonition and for detail." I say: it appears that this view is the one al-Zamakhsharī meant, so it is not a third view.

His saying: «بقوة» is a ḥāl, either from the agent, i.e. "with strength", or from the object, i.e. "with strength", meaning the strength of its proofs and demonstrations; and the first is clearer. The sentence in His saying «فَخُذْها» may be a badal from His saying «فخُذْ ما آتيتك», with the pronoun returning to the meaning of «ما» and not its wording. It may also be accusative by an implied saying, that saying being conjoined to the sentence «كتبنا», the implied form being: "and We wrote, and We said: Take what…". On this the pronoun returns to the tablets, or to the Torah, or to the messages, or to "everything", because it is in the meaning of "things".

His saying: {يَأْخُذُواْ}: the apparent is that it is jussive as the answer to the imperative in His saying «وَأْمُرْ». It must be interpreted, because it does not follow from his commanding them to that that they take it, as shown by the disobedience of some of them in that, for the condition of that is that the two sentences resolve into a condition and a result. It is also said: it is jussive on an implied lām, the implied form being «ليأخذوا», like the verse:

2289 - محمدٌ تَفْدِ نفسَك كلُّ نفسٍ ... إذا ما خِفْتَ مِنْ أمرٍ تَبالا
(O Muḥammad, may every soul ransom your soul whenever you fear some matter of ruin.)

This is the doctrine of al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Mālik sees it as allowed if it is in answer to «قل»; here «قل» is not mentioned, but something with its meaning is mentioned, because the meaning of «وَأْمُرْ» and «قل» is one.

His saying: {بِأَحْسَنِهَا} may be a ḥāl as given for «بقوة», and on this the object of «يأخذوا» is omitted, the implied form being: "they take themselves". The bāʾ may also be redundant, with «أحسنُها» a direct object, the implied form being: "they take the best of it", like the verse:

2290 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سودُ المحاجر لا يَقْرأن بالسُّوَرِ
(… [first half elided in the source] … dark-eyed, they do not recite the sūras.)

This has been treated carefully at His saying, the Exalted: {وَلاَ تُلْقُواْ بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التهلكة} [al-Baqara: 195]. And «أحسن» may be a comparative, on its usual sense, or not, but in the sense of «حَسَنة» as in the verse:

2291 - إنَّ الذي سَمَك السماء بنى لنا ... بيتاً دعائِمُهُ أعزُّ وأطولُ
(He who raised the heaven built for us a house whose pillars are mightier and taller.)

i.e. mighty and tall.

His saying: {سَأُوْرِيكُمْ دَارَ الفاسقين}: They allowed that the seeing here may be of the eye, and this is the apparent, so it takes two objects: one, the pronoun of those addressed, the second «دار». The second: that it is of the heart; this is reported from Ibn Zayd and others, and the meaning: "I shall let you know the conduct of the earlier peoples and the punishment that befell them". It is also said: "دار الفاسقين" is what their affair turned (دار) to, and that is known only by report and notification. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, objecting to this view: "If it were seeing of the heart, it would, being transitivised by the hamza, take three objects. And if someone said: the third object is contained in the meaning, so it is implied, i.e. 'blameworthy' or 'ruined' or 'ablaze', according to the one who said it is Hell, it would be said to him: omitting this object is not allowed, nor is stopping short without it, because it enters upon the mubtadaʾ and khabar; and if it were allowed, it would be with an ugliness in the language not fitting for the Book of Allah the Exalted."

The Shaykh said: "Omitting the third object in the chapter of أعلم, because the meaning indicates it, is allowed; so it is allowed in answer to «هل أعلمتَ زيداً عمراً منطلقاً؟» to say «أعلمتُ زيداً عمراً», omitting «منطلقاً» because the preceding speech indicates it." I say: this is granted, but where is the indication in the speech, as in the example the Shaykh produced? Then he said: "As for his reason that it enters upon the mubtadaʾ and khabar, it does not indicate prohibition, because the khabar of a mubtadaʾ may be omitted for brevity, and the second and third in the chapter of «أَعْلَمَ» may each be omitted for brevity." I say: omission for brevity requires an indication, and there is none here. Then he said: "In his saying 'because it, i.e. «سأريكم», enters upon the mubtadaʾ and khabar' there is looseness", meaning that before the transfer by the hamza it entered upon the mubtadaʾ and khabar.

al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read «سأُوْريكم» with a pure wāw after the hamza, and two explanations are given for it. One, said by al-Zamakhsharī: "It is a widespread dialect in the Ḥijāz; one says أَوْرَني كذا and أَوْرَيْتُه; its explanation is that it comes from أَوْرَيْتُ الزندَ (kindling the fire-stick), for the meaning is: 'make it clear to me and illuminate it so that I may see it clearly'." The second, mentioned by Ibn Jinnī: that it is by lengthening (ishbāʿ), so that a wāw is generated from it. He said: "This is suited by its being a place of threat and warning, so the coming of the wāw is possible." I say: this is like the verse of another:

2292 - اللهُ يعلمُ أنَّا في تَلَفُّتِنا ... يومَ اللقاء إلى أحبابنا صورُ
وأنني حيثما يثني الهوى بَصَري ... من حيث ما سلكوا أَدْنُو فانظورُ
(Allah knows that, in our looking back on the day of meeting, towards our loved ones we are inclined; and that wherever love turns my sight, from wherever they have gone, I draw near and look [lit. "fa-anẓūru"].)

But lengthening is, according to some, a matter of poetic necessity. Ibn ʿAbbās and Qasāma ibn Zayd read: «سأُوْرِثكم». al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a fine reading, which is made sound by His saying, the Exalted, {وَأَوْرَثْنَا القوم} [al-Aʿrāf: 137]."

[Translator's note: the Arabic of this entry has a stray closing parenthesis and misplaced quotation marks around the passage from "ثم قال: وفي قوله لأنها" onward; translated as the sense requires.]

semin-durr:52-52.t:
And the pronoun in {جِئْنَاهُمْ} refers to the disbelievers mentioned earlier, and what is meant by «كتاب» is the class. It was also said that it refers to those contemporary with the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, and that what is meant by the Book is the Qur'an. The bāʾ in «بكتاب» is for transitivity only. And His saying «فَصَّلناه» is an adjective of «كتاب», and what is meant by its detailing is making the truth clear from falsehood, or its being sent down in various portions, as in His saying: {وَقُرْآناً فَرَقْنَاهُ} [al-Isrāʾ: 106]. Al-Jaḥdarī and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with the dotted ḍād, i.e., "We favoured it (faḍḍalnāhu) over other heavenly books." And His saying «على عِلْم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the agent, i.e., "We detailed it knowing its detailing", or from the object, i.e., "We detailed it as comprising knowledge". And «علم» is indefinite for magnification.
And His saying: {هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً}: the majority read the accusative, with two views on it. One: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e., "We detailed it for the sake of guidance and mercy". The second: that it is a ḥāl, either from «كتاب», which is permissible because it is specified by the description, or from the object of «فصَّلناه». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «هدىً ورحمةٍ» in the genitive; al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ explained it as an adjective (naʿt) of «كتاب», in which are the well-known views as in "[I passed] by a man of justice (ʿadl)"; others explained it as a badal (substitute) of it. A group read it «هدىً ورحمةٌ» in the nominative, by implying the mubtadaʾ. Makkī said: "Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī allowed «هدى ورحمة» in the genitive, making it a badal of «علم», and it is possible «هدى ورحمة» on the implied form 'it is guidance and mercy'", as if he had not learned that they are two transmitted readings, so he attributed them in the way of permissibility. And «لقومٍ» is an adjective of «رحمة» and what is conjoined to it.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {تَأْوِيلَهُ}: this has preceded in Āl ʿImrān. Al-Zamakhsharī said here: "The root of «al-taʾwīl» is hamza, wāw, lām, from «āla yaʾūlu»." Al-Khaṭṭābī said: "I interpreted (awwaltu) a thing: I returned it to its beginning (awwal), and the word is derived from «al-awwal»." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "That is an error, because the two roots differ." And «يومَ» is accusative by «يقول», and it has come accusative by saying. And «بالحق»: the bāʾ may be circumstantial, and may be for transitivity, i.e., "they came accompanied by the truth" or "they brought the truth".
His saying: {مِن شُفَعَآءَ}: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) on the mubtadaʾ, and «لنا» is a fronted khabar. It is also possible that «من شفعاء» is an agent and «مِنْ» is also redundant, and this is permissible according to everyone, because the preposition relies on the interrogative. And His saying «فيشفعوا» is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» in the answer to the interrogative, so you have conjoined an interpreted noun to a plain noun, i.e., "Do we have intercessors, so that there is intercession from them for us?"
His saying: {أَوْ نُرَدُّ}: the majority read the nominative of «نُرَدُّ» and the accusative of «فنعملَ». The nominative of «نردُّ» is on the basis that it conjoins a verbal sentence, namely «نُرَدُّ», to a nominal sentence, namely «هل لنا من شفعاء فيشفعوا», and the accusative of «فنعملَ» is on what «فيشفعوا» is accusative on. Al-Ḥasan read both in the nominative as preceded; so Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others narrated from him. Al-Zamakhsharī narrated from him the accusative of «نُرَدّ» and the nominative of «فنعمل». Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read both in the accusative. The accusative of «نُرَدَّ» is by conjunction to «فيشفعوا», an answer upon an answer, and the intercessors would be in one of two things: either in their deliverance from the punishment, or in their return to the world to do righteous deeds, and the intercession then extends over the deliverance or the return; and «فنعملَ» is accusative by conjunction to «فنردَّ». It is also possible that «أو نُرَدَّ» is of the class of «لألزمنَّكَ أو تقضيَني حقي» ("I shall cling to you or you pay me my due") when we imply it as "until you pay me" or "so that you pay me": he made the clinging terminate with the payment of the right or gave it as its reason; so too the noble verse, i.e., "until we are returned" or "so that we be returned", and the intercession is then connected only with the return. As for one who implies «أو» in the sense of «إلا» in the preceding example, who is Sībawayh, the meaning of the verse does not appear on it, since the implied form becomes: "Will intercessors intercede for us unless we are returned?" And this is an exception that is not apparent.
And His saying «ما كانوا» is the agent of «ضَلَّ», and «ما» is a relative noun whose returning pronoun is omitted.

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ الله}: the majority read the majestic name in the nominative as the khabar of «إنَّ»; it is weak to make it a badal (substitute) of the noun of «إنَّ» by position, according to those who hold that, with the relative as the khabar of «إنَّ», and so too if one made it an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān). This is strengthened by the accusative of the majestic name in the reading of Bakkār, for in it the name is a badal or explicative of the noun of «إنَّ» by wording; and it is weak that it be its khabar according to those who hold that both parts are accusative with it, as in his saying:
2209 - When the wing of the night turns black, then come, and let ... your steps be light; our guards are lions.
and his saying:
2210 - The old woman, wily and bold ... eats every night a qafīz.
It was said: what supports that is the nominative reading, i.e., in making it a khabar; so the relative is an adjective of Allah or an explicative of it or a badal of it, or is made a khabar of «إنَّ» according to the explanations preceded; and it may be conjoined to praise (madḥ), in the nominative or accusative.
And His saying: {فِي سِتَّةِ}: the origin of «sitta» is «sidsun»; the sīn was changed into tāʾ, then the dāl met it, being close to it and silent, so assimilation became necessary, and this substitution is obligatory. What indicates that this is the origin is its return in the diminutive to «sudaysa» and in the plural [to «asdās», and their saying: "So-and-so came sixth (sādisan) and sāttan and sādiyan with a yāʾ of two dots] from below"; the poet said:
2211 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... and she counts me, if Allah does not protect, as sixth.
i.e., sādisan, and he changed it into a yāʾ.
[Translator's note: the square brackets in this paragraph are in the source; the text seems to have been disturbed there, so the sentence is rendered as written.]
And {فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ}: the apparent sense is that it is an adverbial of {خَلَقَ السماوات والأرض}; this was found problematic, because the day exists only by the rising of the sun and its setting, and that is only after the existence of the heavens and the earth. They answered it with several answers, among them: that the six is an adverbial of the creation of the earth only; on this His saying {خَلَقَ السماوات} is unrestricted, not qualified by a period, and His saying «والأرض» is an object of an implied verb, i.e., "and He created the earth", and this verb is qualified by a period of six days; and this is a very weak view. And His saying «ثم استوى»: the apparent sense is that the pronoun refers to Allah, the Exalted, with the interpretation mentioned in al-Baqara. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the creation understood from «خَلَق», i.e., "then His creation rose over the Throne". Similarly: {الرحمن عَلَى العرش استوى} [Ṭāhā: 5]. They said: the pronoun in «استوى» may refer to al-Raḥmān, and may refer to the creation, and «الرحمن» would then be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e., "He is al-Raḥmān".
And «al-ʿarsh» is applied to many meanings; among them the throne of a king, and upon this are {نَكِّرُواْ لَهَا عَرْشَهَا} [al-Naml: 41] and {وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيْهِ عَلَى العرش} [Yūsuf: 100]. Among them is authority and might, and upon this is the saying of Zuhayr:
2212 - You two overtook ʿAbs when its throne had been toppled ... and Dhubyān when the sandal slipped under their feet.
2213 - If they kill you, I have toppled their thrones ... through Rabīʿa ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Shihāb.
Among them is the wood with which a well is lined after its lower part is lined with stones. Among them is what meets the instep, in which are the toes. Among them is the roof, and everything that is above you is a ʿarsh; and it is as if the root revolves around height and elevation; and the name is also given to four small stars below al-ʿAwwāʾ.
His saying: {يُغْشِي الليل النهار}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ read here and in sūrat al-Raʿd «يُغْشي» lightened, from aghshā on the pattern afʿala, and the rest read it doubled, from ghashshā on the pattern faʿʿala; the hamza and the doubling are both for transitivity, giving the verb a second object, since it is originally transitive to one, so the agent became an object. Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «يَغْشى» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the shīn, «الليلُ» in the nominative, «النهار» in the accusative; this is al-Dānī's narration from him. Ibn Jinnī narrated from him the accusative of «الليل» and the nominative of «النهار». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Ibn Jinnī's report is the more reliable." There is something to consider in it, in that al-Dānī was more concerned with this craft than Abū l-Fatḥ, though he was below him in knowledge of the ranks [of scholars]. What also supports al-Dānī's narration is that it agrees with the common reading in meaning, in that it made «الليل» the agent in wording and meaning, and «النهار» the object in wording and meaning; and in the reading of the group «الليل» is the agent in meaning and «النهار» the object in wording and meaning. This is because when the two objects in this chapter can each be an agent and an object in meaning, the agent in meaning must be put first so as not to cause confusion, as in "I gave Zayd ʿAmr"; if there is no confusion, as in "I gave Zayd a dirham" and "I clothed ʿAmr in a cloak", it is permissible. And this is as with the plain agent and object, such as "Mūsā struck ʿĪsā" and "Zayd struck ʿAmr". This noble verse is of the class of "I gave Zayd ʿAmr", because each of night and day can be the coverer and the covered, so it is necessary to make «الليل» in the reading of the group the agent in meaning and «النهار» the object, and not the reverse. The reading of al-Dānī agrees with it, since it is explicit about the agency of the night, while the reading of Ibn Jinnī differs from it, and agreement with the group is preferable. I say: al-Zamakhsharī narrated the reading of Ḥumayd as Abū l-Fatḥ narrated it, for he said: "«يُغَشِّي» with doubling: that is, he makes the night overtake the day or the day the night; it admits both, and the evidence for the second is the reading of Ḥumayd ibn Qays «يَغْشى» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, accusative of «الليل» and nominative of «النهار»." End of quotation. There is something to consider in what Abū l-Qāsim said, because of what I mentioned to you that this noble verse is among those in which putting the agent in meaning first is necessary; and it seems that Abū l-Qāsim followed Abū l-Fatḥ in that and did not pay heed, by oversight, to this stated rule.
His saying «يَطْلبه» is a ḥāl from the night, because it is the one spoken of, i.e., "He covers the day, seeking it"; it may be from the day, i.e., "sought", and in sum each of them is mentioned. And «حثيثا» may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e., "a swift seeking", and may be a ḥāl from the agent of «يطلبه», i.e., "urging", or from its object, i.e., "urged". And «al-ḥathth» is haste, speed and urging to do something, like «al-ḥaḍḍ»; so ḥathth and ḥaḍḍ are brothers.
One says: ḥathathtu so-and-so and he hastened; he is ḥathīth and maḥthūth. He said:
2214 - He descended swiftly, as if the musk-pod ... were followed by a blue-eyed, flesh-eating falcon.
This may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, and may be a ḥāl, i.e., "he turned away a swift turning" or "he turned away in this state".
His saying: {والشمس}: Ibn ʿĀmir read here and in al-Naḥl the nominative of «الشمس» and what is conjoined to it, and the nominative of «مُسَخَّرات»; Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim agreed with him in al-Naḥl only on the nominative of {والنجوم مُسَخَّرَاتٍ}; and the rest read the accusative in both places. Abān ibn Taghlib read here the nominative of «النجوم» and what follows it only, like Ḥafṣ in al-Naḥl.
As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, it is mubtadaʾ and khabar: he made it an independent sentence reporting that they are subjected to us by Allah, the Exalted, for our benefits. As for the reading of the group, the accusative in this sūra is by conjunction to «السماوات», i.e., "and He created the sun", and «مسخرات» is on this a ḥāl from these objects. It may also be that these are accusative by an implied «جَعَل», so these accusatives are the first object and «مسخرات» the second object.
As for the reading of Ḥafṣ in al-Naḥl, he put it in the nominative there only because the governor in the accusative there is «سخَّر», which is His saying, the Exalted, {وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر}; had he put «النجوم» and «مسخرات» in the accusative, the wording would have been "He subjected them as subjected things", so emphasis would be necessary; therefore he cut them off from the first and put them in the nominative as an independent sentence. The majority explain it as a confirming ḥāl, which is abundant in their speech, or by implying a verb before «والنجوم», i.e., "and He made the stars subjected", or «مسخرات» is the plural of «musakhkhar», by which a maṣdar is intended, pluralized by considering its kinds, as if it were said: "and He subjected to you the night, the day, the sun, the moon and the stars as subjections", i.e., kinds of subjection.
And His saying {بِأَمْرِهِ} is attached to «مسخرات», i.e., by His facilitation and His will for them in that. The bāʾ may also be circumstantial, i.e., "accompanied by His command, not departing from it in their subjection". And His saying {لَهُ الخلق والأمر}: may be a maṣdar in its normal sense, and may stand in the place of the direct object.

semin-durr:99-99.t: The clause was repeated in His words, the Exalted: {أَوَ أَمِنَ أَهْلُ}: «أفأمِنُوا», as emphasis of that, and in the second clause he brought the noun overt, whereas it should by right be a pronoun, for exaggeration in the emphasis. The meaning of «مكر الله» is the attribution of the created to the Creator, like their sayings "the she-camel of Allah" and "the house of Allah", and what is meant by it is an act with which the disbelievers are punished; it was attributed to Allah since it is punishment for sin, for the Arabs name punishment, in whatever way it may be, by the name of the sin on which the punishment fell, and this is explicit in His words {وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ الله} [آل عمران: 54]; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. I say: it is a good interpretation, and it has already preceded for you in His words {وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ الله} [آل عمران: 54] that it is also of the chapter of correspondence (muqābala). The fāʾ in His words «فلا يأمَنُ» is to alert that punishment follows feeling safe from the scheme of Allah.

semin-durr:100-100.t:
His words, the Exalted: {أَوَلَمْ يَهْدِ}: the majority read «يَهْدِ» with the yāʾ (third person). Then for its agent there are three views, the most evident being that it is the interpreted maṣdar from «أنْ» and what is in its scope, with the object omitted, the implied form being: "Has it not become clear and plain to those who inherit, their outcome and the end of their affair, and Our striking them for their sins had We willed that", for the maṣdar has been formed from «أنْ» and from the answer to «لو». The second: the agent is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "Has Allah not made clear", and this is supported by the reading of whoever read «نَهْدِ» with the nūn. The third: it is a pronoun returning to what is understood from the context of the speech, i.e. "Has what befell the earlier nations not guided", like their saying: "If it is tomorrow, then come to me", i.e. if what is between me and you, of what the context indicates, occurs. On these two views «أنْ» and what is in its scope are, by interpretation as a maṣdar as stated, in the position of object, and the implied form is: "Has Allah not made clear, or has what befell the nations not made clear, Our striking them for their sins had We willed that."
Mujāhid read «نَهْدِ» with the nūn of majesty, and «أنْ» is only an object; and «أنْ» is the lightened form of the heavy one, with «لو» separating it from the verb, and it was already stated that separation by it is rare. «نشاء», though imperfect in form, is past in meaning, because the preventive «لو» makes the imperfect past. In Ibn al-Anbārī's words is the opposite, for he said about «ونطبعُ»: "This is a resumptive verb, disconnected from what precedes, because His words «أَصَبْنا» are past and «نَطْبع» future." Then he said: "It is possible that it is conjoined to «أَصَبْنا», since it is in the sense of nuṣību, and the meaning is: 'if He willed, He would strike them and seal', so he put the past in the place of the future when the sense of futurity is clear, like His words, the Exalted: {إِن شَآءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ} [الفرقان: 10], i.e. yajʿalu, as evidenced by His words «ويجعل لك»." I say: this is strongly evident that this «لو» does not make the imperfect past, and his comparison with the other verse also supports it, and its verification will come at His words «ونطبع».
Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is permissible to return yafʿalu to faʿala in the answer to «لو», like His words {وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ الله لِلنَّاسِ الشر استعجالهم بالخير لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ فَنَذَرُ} [يونس: 11]; His words «فَنَذَرُ» are returned to «لقُضِي»." I say: this is the statement of the majority. The object of «يشاء» is omitted because the answer to «لو» indicates it, the implied form being: "had He willed to punish them or take vengeance on them". Its answer came without the lām, built on one of two permissible options, though the more frequent is the opposite, like His words, the Exalted: {لَوْ نَشَآءُ جَعَلْنَاهُ أُجَاجاً} [الواقعة: 70].
His words: {وَنَطْبَعُ}: there are several views on this clause. One: it is conjoined to «أَصَبْناهم», and it is permissible to conjoin an imperfect to a past because it is in its meaning, and it was stated that «لو» makes the imperfect past. When the Shaykh related Ibn al-Anbārī's statement above, he said: "He made «لو» conditional in the sense of «إنْ», and did not make it the one meaning 'for what would have occurred through the occurrence of something else', and so he made «أَصَبْنا» in the sense of nuṣību. An example of «لو» occurring in the sense of «إنْ» is his saying:
2253 - May the one who hopes in you find you only displaying ... the nobility of the generous, even if you are destitute."
What Ibn al-Anbārī said, al-Zamakhsharī refuted in terms of meaning, but on the supposition that «ونطبعُ» is in the sense of ṭabaʿnā, in which case he conjoined the imperfect to the past because it is in the past's meaning; whereas Ibn al-Anbārī put the interpretation on «أَصَبْنا», which is the answer to «لو نشاء», making it in the sense of nuṣību, so he interpreted the thing conjoined to and returned it to the past; and al-Zamakhsharī's refutation yielded that neither supposition is valid."
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: may «ونطبع» be in the sense of ṭabaʿnā, just as «لو نشاء» is in the sense of «لو شِئْنا», and be conjoined to «أَصَبْناهم»? I say: the meaning does not support it, because the people were already sealed upon their hearts, described by the attribute of those before them of committing sins and being struck for them, and this explanation leads to their being free of this attribute, and that Allah, had He willed, they would have been described by it." The Shaykh said: "This refutation is apparently sound, and its gist is that what is conjoined to the answer is an answer whether we interpret the thing conjoined to or the conjoined; and the answer to «لو» has not yet occurred, whether it is the particle 'for what would have occurred through the occurrence of another' or in the sense of conditional «إنْ»; the striking has not occurred, while sealing the hearts has occurred, so it is not valid to conjoin it to the answer. If «ونطبع» is interpreted in the sense: 'and we continue sealing their hearts', conjunction is possible, because the continuation has not yet occurred even though the sealing has occurred." I say: this first view is impossible for what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned.
The second view: «نطبع» is resumptive and disconnected from what precedes, so it is intended as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and we seal". This is the choice of Abū Isḥāq, al-Zamakhsharī and a group.
The third view: it is conjoined to «يرثون الأرض», as al-Zamakhsharī said. The Shaykh said: "It is a mistake, because what is conjoined to a ṣila is a ṣila, and «يرثون» is a ṣila for «الذين», so separation between parts of the ṣila by a foreigner would be necessary, for His words «أنْ لو نشاء» are either the agent of «يَهْد» or its object, as stated; and on either supposition it has no connection with any part of the ṣila, and is foreign to it, so one does not separate its parts by it, and this view leads to that, so it is a mistake."
The fourth: it is conjoined to what is indicated by the meaning of «أو لم يهد لهم», as though it were said: "They are heedless of guidance and We seal their hearts." Al-Zamakhsharī also said this. The Shaykh said: "It is weak, because it is an implication that is not needed, since its being conjoined to the resumptive is valid under conjunction of clauses, so it is conjoined to the whole of the clause headed by the interrogative particle, and al-Zamakhsharī and others have said it."
His words: {فَهُمْ لاَ يَسْمَعُونَ}: he brought the fāʾ here to announce that their not hearing follows immediately upon the sealing of their hearts.

semin-durr:101-101.t:
His words, the Exalted: {تِلْكَ القرى نَقُصُّ}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "like His words {وهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً} [هود: 72] in being a mubtadaʾ, khabar and ḥāl", meaning that «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ pointing to what comes after it, «القرى» is its khabar, and «نقصُّ» is a ḥāl, i.e. "relating", like His words: {فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهُمْ خَاوِيَةً} [النمل: 52].
