Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the meaning of «تلك القرى» so that it is beneficial speech? I say: it is beneficial, but through the ṣifa, as in your saying 'He is the generous man'." I say: he means that the ḥāl here is obligatory so that the construction conveys benefit, just as the ṣifa is obligatory in your saying "He is the generous man"; do you not see that if you confined yourself to "He is the man" it would not be beneficial? It is also possible that «القرى» is a ṣifa of «تلك», with «نقصُّ» the khabar, and it is possible that «نَقُصُّ» is a khabar after a khabar. «نقصُّ» may remain in its sense of futurity, i.e. "We have related to you of its news, and We shall also relate to you some of its news", and the distant demonstrative is used to alert to the remoteness of their destruction and its being long before the time of the report, so it is of the unseen. In His words «القرى» with the article there is magnification, like His words, the Exalted: "That is the Book", and the saying of the Messenger, peace be upon him: "Those are the chiefs of Quraysh", and the saying of Umayya:
2254 - Those are the noble deeds, not two cups of milk ... mixed with water, which afterwards turned into urine.
«مِنْ» is for partition, as stated, because only what contains admonition and deterrence was related to him, peace be upon him, and not other things.
His words: {فَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ}: the evident view is that all the pronouns return to the people of the towns. Yamān ibn Ribāb said: "The first two pronouns are for the people of the towns, and the pronoun in «كذَّبوا» for their forebears." Ibn ʿAṭiyya also verified it so, i.e. "the sons would not believe in what the fathers had denied". The lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd) was discussed earlier, and that the negation of the verb with it is more emphatic. «ما» is a relative noun, and its returning pronoun is omitted because it is accusative and attached, i.e. "bimā kadhdhabūhu". It is not permissible to imply «به», though the relative is also governed by the bāʾ, because of the difference of attachment.
He said here {بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ} and did not mention what the denial is attached to, while in Yūnus he mentioned it and said: {بِمَا كَذَّبُواْ بِهِ} [يونس: 74]. The difference is that since he omitted it in His words {ولكن كَذَّبُواْ} [الأعراف: 96], the omission continued after that; whereas in Yūnus he made it explicit in His words {فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ} [يونس: 74], {كَذَّبُواْ بِآيَاتِنَا} [يونس: 73], so mentioning it was fitting by conformity. Al-Kirmānī said this meaning.
His words: {كَذَلِكَ يَطْبَعُ الله}, i.e. like that sealing upon the hearts of the people of the towns, from whom belief is negated, Allah seals the hearts of the disbelievers who come after them.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His words, the Exalted: {لأَكْثَرِهِم}: the evident view is that it is attached to wujdān (finding), as in your saying: "I did not find for him any wealth", i.e. I did not come upon any wealth of his, nor did I meet him. The second: it is a ḥāl from «عهد», because originally it is the ṣifa of an indefinite noun, so when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl, the original being: "We did not find a covenant for most of them"; and this is all that Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned. On these two views «وجد» takes one object, which is «مِن عهد», and «مِنْ» is redundant in it because the two conditions are met. The third: it is in the position of accusative as the second object of «وجد», as it is in the sense of knowing, and the object is «من عهد». This may be preferred because the second «وَجَد» is of knowing, not of finding in the sense of coming upon, as proof of which will come. If this is established, the first ought to be so as well, in keeping with the speech and fitting for it. Whoever prefers the first says: the first is for one meaning and the second for another meaning.
His words: {وَإِن وَجَدْنَآ}: this «إنْ» is the lightened form, and it is not operative here because it is joined directly to a verb, so its specificity, which required its being operative, has gone. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "and inna, the matter and the affair: wajadnā", and the apparent sense of this expression is that it is operative and that its ism is the pronoun of the matter and affair. Abū l-Baqāʾ explicitly stated here that it is operative and that its ism is omitted, except that he did not imply it as the pronoun of the affair but something else. He said: "Its ism is omitted, i.e. innā wajadnā"; and this is the school of the grammarians, I mean the belief in the lightened form of these particles being operative, in the open-vowelled «أنْ» on the sound view and in the comparative «كأنْ», while as for the kasra-vowelled lightened «إنْ», it is not. This has been discussed more clearly than this.
«وجد» here takes two objects, the first being «أكثرهم» and the second «لَفاسقين». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Finding is in the sense of knowing, as in your saying 'wajadtu Zaydan dhā l-ḥifāẓ', as evidenced by the entry of the lightened «إنْ» and the distinguishing lām, which is valid only with the mubtadaʾ and khabar and the verbs entering on them." He means that it is specific to the inchoative or to the verbs that abrogate it; this is the school of the majority, and a disagreement from al-Akhfash has preceded, that he allows it on others, and I presented his evidence for that. The lām is the distinguishing one (fāriqa). It was also said: it is a compensation for the doubling. Makkī said: "The lām became obligatory in its khabar as compensation for the doubling." The omitted is the first. It was also discussed earlier that some Kufans make «إنْ» negative, and the lām in the sense of «إلا» in His words, the Exalted: {وَإِن كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً} [البقرة: 143].

semin-durr:103-103.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فَظَلَمُواْ بِهَا}: «ظلموا» may be made to imply the sense "they disbelieved", so it is transitivized with the bāʾ as it is. This is supported by {إِنَّ الشرك لَظُلْمٌ عَظِيمٌ} [لقمان: 13]. The bāʾ may be causal, with the object omitted, its implied form being "they wronged themselves", or "they wronged the people", in the sense that they barred them from belief because of the signs. His words «لأكثرهم», «أكثرهم» and «مِنْ بعدهم»: if we make all these pronouns refer to the earlier nations, there is no objection; but if we make the pronoun in «لأكثرهم» and «أكثرهم» for people in general and the pronoun in «من بعدهم» for the earlier nations, this clause, I mean «وما وجدنا», is parenthetical. Al-Zamakhsharī said so, but there is room for doubt in it: for if the first is general and then something is mentioned in which what comes after and what comes before are subsumed, how can that general be made a parenthetical between two specifics? Moreover, the grammarians define the parenthetical only for what is interposed between two inseparables, whereas for the rhetoricians the parenthetical is more general than that, so that when something is brought between two things mentioned in one story they call it parenthetical.
His words: {كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ}: «كيف» is the khabar of kāna, put before it obligatorily because it has the head of speech; «عاقبة» is its ism. This interrogative clause is in the position of accusative on the dropping of the preposition, since the implied form is: "so look at such and such".

semin-durr:146-146.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بِغَيْرِ الحق}: There are two views about it. One: that it is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, i.e. "they are arrogant, being accompanied by what is not the truth". The second: that it is attached to the verb before it, i.e. "they are arrogant with what is not true", and arrogance with the truth belongs to Allah the Exalted alone.

His saying: {وَإِن يَرَوْاْ}: the apparent is that it is of the eye; it may be of the heart, in which case the second object is omitted because the meaning is understood, like the saying of ʿAntara:

2293 - ولقد نَزَلْتِ فلا تظنِّي غيرَه ... مني بمنزلة المُحَبِّ المُكْرَمِ
(You have indeed alighted, so think nothing else of me but the rank of the honoured lover.)

i.e. "do not think anything else happening from me"; and likewise the noble verse, i.e. "and if they see every sign coming or occurring". Mālik ibn Dīnār read «يُرَوا» passive, from أرى transitivised by the hamza of transitivisation.

His saying {الرشد}: the two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza) here, and Abū ʿAmr in His saying {مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْداً} [al-Kahf: 66] specifically, to the exclusion of the first two (occurrences), read it with two fatḥas, and the rest with ḍamma and sukūn. People differed about it: are the two of one meaning? The majority said: yes, they are two dialects in the maṣdar, like البُخْل and البَخَل, السُّقْم and السَّقَم, الحُزْن and الحَزَن. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: "الرُّشْد with ḍamma and sukūn is soundness in judgement, and with two fatḥas it is religion." They said that for this reason there is agreement on His saying {فَإِنْ آنَسْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ رُشْداً} [al-Nisāʾ: 6] with ḍamma and sukūn, and on His saying {فأولئك تَحَرَّوْاْ رَشَداً} [al-Jinn: 14] with two fatḥas. It is transmitted from Ibn ʿĀmir «الرُّشُد» with two ḍammas, as if from the category of imitation of the vowel (ittbāʿ), like اليُسُر and العُسُر. al-Sulamī read «الرَّشاد» with an alif, so الرُّشْد, الرَّشَد and الرَّشاد are like السُّقْم, السَّقَم and السَّقَام. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «لا يتخذوها» and «يتخذوها» with the pronoun feminine, because السبيل may be feminine. The Exalted said: {قُلْ هذه سبيلي} [Yūsuf: 108].

His saying: {ذلك}: there are two views about it. The more evident: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preposition phrase after it, i.e. "that turning away is because of their denial". The second: that it is in the position of accusative. Then there was disagreement about that: al-Zamakhsharī said: "Allah turned them with that very turning", making it a maṣdar; and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "We did that", making it a direct object; and on both views the bāʾ in «بأنهم» is attached to that omitted element.

His saying: {وَكَانُواْ}: about this sentence there are two possibilities. One: that it is conjoined to the khabar of «أنَّ», i.e. "that is because they denied, and because they were heedless of Our signs". The second: that it is a resumption, in which Allah the Exalted reports of them that it is their nature to be heedless of the signs and of reflecting on them.

semin-durr:147-147.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين كَذَّبُواْ}: about its khabar there are two views. One: that it is the sentence in His saying {حَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ}, and {هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ} a second khabar or a resumption. The second: that the khabar is «هل يُجْزون», and the sentence «حَبِطَتْ» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with «قد» implied with it according to whoever requires that, and the owner of the ḥāl being the agent of «كذَّبوا».

His saying: {وَلِقَآءِ الآخرة}: there are two views about it. One: that it is of the category of annexing a maṣdar to its object, the agent being omitted, the implied form being: "and their meeting the Hereafter". The second: that it is of the category of annexing a maṣdar to an adverbial, in the sense of "and the meeting of what Allah promised in the Hereafter"; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned both. The Shaykh said: "The leading grammarians do not allow annexation to an adverbial, because an adverbial is on the implication of «في», whereas annexation, in their view, is on the implication of the lām or «مِنْ»; but if the operator is used expansively, it is allowed that the adverbial be made accusative like an object, and it is then allowed that its maṣdar be annexed to that adverbial which has been used expansively in respect of its operator; and some grammarians allowed that the annexation be on the implication of «في», as the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's statement suggests."

His saying: {هَلْ يُجْزَوْنَ}: this interrogative means negation, and for that reason «إلا» entered; had its meaning been affirmation (taqrīr), it would be positive, and the entry of «إلا» would be remote or impossible. al-Wāḥidī said here: "An omitted element must be implied, i.e. 'except for what they used to', or 'on what they used to', or 'the recompense of what they used to'." I say: because they are not recompensed with the very thing they used to do, but with its counterpart, and this is clear.

semin-durr:148-148.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن بَعْدِهِ مِنْ حُلِيِّهِمْ}: i.e. "after his passing and going to the appointed time". The two prepositional phrases are attached to «اتخذ», and it is permissible for two prepositions identical in form to be attached to one operator because their meanings differ, since the first is for the beginning of the limit and the second is partitive. «من حُليِّهم» may also be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «عجلاً», because had it been postposed it would have been an adjective, so one would have said: عجلاً مِنْ حليهم.

The two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza) read «حِليِّهم» with kasra on the ḥāʾ; its explanation is imitation of the kasra of the lām; it is the reading of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, and of Ṭalḥa, Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb and al-Aʿmash; and the rest with ḍamma, which is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba ibn Niṣāḥ. In both readings it is the plural of حَلْي, like طيّ, pluralised on فُعول like فَلْس and فُلوس, so its origin is حُلُوي, like ثُدِيّ from ثُدُوْي; then the yāʾ and the wāw came together, the first of them preceded by sukūn, so the wāw was turned into yāʾ and assimilated, and the ʿayn of the word was given kasra, although originally it carried ḍamma, so that the yāʾ would be sound; and you then have two options: leaving the first letter with ḍamma, or making it follow the ʿayn in kasra. This is regular in every plural on فُعول from a defective-lām root, whether the defect is with yāʾ, as in حُلِيّ and ثُدِيّ, or with wāw, such as عُصِيّ and دُلِيّ, plural of عصا and دَلْو. Yaʿqūb read «حَلْيَهم» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and sukūn on the lām, which allows that الحَلْي is a singular intended as a plural, or a generic noun whose singular is حَلْيَة, on the model of قمح and قمحة.

«عِجْلاً» is the object of «اتَّخذ», and «مِنْ حُليِّهم» has had its ruling given. It is possible that «اتَّخذ» takes two objects in the sense of "made", so that «مِنْ حليِّهم» would be the second object. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is omitted, i.e. 'as a god'", and there is no need for that.

About «جَسَداً» there are three views. One: that it is an adjective. The second: that it is an ʿaṭf bayān. The third: that it is a badal; al-Zamakhsharī said it, and it is the best, because جسد is not derived, so it is not used as an adjective except by interpretation, and ʿaṭf bayān among indefinites is rare or impossible according to the majority. He said «جسداً» only so that it might not be imagined that it was drawn or inscribed. الجسد is the body; it is also said: a being of flesh and blood; and both views are transmitted in the exegesis.

His saying: {لَّهُ خُوَارٌ} is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «عِجْلاً», and this strengthens «جسداً» being an adjective, because when an adjective and a badal come together, the adjective is put before the badal. The majority read «خُوار» with a dotted khāʾ and an explicit wāw, which is specifically the sound of cattle, and it is sometimes borrowed for the camel. الخَوَر is weakness, and from it comes: أرضٌ خَوَّارة and رُمْحٌ خَوَّار; and الخَوْران is the passage of dung, and also the sound of beasts. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, and Abū l-Sammāl read «جُؤَار» with jīm and hamza, which is a loud sound.

His saying: {أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ}: if we say that «اتخذ» takes two objects and that the second is omitted, the implied form being "and the people of Moses took after him a calf, a body, as a god", then there is no need to claim the omission of a sentence to which this denial is directed; and if we say that it takes one object in the sense of "made, fashioned", or takes two and the second is «من حليِّهم», then a sentence must be omitted before that for the denial to be directed to it, the implied form being: "and they worshipped it".

«يَرَوا» may be of knowing, which is the apparent, or of the eye, which is remote.

His saying: {وَكَانُواْ ظَالِمِينَ}: two views are possible, the more evident being that it is a resumption, reporting of them this report, and that it is their habit and way in everything, their taking the calf being part of that. It may also be a ḥāl, i.e. "and they had been", that is, "they took it in this settled state of theirs".

semin-durr:172-172.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ}: a badal (substitute) from His saying «من بني آدم» with repetition of the preposition, like His saying: {لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بالرحمن لِبُيُوتِهِمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 33] and {لِلَّذِينَ استضعفوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ} [al-Aʿrāf: 75]. Is it a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) or a partial substitute for the whole? Two sayings; the first is Abū l-Baqāʾ's, the second al-Zamakhsharī's, and it is the clearer, like your saying "I struck Zayd, his back," "I cut him, his hand"; no one parses this as badal al-ishtimāl.
And {ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ} is a direct object. The Kufans and Ibn Kathīr read «ذريتهم» in the singular, the rest «ذُرِّيَّاتهم» in the plural. The Shaykh said: "In the plural reading it is possible that the object of «أخذ» be omitted because the meaning is understood, and «ذريَّاتهم» be a badal from the pronoun of «ظهورهم», just as «من ظهورهم» is a badal from «بني آدم»; and the omitted object is the covenant (al-mīthāq), like His saying {وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُمْ مِّيثَاقاً} [al-Nisāʾ: 154]." He said: "The implied wording is: 'and when your Lord took from the loins of the descendants of the children of Adam the covenant of tawḥīd,' and he borrowed the idea of taking the covenant from the back, as though the covenant, because of its difficulty and the binding to it, is a heavy thing carried on the back."
And likewise the Kufans and Ibn Kathīr read in Sūrat Yā Sīn and in / al-Ṭūr in the two places: «ذريتهم» in the singular; Abū ʿAmr agreed with them on what is in Yā Sīn, and Nāfiʿ agreed with them in the first of al-Ṭūr, which is «ذريتهم بإيمان», but not the second, which is «أَلْحَقْنا بهم ذريَّاتِهم»; so the Kufans and Ibn Kathīr followed one pattern, the singular, and Ibn ʿĀmir the plural, and Abū ʿAmr and Nāfiʿ combined the two as I have shown you.
The Shaykh said, regarding the singular reading in this sūra: "It must be an object of «أخذ», with an omitted muḍāf, that is, 'the covenant of their descendants.'" He means that what was permissible in «ذرياتهم», that it be a badal with the object omitted, is not permissible in it, and that is clear because whoever reads «ذريتهم» in the singular reads it only in the accusative, whereas if it were a badal from «هم» in «ظهورهم» it would be genitive; unlike «ذرياتهم» in the plural, for the kasra can serve as the sign of genitive and of accusative in the sound feminine plural.
His saying: {بلى}: an answer to His saying «أَلَسْتُ». Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Had they said 'yes' (naʿam), they would have disbelieved." He means that a negation, when answered with naʿam, is a confirmation of it, so it is as if they had acknowledged that He is not their Lord. So they transmit it from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him; and there is an objection in it if it is authentic from him, in that this negation had become an affirmation, so how would they disbelieve by confirming the affirmation? Rather the prohibition comes from the linguistic side: namely, that a negation, absolutely, when its affirmation is intended, is answered with balā, even if it is made an affirmation by the entry of the interrogative upon it; and that is to give priority to the side of the wording; and it is not permissible to observe the side of the meaning except in poetry, as in his saying: 2333 - أليس الليلُ يجمعُ أمَّ عمروٍ ... وإيانا فذاك بنا تَدانى
نعم وترى الهلالَ كما أراه ... ويعلوها النهار كما علاني
(Does not the night bring together Umm ʿAmr and us? That brings us near. Yes — and you see the crescent as I see it, and the day rises over her as it rises over me.)
So he answered his saying «أليس» with naʿam, observing the meaning, because it is an affirmation.
His saying: {شَهِدْنَآ}: this is from the speech of Allah the Exalted. It was said: from the speech of the angels. It was said: from the speech of Allah the Exalted and the angels. It was said: from the speech of the descendants. Al-Wāḥidī said: "On this view it is not good to pause at His saying «بلى», and «أَنْ تقولوا» is not attached to «شَهِدْنا» but to His saying «وأَشْهَدَهُمْ»."
His saying: {أَن تَقُولُواْ}: an object of purpose, and the governor in it is either «شهدْنا», that is: "we bore witness lest you should say" — this is the interpretation of the Basrans; as for the Kufans, their principle is to suppose the negating «لا», its implied form being: "lest you say," like {أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ} [al-Naḥl: 15], and the other's saying:
2334 - رَأَيْنا ما رأى البُصَراء فيها ... فآلَيْنا عليها أَنْ تُباعا
(We saw what the discerning saw in her, so we swore concerning her that she not be sold.)
that is, "that she not be sold"; and as for «وأشهدهم», that is: "He made them witness lest you say," or "disliking that you should say." It has already been mentioned that al-Wāḥidī said: "If «شهدنا» is from the speech of the descendants, it must be that «أن تقولوا» is attached to «أَشْهَدَهم»," as though he saw that the construction would become "we bore witness that you say," whether read in the third person or the second, and the witnesses are the sayers in meaning, so the construction ought to have been "we bore witness that we say." But that is not necessary, because the meaning is that some of them bore witness against others, so some of the descendants said: "We bore witness that the others may say likewise." Al-Jurjānī mentioned from some of them another view, that His saying «وإذْ أخَذَ ربك» to His saying «قالوا بلى» is the end of the story of the covenant, then the Exalted began another report with a mention of what the polytheists say on the Day of Resurrection, saying {شَهِدْنا} in the sense of "we bear witness," as al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
2335 - شَهِدَ الحطيئةُ حين يلقى ربَّه ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Al-Ḥuṭayʾa testified, when he meets his Lord…)
that is, "he testifies," so its interpretation would be "he testifies that you say."
Abū ʿAmr read «يقولوا» in both places in the third person, following the preceding nouns, and the rest in the second person, and this is clear on our saying that «شَهِدْنا» is predicated of the pronoun of Allah the Exalted. It was said: on the third-person reading, «أَنْ يقولوا» is attached to «أشهدهم», and «قالوا شهدنا» would be parenthetical between the verb and its reason, and the second person is by iltifāt, so the two pronouns refer to one thing. And is this a matter of literal reality, that Allah brought the descendants out of his back by wiping over it, so they came out like tiny particles (dharr) and He made them speak, so all bore witness that He is their Lord — the believers said it truly in pre-eternity and the polytheists said it out of dissimulation — and a great number hold this; or is it a matter of representation (tamthīl), as a group said, among them al-Zamakhsharī, who made it like the saying of the Exalted {ائتيا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً قَالَتَآ أَتَيْنَا طَآئِعِينَ} [Fuṣṣilat: 11], and the poet's saying:
2336 - إذ قالت الأَنْساع للبطن الحَقِي ...
(When the girth-straps said to the belly: "Join [the back]…")
and the other's saying:
2337 - قالت له ريحُ الصَّبا قَرْقارِ ...
(The east wind said to it [the cloud]: "Rumble!")
and so on.

semin-durr:174-174.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وكذلك نُفَصِّلُ}: that is: "and in the same way as We clarified and detailed the taking of the covenant mentioned before, We make clear and detail the signs." A group read «يُفَصّل» with the third-person yāʾ, the subject being Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:175-175.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {فَأَتْبَعَهُ}: the majority read «أَتْبعه», quadriliteral (Form IV), and there are two views on it. One: that it is transitive to one object, meaning "he overtook him and caught up with him," and it is an exaggeration in his case, / in that he was made a leader for Satan. It is also possible that it takes two objects, because it is transferred by the hamza from tabiʿa, and the second object is omitted, its implied form being: "Satan made him follow his footsteps," that is, he made him a follower of them. Among its taking two objects is the saying of the Exalted: {وأَتْبعناهم ذرياتهم بإيمان} [al-Ṭūr: 21]. Al-Ḥasan and Ṭalḥa, with a disagreement from him, read «فاتَّبعه» with shadda on the tāʾ. And are tabiʿahu and ittabaʿahu one in meaning, or is there a difference between them? It was said both; / and some have shown the difference: tabiʿahu is "he walked in his track," and ittabaʿahu is when he went alongside him in walking. It was also said: ittabaʿahu has the meaning of istatbaʿahu ("he made him follow").
And al-insilākh is stripping oneself of a thing, and from it: the snake's shedding of its skin. There is no inversion (qalb) in the verse, since nothing necessitates it, though some claimed it, saying that its origin is «فانسلختْ منه».

semin-durr:176-176.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَرَفَعْنَاهُ بِهَا}: the accusative pronoun clearly refers back to the one who was given the signs, and the genitive refers to the signs. It was said: the accusative refers to disbelief, understood from what preceded, and the genitive also to the signs, that is: "We would have removed disbelief by the signs you see." It was said: the genitive pronoun refers to the disobedience and the accusative to «الذي». And what is meant by raising is taking away, as you say "the wrongdoer was raised," that is, uprooted and destroyed, that is: "We would have destroyed him because of the disobedience." These are remote sayings, even though they are reported from Mujāhid and others. The «ولكنه» adversative is clear only on the first view. And the meaning of «أخلد» is: he cast himself [down]. The people of Arabic said: "Its origin is from ikhlād, which is permanence and clinging, so the meaning is: he clung to inclining to the earth." Mālik ibn Nuwayra said:
2338 - بأبناء حَيٍّ مِنْ قبائل مالك ... وعمرو بن يربوعٍ أقاموا فأخلدوا
(With sons of a clan from the tribes of Mālik and ʿAmr ibn Yarbūʿ, who settled and stayed for good.)
His saying: {إِن تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ}: this conditional clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "panting in both states." Some of them said: "As for the conditional clause, it scarcely ever occurs in its entirety in the place of a ḥāl, so it is not said «جاء زيد إنْ يَسْأَل يُعط» as a ḥāl; rather, if that were intended, the clause would be made a khabar of a pronoun of that from which the ḥāl is wanted, and it would be said: «جاء زيد وهو إن يسأل يُعط», so the nominal clause is the ḥāl. Yes, they have put the conditional clause in the position of ḥāl, but after taking it out of the reality of the condition, and that clause does not fail either to have joined to it what contradicts it or not. In the first, the omission of the wāw persists, as in «أتيتك إن أتيتني وإن لم تأتني», since it is not hidden that two contradictory conditions in a place like this do not remain with the meaning of conditionality, but turn into the meaning of equalisation, like the two contradictory interrogatives in His saying: {أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6]. In the second, the wāw is necessary, as in «أتيتك وإن لم تأتني», because if you left the wāw and said «أتيتُك إن لم تأتِني» it would be confusing. If this is known, then His saying {إِن تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ أَوْ تَتْرُكْهُ يَلْهَث} is of the first type, because attacking him and leaving him are contradictory."
And kalb (dog): its plural of paucity is aklub, and its plural of multiplicity is kilāb, and they irregularly pluralised aklub as akālib, and kilāb as kilābāt; as for kalīb, it is a collective noun like farīq, not a plural. Ṭarafa said:
2339 - تَعَفَّق بالأَرْطَى لها وأرادَها ... رجالٌ فبذَّت نبلَهم وكليبُ
(It [the oryx cow] took shelter for itself in the arṭā-bushes, and men and a pack of dogs wanted her, but she outstripped their arrows and the pack.)
This root was given earlier in al-Māʾida. It is said: lahatha yalhathu with fatḥa on the ʿayn in the past and imperfect, lahathan and luhthan with fatḥa or ḍamma on the lām, which is the lolling of its tongue in its state of rest and exhaustion; as for other animals, they pant only when exhausted or thirsty. What appears is that this conditional clause has no grammatical position, because it explains the parable mentioned, and this is a clear meaning, as they said regarding the saying of the Exalted {خَلَقَهُ مِن تُرَابٍ}: the clause «خَلَقَه من تراب» explains the saying of the Exalted: {إِنَّ مَثَلَ عيسى عِندَ الله كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ} [Āl ʿImrān: 59].
His saying: {ذَّلِكَ مَثَلُ}: it is permissible that «ذلك» point to the description of the dog, and permissible that it point to the one who stripped himself of the signs, or to the dog. And the particle of likening is omitted from that, that is: "the description of the one stripped or the description of the dog is like those who denied." And it is permissible that the omitted one be from «مثل القوم», that is: "that description, which is the description of the one stripped or the description of the dog, is like the likeness of the people."

semin-durr:55-55.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: {تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e., "humbling yourselves, keeping the supplication hidden, so that it is nearer to being answered". They may also be accusative as maṣdars, i.e., "a supplication of humility and secrecy". Abū Bakr read «خِفية» with kasra on the khāʾ, and this has preceded in al-Anʿām, except that the words of Abū ʿAlī point to «khifya» with kasra meaning fear (khawf); this can come about only on the claim of transposition (qalb), i.e., one holds that the lām precedes the ʿayn, which is remote, and because the wāw ought to have returned to its origin; that is, the yāʾ of «khīfa» comes from a wāw because of its silence and the kasra of what precedes it, and when the wāw was moved later it became vowelled and what precedes it silent, unless it is said that it was changed [and] left as it was. Al-Aʿmash read «وخِيْفة», which supports what al-Fārisī mentioned; Abū Ḥātim reported this reading from him. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «إن الله», bringing the majestic name in place of the pronoun.
[Translator's note: the passage on «khifya»/«khīfa» is terse and partly obscure in the source; it is rendered as closely as possible.]

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً}: two ḥāls, i.e., "call upon Him possessing fear and hope", or "fearing, hoping"; or two objects of purpose, i.e., "for the sake of fear and hope".
His saying: {قَرِيبٌ}: it is not made feminine, though it is a khabar (predicate) of a feminine noun, for several reasons. Among them: that it is in the meaning of "forgiveness" (ghufrān), so it is construed upon it; al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said this and Abū Isḥāq preferred it.
Among them: that it is an adjective of a masculine qualified noun which was omitted while its adjective remained, the implied form being: "The mercy of Allah is a thing near". Among them: that it is in the meaning of pardon, or rain, or womb. Among them: that it is in the sense of kinship, i.e., "possessing nearness (dhāt qurb)", like «ḥāʾiḍ», i.e., "possessing menstruation". Among them: likening faʿīl in the sense of fāʿil to faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, in which the masculine and feminine are equal, like «jarīḥ» (wounded); as this was construed upon it when they said «asīr» and «usarāʾ», «qabīl» and «qubalāʾ», by construal upon «raḥīm» and «ruḥamāʾ», «ʿalīm» and «ʿulamāʾ», «ḥakīm» and «ḥukamāʾ». Among them: that it is a maṣdar that came on faʿīl, like «al-naqīq», the sound of the frog, and «al-ḍaghīb», the sound of the hare; and when it is a maṣdar, singular and masculine are required. Among them: that it is in the sense of mafʿūl, i.e., «muqarraba» (brought near); al-Kirmānī said this and it is not good, because faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl is not subject to analogy, and even on the assumption that it is analogical, it would be from the bare triliteral, not from an augmented one, and «muqarraba» is from the augmented. Among them: that it is of the class of the figuratively feminine, therefore the masculine is permissible, as in «ṭalaʿa al-shams». Some said: "That is not good, because that is where the verb precedes, as in «ṭalaʿa al-shams»; but if it comes later, the feminine is obligatory except in poetic necessity, as in his saying:
2215 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... nor a land whose herbage has grown as hers has grown
I say: this follows the view of Ibn Kaysān, who does not restrict that to poetic necessity but allows it in free prose. Al-Farrāʾ said: «Qarība» and «baʿīda»: if kinship or its absence is meant by them, the Arabs make them feminine only, saying: 'So-and-so (f.) is qarība to me', i.e., in kinship, and 'baʿīda from me', i.e., in kinship; but if nearness in place is meant, both are permissible, because «qarīb» and «baʿīd» stand in the place of "place", so you say: 'so-and-so is qarība and qarīb, baʿīda and baʿīd', the implied form being: 'she is in a near place or a far one'." He cited: 2216 - On the evening when ʿAfrāʾ was not near to you ... so that you could draw close, nor was ʿAfrāʾ far from you.
So he combined the two dialects. But al-Zajjāj rejected al-Farrāʾ's statement and said: "This is an error, because the way of the masculine and feminine is that they conform to their verbs." I say: this word has frequently come masculine in the poetry of the Arabs though it is an adjective of a feminine; Imruʾ al-Qays said:
2217 - Woe to him if he spends the evening and neither Umm Sālim is ... near, nor al-Basbāsa daughter of Yashkur.
And in the Qur'an: {وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ الساعة تَكُونُ قَرِيباً} [al-Aḥzāb: 63]. Abū ʿUbayda said: "«Qarīb» in the verse is not a description of it; it is an adverbial of it and a location, so it comes thus for the feminine, the dual and the plural; if a description is meant by it, agreement is obligatory; and likewise the word «baʿīd»." But ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān al-Akhfash declared him mistaken, saying: "Because if it were an adverbial it would be accusative, as in your saying «inna Zaydan qarīban minka»." And this is not a mistake, because the adverbial may be extended in usage, being given the ruling of plain nouns, so you say: «Zaydun amāmuka» and «ʿAmrun khalfuka» with the nominative of «amām» and «khalf»; the grammarians have stated explicitly that in such as «inna qarīban minka Zaydun», «qarīban» is the noun of «inna» and «Zaydun» its khabar, and that is by extension. And «من المحسنين» is attached to «قريب».

semin-durr:57-57.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {بُشْراً}: the disagreement of the readers about the singular «الريح» and its plural, in relation to the other sūras, has preceded in al-Baqara. As for «بُشْراً»: in this sūra and wherever it occurs in other sūras, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read it with ḍamma on the nūn and the shīn, and it is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Abū Rajāʾ, with disagreement from them, and Shayba ibn Niṣāḥ, al-Aʿraj, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, and the two Bedouins Abū Yaḥyā and Abū Nawfal. In this reading there are two aspects, from which six views result. One: that «nushuran» is the plural of «nāshir», like «bāzil» and «buzul», «shārif» and «shuruf», and it is an irregular plural of fāʿil. Then there is disagreement about the meaning of this «nashr»: it was said that it is by relation, either to «al-nashr», the opposite of folding, or to «al-nushūr» in the sense of bringing to life, as in His saying: {وَإِلَيْهِ النشور} [al-Mulk: 15]; and the meaning is "possessing spreading" or "possessing resurrection", like «lābin» and «tāmir». It was also said: it is a fāʿil from «nashara», the intransitive counterpart of «anshara»; one says «anshara Allāhu al-mayyita fa-nashara», so it is «nāshir», and he cited:
2218 - Until the people say, at what they have seen ... "O wonder at the dead one come back to life!"
It was also said: «nāshir» is in the sense of «munshir», i.e., the one who gives life; you say «nashara Allāhu al-mawtā» and «ansharahā», so faʿala and afʿala on this are of one meaning; and this third is weak.
The second aspect: that «nushuran» is the plural of «nashūr». This has two possibilities. One, which is the more preferable, that it is in the sense of fāʿil, and faʿūl in the sense of fāʿil is pluralized by analogy on fuʿul, like «ṣabūr» and «ṣubur», «shakūr» and «shukur». The second: that it is in the sense of mafʿūl, like «rakūb» and «ḥalūb» in the sense of «markūb» and «maḥlūb»; they said: because the wind is described as dying and described as being brought to life; of the former is his saying: 2219 - I hope that the wind will die ... so that I sit today and rest.
and of the latter their saying: "Allah brought the wind to life and revived it". And faʿūl in the sense of mafʿūl is pluralized on fuʿul, like «rasūl» and «rusul». A large group said so, except that this is not analogical in the singular or in the plural; I mean that faʿūl in the sense of mafʿūl is not analogical — you do not say «Zaydun ḍarūb» or «qatūl» in the sense of «maḍrūb» and «maqtūl» — and the plural of faʿūl in the sense of mafʿūl on fuʿul is not analogical either.
The explanation of the six aspects in this reading: it is the plural of «nāshir» meaning possessing spreading, the opposite of folding. Second: the plural of «nāshir» meaning possessing resurrection. Third: the plural of «nāshir», the intransitive counterpart of «anshara». Fourth: the plural of «nāshir» meaning «munshir». Fifth: the plural of «nushūr» in the sense of fāʿil. Sixth: the plural of «nushūr» in the sense of mafʿūl.
Ibn ʿĀmir read it with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn, and it is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, Yaḥyā ibn Wathāb, al-Nakhaʿī, Ibn Muṣarrif, al-Aʿmash and Masrūq. We have been spared the trouble of explaining this reading by what was mentioned about the reading before it, for it is a lightened form of it, as they said «rusl» for «rusul» and «kutb» for «kutub», so they removed the ḍamma for lightness; and since they did so in the singular, which is lighter than the plural, as in their saying «ʿunq» for «ʿunuq» and «ṭunb» for «ṭunub», what of the plural, which is heavier than the singular?
The two brothers read «نَشْراً» with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn.
Its aspect: it is a maṣdar standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial) with the meaning «nāshira» or «manshūra» or «dhāt nashr», all of it as preceded in its counterpart. It was also said: «nashran» is a confirming maṣdar, since «arsala» and «anshara» are close. It was also said: «nashran» is a maṣdar with the additional letters dropped, i.e., «inshāran», standing in the place of a ḥāl, i.e., «munshiran» or «munsharan», according to what preceded about that.
ʿĀṣim read «بُشْراً» with the single-dotted bāʾ with ḍamma and sukūn on the shīn, and it is the plural of «bashīra», like «nadhīra» and «nudhur». It was also said: the plural of faʿīl, like «qalīb» and «qulub», «raghīf» and «rughuf»; and it is taken in meaning from His saying, the Exalted, «وهو الذي يُرْسِلُ الرياحَ مُبَشِّرات», i.e., they give glad tidings of rain; then the ḍamma was lightened as preceded in «nushur». What supports that is that Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Sulamī and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with ḍamma, and it is transmitted from ʿĀṣim himself. So these are four readings among the seven.
The fifth is what I just mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās and those with him. Masrūq read «نَشَراً» with fatḥa on the nūn and the shīn, and there are two explanations of it: one, which Abū l-Fatḥ reported, that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like «ghayab» and «nashaʾ» for «ghāʾiba» and «nāshiʾa»; the second, that faʿalan is in the sense of mafʿūl, like «qabaḍ» in the sense of «maqbūḍ». Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «بَشْراً» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and sukūn on the shīn; it is also narrated from ʿĀṣim, on the basis that it is the maṣdar of «bashara», triliteral. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «بُشْرى» on the pattern «rujʿā», which is also a maṣdar. These are eight readings: four with nūn and four with bāʾ. This is what relates to the readings and what they are in terms of being singular or plural.
As for their accusative: in the reading of Nāfiʿ and those with him and Ibn ʿĀmir, it is accusative as a ḥāl from «الرياح» or «الريح», according to the disagreement preceded. So too in the reading of ʿĀṣim and what resembles it. As for the reading of the two brothers and Masrūq, it may be a maṣdar or a ḥāl; all this is plain, and so is the reading «بُشْرى» on the pattern «rujʿā». One more thing must be dealt with: whoever reads «الرياح» in the plural and reads «نُشْراً» as a plural, like Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr, it is plain. As for one who reads «الريح» in the singular and «نشراً» in the plural, like Ibn Kathīr, he makes «الريح» a generic noun, so it is a plural in meaning, and so he described it with the plural, like the saying of ʿAntara:
2220 - In it are forty-two milch camels ... black like the covert feather of the raven jet-black.
The ḥāl in some forms may be from the agent of «يُرْسل» or its object, and all this is known from what I have already set out, so there is no need to mention each form in its wording. And «بين» is an adverbial of «يُرْسل» or of the glad tidings, for one who reads it so.
And His saying: {حتى إِذَآ أَقَلَّتْ}: a terminal limit for His saying «يرسل». And «أقلَّتْ» means "carried", from «aqlaltu kadhā», i.e., I carried it with ease; it seems to be taken from «al-qilla» (scarcity), because one says «aqallahu», i.e., he carried it with ease, so he is capable (mustaqill) of what he carries.
And «al-qulla», with ḍamma on the qāf, is the well-known vessel, and «qilāl Hajar» likewise, because the camel «yuqilluhā», i.e., carries them. And «al-saḥāb» (cloud) — its explanation has preceded, and that it is both masculine and feminine, which is why the pronoun refers back to it in the masculine in His saying «سُقْناه». Had it been construed by meaning, as His saying «ثقالاً» was construed, in the plural, He would have said «سقناها». And «لبلدٍ»: al-Zamakhsharī made the lām causal, i.e., "for the sake of its land". The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is a difference between your saying «suqtu lahu mālan» and «suqtu li-ajlihi mālan»; for «suqtu lahu» means you delivered it to him and conveyed it to him, unlike «suqtuhu li-ajlihi», which does not necessarily imply delivering it to him; one may drive wealth to someone else for my sake, and this is plain." The disagreement about lightening and doubling «mayyit» has preceded in Āl ʿImrān. Here and in al-Rūm «يرسل» came in the future form, in keeping with what precedes it, for before it is {ادْعُوه خَوْفاً}, which is future; and in al-Rūm {ليَجْزي الذين}, which is future. As for al-Furqān and Fāṭir, it came in the past form «أرسل», in keeping with what precedes and follows it in the past; for before it is {ألم تَرَ إلى ربِّك كيفَ مَدَّ الظلَّ} and after it {مَرَجَ البحرَيْن}, so the past suited that; al-Kirmānī mentioned it.
And His saying: {فَأَنْزَلْنَا بِهِ}: the pronoun in «به» refers to the nearest mentioned, which is «بلد ميت», and on this the bāʾ must be locative, meaning: "We sent down the water in that dead land". The Shaykh made this the apparent sense. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the cloud. Then there are two views on the bāʾ. One: that it is in the sense of «مِن», i.e., "We sent down the water from the cloud". The second: that it is causal, i.e., "We sent down the water by means of the cloud". It was also said: it refers to the driving understood from the verb, and the bāʾ is also causal, i.e., "We sent down by reason of the driving of the cloud." This is weak, because the pronoun would refer to something not mentioned while it could refer to something mentioned.
And His saying: {فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ}: the disagreement over this hāʾ is like that over the one before it, and we add a view better than those, which is the reference to the water, and one should not depart from it; and «مِنْ» is partitive or for beginning; its counterpart has preceded. And «كذلك» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e., "He brings out the dead with a bringing out like Our bringing out of these fruits."

semin-durr:105-105.t:
His words, the Exalted: {حَقِيقٌ عَلَى أَنْ لاَّ أَقُولَ}: the majority read «على أَنْ» with «على», which is a preposition entering «أَنْ» and what is in its scope. Nāfiʿ read «عليَّ» with «على», which is a preposition entering the first-person yāʾ. «Translator's note: the source text repeats the sentence about the majority reading and Nāfiʿ's reading, with the first-person yāʾ clause, twice; it is translated as written.» As for the reading of the majority, it has six views, of which al-Zamakhsharī mentioned four. He, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "In the wording there is a difficulty, and it does not lack several explanations. One: that it is among what is inverted in speech, as in his saying:
2255 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
and the spears are made wretched by the red, huge-bodied men (al-ḍayāṭira)
its meaning being: 'and the huge-bodied men are made wretched by the spears'." The Shaykh said: "Our colleagues restrict inversion (qalb) to necessity, so the Quran should be kept free of it." I say: people have three schools on it: permissibility generally, prohibition generally, and the distinction: if it yields a novel meaning it is allowed, otherwise prohibited; and its clarification has preceded, and other examples of it in the Mighty Quran will come. On this view this reading becomes like Nāfiʿ's in meaning, since the original is: "Saying the truth is binding upon me", and he inverted the wording and it became: "I am bound to say the truth." He said: "The second: what is obligatory upon you, you are obligated to it; so when saying the truth was binding upon him, he was bound to saying the truth, i.e. obligated to it. The third: ḥaqīq is made to imply the sense 'eager' (ḥarīṣ), as hayyajanī was made to imply the sense 'reminded me' (dhakkaranī) in the verse in al-Kitāb. The fourth: «على» is in the sense of the bāʾ." I say: Abū l-Ḥasan, al-Farrāʾ and al-Fārisī said this view. They said: «على» is in the sense of the bāʾ just as the bāʾ is in the sense of «على» in His words: {وَلاَ تَقْعُدُواْ بِكُلِّ صِرَاطٍ} [الأعراف: 86], i.e. on every. Al-Farrāʾ said: "The Arabs say: 'I shot ʿalā l-qaws and bi-l-qaws' (with the bow), and 'I came ʿalā ḥālin ḥasana and bi-ḥālin ḥasana'." Except that al-Akhfash said: "That is not regular; if you said 'I went ʿalā Zayd' meaning 'with Zayd', it would not be permitted." I say: because the school of the Basrans is the absence of figurative extension in particles. By "the verse" he means the poet's saying:
2256 - When the grey doves sing, it stirs me (hayyajanī) ... even if I had consoled myself about her, Umm ʿAmmār,
and by "al-Kitāb" the book of Sībawayh, which is a proper name by predominance among the people of this craft. The fifth, which is the most apt and the most deeply into the subtleties of the Quran: that Mūsā, peace be upon him, immerses himself in describing himself as truthful on that occasion, especially since it is reported that when Mūsā said to Pharaoh, may Allah curse him: 'I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds', he said to him: 'You lie', so he says: 'I am bound upon saying the truth', i.e. saying the truth is necessary for me, that I be the one saying it and standing by it, and only one like me is content to speak it." The Shaykh said: "This view is valid only if he means that «أن لا أقول» is a ṣifa of him, as you say 'I am on the saying of the truth', i.e. my way and my habit is saying the truth.
The sixth: «على» is attached to «رسول». Ibn Miqsam said: «حقيق» is of the naʿt of «رسول», i.e. 'a messenger, worthy, from the Lord of the worlds, sent on the condition that I say about Allah only the truth'; this is a sound and clear meaning, and most of the exegetes among the linguists overlooked attaching «على» to «رسول», and it did not occur to them to attach it except to «حقيق»."
The Shaykh said: "His statement has an apparent contradiction, because he first implied «أرسلت» as the operator in «على», and finally said 'because they overlooked attaching «على» to «رسول»'. As for this last, it is not permissible according to the Basrans, because «رسول» has been described before taking its object, and that is not permitted; as for attaching it to an implied «أرسلت», indicated by the word «رسول», it is a permissible implication. His statement is to be interpreted as meaning, by his saying 'attached to «رسول»', that since it indicates it, attributing attachment to it is valid." I say: Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma said, after mentioning this view from Ibn Miqsam: "And the four views of al-Zamakhsharī; but these are forced views, and the meaning is only what I mentioned first, i.e. Ibn Miqsam's view, and this has the difficulty that the Shaykh mentioned, of the active participle, or what runs like it, operating while being described.
Nāfiʿ's reading is clear and has three views. One: the speech is complete at His words «حقيق», with «عليَّ» a fronted khabar and «أنْ لا أقول» a delayed mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: "Upon me is not saying other than the truth", i.e. "so I say only the truth". The second: «حقيق» is a fronted khabar and «أن لا أقول» a mubtadaʾ, as explained. The third: «أَنْ لا أقول» is the fāʿil of «حقيق», as though it were said: "It is due and necessary that I not say"; and this is the clearest of the views for its clarity in wording and meaning; and on the last two views «عليَّ» is attached to «حقيق», since you say "ḥaqqa ʿalayhi kadhā". The Exalted said: {أولئك الذين حَقَّ عليهم القولُ}. On the first view it is attached to an omitted word, as is known more than once.
As for the nominative of «حقيق», it has been stated that it may be a fronted khabar, and it may be a ṣifa of «رسول»; on this it is weak for «مِنْ رب» to be a ṣifa, so as not to necessitate putting a non-explicit ṣifa before an explicit one, so it ought to be attached to «رسول» itself, with «مِنْ» for figurative beginning of the extent.
It may be a second khabar.
It may be a mubtadaʾ with what follows as khabar, according to the reading of whoever intensified the yāʾ, and what justified an indefinite as mubtadaʾ then is the attachment of the preposition and its genitive noun to it.
So four views have been gathered for its nominative; and is it in the sense of fāʿil or in the sense of mafʿūl? The evident view is that it admits both generally, I mean on Nāfiʿ's reading and on the reading of others. Al-Wāḥidī said, relating from others: "With Nāfiʿ's reading it admits both, and with the reading of the majority it is in the sense of mafʿūl", for he said: "ḥaqīq on this reading, meaning Nāfiʿ's reading, may be in the sense of fāʿil. Shamir said: the Arabs say 'ḥaqqa ʿalayya an afʿala kadhā'. Al-Layth said: ḥaqqa l-shayʾ means it became obligatory, and 'it is due upon you to do it', and 'ḥaqīq ʿalayya an afʿalahu'; so this is in the sense of fāʿil", then he said: "Al-Layth said: ḥaqīq is in the sense of mafʿūl, and on this you say: 'so-and-so is maḥqūq ʿalayhi to do'. Al-Aʿshā said:
2257 - She is indeed bound to respond to his voice ... and to know that the one helped is granted success.
And Jarīr said:
2258 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... Fall short, for you, by falling short, are deserving."
Then he said: "and ḥaqīq on this reading, meaning the reading of the majority, is in the sense of maḥqūq." End.
Ubayy read «بَأَنْ لا أقول», and this strengthens that «على» is in the sense of the bāʾ. ʿAbd Allāh and al-Aʿmash read «أنْ لا أقول» without a preposition, so it is possible that the preposition is «على» as in the reading of the majority, and that the preposition is the bāʾ as in Ubayy's reading.
«الحقَّ» may be a direct object because it implies the sense of "he charged him with", and may be accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "the saying of the truth"; and the exception is vacated.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ}: «إذا» is the sudden one (fujāʾiyya). It has already been stated that it has three schools: a ẓarf of place, or of time, or a particle. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "idhā is a ẓarf of place in this passage according to al-Mubarrad, in that it is a khabar about a body, while the sound view, held by the people, is that it is a ẓarf of time everywhere." I say: what is well known among the people is the statement of al-Mubarrad, and it is the school of Sībawayh. As for its being time, that is the school of al-Riyāshī, and it is also attributed to Sībawayh. As for his words "in that it is a khabar about a body", it is not here a khabar about a body; rather the khabar of «هي» is the word «ثعبان», not the word «إذا».
Al-thuʿbān is the large male of snakes. Its derivation is from thaʿabtu l-makān, i.e. I made it burst with water; it was likened, in its gliding, to the gliding of water. One says thaʿabtu l-māʾ, I made it burst forth, and it burst forth (inthaʿaba). From it comes mathʿab al-maṭar. In the ḥadīth: "He will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound gushing (yathʿabu) blood." Here there is a question and its answer: He described it once as a thuʿbān, which is the huge, fearsome in creation, and in another place by His words {كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ} [النمل: 10], while al-jānn among snakes is the light, slender in creation; so how are these two attributes combined? Al-Zamakhsharī answered elsewhere than this place with two answers. One: that it combined for it the two things: the largeness of body like the thuʿbān and the lightness of movement and speed of going like the jānn. The second: that at the beginning of its affair it is like the jānn, then grows and its creation increases until it becomes a thuʿbān.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His words, the Exalted: {لِلنَّاظِرِينَ}: attached to an omitted word, because it is a ṣifa of «بيضاء». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is «للناظرين» attached? I say: it is attached to «بيضاء», and the meaning is: 'and lo, it is white for the onlookers', and it is not white for the onlookers except when its whiteness is wondrous, beyond the ordinary, such that people gather to look at it as onlookers gather for marvels." What Abū l-Qāsim mentioned is an interpretation of meaning, not an interpretation of grammatical analysis, and how could he intend a grammatical analysis? He only intended semantic attachment, not technical, like their saying: this speech is attached to that speech, i.e. it is a completion of the meaning for it. And he said in this sūra:
{قَالَ الملأ}

semin-durr:109-109.t:
{قَالَ الملأ}: so he attributed the saying to them. In al-Shuʿarāʾ: «قال للملأ», so he attributed the saying to Pharaoh. Al-Zamakhsharī answered that with three views. One: that this speech issued from him and from them, so here he related it from them and in al-Shuʿarāʾ from him. The second: that he said it originally and his close circle took it from him and said it to those after them. The third: that they said it on his behalf to the people by way of conveying, as kings do: one of them forms an opinion and conveys it to his close circle, then they convey it to the common people. This third is close to the second in meaning.
The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read here and in Yūnus: «بكل سَحَّارٍ», and the rest «بكل ساحر». There is no disagreement that what is in al-Shuʿarāʾ is «بكل سَحَّارٍ». Sāḥir and saḥḥār are like ʿālim and ʿallām, and it is known that the pattern faʿʿāl is a pattern of intensification. What favours «سَحَّار» is that it goes beyond «عليم», both being patterns of intensification. What favours «ساحر» is that the like of it preceded in His words «إنَّ هذا لساحر», and this is in keeping with it.

semin-durr:110-110.t:
In al-Shuʿarāʾ: «بسحره», and here without «ذلك». They said: because the beginning of this verse is built on brevity.
His words: {فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ}: the discussion of «ماذا» has already preceded at the beginning of this work. The majority read «تأمرون» with fatḥa on the nūn. Kardam narrated from Nāfiʿ a kasra on it. On both readings «ماذا» as a whole may be a single noun in the position of accusative as the second object of «تأمرون» after the omission of the yāʾ, with the first object of «تأمرون» omitted, namely the speaker's yāʾ, the implied form being: "With what do you command me?" On Nāfiʿ's reading, you do not say that the first object is omitted; rather it is in the force of the pronounced one, because the kasra indicates it, so this omission is not the omission in the reading of the majority. It is possible that «ما» is interrogative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «ذا» a relative with the ṣila «تأمرون», and the returning pronoun omitted, and the first object also omitted on the reading of the majority; the returning pronoun implied is accusative in position, not transitivized to it with the bāʾ, so its implied form is: "What is it that you command me (tamurūnanīhi)?" Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied it as «تأمروني به», and the Shaykh objected to him, that this necessitates omitting a returning pronoun governed by a preposition by which the relative is not governed, then excused him, saying that he intended the original implication, and then latitude was taken in it so that the preposition was omitted and the pronoun attached to the verb. Is this clause part of the speech of the chiefs, who thus addressed Pharaoh alone out of honour for him, as kings are addressed in the plural form; or did they say it to him and to his companions; or is it from the speech of Pharaoh, on the implication of a saying, i.e. "Pharaoh said to them: so what do you command?" What supports its being from Pharaoh's speech is His words, the Exalted: «قالوا: أرْجِهْ».
Is «تأمرون» from the familiar command (amr), or from the amr which means consultation? The second is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from amartuhu, so he amaranī bi-kadhā, i.e. I consulted him and he advised me an opinion."

semin-durr:177-177.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَآءَ مَثَلاً}: «ساء» has the meaning of «بئس» ("evil is"), and its agent is a latent pronoun in it, and «مثلاً» is a tamyīz (specification) explaining it. It has been mentioned more than once that the agent in this chapter, when it is a pronoun, is explained by what follows it, and the dual, plural and feminine of it are dispensed with, by dualising, pluralising and feminising the specification, according to the Basrans. It was also mentioned that «ساء» originally takes an object, and that the one specified for censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) can only be of the genus of the specification, / and the specification explains the agent, so it is the same as it; so it is necessary that the agent, the specification and the one specified for censure be true of one and the same thing. If this is known, then His saying «القوم» is not true of the specification and the agent; hence an omitted element must be supposed, either in the specification or in the one specified for censure. In the first it is supposed: "evil are the people of a likeness" or "the people of the likeness of the people"; in the second it is supposed: "evil as a likeness is the likeness of the people"; then the muḍāf was omitted in both suppositions and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place; and this clause is an emphasis of the one before it.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «ساء مثلُ القوم» with «مثل» nominative, annexed to «القوم». And it is reported from al-Jaḥdarī likewise, and it is reported from him with kasra on the mīm, sukūn on the thāʾ, ḍamma on the lām and genitive «القوم». This reading ascribed to this group admits of two views. One: that «ساء» is for wonder, indeclinable in implication on the pattern faʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn, like their saying «لقَضُو الرجل», and «مثل القوم» is its agent, the implied form being: "How evil is the likeness of the people!", and the relative noun on this view is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «قوم». The second: that it has the meaning of «بئس», and «مَثَلُ القوم» is the agent, and the relative noun on this is in the position of nominative because it is the one specified for censure, and on this an omitted muḍāf is necessary so that the agent and the one specified are true of the same thing; the implied form being: "evil is the likeness of the people, the likeness of those who…". The Shaykh supposed a specification in this reading, and there is an objection in this, since no specification is needed when the agent is overt, to the point that they made combining the two a necessity (of poetry), as in his saying:
2340 - تَزوَّدْ مثلَ زادِ أبيك فينا ... فنعمَ الزَّادُ زادُ أبيك زادا
(Take provisions like your father's provisions among us; how excellent a provision is your father's provision, as provision!)
And there are three positions on the question: permissible absolutely; prohibited absolutely; and the distinction: if it is different from the wording and gives a new benefit it is permitted, such as «نعم الرجل شجاعاً زيد», and on this is his saying:
2341 - تخيَّرَهُ فلم يَعْدِلْ سواه ... فنِعْمَ المرءُ مِنْ رجلٍ تَهامي
(He chose him and did not prefer another; how excellent a man — a man of Tihāma!)
His saying: {وَأَنفُسَهُمْ كَانُواْ يَظْلِمُونَ}: an object of «يظلمون», and in it is evidence for putting the khabar of kāna before it, because putting the object first indicates putting the governor first, generally. I said "generally" because there are places where that is prohibited, such as {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9]: «اليتيم» is an object of «تقهر», and it is not permissible to put «تقهر» before its jussive-governing particle; and this is open to discussion.
This kāna-clause admits of two views. One: that it is conjoined to the ṣila, which is «كَذَّبوا بآياتنا». The second: that it is resumptive; on both sayings it has no position; the object was put first to give exclusivity, and this follows the way of al-Zamakhsharī and his peers.

semin-durr:178-178.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يَهْدِ الله فَهُوَ المهتدي}: it took into account the wording of «مَنْ» and so used the singular, and took into account its meaning in His saying «أولئك هم الخاسرون» and so used the plural. The yāʾ of «المهتدي» is retained by all the readers because it is retained in the script; a disagreement concerning the one in al-Isrāʾ and a discussion of it will come to you. Al-Wāḥidī said: "«فهو المهتدي»: retaining the yāʾ is permissible on the basis of the original, and dropping it is permissible for lightness, as was said in the verse of the Book [Translator's note: i.e., Sībawayh's Kitāb]:
2342 - فَطِرْتُ بمُنْصُلي في يَعْمَلات ... دوامي الأَيْدِ يَخْبِطْنَ السَّريحا
(So I sped with my sword among swift she-camels, bloody-handed [in their forelegs], striking the leather thong.)
and from it:
2343 - كنَواحِ ريشِ حَمامةٍ نَجْديةِ ... ومَسَحْتَ باللِّثتين عَصْفَ الإِثْمِدِ
(Like the wing-feathers of a Najdī dove, and you wiped the gums with the stalks of kohl.)
Ibn Jinnī said: 'He likened the muḍāf ilayhi to tanwīn, so he dropped the yāʾ for it.'"

semin-durr:179-179.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِجَهَنَّمَ}: two views are permissible regarding this lām. One: that it is the lām of outcome and consequence (ṣayrūra and ʿāqiba), and the one who says so needs it to be the lām of consequence only because of His saying, the Exalted {وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الجن والإنس إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 56], for this is a considered, restricted reason, so how can this also be a reason? And they adduced the poet's saying: 2344 - لِدُوا للموت وابْنُوا للخراب ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Beget for death and build for ruin…)
and the other's saying:
2345 - ألا كلُّ مولودٍ فللموتِ يُوْلَدُ ... ولستُ أرى حَيّاً لحيٍّ يُخَلَّدُ
(Indeed every one born is born for death, and I see no living being made immortal.)
and the other's saying:
2346 - فللموتِ تَغْذُو الوالداتُ سِخالَها ... كما لخرابِ الدور تُبْنَى المساكنُ
(For death mothers nurture their young, as dwellings are built for the ruin of houses.)
The second: that it is for cause, in that since their end was to it, that was made a cause in the manner of figurative usage.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya rebutted the one who made it the lām of consequence, saying: "This is not correct, and the lām of consequence is conceivable only when the agent's act did not aim at the outcome of the matter being that; but here the act was aimed at what the matter comes to [be] — their dwelling in Hell"; and the lām on this is attached to «ذَرَأْنا». It is also permissible that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «كثيراً», because in origin it is an adjective of it had it come later. There is no need to claim inversion, that the origin is: "We created Hell for many," since that is a necessity or rare.
And {مِّنَ الجن} is an adjective of «كثيراً». «لهم قلوب» is a clause in the position of accusative: either an adjective of «كثير» too, or a ḥāl from «كثيراً» even though it is indefinite, for its being specified by the description; or from the latent pronoun in «من الجن», because it carries / a pronoun by virtue of its being an adjective. It is also permissible that «لهم» alone be the description or the ḥāl, and «قلوب» its agent, so it would be a description with a singular, which is preferable. And His saying: {لاَّ يَفْقَهُونَ بِهَا}, and likewise the negated clause, is in the position of an adjective of what precedes it, and this description is almost necessary — were it to occur in other than the Qurʾān — because there is no benefit without it; if you said «لزيد قَلْبٌ وله عينٌ» and stopped, no great benefit would appear from it.

semin-durr:180-180.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الحسنى}: two sayings about it. The clearer: that it is the feminine of «أحسن», and the broken plural of a non-rational being may be described by what the feminine is described by, such as «مآرب أخرى»; and had it been made to agree (in the plural), the construction would have been good, as in His saying: {مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ} [al-Baqara: 184]. The second: that «الحسنى» is a maṣdar on the pattern fuʿlā, like al-rujʿā and al-buqyā. He said:
2347 - ولا يَجْزون مِنْ حُسْنى بسوءٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And they do not repay a good with evil…)
And «الأسماء» here: the words indicating the Creator, the Exalted, such as «الله» and «الرحمن». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What is meant by them is the namings (al-tasmiyāt), by the consensus of the interpreters; nothing else is possible." There is an objection in this, because tasmiya is a maṣdar, and a maṣdar is not invoked with, on both sayings in the explanation of invocation; for the meaning of «فادعوه» is "call Him by them," as in their saying: "O Allah, O Raḥmān, O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity, forgive us." It was said: "name Him by them," as you say «سَمَّيْت ابني بزيد».
His saying: {يُلْحِدُونَ}: Ḥamza read here and in al-Naḥl and Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda «يَلْحدون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ, from laḥada, triliteral. The rest read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, from alḥada. It was said: they are one in meaning, which is inclining and deviating. From it is laḥd al-qabr (the niche-grave), because it is inclined, by digging it to the side, unlike ḍarīḥ (the central trench-grave), which is dug in the middle; and from their speech: "What has the finder done? They said: the niche-digger (al-lāḥid) niched him." Ibn al-Sikkīt held that they are one in meaning and said: "They are turning away from the truth." And alḥada is used more than laḥada. He said:
2348 - ليس الإِمام بالشحيح المُلْحِدِ
(The imam is not the stingy deviator.)
Another said: "laḥada means 'he leaned and attached himself,' and alḥada: 'he inclined and deviated,'" al-Kisāʾī said so. It was also transmitted from him: alḥada: he turned away; laḥada: he inclined. They said: for this reason Ḥamza agreed in al-Naḥl, since its meaning is: "they incline to him."
Abū ʿUbayda transmitted from al-Aṣmaʿī: "alḥada: he disputed and argued; laḥada: he swerved and inclined." The reading of the majority was preferred by consensus on His saying «بإلحاد». Al-Wāḥidī said: "Lāḥid is scarcely heard from the Arabs." I say: their abstaining from the coming of the active participle of the triliteral indicates its rarity, and I have given earlier from their speech «لحده اللاحِد». The meaning of ilḥād in it is that they derived from them [the divine names] names for their gods, so they say: al-Lāt from the word «الله», al-ʿUzzā from the word «العزيز», and Manāt from the word «المَنَّان»; and it is possible that what is meant is that they named Him with what does not befit His majesty.

semin-durr:181-181.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ أُمَّةٌ}: «مَنْ» may be a relative noun or a qualified indefinite, and «يَهْدون» is an adjective of «أمة». Some of them said: "There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: 'and of those We created for Paradise,' which is indicated by what is established for their counterparts, namely His saying: {وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ} [al-ʿArāf: 179]." [Translator's note: the source gives the sūra name as «العراف»; it is al-Aʿrāf.]

semin-durr:149-149.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سُقِطَ في أَيْدِيهِمْ}: The preposition phrase stands in the place of the agent. It is also said: what stands in the place of [the agent] is the pronoun of the maṣdar, which is السُّقوط, i.e. "falling fell in their hands". The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) reported from some that he said: "«سقط» implies an object, which here is the maṣdar, i.e. الإِسقاط, as in your saying «ذُهب بزيد»." He said: "The right form is: it is here the pronoun of the maṣdar which is السُّقوط, because the maṣdar of «سقط» is not الإِسقاط, and because what stands in the place of the agent is the pronoun of the maṣdar and not the maṣdar." al-Wāḥidī reported from al-Azharī that their saying «سُقِط في يده» is like the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

2294 - دَعْ عنك نَهْباً صِيح في حُجُراتِه ... ولكنْ حديثاً ما حديث الرواحلِ
(Leave aside plunder cried out in its precincts, but tell me — what is the tale of the riding camels?)

in that the verb is attributed to the preposition phrase, as if it were said: "the plunderer cried out in its precincts"; and likewise what is meant is «سُقِط في يده», i.e. "regret fell in his hand." I say: his saying "i.e. regret fell" is an explicit statement that what stands in the place of the agent is the preposition, not the pronoun of the maṣdar. al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj reported that one says سُقِط في يده and also أُسقط, except that al-Farrāʾ said: "سَقَط, i.e. the triliteral, is more frequent and better." This expression is used for remorse and bewilderment.

The statements of the lexicographers about its origin were confused. Abū Marwān Ibn Sirāj, the lexicographer, said: "The saying of the Arabs سُقِط في يده is among what has defeated me as to its meaning." al-Wāḥidī said: "It is clear from the statements of the exegetes and the lexicographers that «سُقِط في يده» means 'he regretted', and that it is used in describing the remorseful. As for the account of its origin and what defines it, I have seen nothing from the leading authorities of the language that I accept, except what al-Zajjājī mentioned, for he said: 'His saying, the Exalted, «سُقِط في أيديهم» in the sense of "they regretted" is a composition not heard before the Quran and not known to the Arabs, and it is not found in their poetry. What proves the soundness of that is that when the poets of Islam heard this composition and used it in their speech, the manner of its use was hidden from them, because their habit did not run to it, and Abū Nuwās said:

2295 - ونشوةٌ سُقِطْتُ منها في يدي ...
(And an intoxication from which I was "fallen" into my hand…)

Abū Nuwās is the master-scholar, yet he erred in using this expression, because فُعِلْتُ is formed only from a transitive verb, and «سَقَط» is intransitive and does not become transitive except with a preposition; one does not say «سُقطت», just as one does not say رُغبت or غُضِبت; one says only رُغِب في and غُضِب على. Abū Ḥātim mentioned that «سُقِط فلان في يده» means "he regretted", and this is an error like the saying of Abū Nuwās; had it been so, the composition would have been «ولما سُقطوا في أيديهم» and «سُقِط القومُ في أيديهم». Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is said of one who has regretted a matter and is powerless over it: سُقِط في يده."'"

al-Wāḥidī said: "The mention of the hand here is for two reasons. One: it is said of whatever comes about, even if it is something that cannot be in the hand, 'something disagreeable has come into his hand', likening what occurs in the soul and heart to what is seen with the eye; and the hand is singled out for mention because the committing of sins is by it, so the blame returns to it as it is the principal limb, and so is attributed to it what it did not itself do, as in {ذلك بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ} [al-Ḥajj: 10], though many sins were not put forward by the hand. The second: that regret is an event occurring in the heart whose trace appears in the hand, for the regretful bites his hand and strikes one hand against the other, as in {فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ} [al-Kahf: 42], where turning over the palms is an expression for regret, and as in {وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظالم على يَدَيْهِ} [al-Furqān: 27]. So since the trace of regret occurs in the hand in the way we mentioned, the falling of regret was attributed to the hand; for what appears to the eyes of the act of the regretful is the turning over of the palm and the biting of the fingers and hand, just as joy is a meaning in the heart that a person senses, and what appears of it is the state of stirring, movement, laughter and the like."

al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ولمَّا سُقِط في أيديهم» means: when their regret grew intense, because it is the way of one whose regret and anguish are intense to bite his hand in grief so that his hand becomes something fallen into, since his mouth has fallen into it." It is also said: it is the habit of the regretful to lower his head and rest his chin on his hand, leaning on it, and to be in a posture such that if his hand were removed he would fall on his face, so it is as if the hand is fallen into. The meaning of «في» is «على», so the meaning of «في أيديهم» is "upon their hands", like {وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النخل} [Ṭā Hā: 71]. It is also said: it is taken from السِّقاط, which is abundant error, and the one who errs regrets his deed. Ibn Abī Kāhil said:

2296 - كيف يَرْجُون سِقاطي بعدما ... لَفَّع الراسَ بياضٌ وصَلَعْ
(How can they hope for my slip after whiteness and baldness have wrapped my head?)

It is also said: it is taken from السَّقيط, which is the frost that covers the ground, resembling snow; from it one says سَقَطَت الأرض as one says ثَلَجت; the سَقْط and سَقيط melt at the least warmth and do not remain, and one into whose hand the frost falls obtains nothing from it, so this became a proverb for everyone who loses in his outcome and gains nothing of value from his aim.

Know that «سُقِطَ في يده» was counted by some among the verbs that are not conjugated, like نِعْمَ and بئس. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «سَقَط في أيديهم», active, its agent latent, i.e. "regret fell"; this is the view of al-Zajjāj. al-Zamakhsharī said: "the biting fell." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "loss and disappointment fell"; and all of these are examples. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أُسْقِط», quadriliteral, passive. It has already been mentioned that it is a dialect reported by al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj.

His saying: {وَرَأَوْاْ أَنَّهُمْ}: this is of the heart, and in this there is no need for preposing and postposing as some claimed. He said: "its implied form: when they saw that they had gone astray and regret fell in their hands," saying "because regret and anguish occur only after knowledge."

His saying: {لَئِن لَّمْ يَرْحَمْنَا}: the two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza) read «ترحمنا وتغفر» in the second person, and «ربَّنا» accusative. This is the reading of al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Wathāb, Ibn Muṣarrif, al-Jaḥdarī, al-Aʿmash and Ayyūb; and the rest of the seven read with the third-person yāʾ in both, and «ربُّنا» nominative, which is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, al-Aʿraj, Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar. The accusative is as a vocative, and the second person suits it; the nominative is as an agent. It is possible that this speech came from all of them in succession, or that this was from one group and that from another group: whoever was overcome by fear and was strong enough to face Him addressed Him, asking release from his sin; and whoever was overcome by shame put his speech in the manner of one shy of addressing, so he attributed the verb to the absent.

semin-durr:150-150.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {غَضْبَانَ أَسِفاً}: two ḥāls from Moses according to those who allow multiple ḥāls; and according to those who do not, «أَسِفاً» is made a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «غضبان», so it is a nested ḥāl, or it is made a badal from the first. There is something to consider in this, for the difficulty of fitting it into the categories of badal; the nearest thing said is that it is a badal of part from whole (badal baʿḍ min kull) if we explain الأَسِف as intensely angry, or a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) if we explain it as sorrowful. One says أسِف يأسَفُ أَسَفاً, i.e. his anger became intense. The Exalted said: {فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا انتقمنا مِنْهُمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 55]. It is also said: rather its meaning is "sorrowful," and from it is the saying:

2297 - غيرُ مأسوفٍ على زمنٍ ... ينقضي بالهمِّ والحزن
(Not to be regretted is a time that passes away in worry and sorrow.)

Since the two are close in meaning, the badal is sound as I mentioned to you; and what shows the closeness between them, as al-Wāḥidī said, is the saying:

2298 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
فحزنُ كلِّ أخي حُزْنٍ أخو الغضبِ
(… [first half elided in the source] … for the grief of every man of grief is the brother of anger.)

and al-Aʿshā said:

2299 - أرى رجلاً منكمْ أسِيفاً كأنما ... يَضُمُّ إلى كَشْحَيْه كَفَّاً مُخَضَّبا
(I see a man among you, angry/grieved, as if he were pressing to his flanks a dyed hand.)

This is in the sense of "angry". And in the ḥadīth: «إنَّ أبا بكر رجلٌ أسيف», i.e. sorrowful; and رجلٌ أَسِف is used when the permanence and settledness of the attribute is intended; if time is intended by it, it comes on فاعِل.

His saying: {قَالَ: بِئْسَمَا}: this is the apodosis of «لمَّا», and the discussion of «بئسما» has preceded, but the one specified for blame is omitted, and the agent is latent, explained by «ما خَلَفْتموني»; the implied form being: "evil is the succession in which you succeeded me, your succession."

His saying: {أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ}: about «أَمْرَ» there are two views. One: that it is accusative as an object after the dropping of the preposition, and the verb being given the meaning of what takes its object directly; the original: أَعَجِلْتُمْ عن أمر ربكم. al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says عَجِل عن الأمر when he left it incomplete, and its opposite is تَمَّ, and another made him hasten away from it (أعجله عنه); and it is given the meaning of «سبق» (outstrip) so it is transitivised like it, and one says عَجِلْتُ الأمر; and the meaning: did you hasten away from the command of your Lord?" The second: that it is transitive by itself, not given the sense of another verb.
