Yaʿqūb related: «عَجِلْتُ الشيء» "I outstripped the thing," and أعجلت الرجل "I urged the man to haste," i.e. I made him hurry.

His saying: {يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ}: three views. One: that the sentence is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun of Moses in «أخذ», i.e. "he took him, dragging him to himself." The second: that it is a ḥāl from «رأس»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, and there is something to consider in it because of the lack of a link. The third: that it is a ḥāl from «أخيه»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak," meaning because a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi seldom occurs or is impossible according to some. I say: it has been mentioned more than once that some allow it in cases like this, namely when the muḍāf is a part of the muḍāf ilayhi.

His saying: {قَالَ ابن أُمَّ}: the two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza), Abū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read here and in Ṭā Hā with kasra on the mīm, and the rest with fatḥa. As for the reading with fatḥa, there are two doctrines. The doctrine of the Basrans: that the two are indeclinable on fatḥa because of their being compounded like خمسة عشر; on this «ابن» is not annexed to «أم» but is compounded with it, so the vowel of the two is a vowel of indeclinability. The second: the doctrine of the Kufans, that «ابن» is annexed to «أُمّ», and «أم» is annexed to the first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ has been turned into an alif as it is turned in a vocative annexed to the first-person yāʾ, as in يا غلاماً, then the alif was dropped and the fatḥa sufficed for it, as the kasra suffices for the yāʾ; so the vowel of «ابن» is then a case vowel and it is annexed to «أُمَّ», which is in the position of genitive by annexation.

As for the reading with kasra, on the Basran view it is a kasra of indeclinability on account of the first-person yāʾ, in the sense that we annexed this entire compounded noun to the first-person yāʾ, so its end was given kasra, then the kasra sufficed for the yāʾ; it is therefore a parallel to: يا أحَدَ عشري, then يا أحد عَشرِ with omission. It is not possible that they remain in annexation, since dropping the yāʾ is not allowed because the noun is not a vocative, but is annexed to the vocative, so dropping the yāʾ from it is not allowed. On the Kufan view the kasra is a case kasra, and the yāʾ is dropped, the kasra sufficing for it, as the fatḥa sufficed for its alif. These two views apply to «ابن أم», «ابن عم», «ابنة أم» and «ابنة عم». Know that in these four examples specifically, five dialects are allowed, the most eloquent being: dropping the yāʾ with the kasra sufficing for it; then turning the yāʾ into an alif, so the kasra necessarily becomes fatḥa; then dropping the alif with the fatḥa sufficing for it; then retaining the yāʾ quiescent or with fatḥa. As for other than these four examples, of what is annexed to something annexed to the first-person yāʾ in the vocative, only what is allowed in other than the chapter of the vocative is allowed in it, because it is not the one addressed, as in يا غلامَ أبي and يا غلام أمي; these examples specifically took this course only by placing the two words in the position of a single word and because of frequency of use.

«يابن أمي» is also read with the yāʾ retained quiescent, and similar to it is the saying:

2300 - يابنَ أُمِّي ويا شُقَيِّق نفسي ... أنت خَلَّفْتَني لدهرٍ شديدِ
(O son of my mother, O twin of my soul, you left me behind for a harsh time.)

and the saying of another:

2301 - يا بنَ أمي فَدَتْكَ نفسي ومالي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O son of my mother, may my soul and my wealth ransom you … [rest elided in the source])

It is also read «ابن إمِّ» with kasra on the hamza and the mīm, which is imitation of the vowel. And an example of turning the yāʾ into an alif is the saying:

2302 - يا بنة عَمَّا لا تَلُومي واهْجَعي ...
(O daughter of my paternal uncle, do not blame me, and sleep.)

and his saying:

2303 - كُنْ لي لا عَليَّ يا بن عَمَّا ... نَدُمْ عَزِيزَيْنِ ونُكْفَ الذَّمَّا
(Be for me, not against me, O son of my paternal uncle; we shall remain two mighty ones and be spared blame.)

His saying: {فَلاَ تُشْمِتْ}: the majority have ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from أَشْمت, quadriliteral, «الأعداء» being a direct object. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «فلا تَشْمِتْ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the mīm, and Mujāhid with fatḥa on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the mīm, «الأعداءَ» being accusative as a direct object. In these two readings there are two explanations; the more evident: that شمِت or شَمَت, with kasra or fatḥa on the mīm, is transitive by itself like the quadriliteral أشمت; one says شمت بي زيدٌ العدوَّ, as one says أَشْمَتَّ بي العدو.

The second: that «تَشْمت» is attributed to the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. "do not (Yourself) cause gloating, O Lord," and this is allowed as {الله يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ} is allowed, with an implied governor for "the enemies" accusative as in the reading of the group; so said Ibn Jinnī. There is no need for this artifice because the triliteral «شمت» can be transitive by itself, and implication is contrary to the basic rule. Abū l-Baqāʾ said of this explanation: "do not you cause gloating," making the agent the pronoun of Moses, which is preferable to attributing it to the pronoun of Allah the Exalted. As for his likening it to {الله يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ}, that is allowed only for the sake of correspondence in His saying {إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ} [al-Baqara: 14], and like {وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ الله} [Āl ʿImrān: 54], and it is not allowed apart from correspondence.

Ḥumayd ibn Qays read: «فلا تَشْمِت» like the reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Mujāhid like his reading at first, except that the two made «الأعداء» nominative as agent, making شمت intransitive and so making "the enemies" nominative by it as agent; so the prohibition is in wording addressed to the one addressed, while what is meant by it is someone else, like their saying «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» ("let me not see you here"), i.e. "let there not come from you what requires that the enemies gloat over me."

الإِشمات and الشَّماتة are rejoicing at a calamity that befalls your enemy. He said:

2304 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... والموتُ دون شماتَةِ الأعداء
(… [first half elided in the source] … and death is better than the gloating of enemies.)

It is said: its derivation is from شوامِت الدابة, which are its legs, because gloating turns the heart of the envier between the two states of joy and grief, like the turning about of the legs of the beast. تشميت العاطس and تَسْميته, with shīn and with sīn, is a supplication of good for him; Abū ʿUbayd said: "The shīn is the higher of the two dialects," and Thaʿlab said: "The original in both is the sīn, from السَّمْت, which is directness and guidance." It is also said: the meaning of tashmīt of the sneezer with the dotted letter is that Allah make him firm as He makes firm the legs of the beast. It is also said: rather the pattern تفعيل is for removal, i.e. may Allah remove gloating from him; and with the undotted sīn, i.e. may Allah return him to his first bearing (samt), meaning his form, because he suffers a jolt. Abū Bakr said: "One says سَمَته and سَمَت عليه, and in the ḥadīth: «وسَمَّت عليهما»."

semin-durr:182-182.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين كَذَّبُواْ}: two views are permissible. The clearer: that it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is the future clause after it. The second view: that it is accusative by occupation (ishtighāl) with an implied verb, its implied form being: "We shall draw gradually (sa-nastadrij) those who denied." Al-istidrāj is drawing near stage by stage and seizing little by little, from al-daraj (the step), because one who ascends climbs step by step, and likewise one who descends. It was said: it is taken from al-darj, which is folding, and from it: "he folded (daraja) the garment," and "he rolled up (daraja) the dead man" is the same. The meaning: their terms are folded up.
Al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Wathāb read «سَيَسْتَدْرِجُهم» with the yāʾ, which admits that the agent is the Creator, the Exalted, and it is an iltifāt from the first person to the third; and that the agent is the pronoun of denial understood from His saying «كذَّبوا». Al-Aʿshā said, on istidrāj:
2349 - فلو كنتَ في جُبٍّ ثمانين قامةً ... ورُقِّيْتَ أسبابَ السماءِ بسُلَّمِ
لَيَسْتَدْرِجَنْكَ القولُ حتى تَهِرَّهُ ... وتَعْلَمَ أنِّي عنكمُ غيرُ مُلْجَمِ
(Were you in a pit eighty fathoms deep, and were you raised to the ropes of heaven by a ladder, my speech would draw you on until you loathe it, and you would know that I am not bridled against you.)
It is said: "the boy walked haltingly (daraja)" when he shortens his steps, and "the people passed away (daraja)": some of them died after others.

semin-durr:183-183.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَأُمْلِي}: Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that it be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "and I grant respite"; that it be resumptive; and that it be conjoined to «سنستدرج». There is an objection in this, since in terms of eloquence, had it been so, [it would have been] «ونُمْلي» with the nūn of magnification. It is also permissible that this be close to an iltifāt. Al-imlāʾ is granting respite and prolonging. Al-matīn is the strong. From it is al-matn, which is the middle, because it is the strongest part of a living creature. Matuna yamtunu matānatan, that is, he became strong. The majority read «إنَّ كيدي» with kasra, as resumptive, indicating overpowering. Ibn ʿĀmir, in the transmission of ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, read «أنَّ كيدي» with fatḥa on the hamza, as a reason.

semin-durr:184-184.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ مَا بِصَاحِبِهِمْ}: several views are permissible regarding «ما». One: that it is interrogative, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is «بصاحبهم», that is: "What thing of madness has settled in their companion?" Al-jinna is a maṣdar meaning a state, like al-rikba and al-jilsa. It was said: what is meant by al-jinna is the jinn, as in {مِنَ الجنة والناس}, and then an omitted muḍāf is necessary, that is: "the touch of a jinn" or "the convulsion of a jinn."
The second: that «ما» is negating, that is: "there is no madness in their companion, nor touch of a jinn." Regarding these two clauses — I mean the interrogative or the negated — there are two views. The clearer: that it is in the position of accusative after removal of the preposition, because they suspend (the effect of) reflection, as it is among the verbs of the heart. The second: that the speech is complete at His saying «أو لم يتفكروا», then another speech begins, either an interrogative of denial or a negation. Al-Ḥawfī said: "«ما بصاحبهم» is suspended from an omitted verb indicated by the speech, the implied form being: 'Did they not reflect and so know what is in their companion?'" He said: "And «تفكَّر» is not suspended, because it did not enter upon a clause." This is weak, because they stated that a heart-verb which is transitive by a preposition or to one object, when suspended, does it remain as it was or is it made to include [the meaning of] what takes two objects?
The third: that «ما» is relative, meaning «الذي», the implied form being: "Did they not reflect on that which is in their companion," and on this the speech came out according to their claim. And on our saying that it is negating, «من جنة» would be a mubtadaʾ with «مِنْ» redundant in it and «بصاحبهم» its khabar, that is: "no madness is in their companion."

semin-durr:185-185.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنْ عسى}: concerning «أنْ» there are two views. One — and it is the correct one — that it is the lightened form of «أنَّ», and its noun is the pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn). «عسى» and what falls within its scope is in the position of nominative as its khabar, and no separation is made here between «أنْ» and the khabar even though it is a verb, because the inert verb that is not conjugated resembles nouns; and like it {وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ إِلاَّ مَا سعى} [al-Najm: 39] and {والخامسة أَنَّ غَضَبَ الله عَلَيْهَآ} [al-Nūr: 9] in the reading of Nāfiʿ, because it is a supplication. The khabar of «أنْ» occurred as a clause of request in these last two verses, since «عسى» is for inshāʾ (performative) and «غضب الله» is a supplication.
The second: that it is the maṣdar-forming one; Abū l-Baqāʾ said so, meaning the one with two-letter construction that puts the imperfect in the accusative. This is not good, because the grammarians stated that the maṣdar-forming «أنْ» is attached only to a conjugated verb in any form, that is past, imperfect and imperative, and «عسى» is not conjugated, so how can it occur as its ṣila? And «أنْ» on both views is in the position of genitive, conjoined to «ملكوت», that is: "Did they not look into the fact that the matter and affair is that perhaps…". And «أن يكون» is the agent of «عسى», and then it is complete (tāmma), because whenever it takes «أنْ» and what falls under it as its agent it is complete, and like it in that are awshaka and ikhlawlaqa. About the name of «يكون» there are two sayings. One: it is the pronoun of the affair, and «قد اقترب أجلهم» is its khabar. The second: that it is «أجلُهم», and «قد اقترب» is a clause of verb and agent, the agent being the pronoun of «أجلهم»; but the khabar, which is a verbal clause, was put before its noun, and this and the disagreement over it have been given earlier: namely that Ibn Mālik allows it and Ibn ʿUṣfūr prohibits it, at His saying: {مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 137].
His saying: {فَبِأَيِّ}: attached to «يُؤْمنون», and it is an interrogative clause brought for wonder, that is: "if they do not believe in this discourse, then how will they believe in any other?" And the hāʾ in «بعده» admits of returning to the Qurʾān and of returning to the Messenger, and then the speech involves an omitted muḍāf, that is: "after his report and his story"; and of returning to «أجلهم», that is: "when they die and their term expires, how will they believe after the expiry of their term?" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what do you attach His saying «فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون»? I say: to His saying «عسى أن يكونَ قد اقترب أجلهم». It is as if it were said: 'perhaps their term has drawn near, so what is the matter with them that they do not hasten [to] belief in the Qurʾān before death, and what are they waiting for after the truth has become clear, and in what discourse more true than it do they wish to believe?'" He means the attachment in meaning, linked to what precedes it, not the technical one, and it is clear.
His saying: «ويَذَرهم»: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read it with the yāʾ and a jussive verb; ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr with the yāʾ also and a nominative verb; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir with the nūn and a nominative verb also.
The jussive has also been reported from Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr among the irregular readings. The nominative is from one view, which is resumption, that is: "and He leaves them" or "and We leave them," according to the two readings. / As for the sukūn, it admits of two views. One: that it is a jussive conjoined to the position of His saying «فلا هادي له», because the negated clause is the apodosis of the condition and so is in the position of the jussive, so he conjoined to its position; and it is like His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا الفقرآء فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ وَيُكَفِّرُ} [al-Baqara: 271] with «يكفر» jussive, and like the poet's saying:
2350 - أنَّى سلكتَ فإنني لك كاشحٌ ... وعلى انتقاصِك في الحياة وأزْدَدِ
(Wherever you go, I am your enemy, and I am bent on belittling you in life, and I shall increase.)
Al-Wāḥidī also recited the other's saying:
2351 - فَأَبْلوني بَلِيَّتَكمْ لعلِّي ... أُصالِحُكم وأسْتدرِجْ نَوَيَّا
(So try me with your trial, perhaps I shall reconcile with you and draw my intention gradually.)
He said: "«أستدرج» is carried over to the position of the omitted fāʾ from «فلعلي أصالحكم»." The second: that it is a sukūn of lightening, like the reading of Abū ʿAmr: {يَنصُرْكُمُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 160] and {يُشْعِرُكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 109] and the like. As for the third person, it follows the name of Allah the Exalted, and the first person is by iltifāt from third to first for magnification.

semin-durr:187-187.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا}: two views on it. One: that «أيان» is a fronted khabar and «مُرْساها» a postponed mubtadaʾ. The second: that «أيان» is accusative as an adverbial by an implied verb, which verb makes «مرساها» nominative as its agent; this is the position of Abū l-ʿAbbās. This clause is in the position of accusative because it is a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from «الساعة», and then it ought not to have been in the position of genitive, because it is a substitute for a genitive. Abū l-Baqāʾ stated it explicitly, saying: "The clause is in the position of genitive as a badal from «الساعة», its implied form being: 'they ask you about the time of the arrival of the Hour.'" Except that what prevents its being genitive in position is that the badal is in the intention of repeating the governor, and the governor is «يَسْألونك»; and asking is suspended by the interrogative, and it is transitive; he means the interrogative clause is then in the position of accusative after removal of the preposition, as if it were said: "they ask you, when is the anchoring of the Hour?" So in reality it is a badal from the position of «عن الساعة», because the position of the genitive noun is accusative; and its like among badals, in the best views on it: «عَرَفْتُ زيداً أبو مَنْ هو» ("I knew Zayd — whose father is he").
And «أيان» is an adverbial of time, indeclinable because it includes the meaning of the interrogative, and it is not declined; it is followed by the mubtadaʾ and the imperfect verb, not the past, unlike «متى», which is followed by both types. Most often «أيَّان» is interrogative, as in the poet's saying:
2352 - أيَّان تَقْضي حاجتي أيَّانا ... أما تَرى لفِعْلها إبَّانا
(When will you fulfil my need, when? Do you not see that there is a due time for doing it?)
It may also be conditional, jussive-governing two verbs. The poet said:
2353 - أيَّان نُؤْمِنْكَ تُؤْمَنْ غيرَنا وإذا ... لم تُدْرِكِ الأمنَ منَّا لم تزلْ حَذِرا
(Whenever we give you safety, you will be safe from others; and if you do not attain safety from us, you will remain wary.)
And another said:
2354 - إذا النَّعْجَةُ العَجْفاءُ باتت بقَفْرةٍ ... فأيَّان ما تَعْدِلْ بها الريحُ تَنْزِلِ
(When the lean ewe spends the night in a desolate place, wherever the wind turns her, she will alight.)
The eloquent form is fatḥa on its hamza, and this is the reading of the majority. Al-Sulamī read it with kasra, and it is the dialect of Sulaym. The grammarians differed about «أيَّان»: is it simple or compound? Some held that its origin is «أيّ أوانٍ», so the hamza was dropped against analogy and nothing was given in exchange for it, and the wāw was changed to yāʾ against analogy, so three yāʾs came together, which was found heavy, and one of them was dropped, and the word was built on fatḥa so it became ayyān. They also differed about it: is it derived or not? Abū l-Fatḥ held that it is derived from awaytu ilayhi ("I resorted to it"), because the part resorts to the whole, and the meaning is "what time and what act"; and its pattern is faʿlān or fiʿlān according to the two dialects, and he denied that its pattern is faʿʿāl derived from «أين», because «أين» is an adverbial of place and «أيان» an adverbial of time.
And «مُرْساها» may be an ism maṣdar and may be an ism zamān (noun of time). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مُرْساها»: its anchoring or the time of its anchoring, that is, its establishment and fixing." The Shaykh said: "His supposing 'the time of its anchoring' is not good, because «أيَّان» is an inquiry about time, so it is not sound that it be a khabar about a time except figuratively, as the implied form would be 'at what time is the time of its anchoring,'" and it is good speech. It is said rasā yarsū: it stayed firm, and it is said only of a heavy thing, such as rasat al-safīna tarsū, and arsaytuhā.
His saying: {عِلْمُهَا}: a maṣdar annexed to its object, and the adverbial is its khabar. And His saying «في السماوات» admits of two views. One: that «في» has the meaning of «على», that is: "upon the inhabitants of the heavens," or it is heavy upon the very heavens and earth because of the splitting of this and the quaking of that. The second: that it is in its normal sense of containment, and the meaning is: its heaviness, which is its severity or the exaggeration in concealing it, occurred in these two containers.
His saying: {كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ}: this likening clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the object of «يسألونك». Regarding «عنها» there are two views. One: that it is attached to «يسألونك», and «كأنك حَفِيٌّ» is parenthetical, and its ṣila is omitted, its implied form being: "solicitous of it."
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There is an advancing and delaying in the speech," and there is no need for that because all of these are connected to the verb, for His saying: /"كأنك حفيٌّ" is a ḥāl as passed. The second: that «عن» has the meaning of «الباء», just as «الباء» has the meaning of «عن», as in {فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً} [al-Furqān: 59] and {وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السمآء بالغمام} [al-Furqān: 25], because ḥafī is not transitive with «عن» but with «الباء», as in His saying {كَانَ بِي حَفِيّاً} [Maryam: 47], and it is made to include the meaning of something that is transitive with «عن», that is: "as though you were uncovering, through your solicitude, about it."
Al-ḥafī is the one who inquires thoroughly into a thing, who is assiduous about it, attentive to its affair. He said:
2355 - سؤال حفيٍّ عن أخيه كأنه ... بذُكْرَتِهِ وَسْنانُ أو مُتَواسِنُ
(The question of one solicitous about his brother, as though, by remembering him, he were drowsy or feigning drowsiness.)
And another said:
2356 - فلمَّا التقينا بَيَّن السيفُ بيننا ... لسائلةٍ عنا حَفِيٍّ سؤالُها
(When we met, the sword made clear between us, to a woman asking about us, whose asking is solicitous.)
And al-Aʿshā said:
2357 - فإنْ تَسْأَلي عني فيا رُبُّ سائلٍ ... حَفِيٍّ عن الأعشى به حيث أَصْعَدا
(If you ask about me — many a solicitous inquirer has asked about al-Aʿshā, wherever he went up-country.)
And al-iḥfāʾ is thorough inquiry, and from it "iḥfāʾ of the moustaches," and al-ḥāfī (barefoot), because his foot wore down in thorough travel. And al-ḥafāwa is kindness and gentleness.
ʿAbd Allāh read «حَفِيٌّ بها», and it is evidence for whoever claimed that «عَنْ» has the meaning of «الباء». And ḥafī is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, that is, maḥfūw (treated with solicitude). It was said: in the sense of fāʿil, that is: "as though you were exaggerating in asking about it and straining toward knowledge of its coming."
